# Southern Coal Operating System (SCC-OS)
## Comprehensive Coal Business Function Inventory — WV / VA / KY (plus AL / TN)

**Purpose:** Exhaustive enumeration of every business function, process, human intervention point, data tracking requirement, document, hand-off, state-specific variation, and edge case across a multi-state Central Appalachian coal mining enterprise. Built to scope the SCC-OS platform — the most comprehensive coal operating management system ever built.

**Owner:** Southern Coal Corporation + affiliated Justice family companies
**Build Partner:** BlackRock AI
**Scope States:** West Virginia, Virginia, Kentucky (primary deep-dive); Alabama, Tennessee (footprint awareness)
**Companion Documents:** `SCC_Visual_Forge_Master_Context.md` (product/design brief); `CMS_Schema_Documentation.docx` (database schema); `SCC_Upload_Dashboard_Handoff_v5.md` (UI handoff)

**How this document is organized:** Ten domain sections, each produced by a dedicated research pass. Within each section, sub-areas are listed with their functions. Each function carries eight dimensions:

1. What it is
2. Who performs it (role)
3. Data captured
4. Documents / forms / standards / citations
5. Frequency
6. Hand-offs to other domains
7. State-specific differences (WV / VA / KY)
8. Common edge cases and pain points

**The 10 Domains:**

1. Mining Operations & Production
2. Environmental Compliance & Reclamation
3. Mine Safety & Health
4. Equipment, Maintenance, Reliability & Procurement
5. Finance, Accounting, Tax, Treasury & Audit
6. Land, Mineral Rights, Lease, Royalty & Title
7. Coal Marketing, Sales, Customer, Transportation & Logistics
8. HR, Workforce, Labor, Benefits & Wellness
9. Legal, Risk, Insurance, Bonding, Contracts & Compliance
10. IT, OT, Communications, Cybersecurity & Physical Security

**Total line count: ~13,000 lines. Treat this as a working source of truth — anything added to or modified in any sub-domain should round-trip back into this document.**

# Mining Operations & Production

Scope: All operational and production-side activities at Southern Coal Corporation mines across WV, VA, KY, AL, TN. Each function lists: what it is, who performs it, data fields, documents/forms/permits, frequency, hand-offs, state-specific notes, and edge cases.

Regulatory anchors referenced throughout:
- Federal: 30 CFR 75 (underground), 30 CFR 77 (surface), 30 CFR 90 (Part 50 reporting), 30 CFR 56/57 (M/NM where applicable), 27 CFR 555 (ATF explosives)
- WV: 38 CSR 2 (DEP surface mining rule), WV Code Chapter 22 Art. 3, WV Office of Miners' Health Safety & Training (OMHST) rules
- VA: VA Code Title 45.2 Subtitle II (Chapters 7–10), 4 VAC 25 (Dept. of Energy / DMME successor)
- KY: 405 KAR Chapters 7, 8, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20 (surface mining), KY Reclamation Guaranty Fund quarterly reporting
- Note: Where exact citation could not be verified by web search, the rule is stated functionally without a fake citation.

---

## 1. Surface Mining Methods

### 1.1 Contour Mining
- **What:** Excavation that follows the coal outcrop around a hillside, removing overburden in a strip parallel to the contour. Common in Central App ridge terrain (WV/VA/KY).
- **Who:** Mine superintendent, surface foreman, dozer operator, shovel/excavator operator, haul truck operator, drill operator, blaster, surveyor.
- **Data fields:** Pit ID, bench elevation, seam being mined, daily overburden BCY moved, coal tons hauled, strip ratio (BCY:ton), advance footage along contour, exposed coal footage, equipment hours, operator IDs, shift, weather, delay codes, GPS centerline of cut.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** SMCRA permit (state-issued, OSM-approved), permit boundary map, mining and reclamation plan (MRP), incremental bond release schedule, NPDES permit, sediment control plan, daily mine foreman's report, equipment pre-op forms, blasting records.
- **Frequency:** Continuous (per shift production reporting); plan updates monthly/quarterly; permit amendments event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Survey (volumetrics), Environmental (sediment/water), Reclamation (regrading/seeding behind active face), Lab (raw coal quality), Loadout (tons received), Maintenance (equipment), Engineering (mine plan).
- **State-specific:**
  - WV: 38 CSR 2 governs permit and reclamation; AOC (approximate original contour) variance requires specific findings.
  - VA: Title 45.2 Ch. 10 governs SMCRA program; DMME inspections.
  - KY: 405 KAR Ch. 16/18 (performance standards); separate Reclamation Guaranty Fund quarterly tonnage report.
- **Edge cases / pain points:** Boundary creep into adjacent unpermitted land; outslope failures after rain; mid-pit fault truncation of seam; coal seam pinch-out vs. predicted reserves; reconciling surveyed BCY to truck count.

### 1.2 Area Mining
- **What:** Strip mining of relatively flat or gently rolling terrain in a series of long parallel cuts, casting spoil into the previous cut. Less common in Central App, more applicable in AL.
- **Who:** Same as 1.1, plus dragline operator if used.
- **Data fields:** Strip number, cut width, cut length, dragline cycles, dragline swing angle, draglineBCY/hr, dozer push distances, spoil pile height, advance rate per shift.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** SMCRA permit, MRP, dragline walk plan, blasting plan, daily production sheets.
- **Frequency:** Continuous production; monthly survey reconciliation; annual mid-term permit review.
- **Hand-offs:** Survey, Reclamation (concurrent backfill), Environmental, Maintenance.
- **State-specific:** AL ASMC permitting; reclamation requirements differ.
- **Edge cases:** Dragline boom/bucket downtime cascade; spoil rehandle costs; saturated spoil instability.

### 1.3 Mountaintop Removal (MTR) / Cross-Ridge Mining
- **What:** Removal of upper elevation of a mountain to expose multiple seams; valley fills consume excess spoil.
- **Who:** Mine manager, blast crew, fleet (haul trucks 100T–240T), shovels (rope/hydraulic), dozers (D10/D11), motor graders, water trucks, fueler.
- **Data fields:** Seam stack identifier (each seam's tons separately), bench elevation, valley fill ID, fill lift number, cumulative fill volume, durable rock placement records, underdrain inspection logs.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** SMCRA permit with AOC variance (if applicable), Section 404/CWA permit for valley fills, NPDES, stream mitigation plan, fill construction certifications by PE.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; fill lift certification per lift; valley fill durable rock inspections weekly.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering (fill design), PE certification, Environmental (404/401 compliance), Survey (fill volumetrics, as-built), Reclamation.
- **State-specific:**
  - WV: SMCRA AOC variance + Aquatic Resource Protection (Stream Protection) provisions; valley fill design under 38 CSR 2.
  - KY: 405 KAR Ch. 24 / valley fill standards; durable rock fill requirements.
  - VA: limited MTR; same Title 45.2 framework.
- **Edge cases:** Stream Protection Rule reversals; durable rock vs. non-durable classification disputes; fill toe seep; fill settlement post-reclamation.

### 1.4 Highwall Mining (HWM)
- **What:** Remote-operated continuous miner head pushed horizontally into a seam exposed by a previous surface cut; recovers coal under highwall without removing overburden.
- **Who:** HWM operator, launch vehicle operator, push beam crew, surveyor (entry alignment), maintenance tech, foreman.
- **Data fields:** Entry number, entry azimuth, push depth (ft), web thickness left between entries, seam height entered, tons per entry, cycle time per push, beam count, machine availability %, methane readings at the launch, dust readings.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Mine plan showing HWM entries; ground control plan amendment; ventilation plan addendum (if classified); MSHA notification of HWM operations.
- **Frequency:** Per shift production reporting; entry-by-entry log; weekly equipment exam.
- **Hand-offs:** Survey (entry alignment, web verification), Geology (seam dip and roll), Maintenance (cutter head wear), Lab (quality per entry).
- **State-specific:**
  - WV/VA/KY: classified at state level; KY 405 KAR addresses; WV requires HWM plan; some states limit entry depth.
- **Edge cases:** Loss of communication with miner; bit/cutter wear forcing partial seam recovery; rib roll between entries; methane spike at depth; survey error causing entry collision.

### 1.5 Auger Mining
- **What:** Horizontal auger drilling into exposed seam to extract coal where strip ratio becomes uneconomical.
- **Who:** Auger operator, helper, foreman, surveyor.
- **Data fields:** Hole number, hole depth, auger diameter, flights run, coal tons per hole, web left between holes, cuttings sample.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Permit amendment if auger area added; ground control documentation.
- **Frequency:** Per shift; hole-by-hole.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab (cuttings sample), Survey, Engineering.
- **State-specific:** Generally less regulated than HWM but still under SMCRA.
- **Edge cases:** Hole collapse / lost auger string; spontaneous combustion in auger cavities (legacy hazard); roof fall sealing recovery.

### 1.6 Box Cut / Initial Cut
- **What:** First excavation that creates working room; spoil cannot be cast into a previous cut.
- **Who:** Surface superintendent, blasting crew, fleet.
- **Data fields:** Box cut volume, external spoil location, time to coal exposure.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Initial sequencing in MRP; out-of-pit spoil disposal area approval.
- **Frequency:** Project start; per pit start-up.
- **Hand-offs:** Reclamation (will reclaim out-of-pit spoil), Environmental.
- **Edge cases:** Out-of-pit spoil bond exposure; access road location disputes.

### 1.7 Pre-Stripping (Overburden-Only Phase)
- **What:** Removing overburden ahead of coal recovery to build inventory of exposed reserves.
- **Who:** Drill/blast, dozers, trucks, shovel.
- **Data fields:** BCY moved, exposed coal tons available, exposure ratio.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering (sequencing), Finance (capitalized stripping vs. operating cost).
- **Edge cases:** Accounting treatment under stripping cost guidance (ASC 930); pit slips during prolonged exposure.

---

## 2. Underground Mining Methods

### 2.1 Room-and-Pillar with Continuous Miner (CM)
- **What:** CM cuts coal in entries and crosscuts, leaving pillars for support. Shuttle cars or battery haulers transport coal to belt feeder/breaker.
- **Who:** Section foreman, CM operator, shuttle car operator(s), roof bolter operator(s), scoop operator, electrician, beltman, fireboss/preshift examiner.
- **Data fields:** Section ID, unit number (e.g., 002 MMU), entry width, crosscut spacing, cut sequence (place-changing), feet of advance per shift, tons per cut, methane readings (at face and bleeder), air quantity at last open crosscut, roof bolt count, bolt torque, mesh installed (yes/no), dust pump samples, equipment hours, delay codes.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** MSHA-approved ventilation plan, roof control plan, mine map, pre-shift exam record, on-shift exam record, weekly exam record, methane spot inspection records, dust control plan (Part 90), MMU designation list, escape and evacuation plan.
- **Frequency:** Pre-shift (within 3 hours before shift per 30 CFR 75.360); on-shift each shift (75.362); weekly (75.364); spad/survey monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Ventilation/Safety, Survey (advance, projections), Engineering (mine plan), Maintenance (CM, bolter, shuttle), Lab (face samples), Belt crew.
- **State-specific:**
  - WV: OMHST certified persons (mine foreman, fire boss); WV exam books often kept in parallel with MSHA.
  - VA: Title 45.2 Ch. 8 requires Virginia-certified mine foreman and on-shift/preshift exams documented; § 45.2-903 framework.
  - KY: KY EEC Mine Safety; KY-certified mine foreman and fire boss; preshift/on-shift records under 805 KAR (state mine safety) in parallel with MSHA.
- **Edge cases:** Mantrip delays, missing belt structure, water rise stopping equipment, methane bleed exceeding 1.0%, roof falls, place change with no bolted place ready, last open crosscut air drop.

### 2.2 Longwall Mining
- **What:** Shearer cuts coal across a long face (800–1,500 ft); chocks/shields support roof and advance; armored face conveyor (AFC) carries coal to stage loader and panel belt; gob caves behind shields.
- **Who:** Longwall coordinator, headgate/tailgate operator, shearer operator, shield mover, beltman, electricians, mechanics, ventilation tech.
- **Data fields:** Panel ID, shear cycle count, web depth per pass, tons per shear, AFC amp draws, shield pressures, shield advance count, methane at tailgate, methane at bleeder, bleeder evaluation points, dust readings (designated occupations), face conveyor downtime, shield leg leak count.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Longwall panel plan, ventilation plan (bleeder system, tailgate split), roof control plan, gob ventilation borehole (GVB) plan if used, MSHA panel start notification.
- **Frequency:** Per shift cycle reporting; bleeder evaluations weekly minimum; monthly longwall survey.
- **Hand-offs:** Geology (panel projections, faults), Engineering (panel design), Ventilation/Safety, Maintenance (shields, shearer), Coal Prep (longwall coal often higher fines), Survey.
- **State-specific:** WV and limited VA have active longwalls; states accept MSHA-approved plans largely intact but require state-certified personnel.
- **Edge cases:** Shearer breakdown mid-cut; shield set failures; floor heave; horizon control loss (cutting into roof or floor); recovery / startup move (highest-risk weeks of the year); bleeder evaluation point inaccessible due to fall.

### 2.3 Retreat Mining / Pillar Recovery
- **What:** Extracting previously left pillars while retreating outby; controlled caving behind line.
- **Who:** Section foreman, CM operator, bolters, scoops, fire boss, mining engineer.
- **Data fields:** Pillar number, lifts per pillar, percent recovery, breaker post placement, roof status, methane at face during pull, second-mining sequence diagram.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** MSHA-approved roof control plan with retreat provisions, pillar plan, ATRS use plan.
- **Frequency:** Per cut/per pillar; daily reporting.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering (sequence), Safety (high-risk operation), Ventilation.
- **State-specific:** Some operators prohibit retreat post-Crandall Canyon (UT) policy shifts; WV/VA/KY all permit with approved plans.
- **Edge cases:** Bumps/bounces, sudden caving overruns, unplanned roof fall trapping equipment.

### 2.4 Mains / Sub-Mains / Panels Development
- **What:** Development entries that establish infrastructure (belt, track, intake/return) before production sections begin.
- **Who:** Development section crew (often dedicated separate from production).
- **Data fields:** Mains advance per week, number of entries (typically 4–7), crosscut centers, belt structure installed, power center placement, rail track laid (ft).
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Approved mine plan, ventilation plan, roof control plan, electrical installation drawings.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; weekly progress meetings.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering, Electrical, Belt crew, Survey, Materials supply.
- **Edge cases:** Bottle-necking production due to lagging mains development; ventilation imbalance when adding splits.

### 2.5 Bleeder System Operation
- **What:** Air courses that ventilate worked-out (gob) areas; required by ventilation plan.
- **Who:** Mine foreman, ventilation tech, fire boss.
- **Data fields:** Bleeder fan static pressure, bleeder air quantity, methane at evaluation points, water level in bleeders.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** MSHA-approved ventilation plan, bleeder evaluation report.
- **Frequency:** Weekly evaluation (federal requirement under 75.364).
- **Hand-offs:** Safety/Ventilation, Engineering.
- **Edge cases:** Inaccessible evaluation points after a fall trigger MSHA modification requests.

## 3. Drilling & Blasting

### 3.1 Drill Pattern Design
- **What:** Engineering of blasthole spacing, burden, depth, sub-drill, stemming, and explosive load to achieve required fragmentation and minimize damage to highwall.
- **Who:** Mine engineer, blasting engineer, blaster-in-charge.
- **Data fields:** Bench ID, pattern ID, hole diameter, spacing (ft), burden (ft), bench height, sub-drill, stemming length, hole inclination, total holes, design powder factor (lb/BCY), explosive product mix.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Blasting plan (per SMCRA), pattern drawing, drill plan.
- **Frequency:** Per shot (pre-blast); design library reviewed monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Drilling crew, Blasting crew, Survey (pattern stake-out).
- **State-specific:** WV/VA/KY all require SMCRA blasting plan; state-certified blasters required (WV blaster cert, VA blaster cert under Title 45.2, KY blaster license under 805 KAR).
- **Edge cases:** Voids/mudseams causing flyrock; varying overburden lithology; pattern overlap with previous shot.

### 3.2 Blasthole Drilling
- **What:** Production drilling of designed pattern using rotary blasthole drills (e.g., DM45/DML/PV271).
- **Who:** Drill operator, drill mechanic, drill helper.
- **Data fields:** Hole number, easting/northing, collar elevation, hole depth drilled, drill time, penetration rate, water encountered (yes/no/depth), cuttings classification, hole condition (open/sloughed), drill operator ID, downtime codes.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Drill log, daily drill report.
- **Frequency:** Per hole; daily totals; monthly meters drilled per drill.
- **Hand-offs:** Blasting crew, Survey (as-drilled hole positions), Geology (cuttings).
- **Edge cases:** Lost drill steel; abandoned holes; misalignment causing burden problems; drill bit life tracking.

### 3.3 Hole Loading
- **What:** Charging blastholes with ANFO, emulsion, or blends; placement of boosters, detonators, and stemming.
- **Who:** Licensed blaster, powder crew, MMU (Mobile Manufacturing Unit) operator.
- **Data fields:** Per-hole: product type, lbs loaded, deck count, booster count, det delay, stemming type, stemming length, water in hole (yes/no), loaded by, time loaded.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Shot record / blast log (required for ATF inventory and SMCRA), Daily Summary of Explosives Transactions (ATF), magazine inventory reconciliation, blaster's signature.
- **Frequency:** Per shot.
- **Hand-offs:** ATF reporting (theft/loss within 24 hours), Magazine custodian, Environmental (NOx fume potential).
- **State-specific:**
  - WV: pre-blast survey notifications to property owners within 0.5 mi; blasting log retention.
  - VA: Title 45.2 + DMME blasting regs; 0.5 mi pre-blast survey.
  - KY: 805 KAR / 405 KAR blasting; pre-blast survey at owner request.
- **Edge cases:** Wet holes requiring emulsion; oversized booster; misfired holes; overloaded holes causing flyrock; magazine inventory variance.

### 3.4 Initiation Systems & Tie-In
- **What:** Connecting holes with shock tube, electronic detonators, or detonating cord; selecting delay sequence to control vibration and fragmentation.
- **Who:** Blaster-in-charge, blast crew.
- **Data fields:** Surface delay layout, in-hole delay, total MIS (max instantaneous charge), scaled distance to nearest protected structure.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Tie-in diagram, shot card.
- **Frequency:** Per shot.
- **Hand-offs:** Surface owners (notification), Seismograph monitoring.
- **Edge cases:** Cut-offs; misfires; lightning hold; weather hold.

### 3.5 Blast Execution & Guarding
- **What:** Clearing the blast area, posting guards on access roads, audible warning, firing the shot, post-blast inspection.
- **Who:** Blaster-in-charge, guards, foreman.
- **Data fields:** Shot date/time, weather (wind speed/direction, temp, humidity, inversion conditions), guard post log, all-clear time.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Blast log (date, time, location, lbs, scaled distance, seismograph), neighbor notification log.
- **Frequency:** Per shot.
- **Hand-offs:** Local LEO/911 (notification in some jurisdictions), Environmental (fume drift).
- **State-specific:**
  - WV: Office of Explosives and Blasting (within DEP) oversees; 38 CSR 2 + blasting rule; blast schedule published.
  - VA: Title 45.2 Ch. 11 / DMME blasting regs.
  - KY: 405 KAR Ch. 16 covers blasting; Department for Natural Resources oversight.
- **Edge cases:** Flyrock incidents (mandatory reporting), unexpected vibration exceedance, dust plume drift.

### 3.6 Blast Vibration & Airblast Monitoring
- **What:** Seismograph deployment near protected structures to record peak particle velocity (PPV) and airblast (dB) for each shot.
- **Who:** Blasting engineer, seismograph tech, third-party monitoring firm (sometimes).
- **Data fields:** Seismograph serial, deployment location (lat/long), distance to shot, PPV (in/sec) on three axes, airblast (dB), waveform file, frequency.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Seismograph report per shot, structure inventory.
- **Frequency:** Per shot near protected structures (typically every shot under SMCRA).
- **Hand-offs:** Citizen complaint resolution, Engineering (refine pattern), Environmental.
- **State-specific:** All three follow OSM scaled-distance or site-specific limits (typ. 1.0 in/sec PPV, 133 dB airblast).
- **Edge cases:** Seismograph fails to trigger; complaint without exceedance; structure damage claims.

### 3.7 Powder Factor & Fragmentation Analysis
- **What:** Post-shot review of fragmentation (P80 size) vs. design to refine future patterns.
- **Who:** Blasting engineer, shovel operator feedback.
- **Data fields:** Pile profile, photo-based size distribution (Split-Desktop / WipFrag), digging rate impact, secondary breakage events.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Fragmentation report.
- **Frequency:** Per shot or weekly composite.
- **Hand-offs:** Loading (productivity), Crushing.
- **Edge cases:** Oversize bridging the crusher; tight muck pile slowing shovel.

### 3.8 Explosives Storage & ATF Compliance
- **What:** Operation of magazines storing high explosives, detonators, boosters per 27 CFR 555.
- **Who:** Magazine keeper / blaster, mine operations.
- **Data fields:** Magazine ID, type (Type 1–5), construction class, distance to inhabited structures, daily inventory by product, receipts, issues to shot, returns, employee responsible.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** ATF Federal Explosives License (FEL), magazine inspection log, Daily Summary of Magazine Transactions (DSMT), employee possessor lists (ATF Form 5400.28), theft/loss report (ATF Form 5400.5 within 24 hours).
- **Frequency:** Daily inventory; theft/loss event-driven within 24 hours.
- **Hand-offs:** ATF, State Fire Marshal (WV, KY require state explosive permit too).
- **State-specific:**
  - WV: WV State Fire Marshal explosives license also required.
  - KY: KY Department of Housing/Fire Marshal explosives permit.
  - VA: VA State Police explosives certification of handlers.
- **Edge cases:** Inventory variance triggers ATF investigation; magazine site distance violation when neighborhood encroaches.

## 4. Mine Planning & Sequencing

### 4.1 Long-Range Mine Plan (LRP / Life-of-Mine)
- **What:** Multi-year plan defining pit progression, reserves to be mined, equipment fleet, infrastructure, reclamation.
- **Who:** Chief mine engineer, planning engineers, GM.
- **Data fields:** Yearly tons by seam, strip ratio curve, capital schedule, equipment retirement/acquisition, permit needs.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** LOM plan document, reserve report, permit acquisition timeline.
- **Frequency:** Annual update; full re-baseline every 3–5 years.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (capex), Reserves (SK-1300 reporting if public), Permitting.
- **Edge cases:** Reserve write-downs; coal market collapse forcing re-sequencing.

### 4.2 Mid-Range / Budget Plan (12–24 months)
- **What:** Quarterly forecasts of tons per pit/section by month for budget and contractual deliveries.
- **Who:** Mine engineers, ops superintendents.
- **Data fields:** Monthly tons by seam, by quality grade; cost per ton forecast; equipment hours forecast.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Budget book, sales contract delivery schedule.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly re-forecast; annual budget.
- **Hand-offs:** Sales/Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain.
- **Edge cases:** Weather variance, equipment availability, geology surprises.

### 4.3 Short-Range / Operational Plan (1–13 weeks)
- **What:** Weekly section/pit projections, equipment placement, manning, sequencing of cuts.
- **Who:** Section foreman, mine engineer, superintendent.
- **Data fields:** Cut sequence, projected feet of advance, projected tons, equipment moves, manpower assignment.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Weekly plan map, projection sheets.
- **Frequency:** Weekly (often updated daily).
- **Hand-offs:** Operations, Maintenance (planned moves), Survey (stake-out).
- **Edge cases:** Equipment breakdowns shifting the entire sequence.

### 4.4 Pit / Section Plan
- **What:** Detailed plan of next 30–60 days of a specific pit or underground section.
- **Who:** Mine engineer, section foreman.
- **Data fields:** Bench plans (surface) or projection map (UG), spoil placement, haul road location, escape routes.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Pit map, section projection.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Survey, Operations, Safety.

### 4.5 Reserve / Resource Estimation
- **What:** Calculation of in-place coal tons by category (proven/probable/inferred) and recoverable tons.
- **Who:** Geologist, mining engineer, qualified person (QP) under SK-1300 if public-reported.
- **Data fields:** Drillhole assays, seam thicknesses, BD, structure, mining height, recovery factor, dilution, ash/sulfur/BTU averages, ownership status.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Reserve report, technical report summary (TRS) if public, lease coverage maps.
- **Frequency:** Annual restatement; ad hoc for acquisitions.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance/Investor Relations, Legal (leases), Permitting.
- **Edge cases:** Lease expirations dropping reserves; QP disagreements; geological model revisions.

### 4.6 Permit Acquisition & Amendment Sequencing
- **What:** Long-lead planning of new permits and revisions so mining never runs out of permitted ground.
- **Who:** Permitting manager, environmental, engineering.
- **Data fields:** Permit number, acres, status (pre-app, NOI, draft, public notice, issued), expected issuance date, mining sequence dependency.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Application packages, public notice, hearing records.
- **Frequency:** Tracked weekly; events as they occur.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental (heavy overlap), Operations.
- **State-specific:** WV/VA/KY have different application templates and review timelines; KY frequently 12–18 months for new SMCRA.
- **Edge cases:** Permits stalled in litigation; cumulative hydrologic impact assessments delaying issuance.
