## 5. Geology & Exploration

### 5.1 Core / Rotary Exploration Drilling
- **What:** Drilling boreholes to characterize seam thickness, structure, quality, overburden, hydrology.
- **Who:** Geologist, drill contractor.
- **Data fields:** Hole ID, location (NAD83 state plane), collar elev, total depth, drilling method, recovery %, lithology log, seam intercepts (top/bottom), water levels, gas readings.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** State exploration notice/permit (KY requires under 405 KAR 20:010), borehole abandonment / plugging records, lease access.
- **Frequency:** Project-driven; annual exploration budgets.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab (core quality), Engineering (model update), Hydrology, Reclamation (plug, restore).
- **State-specific:** KY 405 KAR 20:010 exploration permit; WV exploration notice to DEP; VA notification to DMME.
- **Edge cases:** Lost circulation; hole deviation; coal core "wash-out"; abandoned holes becoming hydrologic shortcuts.

### 5.2 Geophysical Logging
- **What:** Wireline tools (density, gamma, caliper, sonic) run in boreholes to confirm seam picks and calculate density-derived ash.
- **Who:** Logging contractor, geologist.
- **Data fields:** LAS file per log run, depth-correlated curves, seam pick depths, density-derived ash.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Log run report.
- **Frequency:** Per hole.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab (verification), Engineering.
- **Edge cases:** Tool stick; depth shifts; equivalence between density-derived ash and lab ash.

### 5.3 Seam Correlation & Structure Mapping
- **What:** Building geological model — seam top/bottom surfaces, faults, splits, washouts.
- **Who:** Geologist, GIS tech.
- **Data fields:** Seam top/bottom surfaces, isopach maps, structure contour maps, fault traces, split geometry, paleochannels.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Geological model file (Minex, Vulcan, Carlson), structure maps in permit.
- **Frequency:** Continuous update; quarterly model release.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering (mine plan), Survey (verification at face).
- **Edge cases:** Splits not predicted; faults causing seam loss; rolls that change mining height week-to-week.

### 5.4 Quality Modeling
- **What:** Building quality block model (ash, sulfur, BTU, moisture, volatile, HGI) from drillhole assays.
- **Who:** Geologist, quality engineer.
- **Data fields:** Quality by hole (raw and washed at multiple SG), composite by seam, block model quality attributes.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Quality model report.
- **Frequency:** Updated each new drilling campaign; quarterly reconciliation vs. actuals.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab (assay reconciliation), Sales (contract spec matching), Coal Prep (washability).
- **Edge cases:** Bias between model and shipped quality; oxidized seam outcrop areas.

### 5.5 Methane / Gas-in-Place Studies (Underground)
- **What:** Desorption tests on core for in-situ gas content (for ventilation/degas planning).
- **Who:** Geologist, lab.
- **Data fields:** Gas content (scf/ton), desorption curves, lost gas estimate.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Desorption report.
- **Frequency:** Per new panel area exploration.
- **Hand-offs:** Ventilation engineer, Degas (GVB) program if applicable.
- **Edge cases:** High gas content panel forcing ventilation plan changes.

### 5.6 Hydrogeologic Characterization
- **What:** Determining aquifers, recharge, transmissivity for mine drainage prediction (PHC).
- **Who:** Geologist, hydrogeologist.
- **Data fields:** Static water levels by hole, pump test data, water chemistry (baseline).
- **Documents/forms/permits:** PHC (Probable Hydrologic Consequences) section of SMCRA permit, CHIA inputs.
- **Frequency:** Permit-driven; periodic monitoring.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental, Permitting.
- **Edge cases:** Inter-basin transfer claims; well/spring complaints from neighbors.

---

## 6. Surveying

### 6.1 Monthly Volumetric Survey (Surface)
- **What:** End-of-month survey of pits, spoils, stockpiles to compute moved volumes, exposed coal, inventory.
- **Who:** Mine surveyor, surveying contractor.
- **Data fields:** Topo surface for current month, surface for previous month, BCY moved, coal exposed (tons), stockpile tons by location, reconciliation to truck count/scale.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Monthly survey report, signed by licensed surveyor (WV, VA, KY all require LS for boundary; volumetrics may be done by mine surveyor).
- **Frequency:** Monthly (typically last 1–2 days of month or first day).
- **Hand-offs:** Accounting (inventory valuation), Engineering (plan vs. actual), Production reporting (reconciliation).
- **Edge cases:** Drone weather hold; survey grid not flown to fill edges; differences between drone DEM and ground truth.

### 6.2 Drone / UAV / LiDAR Survey
- **What:** UAV-based photogrammetry or LiDAR collection for topo, stockpiles, fills.
- **Who:** Part 107 pilot (surveyor or contractor).
- **Data fields:** Flight log, GCP positions, RMS error, point cloud (LAS), DEM, orthomosaic.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** FAA Part 107 currency, flight log, authorization for any restricted airspace.
- **Frequency:** Monthly; ad-hoc for fill certifications.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering, Environmental.
- **Edge cases:** Vegetation under-classification; canopy-covered ground; weather windows.

### 6.3 Underground Survey
- **What:** Spad-and-spad-line survey of underground workings — entries, crosscuts, sections.
- **Who:** Mine surveyor, surveyor's helper.
- **Data fields:** Spad coordinates, sight distances, projection azimuth, advance per section per period, mine map update.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Updated mine map (statutory — kept current within prescribed time; certified annually by PE/LS).
- **Frequency:** Monthly (face advance); annual certification of mine map.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering, Ventilation (split survey), Safety (escape route accuracy).
- **State-specific:**
  - WV: Mine map filed with OMHST; PE/LS certification of UG mine map annually.
  - VA: Title 45.2 mine map filing requirements.
  - KY: Mine map filed with KY EEC Mine Safety; periodic update.
- **Edge cases:** Map error compounding into ventilation plan errors; outdated maps for mine rescue use.

### 6.4 Pre-Blast Survey (Drill Pattern Stake-Out)
- **What:** Surveying drill pattern locations onto bench prior to drilling.
- **Who:** Surveyor.
- **Data fields:** Hole stake easting/northing/elevation per design.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Stake-out sheet.
- **Frequency:** Per pattern.
- **Hand-offs:** Drillers.
- **Edge cases:** Stake loss due to weather; pattern modification after partial drilling.

### 6.5 Post-Blast / As-Drilled Survey
- **What:** As-built hole positions, post-shot pile, residual highwall.
- **Who:** Surveyor.
- **Frequency:** Per shot or weekly composite.
- **Hand-offs:** Blasting engineer, Engineering.

### 6.6 Pre-Blast Structure Survey (Neighbors)
- **What:** Pre-existing damage inventory at protected structures within blast influence zone, performed before mining begins.
- **Who:** Pre-blast surveyor (often third-party).
- **Data fields:** Owner name, structure address/photos/condition notes, signed acknowledgement.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Pre-blast survey report filed with state.
- **Frequency:** Pre-mining for each structure within radius (typ 0.5 mi WV/VA/KY).
- **Hand-offs:** Citizen complaint resolution.
- **State-specific:** WV statutory pre-blast survey; KY pre-blast survey on request; VA similar.
- **Edge cases:** Owner refuses access; damage claims for pre-existing conditions.

### 6.7 Boundary Survey & Permit Boundary Maintenance
- **What:** Maintaining accurate permit boundary stakes/flags; verifying mining stays inside permit.
- **Who:** Licensed surveyor.
- **Data fields:** Boundary coordinates, monumentation, deed/lease references.
- **Frequency:** As needed; before approaching boundary.
- **Hand-offs:** Operations (stop-mining triggers), Legal.
- **Edge cases:** Encroachment over permit boundary = TDN / NOV; mining off-lease = trespass/legal action.

### 6.8 Reclamation As-Built Survey
- **What:** Final regrade survey to demonstrate AOC or approved post-mining topo for bond release.
- **Who:** Surveyor, reclamation supervisor.
- **Frequency:** Per Phase 1/2/3 bond release event.
- **Hand-offs:** Reclamation/Environmental.

---

## 7. Coal Preparation / Wash Plants

### 7.1 Raw Coal Receiving / Stockpile Feed
- **What:** Raw coal arriving via belt, truck, or rail from mines (own or contract) is dumped and reclaimed to the plant feed.
- **Who:** Plant operator, dump attendant, front-end loader operator.
- **Data fields:** Source mine, seam, raw tons received, moisture, top size, foreign material rejects.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Plant feed log; if interstate, mine-of-origin tag for Part 50 reporting.
- **Frequency:** Per shift.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab (raw sample), Loadout/Inventory.
- **Edge cases:** Wrong-quality coal dumped on wrong pile; tramp metal (bolts/cable) reaching primary crusher.

### 7.2 Primary Crushing / Sizing
- **What:** Reduction of raw coal to plant feed size (typ. 2"–6") via rotary breakers, roll crushers, or feeder-breakers.
- **Who:** Plant operator, mechanic.
- **Data fields:** Throughput (tph), amp draw, downtime, screen oversize %.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Plant operating log.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance.
- **Edge cases:** Tramp iron, oversize bridging.

### 7.3 Heavy Media Vessel (HMV) Circuit
- **What:** Coarse coal (typ +1mm or +0.5") separated from rock via magnetite-water suspension at controlled SG.
- **Who:** Plant operator, plant chemist (media control).
- **Data fields:** Vessel feed tph, separation SG, magnetite circulating density, magnetite losses (lb/ton), partition curve data, ash on clean coal product, ash on refuse, Ep value.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Daily plant report; sampling per ASTM/ISO procedures.
- **Frequency:** Per shift; partition curves quarterly or as troubleshooting.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab (ash, moisture, sulfur), Magnetite supplier (deliveries).
- **Edge cases:** Magnetite loss spikes; SG drift; misplaced material.

### 7.4 Dense Medium Cyclones (DMC)
- **What:** Smaller coal (typ. 0.5mm–1"–2") separated by magnetite cyclones.
- **Who:** Plant operator.
- **Data fields:** Cyclone feed pressure, inlet density, vortex finder wear, spigot wear, partition data.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** Cyclone wear changing partition; pressure swings.

### 7.5 Spiral Concentrators / Fine Coal Circuit
- **What:** Gravity separation of fine coal (typ 0.15–1 mm) using spirals.
- **Who:** Plant operator.
- **Data fields:** Spiral feed slurry density, splitter positions, clean/middling/refuse split, ash on each product.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; splitter adjustment by shift.
- **Edge cases:** Splitter set wrong; spiral wear; feed surges.

### 7.6 Froth Flotation (Ultra-Fines)
- **What:** Recovery of -0.15 mm coal via flotation cells using collector (diesel/MIBC).
- **Who:** Flotation operator, plant chemist.
- **Data fields:** Reagent dosages, cell pulp level, froth depth, recovery %, ash on concentrate.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Reagent supply chain, Environmental (reagent runoff).
- **Edge cases:** Lost recovery due to oxidized fines; reagent overdose.

### 7.7 Sizing Screens (Sieve Bend, Banana, Horizontal)
- **What:** Wet/dry screens that separate by size before/after gravity circuits.
- **Who:** Plant operator, mechanic.
- **Data fields:** Screen panel condition, blinding events, undersize/oversize splits.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; panel changes scheduled.
- **Edge cases:** Blinded panels reducing throughput; wear-out hidden until quality drift.

### 7.8 Centrifuges (Coarse, Fine, Screen-Bowl)
- **What:** Mechanical dewatering of clean coal product to ship-ready moisture.
- **Who:** Plant operator, mechanic.
- **Data fields:** Centrifuge basket wear, motor amps, product moisture %, vibration.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** Basket cracking; bearing failure; moisture out of spec.

### 7.9 Thickeners / Clarifiers
- **What:** Settles fine refuse out of plant water for recycle.
- **Who:** Plant operator, water treatment tech.
- **Data fields:** Underflow density, overflow clarity (TSS), flocculant dosage, rake torque.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Slurry impoundment (underflow), Water treatment.
- **Edge cases:** Thickener upset = plant shutdown; flocculant shortage.

### 7.10 Filter Press / Belt Press (Fine Refuse Dewatering)
- **What:** Mechanical dewatering of fine refuse to filter cake for disposal (alternative to slurry impoundment).
- **Who:** Press operator.
- **Data fields:** Cycle count, cake moisture %, tons of cake produced.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Refuse haulage to coarse refuse fill.
- **Edge cases:** Cloth blinding; cycle time creep.

### 7.11 Magnetite Recovery
- **What:** Recovery of magnetite from clean coal and refuse via magnetic separators.
- **Who:** Plant operator.
- **Data fields:** Magnetite consumption lb/ton, magnetic field strength.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** High magnetite loss eating margin.

### 7.12 Plant Sampling (ASTM D2234, D2013, D7430)
- **What:** Mechanical and manual sampling at multiple plant points for QC.
- **Who:** Plant sampler, lab tech.
- **Data fields:** Sample point, time, mass, increment count.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Sample log; chain of custody.
- **Frequency:** Per shift composite (typical).
- **Hand-offs:** Lab.
- **Edge cases:** Sampler malfunction (bias); composite contamination.

### 7.13 Plant Process Control / DCS
- **What:** Distributed control system or PLC HMI runs plant; trends and alarms recorded.
- **Who:** Plant operator, controls technician.
- **Data fields:** Tag values (densities, flows, levels, pressures, amp draws), alarm logs.
- **Frequency:** Real-time.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance reliability program; Engineering.

### 7.14 Plant Downtime / Delay Coding
- **What:** Categorized recording of every minute of downtime by cause.
- **Who:** Plant operator, plant superintendent.
- **Data fields:** Start/end time, equipment, reason code (mechanical / electrical / process / no feed / no clean coal storage / shipping / weather / planned maint), description.
- **Frequency:** Per shift.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance/Reliability, Engineering.
- **Edge cases:** "Cascading" delays attributed to wrong root cause.

### 7.15 Refuse Handling (Coarse)
- **What:** Removal of coarse refuse to disposal area (refuse fill).
- **Who:** Refuse truck driver, dozer operator.
- **Data fields:** Truck count or belt tonnage, dump location, lift placement.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Refuse disposal area permit (SMCRA), MSHA refuse pile plan (when applicable), inspection log.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; weekly inspection.
- **Hand-offs:** Geotech (pile stability), Environmental (NPDES, sediment), Survey.
- **Edge cases:** Spontaneous combustion / smoldering; pile slope failure.

### 7.16 Refuse Handling (Fine / Slurry)
- **What:** Pumping thickener underflow to slurry impoundment, or pressing to cake.
- **Who:** Pump operator, embankment tech.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; impoundment monitoring per MSHA-approved plan (typically weekly + quarterly + annual).
- **Hand-offs:** Geotech, MSHA Impoundment Program.
- **Edge cases:** Slurry breakthroughs (Buffalo Creek, Martin County legacy); freeboard violations.

---

## 8. Loadouts

### 8.1 Silo / Stockpile Management at Loadout
- **What:** Receiving clean coal from plant and storing in silos or piles for shipment.
- **Who:** Loadout operator, scale operator, dozer operator.
- **Data fields:** Silo level (tons), pile inventory by grade, FIFO age, surveyed pile tons, moisture.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Inventory ticket, daily pile log.
- **Frequency:** Per shift; monthly survey reconciliation.
- **Hand-offs:** Sales (available inventory), Finance (book inventory), Lab.
- **Edge cases:** Silo bridging, segregation, frozen pile, mixing of grades.

### 8.2 Truck Loadout
- **What:** Loading bottom-dump, end-dump, or quad-axle trucks via flood-loader or front-end loader.
- **Who:** Loadout operator, scale operator.
- **Data fields:** Truck #, carrier, gross/tare/net weight, time loaded, destination, ticket #, driver, grade loaded, moisture.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Bill of lading / scale ticket; certified scale ticket (NTEP); DOT bill of lading; coal severance form (state).
- **Frequency:** Per truck.
- **Hand-offs:** Sales, Finance, State severance tax filings, Customer.
- **State-specific:**
  - WV: Coal severance tax; weighmaster certification per state weights & measures.
  - VA: Coal severance and license tax.
  - KY: Coal severance tax (KY Dept. of Revenue); separate KY DOT haul-road permitting on coal haul roads.
- **Edge cases:** Overweight trucks (DOT fines); scale out of calibration; printer failure.

### 8.3 Rail Loadout (Unit Train, Manifest)
- **What:** Loading rail cars (typically 100-ton or 110-ton open-top, sometimes covered hoppers) from flood-load chute, batch weigh, or load-on-the-fly.
- **Who:** Loadout operator, train coordinator, railroad conductor.
- **Data fields:** Train ID, locomotive number, car numbers in order, individual car tare/gross/net, train total tons, BTU/ash/sulfur per train (lab), bill of lading, destination, customer.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Rail bill of lading, certified batch-weigh records, NTEP scale cert, RR weighing-in-motion (WIM) cert, demurrage records, AAR car condition.
- **Frequency:** Per train (often 1–3 trains/day at large loadouts).
- **Hand-offs:** Sales/Logistics, Lab (composite analysis for invoice), Customer.
- **Edge cases:** Overload cars (carrier-imposed penalty), missed window (demurrage), frozen coal not unloading at destination (use of freeze-conditioning agent).

### 8.4 Barge Loadout
- **What:** Loading river barges on the Big Sandy / Ohio / Kanawha / Tennessee systems via stacker/conveyor.
- **Who:** Dock operator, river logistics coordinator.
- **Data fields:** Barge name/number, draft survey tons, owner, fleet boat, destination.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Barge BOL, USCG documents, USACE permits for terminal.
- **Frequency:** Per barge.
- **Hand-offs:** River logistics, USCG.
- **Edge cases:** River level too low / too high; freeze; lock outages.

### 8.5 Scale Certification & Calibration
- **What:** Certified truck scales and batch-weigh hoppers must be calibrated to state weights & measures and NTEP standards.
- **Who:** Scale service company, state inspector.
- **Data fields:** Cal date, test weight values, error %, sealed/unsealed status.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** State scale certificate, NTEP cert, calibration ticket.
- **Frequency:** Calibration typically semi-annual or annual; state inspection annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Sales/Customer (invoicing).
- **State-specific:** WV Weights & Measures, VA Office of Weights and Measures, KY Division of Weights and Measures.
- **Edge cases:** Drift between cal cycles, dispute resolution if customer claims weight error.

### 8.6 Quality at Loadout (Sample Tower)
- **What:** Mechanical sampler at the loadout boom or chute collects representative sample of shipped product.
- **Who:** Sampler tech, lab.
- **Data fields:** Sample mass, increments, sample ID linked to BOL/train.
- **Frequency:** Per shipment.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab.
- **Edge cases:** Sampler bias affecting invoice quality.

---

## 9. Stockpile Management

### 9.1 Raw Coal Stockpiles
- **What:** Surge stockpiles between mine and plant by mine/seam/quality.
- **Who:** Plant operator, FEL operator.
- **Data fields:** Pile ID, source mine, seam, tons, moisture, ash, sulfur, BTU, age.
- **Frequency:** Per shift updates; monthly survey.
- **Edge cases:** Pile aging causing oxidation; mixing wrong-quality sources.

### 9.2 Clean Coal Stockpiles by Grade
- **What:** Segregated stockpiles for different products (e.g., met low-vol, met high-vol, steam high-ash).
- **Who:** Loadout operator.
- **Data fields:** Grade ID, tons, quality, customer reservation status.
- **Hand-offs:** Sales.
- **Edge cases:** Cross-contamination of grades; FIFO not enforced leading to oxidation.

### 9.3 Reject / Refuse Stockpile
- **What:** Coarse refuse short-term storage before placement at disposal area.
- **Who:** Refuse haul crew.
- **Data fields:** Tons hauled, placement location.
- **Hand-offs:** Refuse disposal area mgmt.

### 9.4 Stockpile Survey & Reconciliation
- **What:** Monthly drone/GNSS pile surveys reconciled against accounting books.
- **Who:** Surveyor.
- **Data fields:** Surveyed tons, book tons, variance %, density factor used.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (inventory adjustment).
- **Edge cases:** Density assumptions wrong; pile heel under loader not surveyed.

### 9.5 Spontaneous Combustion Monitoring
- **What:** Thermal monitoring (thermocouples, IR) and pile shaping practices for high-vol coals prone to self-heating.
- **Who:** Stockpile foreman.
- **Data fields:** Hot spot location, temperature, action taken (re-shape, water, dig out).
- **Frequency:** Weekly visual; thermography quarterly or as triggered.
- **Edge cases:** Hot pile in summer with no rapid response = pile burn.

---

## 10. Production Reporting

### 10.1 Shift Production Report
- **What:** End-of-shift report by section/pit detailing tons, feet/BCY, delays, equipment performance, manning.
- **Who:** Section/surface foreman.
- **Data fields:** Section ID, shift, manning, tons (clean if estimated, raw if at mine), feet of advance, equipment hours, delay codes, incidents.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Daily mine foreman's report (state-required record).
- **Frequency:** Per shift.
- **Hand-offs:** Mine office, Maintenance, Safety.
- **State-specific:** WV / VA / KY all have state mine foreman's report formats parallel to MSHA record requirements.

### 10.2 Daily Production Report
- **What:** Roll-up of all shifts per mine.
- **Who:** Mine clerk / superintendent.
- **Data fields:** Day total tons by section/seam, hours, manning, vs. plan, vs. budget.
- **Frequency:** Daily by 8 a.m.
- **Hand-offs:** Mine GM, Sales, Finance.

### 10.3 Weekly Production Report
- **What:** Week roll-up plus forecast next week.
- **Frequency:** Weekly (typically Sunday/Monday morning).

### 10.4 Monthly Production Report
- **What:** Reconciles surveyed volumes, scale tons, plant input/output, inventory changes, lab quality.
- **Who:** Mine engineer, controller.
- **Data fields:** Mined tons (survey-reconciled), shipped tons, inventory delta, plant yield, quality.
- **Frequency:** Monthly close.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance, Tax (severance), Sales, Reserves.

### 10.5 MSHA Quarterly Employment & Production Report (Form 7000-2)
- **What:** Federal-required reporting of employee hours and coal production by mine ID per 30 CFR Part 50.
- **Who:** Safety/HR clerk.
- **Data fields:** MSHA mine ID, employee hours worked (by subunit), tons produced, contractor hours.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** MSHA Form 7000-2.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** MSHA (federal), incident rate calculations.
- **Edge cases:** Contractor hours mis-categorized; subunit code errors.

### 10.6 State Production Reports
- **What:** Various state reports of production for tax, royalty, and trust fund purposes.
- **Who:** Mine clerk, tax dept.
- **Documents/forms/permits:**
  - WV: WV Severance Tax (monthly/quarterly), DEP production by permit (annual).
  - VA: VA Coal Severance and License Tax.
  - KY: KY Severance Tax; KY Reclamation Guaranty Fund quarterly tons (per 405 KAR — verified, records retained 6 years).
  - AL: ASMC and Dept. of Revenue.
  - TN: OSMRE (TN is federal program).
- **Frequency:** Monthly to quarterly varies.
- **Edge cases:** Reporting mismatches between BOL tons and severance return triggering audit.

### 10.7 Royalty Reporting (Per Lease)
- **What:** Coal tons attributed to each lease tract for royalty payment.
- **Who:** Land/lease admin, mine engineer.
- **Data fields:** Lease ID, tract acres, tons mined this period, sales price, royalty rate, minimums.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Land department, AP/royalty payments.
- **Edge cases:** Allocation between adjacent leases when mining crosses tract lines; minimum royalties when no production.

---

## 11. Delay & Downtime Coding

### 11.1 Delay Code Library
- **What:** Standardized list of reason codes used at every level of production reporting.
- **Categories (typical):**
  - **Mechanical** — Engine, hydraulics, drive train, undercarriage, breakage
  - **Electrical** — Power loss, motor, controls, cables, transformer trip
  - **Operational** — No operator, shift change, meal break, training, mantrip in/out, examinations, dust pump install, rock dusting
  - **Geological** — Roof fall, floor heave, water, gas, bad top, seam roll, fault
  - **Weather** — Lightning hold, rain (haul road), fog, snow/ice, temperature extremes
  - **No truck / No haul** — Trucks down, dispatcher hold, truck queue
  - **No place to dump** — Dump spotter unavailable, dump full, spoil regrade required
  - **No feed** — Plant: silo full, customer not ready, no rail cars, no barges, river closed
  - **Material handling** — Belt down, feeder breaker, crusher, scale issue
  - **Blasting** — Pre-blast clearing, post-blast inspection, lightning hold during loading
  - **Safety / Examination** — Pre-shift, weekly exam, dust survey, MSHA inspection
  - **Move / Setup** — Equipment relocation, longwall move, section move
  - **Planned maintenance** — PM schedule, rebuild
  - **Power outage** — Utility outage
  - **Inspection / Regulatory** — MSHA, state inspection (production stoppage)
  - **Strike / Labor**
- **Who:** Operators record at face; foreman approves; clerk codes; engineer audits.
- **Data fields:** Start time, end time, duration, code, sub-code, equipment, description, related incident #.
- **Frequency:** Real-time / per shift entry.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance reliability (mechanical/electrical), Engineering (geological), HR (labor/safety).
- **Edge cases:** Operators choosing easy codes (no operator vs. no place to dump); double-counting concurrent delays; debate over what counts as "production time" denominator.

### 11.2 Delay Analysis & Pareto Reporting
- **What:** Weekly/monthly Pareto of delay codes to drive reliability improvement.
- **Who:** Production engineer.
- **Frequency:** Weekly.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance, Engineering.

---

## 12. Geotechnical (Production-Side)

### 12.1 Highwall Stability Monitoring
- **What:** Visual and instrumented monitoring of highwalls for cracks, raveling, slip surfaces.
- **Who:** Surface foreman, engineering, geotech consultant.
- **Data fields:** Crack widths over time, prism/radar displacements, extensometers, photo log, tension crack maps.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Highwall inspection log; ground control plan.
- **Frequency:** Pre-shift visual; instrumented monitoring continuous; engineering review weekly.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety (evacuation), Engineering (mine plan changes).
- **Edge cases:** Slope failure with equipment in pit; tension crack discovered behind crest.

### 12.2 Pit Slope Design Compliance
- **What:** Verifying actual slope angles match designed angles.
- **Who:** Engineering, survey.
- **Data fields:** Design vs. as-built bench/inter-ramp/overall slope angles.
- **Frequency:** Monthly with survey.
- **Hand-offs:** Geotech.

### 12.3 Spoil Stability Monitoring
- **What:** Monitoring of spoil piles, especially side-hill fills and durable rock fills.
- **Who:** Engineering, geotech, dozer foreman.
- **Data fields:** Pile angle, settlement, seep emergence.
- **Frequency:** Weekly.

### 12.4 Refuse Impoundment Monitoring (Slurry Dam)
- **What:** Instrumented monitoring of slurry impoundments per MSHA-approved plan (often piezometers, inclinometers, weirs).
- **Who:** Engineer of record (PE), embankment tech.
- **Data fields:** Phreatic surface, freeboard, settlement, decant flow, water quality.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** MSHA-approved impoundment plan; PE-certified annual inspection; MSHA Form 7000-26 (impoundment inspection); 5-yr engineering review.
- **Frequency:** Weekly visual; piezometer monthly; PE quarterly; annual certified; 5-year engineering recertification.
- **Hand-offs:** MSHA Impoundment Branch, State dam safety, Environmental.
- **Edge cases:** Freeboard violations from storm events; piping/seepage; sinkhole into underground works.

### 12.5 Coarse Refuse Pile / Dump Monitoring
- **What:** Inspections of valley fills and coarse refuse fills under MSHA Part 77 / 30 CFR 77.215.
- **Who:** Geotech, PE, foreman.
- **Frequency:** Weekly; annual certified.

### 12.6 Pillar Design Verification (Underground)
- **What:** Monitoring pillar performance vs. design (ARMPS-style analysis, observed stress).
- **Who:** Ground control engineer.
- **Data fields:** Pillar dimensions, depth of cover, observed condition.
- **Frequency:** Continuous design check.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering, Roof control plan.

### 12.7 Subsidence Monitoring (Above Underground Workings)
- **What:** Monitoring of subsidence above longwall panels and retreat areas.
- **Who:** Subsidence engineer, surveyor.
- **Data fields:** Monument elevation change, structure damage claims, water well changes.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Subsidence control plan (SMCRA), pre-mining structure surveys.
- **Frequency:** Per panel cycle; post-mining longitudinal monitoring.
- **State-specific:** WV/VA water replacement obligations; KY similar.

---

## 13. Hydrology / Mine Water Management

### 13.1 Mine Dewatering (Surface)
- **What:** Removing pit water via pumps to sediment ponds.
- **Who:** Pump tech, foreman.
- **Data fields:** Pump runtime, gpm pumped, discharge point, water level in pit.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** NPDES outfall registration; pump install records.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; daily readings.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental (NPDES sampling at outfall).
- **Edge cases:** Pump failure flooding pit; discharge exceeding permit limit.

### 13.2 Underground Dewatering
- **What:** Pumping mine water from low points to surface via stage pumps or borehole pumps.
- **Who:** Pump tech, electrician.
- **Data fields:** Pump runtime, gpm, head, electrical consumption.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental (surface discharge).
- **Edge cases:** Storm inflow exceeding pump capacity; old workings inundation risk (Quecreek-style).

### 13.3 Diversion Ditches & BMPs
- **What:** Surface diversion to keep clean water out of disturbed area.
- **Who:** Reclamation/environmental.
- **Frequency:** Inspections weekly.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental.

### 13.4 Sediment Pond Operation
- **What:** Detention ponds settle disturbed-area runoff before NPDES discharge.
- **Who:** Pond inspector, environmental.
- **Data fields:** Pond freeboard, sediment volume, sample results.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Pond design, NPDES.
- **Frequency:** Weekly + after storms.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental for sampling.

### 13.5 Pre-Mining Hydrologic Monitoring
- **What:** Baseline groundwater/surface water monitoring before mining begins (per PHC/CHIA).
- **Frequency:** Quarterly minimum, often monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental.

---

## 14. Mine Ventilation (Production Side)

### 14.1 Main Fan Operation
- **What:** Surface main fan(s) provide ventilation pressure for the mine.
- **Who:** Outby maintenance / fan attendant.
- **Data fields:** Fan rpm, static pressure (water gauge), motor amps, vibration, runtime.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Daily fan chart (MSHA-required), monthly fan inspection.
- **Frequency:** Continuous monitoring; daily chart review; monthly mechanical inspection.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance, MSHA.
- **Edge cases:** Fan trip = mine evacuation under most plans; storm-induced power loss.

### 14.2 Air Quantity Surveys
- **What:** Vane anemometer surveys of air quantity at each split, last open crosscut, intake, return, bleeders.
- **Who:** Ventilation tech, mine foreman.
- **Data fields:** Location, area (sq ft), velocity (fpm), quantity (cfm), date, examiner.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Ventilation map updated quarterly (typical); air quantity log.
- **Frequency:** Each shift at face (on-shift); weekly comprehensive; ventilation map quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety, Engineering.

### 14.3 Methane Monitoring
- **What:** Spot checks with handheld detectors at face, returns, bleeders, plus continuous monitors on equipment and at strategic points.
- **Who:** CM operator, fire boss, foreman, ventilation tech.
- **Data fields:** Location, time, % methane, action taken if >1.0%.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Methane log; AMS (atmospheric monitoring system) alarms.
- **Frequency:** Continuous (machine sensors); per cut (operator); pre-shift and on-shift.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety, MSHA (if reportable spike).
- **Edge cases:** Sensor calibration drift; methane spike requiring evacuation.

### 14.4 Stopping / Overcast / Regulator Construction & Maintenance
- **What:** Ventilation control structures separating intake from return.
- **Who:** Outby crew, mason crew.
- **Data fields:** Stopping location, condition, leakage estimate, build date.
- **Frequency:** Construction event-driven; inspection weekly.

### 14.5 Belt Air Course Management
- **What:** Compliance with belt air use rules (where applicable) and CO/AMS monitoring.
- **Who:** Beltman, ventilation tech.
- **Data fields:** CO ppm readings, alarm logs.
- **Frequency:** Continuous (AMS), weekly examination.

### 14.6 Gob Degasification (GVB Wells)
- **What:** Vertical wells into gob to remove methane to surface.
- **Who:** Gas operations group (often separate or contracted).
- **Data fields:** Well status, gas production (Mcf/day), CH4 %, water make.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** State oil & gas permits (WV DEP O&G, VA DGMR, KY DOGC), MSHA approval of plan, mineral owner agreements.
- **Frequency:** Continuous well monitoring.
- **Hand-offs:** Mineral owners, environmental (flare/sales).
- **Edge cases:** Gob well casing collapse from subsidence; water make exceeding lift capacity.

---

## 15. Roof / Ground Control

### 15.1 Roof Bolting
- **What:** Installation of roof bolts per approved plan (resin, mechanical, combination).
- **Who:** Roof bolter operator.
- **Data fields:** Hole length, bolt type, bolt length, anchorage, torque (if mech), resin volume/cure, mesh used, pattern, location (entry/crosscut).
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Approved roof control plan; bolt installation records (some jurisdictions); pull-test records.
- **Frequency:** Continuous with advance; pull tests at intervals (e.g., per supplier QC).
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering, Maintenance (bolter PMs), Supply (bolts/resin inventory).
- **State-specific:** WV/VA/KY all require state-approved roof control plan in addition to MSHA; periodic plan review.
- **Edge cases:** Wrong bolt length; resin cure failure in cold weather; "blind" bolting in bad top.

### 15.2 Secondary Support (Cribs, Posts, Cans, Cable Bolts)
- **What:** Additional support added where roof conditions are deteriorating or for high-stress areas (e.g., longwall tailgate).
- **Who:** Section crew, dedicated support crew.
- **Data fields:** Location, support type, count, install date.
- **Frequency:** As needed.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering, Ground control specialist.

### 15.3 Roof / Rib Mapping & Inspection
- **What:** Documentation of roof conditions, rib rolls, anomalies.
- **Who:** Foreman, ground control engineer.
- **Data fields:** Geo-tagged photos, condition codes, action taken.
- **Frequency:** Pre-shift / on-shift / weekly.

### 15.4 Mesh / Screening
- **What:** Installing welded wire mesh or screen between bolts to retain loose material.
- **Who:** Bolter operator.
- **Frequency:** Per cycle in plan-required areas.

### 15.5 Roof Fall Reporting (MSHA)
- **What:** Reporting all roof falls per Part 50 (immediate reporting for entrapment/injury; recordable for unplanned roof fall of certain size).
- **Who:** Mine foreman, safety.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** MSHA 7000-1 if injury; ground control plan revision.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety, Engineering.

---

## 16. Belt Conveyors & Material Handling

### 16.1 Belt Operation & Monitoring
- **What:** Operation of belt conveyor system from face to plant feed / loadout.
- **Who:** Beltman, plant operator, motor control center attendant.
- **Data fields:** Belt amps, tonnage scale (tph), slip detection, sequence start/stop logs, runtime hours.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Belt installation records, splice records, fire suppression certification.
- **Frequency:** Continuous monitoring.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance, Safety (fire systems).
- **Edge cases:** Belt fire, belt slip, belt slip clutch trip, hot bearings.

### 16.2 Belt Examination (Weekly)
- **What:** Comprehensive belt examination per 30 CFR 75.1731 / Part 77.
- **Who:** Certified examiner.
- **Data fields:** Splice condition, structure condition, accumulations, fire suppression.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Belt examination book.
- **Frequency:** Weekly.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance.

### 16.3 Belt Cleanup / Accumulation Control
- **What:** Removing coal accumulations under belts to prevent friction fires.
- **Who:** Cleanup crew, beltman.
- **Frequency:** Per shift; rock dust applied weekly along intake.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety, Rock dust crew.

### 16.4 Belt Splicing
- **What:** Vulcanized or mechanical splices.
- **Who:** Splicing contractor / crew.
- **Data fields:** Splice number, date, length, technician, supplier.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven; tracked for life of belt.

### 16.5 Crusher / Feeder Breaker Operation
- **What:** Operating in-line crushers (rotary breaker, feeder-breaker, sizers).
- **Who:** Section crew, plant operator.
- **Data fields:** tph, amps, pick wear.

### 16.6 Stacker / Reclaimer (Where Used)
- **What:** Pile management with mechanized stacker and reclaimer.
- **Frequency:** Continuous when running.

---

## 17. Pumps & Dewatering (Operational Detail)

### 17.1 Pump Inventory & Installation
- **Data fields:** Pump tag, type, hp, head/flow rating, install date, location, suction/discharge sizing.
- **Frequency:** Asset-based.

### 17.2 Pump PM & Repair
- **Who:** Pump tech / electrician.
- **Frequency:** Hours-based PM cycles.

### 17.3 Pump Runtime / Energy Tracking
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (power cost), Environmental (water balance).

### 17.4 Stage Pump Setups (Underground)
- **What:** Series pumps lifting water in stages from sump to surface.
- **Frequency:** Reconfigured as workings change.

---

## 18. Fuel & Lube Field Delivery

### 18.1 Field Fueling Operations
- **What:** Fuel truck deliveries to equipment in pit / on surface.
- **Who:** Fuel/lube truck driver.
- **Data fields:** Equipment unit #, gallons dispensed, hour meter, time.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Fuel slip; SPCC plan compliance; Form R / Tier II if thresholds exceeded.
- **Frequency:** Per shift.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance (fuel burn rate), Environmental (SPCC), Finance.
- **Edge cases:** Cross-contamination of fuels; spillage requiring SPCC response.

### 18.2 Lube Service
- **What:** Greasing, filter changes in field per OEM intervals.
- **Who:** Lube tech.
- **Data fields:** Lube points serviced, oil sample results, filter changes.
- **Frequency:** Per OEM interval (hours/days).
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance reliability (oil analysis program).

### 18.3 Bulk Storage Compliance
- **What:** Above-ground/under-ground bulk fuel tanks.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** SPCC, EPA UST/AST if applicable, state tank registration.
- **Frequency:** SPCC review every 5 yrs; weekly inspection.

---

## 19. Examinations (Production-Relevant)

### 19.1 Pre-Shift Examination (Underground)
- **What:** Examiner travels each work area within 3 hours before each shift, checking for hazards, methane, ventilation, roof.
- **Who:** Certified preshift examiner (federal + state cert).
- **Data fields:** Areas examined, methane readings, air quantity, hazards noted, corrective actions, examiner signature, time-in/time-out.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Pre-shift exam book; 30 CFR 75.360 (federal); state-required version.
- **Frequency:** Before each shift.
- **State-specific:**
  - WV: state preshift requirement parallel to federal; certified fire boss / mine foreman.
  - VA: § 45.2-903 framework; certified person.
  - KY: KY-certified mine foreman; KY exam book.
- **Edge cases:** Hazard noted but corrective action not taken before shift sent in = federal violation.

### 19.2 On-Shift Examination
- **What:** Examination during the shift for hazards, methane, ventilation, dust.
- **Who:** Section foreman.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** On-shift exam book; 30 CFR 75.362 (UG) / 30 CFR 77 (surface).
- **Frequency:** Each shift.

### 19.3 Weekly Examination (Underground)
- **What:** Examination of return air courses, bleeders, idle areas, seals.
- **Who:** Certified examiner.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Weekly exam book; 30 CFR 75.364.
- **Frequency:** Weekly.

### 19.4 Surface On-Shift Examination
- **What:** Per VA Title 45.2 Ch. 9 and federal 30 CFR 77, certified person performs on-shift exam of surface working areas each production shift.
- **Who:** Certified surface foreman.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Surface exam book.
- **Frequency:** Each production shift.
- **State-specific:** VA explicitly codified work-area exam regimen for surface mines; WV and KY require certified surface foreman with parallel exam duties.

### 19.5 Methane Exam at Surface Coal Handling Facilities
- **What:** Per VA Title 45.2 (verified), at least one methane exam per production shift at any surface installation where coal is handled or stored, plus test before any welding/cutting/open flame.
- **Frequency:** Per shift + hot work events.

### 19.6 Air Quality Exam at Surface/UG Intersect
- **What:** Per VA Title 45.2 (verified), when a surface op intersects an underground mine, auger hole, or other underground working, certified person performs air-quality exam.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.

### 19.7 Examination of Surface Areas of Underground Coal Mines
- **What:** Per VA § 45.2-903 (verified), made in accordance with weekly and daily/on-shift exam requirements for surface coal mines.
- **Frequency:** Weekly + on-shift.

### 19.8 Mine Examiner Quarterly Review of Citations
- **What:** Per 2012 MSHA rule, operator reviews with examiners on quarterly basis all citations/orders issued in areas where examinations are required.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Training/review documentation.

---

## 20. Beltline Cleanup & Rock Dusting (Production Tempo)

### 20.1 Rock Dust Application
- **What:** Application of incombustible rock dust on roof, ribs, and floor of intake and return airways to meet 80% incombustible (federal).
- **Who:** Rock duster (dedicated crew or section), foreman.
- **Data fields:** Location dusted, tons/lbs applied, dust sample location, dust survey results (% incombustible).
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Rock dust application log; MSHA dust band samples; 30 CFR 75.402–75.403.
- **Frequency:** As needed to maintain compliance; sampling MSHA-driven; weekly band sampling internal common.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety, MSHA.
- **Edge cases:** Belt advance outpacing rock dust crew = citation risk.

### 20.2 Beltline / Track Cleanup
- **What:** Coal/spillage removal from beltline, transfer points, track.
- **Who:** Cleanup crew.
- **Frequency:** Each shift (typical).

### 20.3 Sample Collection for Dust Analysis
- **What:** Band samples sent to lab for % incombustible.
- **Who:** Examiner.
- **Frequency:** Monthly internal; MSHA samples as scheduled.

---

## 21. Mine Rescue Station Readiness (Operational)

### 21.1 Mine Rescue Team Roster & Training
- **What:** Maintaining a trained mine rescue team (in-house or contracted).
- **Who:** Safety mgr, mine rescue captain.
- **Data fields:** Team members, training hours, qualifications, contest scores.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Training records per 30 CFR 49; state-specific MRT records.
- **Frequency:** Monthly drills; annual benchwork.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety, MSHA District.

### 21.2 Apparatus & Equipment Readiness
- **What:** BG4 / SCSR / W65 apparatus, gas detectors, communication gear maintained.
- **Frequency:** Per OEM PM intervals; checked monthly.

### 21.3 Mine Rescue Plan & Maps
- **What:** Up-to-date mine maps, escape plans, rescue chamber locations available.
- **Frequency:** Updated quarterly.

---

## 22. Diesel Equipment Particulate Management (Underground)

### 22.1 Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) Maintenance
- **What:** PM and cleaning of DPFs on UG diesel equipment per MSHA Part 75.
- **Who:** Diesel mechanic.
- **Data fields:** Filter cleaning date, back-pressure, regeneration cycles.
- **Frequency:** Per OEM/MSHA interval.

### 22.2 Approved Diesel Equipment List
- **What:** Maintaining MSHA approval (Part 7 / Part 36) status per unit.
- **Frequency:** Per change/refurb.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance/Engineering.

### 22.3 Diesel Particulate Matter (DPM) Sampling
- **What:** Personal sampling for DPM exposure.
- **Frequency:** As required by 30 CFR 72.520.

### 22.4 Ventilation Per Diesel Unit
- **What:** Confirming nameplate ventilation rate per diesel unit on the section.
- **Frequency:** Continuous (cannot exceed approved units' total ventilation needs).

---

## 23. Equipment-Specific Production Tracking

### 23.1 Continuous Miner (CM) Production
- **Data fields:** Cuts per shift, ft per cut, tons per cut, place changes, dust pump install, methane spot readings, downtime, run time, cut sequence diagram.

### 23.2 Roof Bolter Production
- **Data fields:** Bolts installed, holes drilled, bit life, resin used, mesh installed.

### 23.3 Shuttle Car / Battery Hauler Production
- **Data fields:** Trips per shift, tons per trip, tram time, cable damage events (shuttle).

### 23.4 Longwall Shearer Production
- **Data fields:** Passes per shift, tons per pass, downtime (face, headgate, tailgate, stage loader).

### 23.5 Shovel / Excavator Production (Surface)
- **Data fields:** Bucket loads per shift, BCY/hr, fill factor, swing angle, cycle time, hang time waiting for trucks.

### 23.6 Haul Truck Production
- **Data fields:** Loads per shift, tons per load, cycle time, haul distance, queue time, dump time, fuel burn.

### 23.7 Dozer Production
- **Data fields:** Hours, BCY pushed (push monitoring), idle %, undercarriage hours.

### 23.8 Grader / Water Truck Production
- **Data fields:** Hours, miles of road maintained, water applied (gal).

### 23.9 Drill Production
- **Data fields:** Meters/feet drilled per shift, penetration rate, bit life, fuel burn.

### 23.10 Fleet Telematics Integration
- **What:** OEM telematics (Cat MineStar / Komatsu Modular / Hexagon / Wenco) producing event-level data feeding production reporting.
- **Hand-offs:** IT/Data engineering.

---

## 24. Mine Communication & Tracking (Production-Enabling)

### 24.1 Underground Communication System
- **What:** Leaky feeder / mesh radio / PED system for voice and data.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Part 75 Subpart R requirements for two-way communication.
- **Frequency:** Daily check; weekly examination.

### 24.2 Underground Tracking (Personnel & Equipment)
- **What:** Required electronic tracking under MINER Act Part 75.1505.
- **Data fields:** Personnel location, equipment location, last reading time.

### 24.3 Refuge Chambers / Caches
- **What:** Pre-positioned breathable air refuges; cache locations.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** Emergency Response Plan (ERP).
- **Frequency:** Weekly check; monthly comprehensive.

---

## 25. Coal Quality (Operations Interface with Lab)

### 25.1 In-Stream Quality Monitoring
- **What:** On-belt analyzers (PGNAA, e.g., Gamma-Metrics / Scantech) measuring ash/moisture/BTU.
- **Data fields:** Real-time tag stream.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab (verify), Sales (blending decisions).

### 25.2 Pit / Section Quality Sampling
- **What:** Channel samples or grab samples at face for quality verification.
- **Who:** Mine foreman, geologist.
- **Frequency:** Per cut or per shift.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab, Geology (model reconciliation).

### 25.3 Blending Decisions at the Pit
- **What:** Choosing which pit/section/seam to feed to which stockpile or plant feed based on customer spec needs.
- **Who:** Mine engineer, quality engineer.
- **Frequency:** Daily/shift.
- **Hand-offs:** Sales (commitments), Loadout.

---

## 26. Inspections, NOVs, and Production Impacts

### 26.1 MSHA Inspection Hosting
- **What:** Federal regular inspections (E01 surface 2/yr; E01 UG 4/yr) plus spot inspections.
- **Who:** Safety, mine GM.
- **Data fields:** Inspection dates, inspector, citations, abatement dates, contests.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** MSHA Form 7000-3; citations/orders.
- **Frequency:** Per inspection event.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety/Legal/Operations (for abatement).

### 26.2 State Inspection Hosting
- **State-specific:** WV OMHST + DEP; VA DMME (Energy); KY EEC Mine Safety + DMRE.
- **Frequency:** Varies; commonly monthly or quarterly.

### 26.3 NOV / Citation Abatement
- **Data fields:** Citation #, condition cited, abatement plan, completion date, terminator inspector.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering (if plan change required).
- **Edge cases:** D-order shutting down section; pattern of violations (POV).

### 26.4 Imminent Danger / 107(a) Withdrawal
- **What:** Immediate stoppage of section/mine until hazard abated.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety, Operations.

---

## 27. Lease & Surface Owner Coordination

### 27.1 Surface Use Agreements / Damage Settlements
- **What:** Coordination with surface owners affected by mining (vibration, dust, road use).
- **Who:** Land department, community relations.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Legal, Finance.

### 27.2 Water Replacement (Subsidence / Impact)
- **What:** Replacement of domestic water supplies impacted by underground mining or surface activities.
- **Documents/forms/permits:** State water replacement statute (WV statutory; KY/VA similar).
- **Frequency:** Event-driven; ongoing if alternate supply installed.

### 27.3 Haul Road / Public Road Coordination
- **What:** Maintenance and permitting of coal haul roads (often state-permitted under bonded coal haul system in KY).
- **State-specific:**
  - KY: Coal haul road system with extended weight limits requires permit + bond + road use payments.
  - WV: Coal Resource Transportation System (CRTS) parallel concept.
  - VA: similar coal hauler programs.

---

## 28. Production Data Hand-Offs Master Map

The product (SCC-OS) must move the following data between functions:

- **Production → Lab:** raw and clean samples per shift; chain-of-custody.
- **Production → Engineering:** survey volumes, advance/yield, plan-vs-actual.
- **Production → Safety:** delay codes for examination/inspection time, incidents, refuge/comm checks.
- **Production → Environmental:** dewatering volumes, sediment pond status, NPDES outfall flags, refuse placement.
- **Production → Maintenance:** delay codes mech/elec, equipment hours, oil sample triggers, PM due lists.
- **Production → Finance:** tons mined/shipped, royalty allocation, severance tax basis, inventory adjustments, scale tickets, fuel slips.
- **Production → Sales:** available tons by grade, projected shipments, quality forecasts.
- **Production → HR:** hours worked by employee (Part 50), classifications, certifications expiring.
- **Production → ATF/State Fire Marshal:** explosives transactions, theft/loss events.
- **Production → MSHA:** Part 50 quarterly tons/hours, immediate-notification events.
- **Production → State DEP/Energy/DMRE:** monthly production, NPDES discharge monitoring, blasting reports, severance returns.

---

## 29. Edge Cases & Pain Points (Cross-Cutting)

- **Reconciliation triangle:** survey BCY vs. truck count vs. scale tons rarely agree; SCC-OS must allow variance with audit trail.
- **Permit boundary creep:** GPS-driven prevention vs. operator override.
- **Lease attribution at boundary:** tons mined within ft of lease line need fractional allocation.
- **Multi-seam operations:** simultaneous mining of stacked seams in MTR requires careful tons-by-seam attribution for royalty/tax.
- **Contract miner production:** contractors often have their own systems and MSHA IDs — data must roll up to operator.
- **Wet vs. dry tons:** moisture basis errors propagate to royalty, sales, and severance.
- **Weighted-average quality vs. blend math:** mistakes in tonnage weighting cause customer claims.
- **Lab turnaround vs. shipment commitments:** ship-before-quality-known scenarios.
- **Shift change loss:** unaccounted production time at shift handover.
- **"Phantom" production:** loadout ahead of plant accounting; inventory built without true production.
- **Idle mine days:** must still record exam books, fan charts, pump readings, even with zero tons.
- **Mine ID vs. Permit ID vs. Cost Center ID:** rarely 1:1; SCC-OS must map cleanly.
- **Subcontractor blasters:** records and ATF chain stays with the operator.
- **Weather-driven slack capacity:** spring rains routinely take 5–15% of WV/VA/KY surface production days; planning must absorb.
- **AMS / atmospheric monitor data tsunami:** millions of data points/day requiring summarization.
- **Roof bolter dust pumps:** install and recover schedule often misses, causing Part 90 issues.
- **Old workings inundation:** verifying that mining is not approaching unmapped abandoned mine pools (Quecreek lesson).
- **Self-heating coal at stockpile:** age-out rules must be enforced.
- **Coal dust explosion hazard tracking:** rock dust band sample lag.
- **Cross-state permitting differences:** SCC operating in 5 states needs state-aware workflows everywhere.

---

## 30. Annual / Quarterly / Periodic Production Cycle Events

- **Annual:** Mine map certification (UG), refuse impoundment certified inspection, fan static pressure validation, equipment overhaul cycle, reserves restatement, budget, MSHA training refresh.
- **Quarterly:** MSHA 7000-2, KY Reclamation Guaranty Fund report, examiner citation review, ventilation map update, geological model refresh.
- **Monthly:** Survey volumetric, production close, inventory reconciliation, royalty allocation, severance reporting (state varies), pre-shift exam book audit, fan inspection.
- **Weekly:** Production planning, beltline cleanup, weekly UG exam, refuse pile inspection, impoundment piezometer (most plans), bleeder evaluation, plant downtime Pareto.
- **Daily:** Shift production reports, fuel/lube, scale ticket reconciliation, foreman's report.
- **Per Shift:** Pre-shift exam, on-shift exam, methane spots, dust pumps, delay coding, sample collection.
- **Event-driven:** Roof fall, citation, blast, equipment major failure, MSHA reportable, NPDES exceedance, theft/loss of explosives, mine fire, mine rescue activation.

---

Notes on verified vs. inferred citations:
- VA Title 45.2 § 45.2-903 framework, on-shift exam per production shift, methane exam at coal-handling installations, and air-quality exam at surface/UG intersect were verified via search of VA Code Title 45.2.
- KY Reclamation Guaranty Fund quarterly tonnage reporting with 6-year retention was verified via search of 405 KAR.
- WV 38 CSR 2 framework for SMCRA permitting and production tonnage tracking was verified.
- Federal 30 CFR 75.360, 75.362, 75.364 pre-shift/on-shift/weekly exam framework with quarterly examiner-citation review was verified via Federal Register.
- Where specific subsection numbers were not verified by search, regulations are described functionally without fabricating citations.

# Domain 2: Environmental Compliance & Reclamation

# Environmental Compliance & Reclamation

Scope: every recurring environmental, water, air, waste, reclamation, SMCRA, consent-decree, citizen-participation, and inspection workflow run by Southern Coal Corporation and its 26-plus affiliated entities across WV, VA, KY (plus AL/TN operations). State-specific regulators referenced throughout:

- **WV** — WVDEP Division of Mining and Reclamation (DMR) for SMCRA, Division of Water and Waste Management (DWWM) for NPDES/water/waste, Division of Air Quality (DAQ) for air. Rules: Title 47 CSR (water), Title 38 CSR (mining), Title 45 CSR (air).
- **VA** — VA DEQ for water/air/waste; Virginia Energy (formerly DMME) Division of Mined Land Repurposing (DMLR/MLR) at Big Stone Gap for SMCRA. Rules: 9 VAC 25 (water), 9 VAC 5 (air), 9 VAC 20 (waste), 4 VAC 25-130 (coal SMCRA permanent program), Title 45.2 Code of Virginia.
- **KY** — KY Energy and Environment Cabinet (EEC); Department for Environmental Protection (DEP) Division of Water (DOW, KPDES), Division for Air Quality, Division of Waste Management; Department for Natural Resources (DNR) Division of Mine Reclamation and Enforcement (DMRE) and Division of Mine Permits (DMP). Rules: 401 KAR (environmental), 405 KAR (mining).
- **Federal overlay** — EPA Region 3 (WV/VA), Region 4 (KY/TN/AL), OSMRE Charleston/Lexington/Knoxville field offices, USACE Huntington/Norfolk/Louisville/Nashville Districts.
- **Consent Decree** — *United States, et al. v. A&G Coal Corp., et al.*, Case No. 7:16-cv-00462-GEC (W.D. Va.), entered against Southern Coal, A&G Coal, Premium Coal, Justice-affiliated entities. Co-plaintiffs: EPA, WV, VA, KY, TN, AL. Federal stipulated penalties + per-state stipulated penalties. Independent monitor and quarterly reporting regime.

---

## 1. NPDES / KPDES Water Permitting

### 1.1 New Individual NPDES/KPDES Permit Application

1. **What it is**: Application for a new individual NPDES/KPDES outfall permit covering sediment ponds, treatment system discharges, mine drainage, prep plant discharges, or stormwater associated with mining activity.
2. **Performs**: Environmental Permit Engineer / consulting firm; reviewed by Environmental Manager; signed by Responsible Corporate Officer (RCO) per 40 CFR 122.22.
3. **Data captured**: Outfall lat/long, receiving stream + segment, watershed code, design flow, expected flow regime, source(s) (active mining, post-mining, prep plant, raw water, stormwater), treatment description, antidegradation tier review, mixing zone justification, anticipated effluent quality (pH, TSS, Fe, Mn, Al, Se, sulfate, conductivity), upstream water quality, 303(d) listing status, TMDL allocation if applicable.
4. **Documents/forms**:
   - WV: Application Form WW-NPDES (Form 1, Form 2C, Form 2F as applicable) submitted via WV ePermitting (ePermit) portal; antidegradation review per 47 CSR 2 §4.1; CN-22 series for coal mining NPDES (paired with Article 3 SMCRA application).
   - VA: VA DEQ VPDES application via CEDS (Comprehensive Environmental Data System) — Forms 1, 2C, 2D, 2F; Mining NPDES Permit Application coordinated with DMLR.
   - KY: KPDES application via KY DEP eForms; coal mining DOW-NPDES form; cross-references SMCRA application to DMP.
5. **Frequency**: Per new outfall / new permit area / new disturbance area.
6. **Hand-offs**: Engineering (pond designs, flow projections) → Permitting → Public Notice coordinator → Legal (antidegradation challenges) → Operations (NOI / start-of-discharge).
7. **State-specific**:
   - **WV**: Public notice runs in newspaper of general circulation in county of discharge, minimum 30 days; antidegradation tier 1/2/2.5/3 (Tier 2.5 = naturally reproducing trout waters); WVDEP DWWM Permitting Handbook governs schedule.
   - **VA**: 30-day public notice; "Tier III exceptional waters" review; coordination required between DEQ (water) and DMLR (SMCRA) on coordinated mining permits.
   - **KY**: DOW issues KPDES; DMP issues SMCRA; both publish public notice. KPDES uses state forms, not federal EPA forms.
8. **Edge cases**: 303(d)-listed receiving stream forcing TMDL-based limits (especially selenium, conductivity, sulfate, TDS); antidegradation Tier 2 requiring "social and economic justification" demo; outfall added late by Operations without permit modification; permit shielded by Sackett-era WOTUS rescoping disputes.

### 1.2 NPDES/KPDES Permit Modification (Minor and Major)

1. **What it is**: Amendment to existing permit (add outfall, change limits, change monitoring frequency, change facility location, change ownership/operator).
2. **Performs**: Permit Engineer / Environmental Manager; legal review for major mods.
3. **Data captured**: Reason for modification, affected outfalls, revised limits/parameters, public notice trigger Y/N, antidegradation re-review trigger.
4. **Documents/forms**: Modification request letter + Form 2C revisions; in WV CN-25/CN-26 series and Article 3 modification cross-reference; VA DEQ Modification Form; KY DOW modification form.
5. **Frequency**: Several per quarter across the company portfolio.
6. **Hand-offs**: Operations request → Engineering → Permit Engineer → Public Notice (if major) → State agency.
7. **State-specific**: WV distinguishes minor mod (no public notice) vs major mod (full public notice + antideg); VA mirrors federal 40 CFR 122.62/.63; KY same.
8. **Edge cases**: Operator change-of-ownership requiring concurrent SMCRA transfer; relocating outfall without acknowledging WOTUS jurisdictional change; trying to add a selenium-impacted outfall as "minor."

### 1.3 NPDES/KPDES Permit Renewal

1. **What it is**: Permit reissuance every 5 years.
2. **Performs**: Permit Engineer 180+ days before expiration.
3. **Data captured**: Application date, current permit number, historical DMR summary (last 3-5 years), exceedance history, treatment changes, current outfall inventory, current effluent quality.
4. **Documents/forms**: Form 2C with renewal supplement; WV CN-29 renewal cover; permit shield assertion list.
5. **Frequency**: 5-year cycle per permit. Many SCC permits run staggered.
6. **Hand-offs**: Permitting → Compliance (DMR pull) → Operations → State.
7. **State-specific**: WV "administratively continued" status if WVDEP misses reissuance deadline; VA same; KY same.
8. **Edge cases**: Letting permit lapse without timely renewal app (becomes unauthorized discharge); new water quality criteria adopted between cycles forcing tightened limits at renewal (selenium chronic 8.5 µg/L lentic / 3.1 µg/L lotic egg-ovary criterion etc.).

### 1.4 Public Notice and Antidegradation Review

1. **What it is**: Statutory public participation step including newspaper notice, agency comment period, public hearing if requested.
2. **Performs**: Permit Engineer + Communications + State agency.
3. **Data captured**: Notice date, newspaper, page, comment deadline, comments received, hearing requested Y/N, hearing date, hearing transcript, response-to-comments document.
4. **Documents/forms**: Public Notice draft; Affidavit of Publication; Comment Log; Response to Comments; Antidegradation Review Memo (Tier 1/2/2.5/3).
5. **Frequency**: Each new permit, major mod, renewal.
6. **Hand-offs**: Permitting → Communications → Legal → State.
7. **State-specific**: WV 47 CSR 2 antideg tier system; VA 9 VAC 25-260-30 antideg; KY 401 KAR 10:030 antideg.
8. **Edge cases**: Citizen groups (Appalachian Voices, OVEC, SELC, WV Highlands Conservancy, SACE) submitting voluminous technical comments triggering reissuance delays; public hearing requested late.

---

## 2. Outfall Monitoring & Sampling

### 2.1 Routine Effluent Sampling per Permit

1. **What it is**: Collection of grab or composite samples at each permitted outfall per the parameter/frequency matrix in the permit.
2. **Performs**: Site Environmental Tech / contract sampling firm (e.g., REIC, MicroBac, Pace, Eurofins, Appalachian Analytical, WV Tri-State).
3. **Data captured**: Sample date/time, collector ID, sample location (outfall ID), sample type (grab/composite), preservation, holding time start, field pH, field temp, field conductivity, field DO, flow estimate, chain-of-custody (COC) #, lab ID, parameter results, MDL/RL, qualifiers, field duplicate flag.
4. **Documents/forms**: Field sampling sheet; Chain-of-Custody form; Lab report (PDF + EDD CSV/EQuIS); internal sampling log.
5. **Frequency**: Per permit — typically monthly (most parameters), quarterly (Se, sulfate, hardness), semi-annual (WET), some weekly (TSS at high-risk outfalls), continuous for pH at treatment plants.
6. **Hand-offs**: Field Tech → Lab → Compliance Analyst → DMR Prep.
7. **State-specific**: WV requires specific QA/QC under 47 CSR 10 and permit Part C; VA references 9 VAC 25-31; KY references 401 KAR 5:065. All require EPA-approved methods (40 CFR 136).
8. **Edge cases**: Holding time violations (Fe/Mn 6 months but pH 15 min; TSS 7 days); composite sampler malfunction during storm event; lab QC failure forcing reanalysis past holding time; field pH meter not calibrated; sampler took grab during dry weather at stormwater-only outfall.

### 2.2 Parameter Matrix Tracking

1. **What it is**: Master list of every parameter monitored at every outfall by frequency, limit (monthly avg / daily max / instantaneous max), and method.
2. **Performs**: Compliance Analyst; auto-populated from permit ingestion.
3. **Data captured**: Permit #, outfall #, parameter (CAS#/STORET code), units, monthly avg, daily max, instantaneous max, sample type, frequency, EPA method, MDL required, units conversion factor.
4. **Documents/forms**: Internal Parameter Matrix (spreadsheet today, system-of-record going forward); WV permit Part C; VA permit Part I.A; KY permit Section I.
5. **Frequency**: Reviewed at every renewal and modification.
6. **Hand-offs**: Permit ingestion → Compliance → Lab scheduling → DMR config.
7. **State-specific**: Typical coal mining parameter set — pH, TSS, Fe (total), Mn (total), Al (total recoverable on TMDL waters), Se (total recoverable), sulfate, TDS, conductivity, hardness, alkalinity, settleable solids, oil & grease, flow. Treatment plant adds: residual Cl2, temp, DO. Trout water permits add: temp, turbidity. WV "narrative" permits may add: WVSCI/GLIMPSS biomonitoring.
8. **Edge cases**: Two outfall numbers same lat/long; parameter required on permit but lab not accredited for it; method change mid-permit; "monitor only" vs enforceable limit confusion.

### 2.3 Flow Measurement

1. **What it is**: Continuous or instantaneous flow at each outfall; required to compute mass-based limits and loadings.
2. **Performs**: Site Environmental Tech.
3. **Data captured**: Flow method (V-notch weir, Parshall flume, area-velocity, bucket-stopwatch, estimated), reading, datalogger ID, calibration date.
4. **Documents/forms**: Flow measurement log; weir calibration certificate.
5. **Frequency**: At every sample event; continuous if mass limits.
6. **Hand-offs**: Field → DMR.
7. **State-specific**: All three states accept standard weir/flume; "estimated" flow allowed for low/intermittent outfalls if justified.
8. **Edge cases**: Pond overtopping not captured by primary discharge structure; flow estimated to keep computed loading under limit (enforcement risk); weir blade not level / silted-in.

### 2.4 Holding Time and Preservation Management

1. **What it is**: Discipline around 40 CFR 136 holding times and preservation chemistry per parameter.
2. **Performs**: Field Tech + Lab.
3. **Data captured**: Sample collected timestamp, lab received timestamp, analysis timestamp, preservative used (H2SO4, HNO3, NaOH, none), cooler temp on receipt.
4. **Documents/forms**: COC, lab login report.
5. **Frequency**: Every sample.
6. **Hand-offs**: Field → Lab.
7. **State-specific**: Universal federal rule; WV/VA/KY enforce by reference.
8. **Edge cases**: pH > 15 min, residual Cl2 immediate, BOD 48 hrs, TSS 7 days, metals 6 months (preserved), Se 6 months (preserved), mercury 28 days. Sample tossed when cooler arrives >6 °C.

---

## 3. DMR Submission

### 3.1 DMR Compilation

1. **What it is**: Monthly compilation of all sample results into DMR for each outfall.
2. **Performs**: Compliance Analyst.
3. **Data captured**: Permit #, outfall #, monitoring period, parameter code, sample type, units, qty1/qty2 (avg/max), conc1/conc2/conc3, number of excursions (NOEX), frequency of analysis (FOA), no-data indicator (NODI codes A-Z), permittee comments.
4. **Documents/forms**: NetDMR DMR or state eDMR equivalent; signed by Cromerr-authorized signatory.
5. **Frequency**: Monthly (or per-permit period).
6. **Hand-offs**: Lab EDD → Compliance Analyst (validate vs limits) → Signatory → Submit.
7. **State-specific**:
   - **WV**: Submit via WV ePermitting eDMR module (state-built, ties to ESS); also uploads to ICIS via state.
   - **VA**: Submit via NetDMR (federal). VA DEQ migrated to NetDMR.
   - **KY**: Submit via KY DEP eDMR (state-built) or NetDMR for federally-issued permits; mining quarterly groundwater goes via DMRE on SME-90E form.
8. **Edge cases**: NODI code misuse (using "9" when "C" was correct); late DMR auto-counts as violation; signatory not authorized in CDX; "no discharge" outfall still requires NODI-coded DMR.

### 3.2 DMR Signature and Submission (CROMERR)

1. **What it is**: Cryptographically signed submission via EPA CDX or state portal under 40 CFR 3 (CROMERR).
2. **Performs**: Cromerr-registered Responsible Corporate Officer or duly authorized representative.
3. **Data captured**: Signer name, role, CDX user ID, submission timestamp, hash/checksum, copy-of-record (COR) reference.
4. **Documents/forms**: Subscriber Agreement on file with EPA; CDX confirmation email; COR PDF.
5. **Frequency**: Per DMR submission.
6. **Hand-offs**: Compliance → Signatory → State/EPA.
7. **State-specific**: WV eDMR has its own subscriber agreement; KY eDMR similar; VA via NetDMR uses CDX.
8. **Edge cases**: Signer leaves company without delegating; CDX password lockout on submission day; submission "saved" but never "submitted."

### 3.3 DMR Deadlines

1. **What it is**: Statutory due dates per permit.
2. **Performs**: Compliance.
3. **Data captured**: Period end, due date, submission date, days late.
4. **Documents/forms**: DMR cover sheet.
5. **Frequency**: Most coal mining permits — DMR due by 28th of the month following the monitoring period (per EPA standard); some WV permits require 10th of following month.
6. **Hand-offs**: Compliance → State.
7. **State-specific**: Confirm per-permit; do not assume.
8. **Edge cases**: Late submission auto-flags ICIS violation; weekend/holiday rollover rules vary.

---

## 4. Exceedances, Violations & Notifications

### 4.1 5-Day Exceedance Notification (WV)

1. **What it is**: WV-specific requirement to notify WVDEP within 5 days of becoming aware of any effluent limit exceedance.
2. **Performs**: Compliance Analyst / Environmental Manager.
3. **Data captured**: Outfall, parameter, limit type (avg/max/instant), result, sample date, date of awareness, cause, immediate corrective action, signature.
4. **Documents/forms**: 5-Day Letter on company letterhead to WVDEP DWWM (and DMR District Office for mining); also entered in eDMR with comment.
5. **Frequency**: Per exceedance event.
6. **Hand-offs**: Compliance → Environmental Manager → WVDEP.
7. **State-specific**:
   - **WV**: 5-day written notice obligation in 47 CSR 10 / individual permit Part C; oral 24-hour notice for any "noncompliance that may endanger health or environment" (47 CSR 10 §5.1.f).
   - **VA**: Permit Part II.G requires 24-hour oral + 5-day written for any exceedance "endangering health or environment"; otherwise reported via DMR.
   - **KY**: 401 KAR 5:065 §1(12) — 24-hour oral notice for noncompliance endangering health/environment + 5-day written follow-up; other noncompliance reported with DMR.
8. **Edge cases**: Lab reports late, so "date of awareness" is the lab report date — but enforcement may argue date of sampling; sample re-analyzed and revised result triggers retroactive 5-day clock; multi-day average exceedance vs single-event exceedance.

### 4.2 Single Event Violation (SEV) Tracking

1. **What it is**: Per-event noncompliance treated as discrete violation for enforcement and stipulated penalty purposes.
2. **Performs**: Compliance + Legal.
3. **Data captured**: SEV ID, outfall, parameter, result, limit, magnitude (% over), TR (technical review) flag, RNC (reportable noncompliance) flag, ICIS upload flag, CD-stipulated penalty owed flag.
4. **Documents/forms**: SEV log; CD quarterly report appendix; ICIS-NPDES violation record (state-uploaded).
5. **Frequency**: Per-event.
6. **Hand-offs**: Compliance → Legal → Consent Decree reporting.
7. **State-specific**: All three states feed ICIS; WV uses DMR Pollutant Loading Tool to classify; CD requires per-outfall, per-parameter, per-day classification.
8. **Edge cases**: Multi-parameter same-day exceedance — is it 1 SEV or many? CD definition controls. Resampling within 24 hours showing compliance does not erase the SEV.

### 4.3 Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Abatement

1. **What it is**: Documented investigation of cause + corrective/abatement actions for each exceedance.
2. **Performs**: Environmental Manager + Plant/Mine Foreman + (if CD-required) third-party.
3. **Data captured**: Cause (treatment upset, storm overflow, sampling error, chemistry imbalance, equipment failure, etc.), immediate action, long-term corrective action, target completion date, responsible party, verification of return-to-compliance.
4. **Documents/forms**: RCA Report; Abatement Plan; resample results; closeout memo. CD may require submittal of RCA within 30 days to EPA/states.
5. **Frequency**: Per exceedance / per cluster of exceedances.
6. **Hand-offs**: Operations ↔ Environmental ↔ Engineering ↔ Legal ↔ Independent Monitor (if CD).
7. **State-specific**: WV "single event violation" + Cessation Order risk if not abated; VA "Notice of Violation" + Consent Order; KY DMRE "Notice of Non-Compliance" (NON).
8. **Edge cases**: Same outfall, same parameter, repeated — escalates to Pattern of Violations (POV); abatement plan accepted on paper but not implemented.

### 4.4 Consent Decree Stipulated Penalty Calculation

1. **What it is**: Per-event monetary penalty owed to EPA/states under the CD penalty schedule, escalating with violation duration and recurrence.
2. **Performs**: Compliance + Legal + Finance.
3. **Data captured**: Violation type (effluent exceedance, late report, missed milestone, monitoring failure, RCA failure), days of violation, $/day per CD Appendix, allocation among federal/WV/VA/KY/TN/AL co-plaintiffs.
4. **Documents/forms**: Stipulated Penalty Worksheet; payment letter to DOJ/EPA + states; check or wire confirmation; CD quarterly report inclusion.
5. **Frequency**: Per quarterly compliance report (or per demand letter from EPA/DOJ).
6. **Hand-offs**: Compliance → Legal → Finance/AP → DOJ trust account / state treasuries.
7. **State-specific**: CD allocates split among federal and 5 state plaintiffs per Appendix; each state has independent right to assess.
8. **Edge cases**: Disputed application of penalty schedule (force majeure defense pending); penalty escalator at days 31 / 91 / 181; calculation differs when multiple parameters trip same outfall same day.

---

## 5. Whole Effluent Toxicity (WET) Testing

### 5.1 Routine WET Testing

1. **What it is**: Biological toxicity testing of effluent using sensitive aquatic species (chronic *Ceriodaphnia dubia* and *Pimephales promelas* fathead minnow; acute *Daphnia magna* / fathead).
2. **Performs**: Contract WET-certified lab (e.g., REIC, Pace, GEI, BSA).
3. **Data captured**: TUc, TUa, IC25, LC50, NOEC, dilution series, control survival/reproduction, reference toxicant QC, TIE results if triggered.
4. **Documents/forms**: WET Test Report; TRE/TIE plan if trigger met.
5. **Frequency**: Typically quarterly or semi-annual; permit-specific.
6. **Hand-offs**: Field/Lab → Compliance → State if failure.
7. **State-specific**: WV 47 CSR 2 + WET protocol; VA DEQ WET program; KY 401 KAR 10:031.
8. **Edge cases**: Reference toxicant out of control; control survival < 80%; sample preservation/temperature; passing TUc but failing instream waste concentration (IWC); selenium-driven TIE.

### 5.2 Toxicity Reduction Evaluation (TRE) / Toxicity Identification Evaluation (TIE)

1. **What it is**: Multi-phase investigation triggered by WET failure to identify the toxicant and reduce it.
2. **Performs**: Specialist consultant.
3. **Data captured**: Phase I (characterization), Phase II (identification), Phase III (confirmation); causative toxicant; treatment recommendation; schedule.
4. **Documents/forms**: TRE/TIE Plan, Interim Reports, Final Report.
5. **Frequency**: Per failure trigger (typically 2 consecutive failures).
6. **Hand-offs**: Environmental → Consultant → State.
7. **State-specific**: All three states use EPA Toxicity Reduction Evaluation Guidance; schedules included in permit.
8. **Edge cases**: Salt toxicity (TDS/sulfate/conductivity) — hard to "treat" without RO/IX; metals toxicity overlapping with WQS metals exceedance.

---

## 6. Stream Monitoring & Biological Assessment

### 6.1 Upstream/Downstream Chemical Monitoring

1. **What it is**: Sample stations above first mine discharge and below last mine discharge to demonstrate instream impact (or lack thereof).
2. **Performs**: Site Tech / consultant.
3. **Data captured**: Same parameters as effluent + WQS parameters (hardness, Ca, Mg, total/dissolved metals, conductivity, sulfate, chloride).
4. **Documents/forms**: Instream Monitoring Report; CHIA (Cumulative Hydrologic Impact Assessment) update.
5. **Frequency**: Permit-specific; commonly quarterly.
6. **Hand-offs**: Field → Permit Engineer → CHIA → DMR section.
7. **State-specific**: WV requires for SMCRA Article 3 permits + many NPDES; VA per DMLR; KY per DMP + DOW.
8. **Edge cases**: Upstream sample contaminated by neighboring operator; flow-weighted vs grab discrepancy.

### 6.2 Biological (Benthic Macroinvertebrate) Assessment

1. **What it is**: Periodic benthic macroinvertebrate sampling and computation of state-specific multi-metric index.
2. **Performs**: Qualified biologist (consultant).
3. **Data captured**: Sample location, riffle/run habitat code, family/genus IDs, abundances, EPT taxa count, %EPT, HBI, ChC, computed index score, condition class (very good/good/gray zone/impaired).
4. **Documents/forms**: Bioassessment Report with QA narrative; data deliverable.
5. **Frequency**: Annual to biennial typically; index period (spring April–June primary).
6. **Hand-offs**: Consultant → Permit Engineer → State for TMDL / narrative review.
7. **State-specific**:
   - **WV**: WVSCI (family-level, 6 metrics, 0-100 scale, impairment threshold 60.6); GLIMPSS (genus-level, geographically/seasonally stratified, used since ~2014 for assessment).
   - **VA**: VSCI (Virginia Stream Condition Index, family-level, 8 metrics, impairment threshold 60).
   - **KY**: MBI (Macroinvertebrate Bioassessment Index) per KY DOW, with separate Bluegrass / Mountain regions and KIBI fish index.
8. **Edge cases**: Conductivity-driven impairment (WV/KY Central Appalachian narrative-based 303(d) listings); Phase IV/V CHIA disputes; "gray zone" results forcing follow-up; mining permit conditioned on biomonitoring "no degradation."

### 6.3 Stream Habitat Assessment

1. **What it is**: RBP habitat scoring (EPA Rapid Bioassessment Protocol) of physical stream condition at each bio station.
2. **Performs**: Same biologist team.
3. **Data captured**: 10 RBP metrics for high-gradient streams (epifaunal substrate, embeddedness, velocity/depth regime, sediment deposition, channel flow status, channel alteration, frequency of riffles, bank stability, bank vegetative protection, riparian veg width).
