- **Data captured:** Time of incident, time of knowledge, time of call, MSHA hotline confirmation #, caller name, event description, location, persons involved.
- **Documents/forms:** Internal notification log; MSHA Form 7000-1 follows within 10 working days.
- **Frequency:** Per qualifying event.
- **Hand-offs:** First-responder → Safety Director → MSHA hotline → State agency hotline → Corporate → Legal/Insurance.
- **State-specific:** WV 304-558-1425 / VA 540-523-8208 / KY 502-573-0140 separate notification lines; state windows can be even shorter (WV within 15 min, parallels federal).
- **Pain points:** Defining "knowledge"; the 15-min clock is unforgiving; missed calls trigger automatic citation; multiple notification channels.

### MSHA Form 7000-1 Accident/Injury/Illness Report
- **What it is:** Detailed report for every accident (as defined in §50.2) and every occupational injury and illness, even if no time lost. Four-part color-coded form; one per injured person.
- **Who performs it:** Safety Director / Safety Clerk completes; mine medical/EMT contributes injury details; supervisor signs.
- **Data captured:** Mine ID, contractor ID, date/time of injury, person ID & SSN (last 4), occupation code, mine experience years, job experience years, location code (UG face/UG outby/surface/prep plant/office/shop), activity at time, accident category code, nature of injury code, body part code, source of injury, days lost, days restricted, return-to-work date, classification (fatal / nonfatal days lost / non-injury accident / occupational illness), narrative.
- **Documents/forms:** MSHA Form 7000-1 (4-part color-coded); Copy 4 retained at mine for 5 years; electronic equivalent via MSHA Electronic Filing.
- **Frequency:** Within 10 working days of accident/injury/illness diagnosis.
- **Hand-offs:** Supervisor near-miss report → Safety → MSHA portal → MSHA Pittsburgh statistics → quarterly check against 7000-2 hours for incident rate.
- **State-specific:** WV requires concurrent state injury report (WV Form WC-IR-1); VA state injury report; KY state injury report. State workers comp filing on separate path.
- **Pain points:** Occupation/activity codes change periodically; "lost workday" vs "restricted duty" determination contentious; rate calculation errors snowball.

### Mine Emergency Notification — Specific Events
- **What it is:** Beyond §50.10, certain events require additional notifications (e.g., methane ignition logs to MSHA District; refuse impoundment failures to state dam safety authorities; explosions trigger investigation team).
- **Who performs it:** Safety Director; Environmental Manager (for impoundments).
- **Data captured:** Event-specific data (methane ignition: location, methane concentration, ignition source; impoundment: phreatic levels, slope movement).
- **Documents/forms:** Methane ignition report (MSHA District); refuse impoundment incident report (WV DEP/VA DMME/KY DEP).
- **Frequency:** Per event.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety/Environmental → MSHA → state agency → impoundment engineer.
- **State-specific:** WV DEP Dam Safety; VA DMME-DMM; KY Division of Mine Reclamation & Enforcement.
- **Pain points:** Multiple agencies; conflicting notification timelines.

---

## Training (30 CFR Part 46 & Part 48)

### Part 48 New Underground Miner Training
- **What it is:** 40-hour minimum new-miner training for all UG miners (whether new to mining or returning after extended absence) before working in a UG mine. Covers MSHA rights, hazard recognition, escape/evacuation, communications, first aid, transportation, electrical, ground control, ventilation, methane, dust, health, and 8-hour task training.
- **Who performs it:** MSHA "Blue Card" approved instructor (mine trainer or contracted school).
- **Data captured:** Miner name, SSN, MSHA ID, training topics, hours per topic, instructor name & Blue Card #, exam scores, completion date.
- **Documents/forms:** MSHA Form 5000-3 (Certificate of Training); approved training plan on file with District.
- **Frequency:** Once before starting (per miner); 40 hours total.
- **Hand-offs:** HR hire → Training Coordinator → Blue Card instructor → records → mine.
- **State-specific:** WV requires state miner certification card (state law also requires "apprentice miner" status and progression to "experienced underground miner" after 1 year + state exam). VA similar. KY requires KY underground miner certification (separate exam).
- **Pain points:** Coordinating 40 hrs of training before payroll start; mining-school schedule constraints; out-of-state hires need to re-cert per state.

### Part 48 New Surface Miner Training (Coal Surface)
- **What it is:** 24-hour new-miner training for surface coal miners — note Part 48 applies to surface coal mines despite common Part 46/48 confusion. Topics: MSHA rights, transportation, communications, escape, first aid, health, ground control, electrical, ventilation, equipment.
- **Who performs it:** Blue Card instructor.
- **Data captured:** Same as UG.
- **Documents/forms:** MSHA Form 5000-3.
- **Frequency:** Once before starting; 24 hrs.
- **Hand-offs:** HR → Training → mine.
- **State-specific:** WV surface miner certification additional; VA & KY state surface cards required.
- **Pain points:** Surface coal miners sometimes assume Part 46 applies — it does not.

### Part 46 New Miner Training (Surface Non-Coal — limited applicability for Southern Coal but applies to some prep-plant or aggregate operations)
- **What it is:** 24-hour new-miner training for surface non-coal/non-MNM with no Blue Card requirement; trainer must be "competent."
- **Who performs it:** Mine-designated competent trainer (no MSHA Blue Card required).
- **Data captured:** Miner name, SSN, topics, hours, trainer name, completion.
- **Documents/forms:** MSHA Form 5000-23 OR equivalent under §46.9(b); approved training plan on file (operator self-approved, kept on site, available to MSHA on request — no District approval needed).
- **Frequency:** Once before starting.
- **Hand-offs:** Trainer → records → mine.
- **State-specific:** State rules may still apply if state code covers the facility.
- **Pain points:** Plan format flexibility = inconsistency; assuming Blue Card not needed for surface coal (it IS needed).

### Annual Refresher Training (Part 48 — 8 hr)
- **What it is:** 8-hour annual refresher required for every UG and surface coal miner; covers updates to standards, accident review, ventilation/roof/electrical refresher, escape drills.
- **Who performs it:** Blue Card instructor.
- **Data captured:** Topics, hours, instructor, completion date, miner sign-in.
- **Documents/forms:** MSHA Form 5000-3.
- **Frequency:** Annually within 12 months of prior refresher.
- **Hand-offs:** Training Coordinator → mine → MSHA on inspection.
- **State-specific:** WV requires separate state annual retraining (8 hr UG / 4 hr surface mine task); VA requires 8 hr; KY requires 8 hr UG retraining annually.
- **Pain points:** Tracking 12-month rolling deadlines; rolling crew of contractors; correlating state vs federal retraining.

### Annual Refresher Training (Part 46 — 8 hr)
- **What it is:** 8-hour annual refresher; can be online; trainer is "competent person."
- **Who performs it:** Competent trainer.
- **Data captured:** Same as Part 48 refresher.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 5000-23 or equivalent.
- **Frequency:** Annually.
- **Hand-offs:** Trainer → records.
- **State-specific:** Limited Southern Coal applicability.
- **Pain points:** Tracking online completion certificates.

### New Task Training (Both Parts)
- **What it is:** Training before assigning miner to new task with health/safety implications (e.g., assignment to roof bolter, scoop, longwall, blasting); includes hazards, controls, equipment-specific procedures.
- **Who performs it:** Foreman or trainer "knowledgeable of task."
- **Data captured:** Miner, task, equipment, hazards covered, demonstration verified, date, trainer.
- **Documents/forms:** Task training certification (often Form 5000-23/5000-3 with task block).
- **Frequency:** Each new task assignment.
- **Hand-offs:** Foreman → Training Coordinator → records.
- **State-specific:** WV requires state-recognized task instructor.
- **Pain points:** Documenting "new" vs prior experience; informal task changes during shift.

### Newly Employed Experienced Miner (Part 48 — 8 hr) / Newly Hired Experienced Miner (Part 46)
- **What it is:** Reduced training (typically 8 hr or less) for miner with prior mining experience hired by new operator; covers site-specific hazards and emergency procedures.
- **Who performs it:** Blue Card (Part 48) or competent trainer (Part 46).
- **Data captured:** Prior experience verification, topics covered, completion.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 5000-3 / 5000-23.
- **Frequency:** Once at hire.
- **Hand-offs:** HR verifies prior records → Training → mine.
- **State-specific:** Out-of-state experience often not transferable; WV typically requires state exam regardless.
- **Pain points:** Verifying prior employment hours; missing prior 5000-3s from prior employer.

### Site-Specific Hazard Training
- **What it is:** Short training for any person (visitor, vendor, contractor, surveyor) entering the mine site; covers site map, hazards, evacuation, PPE.
- **Who performs it:** Foreman, safety, or designated trainer.
- **Data captured:** Visitor name, company, escort, hazards reviewed, sign-in date/time.
- **Documents/forms:** Site-specific hazard awareness training log.
- **Frequency:** Each entry by non-trained person.
- **Hand-offs:** Guard shack → Safety → escort.
- **State-specific:** All states require.
- **Pain points:** Compliance for one-off visitors; lost sign-in sheets.

### Hazard Training (Contractors)
- **What it is:** Contractors must receive equivalent Part 46/48 training OR site-specific hazard training if work is short-duration. Long-duration contractors (>5 days or doing miner-like work) need full training.
- **Who performs it:** Contractor's trainer or mine's trainer.
- **Data captured:** Contractor name, MSHA contractor ID, employee names, training dates, training type.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 5000-3 or 5000-23 from contractor; site-specific training log.
- **Frequency:** Per contractor hire and per project.
- **Hand-offs:** Contractor → mine Safety → records.
- **State-specific:** State requires state cards for in-state contractors.
- **Pain points:** Contractors moving across mines daily; expired training cards; surprise §104(g) orders.

### Approved Training Plan
- **What it is:** Part 48 plans require MSHA District approval; Part 46 plans are operator-self-approved but must be kept on site. Plan lists trainers, topics, schedule, locations, hours.
- **Who performs it:** Training Coordinator drafts; District EFS specialist approves (Part 48).
- **Data captured:** Plan ID, mine ID, trainers list, topics, hours per topic, instructional aids, approval date, expiration.
- **Documents/forms:** Part 48 Training Plan (district-stamped); Part 46 Training Plan (self-approved on file).
- **Frequency:** Updated for any significant change; reviewed annually.
- **Hand-offs:** Coordinator → District EFS → mine.
- **State-specific:** WV state plans require WV OMHST approval; VA state plans via DOE; KY plans via OMSL.
- **Pain points:** Plan revisions during personnel changes; instructor turnover; District backlog on approvals.

### Instructor & Blue Card Approvals
- **What it is:** MSHA approves Part 48 trainers ("Blue Card") via application, background, and demonstrated competency; specialty approvals for first aid, mine rescue, etc.
- **Who performs it:** Trainer applies; MSHA Educational Field Services reviews.
- **Data captured:** Trainer name, Blue Card #, subjects approved, expiration, renewal training records.
- **Documents/forms:** MSHA Trainer Approval Application; Blue Card.
- **Frequency:** Initial approval; ongoing as new subjects added.
- **Hand-offs:** Trainer → EFS → mine records.
- **State-specific:** WV approved instructor list; VA state instructor list; KY state instructor list.
- **Pain points:** Limited trainer pool in Appalachia; recruiting & retaining Blue Card holders.

### Training Recordkeeping (Form 5000-23 vs 5000-3)
- **What it is:** Form 5000-23 is the standard Certificate of Training used for Part 46 (and acceptable for Part 48 refresher per §46.9). Form 5000-3 is the formal Part 48 Certificate signed by Blue Card. Both must be kept for 2 years (Part 46) or 5 years (Part 48 — typically 2 yrs by reg, but 5 commonly retained).
- **Who performs it:** Training Coordinator; HR.
- **Data captured:** Miner name, SSN/MSHA ID, training type, hours, trainer name & approval #, date, location, mine.
- **Documents/forms:** MSHA Form 5000-23 (Part 46); MSHA Form 5000-3 (Part 48); LMS/training-software equivalents.
- **Frequency:** Per training event.
- **Hand-offs:** Trainer → records → miner copy → MSHA on demand.
- **State-specific:** WV/VA/KY all have state training certificates (often a miner's wallet card).
- **Pain points:** Loss of records during operator changes; miner doesn't have prior certs; MSHA wants instant retrieval during inspection.

---

## State Certifications

### WV OMHST Certifications
- **What it is:** WV Office of Miners' Health, Safety & Training issues state certifications required to perform specific roles at WV mines: Underground Mine Foreman / Fire Boss; Surface Mine Foreman; Underground Mine Electrician; Surface Mine Electrician; Apprentice Miner; Inexperienced Surface Miner; Experienced UG Miner; Shot Firer (Blaster); EMT-Mine; Methane Testing; Hoisting Engineer; Belt Examiner; Dust Sampler.
- **Who performs it:** Individual takes WV exam administered by OMHST; mine pays fees and confirms experience.
- **Data captured:** Certificant name, cert type, cert #, issue date, expiration, retraining due, exam scores, experience verification (e.g., 5 yrs UG for Mine Foreman-Fire Boss; 3 yrs surface for Surface Foreman).
- **Documents/forms:** WV Cert Application; experience affidavit; OMHST wallet card; annual retraining sign-in.
- **Frequency:** Initial exam; annual retraining (typically 8 hrs UG / surface specific).
- **Hand-offs:** Miner → mine HR → OMHST → cert issuance → wallet card → mine records.
- **State-specific:** WV-only — does NOT transfer to VA or KY automatically. WV-resident or WV-employed requirement.
- **Pain points:** $35 application fee; experience verification disputes; annual retraining tracking across hundreds of certs.

### VA DOE / Division of Mines Certifications
- **What it is:** VA Department of Energy (Division of Mines for coal; Division of Mineral Mining for non-coal) issues: Underground Mine Foreman; Surface Mine Foreman; Underground Electrician; Surface Electrician; Dust Sampler; Gas Detection (Methane Testing); EMT-Mine; Mine Foreman Surface (mineral mining); Blaster; Hoisting Engineer; First Aid Instructor; General Coal Miner.
- **Who performs it:** Individual applies; VA Board of Coal Mining Examiners (BCME) administers exam.
- **Data captured:** Certificant name, cert type, cert #, issue date, 5-year renewal date, exam results, work experience.
- **Documents/forms:** VA Certification Application (DMM-200 series for mineral mining; DMME forms for coal); experience affidavit; 5-year renewal course completion.
- **Frequency:** Initial exam; 5-year renewal cycle (online course or re-exam); $10 fee.
- **Hand-offs:** Miner → mine HR → DOE → exam → cert issuance → 5-yr renewal tracker.
- **State-specific:** VA-only; surface coal foreman requires 5 yrs experience (1 yr at a surface mine).
- **Pain points:** 5-year cycle easy to miss; BCME exam schedule limited; coal vs mineral mining certs distinct.

### KY OMSL Certifications
- **What it is:** KY Office of Mine Safety & Licensing issues: Mine Foreman (UG); Surface Mine Foreman; Underground Mine Electrician; Surface Mine Electrician; Underground Miner; Surface Miner; Surface Mine Equipment Operator (SMEO); EMT-Mine (Mine Emergency Technician per 805 KAR 7:080); Blaster (30-hr course + exam); Hoisting Engineer; Inexperienced Miner; Mine Foreman Annual Retraining.
- **Who performs it:** Individual applies; KY DMS administers exam; KY OMSL issues card.
- **Data captured:** Certificant, type, #, issue date, annual retraining due, exam scores, experience.
- **Documents/forms:** KY Mine Safety certification application; experience affidavit; MET training certificate.
- **Frequency:** Initial exam; annual retraining for foreman/electrician/MET.
- **Hand-offs:** Miner → mine HR → KY OMSL → exam → card → mine records.
- **State-specific:** KY-only; KY MET ≠ MSHA EMT; KY blaster cert separate from OSMRE blaster cert.
- **Pain points:** Annual retraining for MET, foreman; cross-border miners need three sets of cards.

### Mine Foreman / Section Foreman (cross-state)
- **What it is:** Person in charge of working section; conducts preshift, onshift, and weekly examinations; supervises crew; first responder.
- **Who performs it:** Certified individual.
- **Data captured:** Foreman name, state cert #s (all three), shift assignment, current sections supervised.
- **Documents/forms:** State cert cards; daily section log; examination books.
- **Frequency:** Daily duty.
- **Hand-offs:** Foreman → Mine Manager → Safety → Examination Book → MSHA inspector.
- **State-specific:** Each state requires its own foreman card; experience requirements differ (WV 5 yr UG, VA 5 yr, KY varies).
- **Pain points:** Foreman shortage; succession planning; loss of certified foreman halts production.

### Underground / Surface Electrician
- **What it is:** Performs electrical work on mine equipment up to specified voltage (often 1000V+); state cert separate from licensed electrician trade.
- **Who performs it:** Certified mine electrician.
- **Data captured:** Cert #s, voltage level authorized, scope (UG vs surface), employer.
- **Documents/forms:** State electrician cert; permissibility exam log; weekly electrical exam.
- **Frequency:** Daily as assigned.
- **Hand-offs:** Electrician → maintenance planner → Safety on electrical citations.
- **State-specific:** WV exam covers AC/DC, permissibility, grounding; VA requires journeyman or master electrical license as base; KY OMSL separate cert.
- **Pain points:** Aging workforce; competing demand from non-mining electrical jobs.

### Fire Boss / Certified Mine Examiner
- **What it is:** Person qualified to conduct preshift and weekly examinations including methane checks. In WV, "Mine Foreman-Fire Boss" combines both functions.
- **Who performs it:** State-certified fire boss.
- **Data captured:** Cert #s, exam locations assigned, methane spotter & detector calibration current.
- **Documents/forms:** State cert; preshift exam book; methane detector calibration log.
- **Frequency:** Per shift; per week.
- **Hand-offs:** Fire boss → foreman → next shift → exam book.
- **State-specific:** WV — Fire Boss merged with UG Foreman; KY separate; VA combined under Mine Foreman.
- **Pain points:** Methane detector cal traceability.

### Blaster / Shot Firer
- **What it is:** Person authorized to handle, place, and detonate explosives. Federal OSMRE blaster cert governs surface coal blasting under SMCRA; state cert governs mining blasting.
- **Who performs it:** Certified blaster.
- **Data captured:** Federal cert #, state cert #, magazine location, blast log entries.
- **Documents/forms:** OSMRE Blaster Certification; WV blaster cert (Office of Explosives & Blasting under WV DEP); VA blaster cert (DOE — Division of Mines/Mineral Mining); KY blaster cert (DMS — 30-hr course + exam).
- **Frequency:** Per blast.
- **Hand-offs:** Blaster → safety → blast log → state agency on incident.
- **State-specific:** KY requires 30-hr initial blaster course before exam; WV requires blaster license through WV DEP Office of Explosives & Blasting; VA blaster cert separate for surface coal vs mineral mining.
- **Pain points:** Cert reciprocity across states; ATF responsible person background checks separate.

### EMT-Mine
- **What it is:** Emergency Medical Technician specifically certified for mine environment; staffs first aid station, responds to underground emergencies, paired with rescue teams. Required at certain UG mines depending on miner count.
- **Who performs it:** Mine-employed or contracted EMT-M.
- **Data captured:** EMT cert #, mine-specific endorsement, scope (BLS, ALS), shift coverage, equipment inventory.
- **Documents/forms:** State EMT license; state mine endorsement; first aid station inventory log.
- **Frequency:** Per shift coverage; recert per state EMS rules.
- **Hand-offs:** EMT → injured miner → outside ambulance/hospital → Safety.
- **State-specific:** WV requires EMT-M endorsement through WV OMHST + WV OEMS; VA requires Mine EMT recognition; KY recognizes KY MET (Mine Emergency Technician) as the parallel role.
- **Pain points:** Combined EMS + mine certification rare; coverage during turnover.

### Mine Rescue Team Member
- **What it is:** Member of organized mine rescue team certified to enter mine atmospheres unsafe to ordinary miners using BG-4 (or equivalent) closed-circuit breathing apparatus. Each UG mine must have access to two teams within 1 hour.
- **Who performs it:** Trained team member (own employee or contract service — Mountaineer Mine Rescue, Eastern Associated, Murray, Alpha Mine Rescue, etc.).
- **Data captured:** Team roster, member cert dates, physical exam date, drill participation, equipment inventory, team type (operational / benchmark).
- **Documents/forms:** Mine rescue team roster (filed with MSHA); team training records; annual physical results.
- **Frequency:** Monthly training (8 hrs); annual physical; annual contests/drills.
- **Hand-offs:** Team captain → Safety → MSHA District (during emergency).
- **State-specific:** All three states require mine rescue capability; WV operates state mine rescue program; VA/KY rely heavily on commercial teams.
- **Pain points:** Team retention; expensive equipment (BG-4 rebuild costs); finding fit personnel for arduous work.

### Rock Dusting / Dust Sampling Certifications
- **What it is:** Persons certified to take respirable dust samples (under Part 70, 71, 90, and silica rule) and to verify rock-dust application sufficient to prevent coal dust propagation.
- **Who performs it:** Certified dust sampler / rock duster.
- **Data captured:** Sampler cert #, MSHA Dust Sampling Operator number, sample locations, results, calibration logs.
- **Documents/forms:** MSHA dust sampling card; sample chain of custody; lab analysis report.
- **Frequency:** Per sampling event.
- **Hand-offs:** Sampler → lab (Pittsburgh Tech Support) → Safety → MSHA online portal.
- **State-specific:** WV state dust sampler endorsement; KY state recognition.
- **Pain points:** Sample voiding for procedural errors; new silica rule changes calibration flow rate.

### Methane Testing Cert
- **What it is:** Certified person who can use methane detector to check air quality before energizing equipment, entering area, blasting, etc.
- **Who performs it:** Certified methane tester (often foreman, electrician).
- **Data captured:** Cert #, detector serial, calibration date, readings.
- **Documents/forms:** State cert; methane detector calibration record.
- **Frequency:** Multiple times per shift.
- **Hand-offs:** Tester → foreman → exam book.
- **State-specific:** WV methane testing endorsement; VA Gas Detection cert; KY methane testing cert.
- **Pain points:** Bump-test vs calibration distinction; equipment downtime on detector failure.

---

## Ventilation

### Ventilation Plan (UG — MSHA District Approved)
- **What it is:** Site-specific MSHA-approved plan governing air quantity, splits, methane controls, dust controls, bleeder systems, seal management, fan operation, etc. (30 CFR 75.370).
- **Who performs it:** Mine Engineer (Ventilation) drafts; District Ventilation Specialist reviews & approves; updated for any material change.
- **Data captured:** Plan ID, approval date, approval letter, fan curves, intake/return quantities, methane liberation, section configurations, bleeder design, seal locations, monitor placements, dust parameters.
- **Documents/forms:** Approved Ventilation Plan; District approval letter; revision log.
- **Frequency:** Approval initial; 6-month review; revisions ad hoc.
- **Hand-offs:** Mine Engineer → District Vent Specialist → Mine Manager → all shift foremen.
- **State-specific:** WV requires concurrent state ventilation plan approval; VA & KY likewise.
- **Pain points:** Slow District approval; revisions during plan changes (longwall moves, new development) delay production; conflicting state vs federal requirements.

### Plan Revisions
- **What it is:** Required revision submitted whenever conditions change (mining height, equipment, section, fan, methane liberation, seal addition).
- **Who performs it:** Mine Engineer; District approves.
- **Data captured:** Revision #, change summary, effective date, approval date.
- **Documents/forms:** Plan revision submittal, District approval letter.
- **Frequency:** Per material change.
- **Hand-offs:** Mine Eng → District → mine.
- **State-specific:** Parallel state revision required.
- **Pain points:** Production halts pending approval; informal "field" deviations risk citation.

### Quarterly Air Measurements (Air Quantity Surveys)
- **What it is:** Required quantity readings at intake, returns, splits, working faces (at least every 31 days; weekly in many locations under §75.364). Quarterly comprehensive survey.
- **Who performs it:** Certified examiner / mine engineer.
- **Data captured:** Date/time, location code, anemometer reading, area dimensions, velocity, quantity (cfm), methane concentration, temperature.
- **Documents/forms:** Air measurement book (electronic per PIB allowance); examination book entries.
- **Frequency:** Each shift face; weekly outby; quarterly comprehensive.
- **Hand-offs:** Examiner → Vent Engineer → exam book → MSHA inspector on demand.
- **State-specific:** Each state requires parallel air-quantity recordkeeping.
- **Pain points:** Anemometer calibration; consistent technique across personnel.

### Methane Monitoring & CH4 Calibrations
- **What it is:** Continuous methane monitoring on continuous miners, longwalls, and belts; handheld checks throughout shift; trip points (1.0% deenergize face; 1.5% withdraw; 2.0% bleeder).
- **Who performs it:** Equipment operators (handheld); electricians (monitor calibration); foremen (check).
- **Data captured:** Monitor serial #, location, calibration date, span gas lot, calibration result, alarms/trips, methane readings throughout shift.
- **Documents/forms:** Methane monitor calibration log; continuous monitor strip-chart or electronic log; preshift book.
- **Frequency:** Every 31 days calibration; daily bump-test; continuous monitoring.
- **Hand-offs:** Electrician calibrates → foreman uses → exam book → MSHA.
- **State-specific:** State law parallels (WV 22A-2).
- **Pain points:** Sensor drift; documentation gaps cause citations; false alarms causing unnecessary withdrawals.

### Sealed Area Monitoring
- **What it is:** Inspection of permanent seals (Mine Vent Stoppings) and atmospheres behind them; monitoring of bleeder evaluation points; tracking of any explosive atmosphere behind seals (§75.336).
- **Who performs it:** Certified examiner with mine engineer oversight.
- **Data captured:** Seal ID, type (40 psi / 50 psi / 120 psi), date built, location, weekly exam date/initials, atmosphere samples (O2/CH4/CO).
- **Documents/forms:** Seal log; sample analysis; weekly exam entry.
- **Frequency:** Weekly inspection; sampling per plan.
- **Hand-offs:** Examiner → Vent Engineer → exam book → District.
- **State-specific:** State law mirrors.
- **Pain points:** Sealed areas hidden — relying on indirect monitoring; building seals requires specialized contractor.

### Bleeder Evaluations
- **What it is:** Weekly examination of bleeder system to confirm it dilutes and removes methane from worked-out areas. §75.364.
- **Who performs it:** Certified examiner.
- **Data captured:** Evaluation date, bleeder split #, air quantity, methane%, evaluation points checked, status (effective / ineffective).
- **Documents/forms:** Weekly exam book; bleeder evaluation diagram.
- **Frequency:** Weekly (≤7-day intervals).
- **Hand-offs:** Examiner → Vent Engineer → exam book.
- **State-specific:** Parallel state requirements.
- **Pain points:** Long bleeder traverses; gob inaccessibility; ineffective findings stop adjacent mining.

### Fan Certifications & Pressure Recordings
- **What it is:** Main mine fans must be examined/tested daily; pressure differential recorded; alarm/automatic shutdown systems tested.
- **Who performs it:** Surface fan attendant / electrician.
- **Data captured:** Fan ID, date/time, pressure (water gauge inches), motor amps, vibration, alarm test, run status.
- **Documents/forms:** Fan exam book (§75.310); fan chart recording.
- **Frequency:** Daily examination; continuous pressure recording; weekly alarm test.
- **Hand-offs:** Attendant → Surface Foreman → exam book.
- **State-specific:** State requires.
- **Pain points:** Old fan controls; chart recorder maintenance; alarm test documentation.

### Diesel Particulate Sampling
- **What it is:** Where diesel equipment used UG, sampling for diesel particulate matter (DPM) per §72.520; control via filters and engine specs.
- **Who performs it:** Sampler / Industrial Hygienist.
- **Data captured:** Sample location, occupation, DPM µg/m³, engine list.
- **Documents/forms:** DPM sample log; lab report.
- **Frequency:** Per plan (varies).
- **Hand-offs:** Sampler → lab → Safety.
- **State-specific:** Federal-focused; state echoes.
- **Pain points:** Limited diesel use in UG coal, but applies; new low-sulfur fuel & DPF requirements.

---

## Roof / Rib / Ground Control

### Roof Control Plan (MSHA District Approved)
- **What it is:** Site-specific plan (§75.220) specifying bolt pattern, bolt type, bolt length, secondary support, mining height, pillar dimensions, retreat practices, intersection requirements, weak-strata controls.
- **Who performs it:** Mine Engineer (Ground Control); District Roof Control Specialist approves.
- **Data captured:** Plan ID, approval date, bolt patterns by seam zone, pillar dimensions, top-hole criteria, supplemental support standards, retreat sequence.
- **Documents/forms:** Approved Roof Control Plan; revisions; District letter.
- **Frequency:** Initial; 6-month review; revisions per condition change.
- **Hand-offs:** Mine Eng → District → all foremen.
- **State-specific:** State approval parallel.
- **Pain points:** Plan revisions slow; deviations cited.

### Test Holes & Scaling
- **What it is:** Drilling exploratory holes to assess overlying strata thickness/character; scaling loose material from roof and ribs.
- **Who performs it:** Roof bolter / continuous miner operator / foreman.
- **Data captured:** Hole location, depth, strata log, scale operations log.
- **Documents/forms:** Test hole log; daily section book.
- **Frequency:** Per advance; per condition change.
- **Hand-offs:** Operator → foreman → Mine Engineer.
- **State-specific:** Parallel.
- **Pain points:** Documenting informal activity.

### Bolt Installation Records
- **What it is:** Recording bolts installed per shift — length, type, pattern, locations.
- **Who performs it:** Roof bolter operator; section foreman.
- **Data captured:** Date/shift, section, location (XC#), bolt count by type, pattern verification, anchorage test results.
- **Documents/forms:** Roof bolter daily log; bolt anchor test record (§75.204).
- **Frequency:** Per shift.
- **Hand-offs:** Operator → foreman → engineer → exam book.
- **State-specific:** State documentation parallel.
- **Pain points:** Operator paperwork burden; anchorage tests forgotten.

### Convergence Monitoring
- **What it is:** Measuring roof-to-floor convergence over time at instrumented stations; pillar stress monitoring.
- **Who performs it:** Mine Engineer / Ground Control specialist.
- **Data captured:** Station ID, baseline, periodic readings, convergence rate, alert thresholds.
- **Documents/forms:** Convergence log; ground control engineering report.
- **Frequency:** Periodic per plan.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineer → Mine Manager.
- **State-specific:** Engineering best practice; not state-specific.
- **Pain points:** Sensor maintenance; trending across many stations.

### Cribs, Posts, Secondary Support
- **What it is:** Installation of wooden cribs, hydraulic posts, cable bolts, mesh, etc. as secondary support per plan or conditions.
- **Who performs it:** Section crew / foreman direction.
- **Data captured:** Support type, location, installation date.
- **Documents/forms:** Section daily log.
- **Frequency:** As needed.
- **Hand-offs:** Crew → foreman → engineer.
- **State-specific:** Parallel.
- **Pain points:** Material stocking; installation quality.

### Fall-of-Ground Investigations
- **What it is:** Any fall of roof, rib, or face that disrupts ventilation/access or causes injury is reportable; full investigation including root cause.
- **Who performs it:** Mine Engineer + Safety + MSHA inspector.
- **Data captured:** Fall location, dimensions (length/width/height), geological description, support in place, contributing factors, persons affected, corrective action.
- **Documents/forms:** Internal investigation report; MSHA Form 7000-1 if injury; §50.10 call if §50.2(h) event.
- **Frequency:** Per event.
- **Hand-offs:** Foreman → Safety → MSHA → Engineering → corrective action.
- **State-specific:** State agencies investigate parallel.
- **Pain points:** Multiple investigations; preserving scene; root-cause discipline.

---

## Dust Control

### Rock Dusting Application & Frequency
- **What it is:** Application of inert (limestone) rock dust to coal mine surfaces to prevent coal-dust propagation in event of ignition. Required to maintain ≥80% total incombustible content (TIC) in intake; ≥80% in returns; ≥85% in critical zones.
- **Who performs it:** Rock duster operator; foreman verifies.
- **Data captured:** Date/shift, section, footage dusted, tons of rock dust used, equipment used.
- **Documents/forms:** Daily rock dusting log; rock dust delivery tickets.
- **Frequency:** Continuous (per mining cycle); driven by sample band results.
- **Hand-offs:** Crew → foreman → exam book → Mine Engineer.
- **State-specific:** State law parallels (WV 22A-2).
- **Pain points:** Logistical — moving rock dust; documenting volumes; sample-band failures trigger remedial dusting.

### Rock Dust Sample Bands & Lab Analysis
- **What it is:** Periodic sampling of dust bands at intervals along returns, intakes, and belts; analyzed at MSHA Pittsburgh Lab or accredited lab for TIC%.
- **Who performs it:** Certified sampler.
- **Data captured:** Sample ID, location, date, lab result %TIC, pass/fail.
- **Documents/forms:** Rock dust sample log; chain of custody; lab report.
- **Frequency:** Per plan (often quarterly to monthly).
- **Hand-offs:** Sampler → lab → Safety → exam book.
- **State-specific:** Federal-driven; states may piggyback.
- **Pain points:** Failed samples = §75.403 citation; remedial dusting required immediately.

### Respirable Coal Mine Dust Sampling (Part 70 / 71 / 90)
- **What it is:** Sampling of respirable coal mine dust on Designated Occupations (DOs) under Part 70 (UG miners); Part 71 (surface coal); Part 90 (Part 90 miners — formerly Section 203(b) miners with X-ray evidence). PEL = 1.5 mg/m³.
- **Who performs it:** Certified Dust Sampling Operator (mine staff or MSHA inspector).
- **Data captured:** Sampler #, DO/MMU/DA designation, miner name, location, sample weight, shift duration, calibration, lab result.
- **Documents/forms:** Dust sampling card (MSHA-issued); sample submission form; quarterly compliance summary.
- **Frequency:** Per Part 70 — quarterly cycle of 5 valid samples on each DO; monthly bimonthly variants.
- **Hand-offs:** Sampler → MSHA via online portal → results → corrective action if exceedance.
- **State-specific:** State dust certification.
- **Pain points:** Sample voids; flow-rate accuracy; new silica rule conformance.

### Respirable Silica Sampling (30 CFR Part 60 — 2024 Rule, currently stayed)
- **What it is:** Sampling for respirable crystalline silica at PEL 50 µg/m³ with action level 25 µg/m³ (8-hr TWA). Coal mine compliance dates were April 2025 but stayed by 8th Circuit Court of Appeals on April 11, 2025.
- **Who performs it:** Industrial Hygienist / certified sampler.
- **Data captured:** Sample at 1.7 L/min flow rate (per ISO); miner ID; location; PEL exceedance flag.
- **Documents/forms:** Part 60 sample log; medical surveillance triggers; respiratory protection records.
- **Frequency:** Per current state of rule (currently stayed; monitor for updates).
- **Hand-offs:** IH → lab → Safety → medical surveillance program if applicable.
- **State-specific:** Federal-driven; states tracking.
- **Pain points:** Rule status uncertainty (stayed → enforcement deferred); concurrent operation of legacy 1.5 mg/m³ coal dust rules at 2.0 L/min vs new silica rule at 1.7 L/min.

### Personal Dust Monitor (PDM) Deployments
- **What it is:** Continuous Personal Dust Monitor (CPDM) — required for Designated Occupations and Part 90 miners; real-time TWA reading.
- **Who performs it:** Miner wears unit; sampler manages program.
- **Data captured:** Miner ID, unit serial, shift TWA, end-of-shift download, calibration.
- **Documents/forms:** CPDM logs; quarterly summary.
- **Frequency:** Per DO/Part 90 — every shift sampled in compliance cycles.
- **Hand-offs:** Miner → sampler → MSHA portal.
- **State-specific:** Federal.
- **Pain points:** Unit cost ($15K each); battery life; data download.

### Mine Ventilation/Dust Control Plan (Combined Dust Plan §75.371(t))
- **What it is:** Dust-control aspects of the ventilation plan: water sprays, scrubbers, methods, DO designation.
- **Who performs it:** Mine Engineer + District.
- **Data captured:** DO list, control specs, scrubber maintenance.
- **Documents/forms:** Plan section; revisions.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; revised with conditions.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineer → District → mine.
- **State-specific:** Federal-driven.
- **Pain points:** Scrubber maintenance often inadequate.

### Quartz / Silica Lab Analysis
- **What it is:** Coal mine dust samples are analyzed for quartz; if >5% quartz, PEL reduced (legacy formula 10/% quartz mg/m³). New rule consolidates under Part 60.
- **Who performs it:** MSHA Pittsburgh Tech Center / commercial lab.
- **Data captured:** Sample ID, dust mg/m³, quartz %, calculated reduced PEL.
- **Documents/forms:** Lab report; corrective action.
- **Frequency:** Per sample with quartz analysis.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab → MSHA → mine.
- **State-specific:** Federal.
- **Pain points:** Geology variability; reduced PEL triggers.

---

## Impoundment Safety (30 CFR 77.216)

### Coal Refuse Impoundment Annual Certification (§77.216-4)
- **What it is:** Annual report and certification by registered professional engineer of impoundment status, including embankment stability, instrumentation review, spillway condition, phreatic surface.
- **Who performs it:** Registered PE (typically third-party — Stantec, Marshall Miller, Schnabel, BPC, Geo-Hydro).
- **Data captured:** Impoundment ID, MSHA dam ID, capacity, current pool elevation, freeboard, slope geometry, phreatic data, instrumentation readings, PE certification.
- **Documents/forms:** Annual Report Form (§77.216-4); certifying PE seal; submitted to MSHA District and (per state) state dam safety.
- **Frequency:** Annually (calendar year).
- **Hand-offs:** PE → mine Environmental → MSHA District → State Dam Safety (WV DEP / VA DMME / KY DOW).
- **State-specific:** WV DEP Dam Safety; VA DMME Division of Mined Land Reclamation; KY Division of Mine Reclamation.
- **Pain points:** PE scheduling; instrumentation maintenance; cost ($30–80K per impoundment per year).

### 7-Day Impoundment Inspections (§77.216-3)
- **What it is:** Visual inspections at intervals not exceeding 7 days of dam crest, slopes, abutments, spillway, decant, instrumentation.
- **Who performs it:** Designated inspector (mine engineer or environmental staff).
- **Data captured:** Inspection date, dam ID, observations (cracks, seepage, slumps, slope condition, water level, spillway condition), corrective actions.
- **Documents/forms:** Weekly inspection report; logbook.
- **Frequency:** Every 7 days.
- **Hand-offs:** Inspector → Environmental Manager → MSHA on request.
- **State-specific:** State requires similar.
- **Pain points:** Weather-dependent access; documentation rigor; small issues escalating.

### Instrumentation Monitoring (Piezometers, Survey Monuments, Inclinometers)
- **What it is:** Reading and trending of piezometers (phreatic levels), survey monuments (settlement), inclinometers (slope movement), seepage weirs.
- **Who performs it:** Survey crew / instrumentation technician / PE.
- **Data captured:** Instrument ID, reading, baseline, trend, alert/alarm.
- **Documents/forms:** Instrumentation database; PE review.
- **Frequency:** Weekly to monthly per plan.
- **Hand-offs:** Tech → PE → Mine Engineering → MSHA in annual report.
- **State-specific:** Required by state dam safety.
- **Pain points:** Sensor failure; lost monuments; trending analysis.

### Emergency Action Plan (EAP)
- **What it is:** Written plan for response to dam emergency — incident classification levels, notification flowchart, downstream inundation maps, evacuation, communications.
- **Who performs it:** Mine Environmental + PE; tabletop exercises with emergency mgmt.
- **Data captured:** EAP version, last update, last drill, emergency contact list, downstream population at risk, inundation map.
- **Documents/forms:** EAP document (state-specific format); annual update letter.
- **Frequency:** Annual review; major update for changes; tabletop drill annually.
- **Hand-offs:** EAP holder → County Emergency Management → State EOC → mine Safety.
- **State-specific:** WV DEP, VA DMME, KY DOW each have specific EAP requirements; downstream population thresholds determine plan rigor.
- **Pain points:** Coordinating with multiple county EMAs; updating downstream populations.

### Spillway Capacity Verification
- **What it is:** Confirming spillway can pass design storm (often Probable Maximum Flood — PMF — for high-hazard); hydraulic and hydrologic analysis updated periodically.
- **Who performs it:** PE.
- **Data captured:** Design storm, peak inflow, spillway rating curve, freeboard at design.
- **Documents/forms:** Hydrology/hydraulic study; impoundment design package update.
- **Frequency:** Initial; periodic (5-10 yr) or after major modification.
- **Hand-offs:** PE → MSHA Tech Support → mine.
- **State-specific:** State design standards differ.
- **Pain points:** Updated rainfall data (Atlas 14 → Atlas 15); capacity erosion over time.

### Phreatic Surface Monitoring
- **What it is:** Tracking internal water level via piezometers; high phreatic surface threatens embankment stability.
- **Who performs it:** Instrumentation tech; PE interprets.
- **Data captured:** Piezo ID, elevation, baseline, current, threshold.
- **Documents/forms:** Piezometer log; PE annual report.
- **Frequency:** Weekly to monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Tech → PE → mine Engineering.
- **State-specific:** Required.
- **Pain points:** Trend interpretation; alarm thresholds.

---

## Examinations

### Preshift Examination (UG — §75.360)
- **What it is:** Examination of every working section, belt conveyor, escape route, return air course, and other underground area for hazards (methane, oxygen, condition) within 3 hours before next shift enters.
- **Who performs it:** Certified examiner (mine foreman / fire boss).
- **Data captured:** Date, shift, examiner name, areas examined, methane readings, hazards found, corrective actions, time of exam, time of completion.
- **Documents/forms:** Preshift Exam Book (paper or MSHA-approved electronic under PIB P14-V-01).
- **Frequency:** Per shift, before crew enters.
- **Hand-offs:** Examiner → on-shift foreman → MSHA inspector on demand.
- **State-specific:** State law parallels (WV 22A-2-7; VA; KY).
- **Pain points:** 3-hour window tight; hazard wording for follow-up; electronic exam book MSHA approval status.

### On-shift Examination (UG — §75.362)
- **What it is:** Continuing examination during shift to ensure conditions remain safe; specifically test methane every 20 minutes at face during cutting and loading; tests at belts every shift; tests of electrical equipment.
- **Who performs it:** Section foreman + designated examiners.
- **Data captured:** Methane checks throughout shift; conditions monitored; corrective actions.
- **Documents/forms:** Onshift Exam Book (per §75.363 hazard recordings; §75.362 onshift entries).
- **Frequency:** Throughout shift; specific methane intervals.
- **Hand-offs:** Foreman → exam book → next shift.
- **State-specific:** State parallel.
- **Pain points:** Documenting 20-min methane checks; reconciling foreman daily activity.

### Weekly Examination (UG — §75.364)
- **What it is:** Weekly examination of return air courses, bleeder systems, hard-to-reach areas, seals, abandoned areas; certification of areas examined.
- **Who performs it:** Certified examiner (mine foreman).
- **Data captured:** Date, areas examined, hazards found, methane readings, certifications at observation points (initials/date/time on dated certification boards).
- **Documents/forms:** Weekly Exam Book; certification cards/boards along examined routes.
- **Frequency:** Each week (interval not exceeding 7 days).
- **Hand-offs:** Examiner → exam book → MSHA inspector.
- **State-specific:** State parallel.
- **Pain points:** Long traverses; certifications must be at enough points to demonstrate full coverage; missed seal exam = citation.

### Workplace Exam (Surface Coal — §77.1713 Daily Inspection)
- **What it is:** Surface coal mines use §77.1713 daily inspection of working areas by certified person; differs from Part 56/57 (MNM) workplace exam under §56.18002.
- **Who performs it:** Surface foreman or certified person.
- **Data captured:** Date, areas inspected, hazards, corrective actions, certifier.
- **Documents/forms:** Daily inspection record book.
- **Frequency:** At least daily.
- **Hand-offs:** Foreman → exam book → MSHA.
- **State-specific:** State daily exam parallel.
- **Pain points:** Common confusion with MNM Part 56/57 rules; recordkeeping rigor.

### Belt Examinations (UG — §75.362(b))
- **What it is:** Each belt conveyor examined at least once per shift; specific attention to alignment, accumulation, rollers, fire-suppression, belt slip.
- **Who performs it:** Belt examiner (certified).
- **Data captured:** Belt ID, date, shift, hazards (accumulation depth, slip, misalignment), corrective actions.
- **Documents/forms:** Belt exam book; CO sensor log along belts.
- **Frequency:** Once per shift per belt; continuous CO monitoring.
- **Hand-offs:** Examiner → foreman → exam book.
- **State-specific:** State parallel.
- **Pain points:** Float dust accumulation citations; CO sensor maintenance.

### Hoist Examinations (UG — §75.1400 series)
- **What it is:** Daily examination of personnel hoisting equipment; weekly more detailed; monthly inspection of ropes; annual hoist inspection.
- **Who performs it:** Hoist examiner; certified hoist engineer.
- **Data captured:** Hoist ID, exam type, components inspected, defects, corrective action.
- **Documents/forms:** Hoist exam book; rope inspection log.
- **Frequency:** Daily, weekly, monthly, annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Examiner → maintenance → records.
- **State-specific:** State requires hoist engineer cert (WV, KY).
- **Pain points:** Rope condition assessment; recordkeeping discipline.

### Electrical Exams (Weekly — §75.512)
- **What it is:** Weekly examination of electric equipment by qualified person; verify guarding, grounding, permissibility (where applicable).
- **Who performs it:** Certified mine electrician (qualified person).
- **Data captured:** Equipment ID, date, defects, corrective actions, completion.
- **Documents/forms:** Electrical exam log (§75.512-2).
- **Frequency:** Weekly.
- **Hand-offs:** Electrician → maintenance → MSHA.
- **State-specific:** State electrician cert required.
- **Pain points:** Identifying all equipment in inventory; "qualified person" definition.

### Permissibility Exams (UG — §75.503-§75.512)
- **What it is:** Examination of permissible (explosion-proof) electric equipment to verify enclosure integrity, flame paths, fastenings; weekly.
- **Who performs it:** Qualified electrician (permissibility examiner).
- **Data captured:** Equipment ID, gap measurements, fastenings, conduit, defects, corrective.
- **Documents/forms:** Permissibility exam log.
- **Frequency:** Weekly.
- **Hand-offs:** Electrician → maintenance → exam book.
- **State-specific:** State parallel.
- **Pain points:** Gap measurement consistency; downtime for thorough exam.

### Recordkeeping in Official Mine Record Books / Electronic Equivalents
- **What it is:** Statutorily required entries in bound paper books — preshift, onshift, weekly, methane, electrical, hoist, fan, belt, rock dust, etc. MSHA has approved electronic recordkeeping per PIB P14-V-01 if functionally equivalent.
- **Who performs it:** Each role's examiner; recordkeeper.
- **Data captured:** All above examination types.
- **Documents/forms:** Bound, indelible record books OR approved electronic system.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Examiner → book → MSHA on inspection.
- **State-specific:** State requires parallel state books in WV.
- **Pain points:** Two recordkeeping systems (state + federal); illegible handwriting; missing entries cause citations.

---

## Emergency Response

### Mine Emergency Response Plan (ERP — §75.1502)
- **What it is:** Required for every UG coal mine; comprehensive plan for self-rescue, escape, refuge, communications, tracking, training, drills, family notification.
- **Who performs it:** Mine Safety Director + Mine Manager; submitted to District for review.
- **Data captured:** ERP version, approval date, refuge alternative locations, SCSR cache locations, communication map, tracking system, rescue team contracts, family notification list.
- **Documents/forms:** ERP document; District review letter; revisions.
- **Frequency:** Annual review; revisions for any material change.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety Director → District → mine personnel → families.
- **State-specific:** State ERP also required (WV particularly stringent post-Sago/UBB).
- **Pain points:** Coordination across federal/state plans; family notification list maintenance.

### Refuge Alternatives (Chambers / Mobile — §75.1506)
- **What it is:** Pre-positioned (or mobile) chambers providing breathable atmosphere, food, water, communications for 96 hours; required to be within 1000 ft of working face (working section) and 30 min of farthest point.
- **Who performs it:** Refuge mfg/installer; mine maintenance.
- **Data captured:** Refuge ID, type, location, capacity, last inspection, consumables expiration, communications connection.
- **Documents/forms:** Refuge installation report; weekly inspection log; consumables inventory.
- **Frequency:** Installation; weekly inspection; consumables rotation.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance → Safety → MSHA verification.
- **State-specific:** State requires.
- **Pain points:** Mobile chamber location changes; consumables rotation discipline.

### SCSR (Self-Contained Self-Rescuer) Program (§75.1714)
- **What it is:** Each UG miner carries SCSR; cache of additional SCSRs throughout escape route to provide ≥1 hour of breathing during evacuation; monthly external inspection; periodic factory functional test.
- **Who performs it:** Each miner (carry); Safety (cache management); SCSR vendor (factory test).
- **Data captured:** SCSR serial #, manufacture date, expiration, location/cache, monthly inspection date/initials, factory test date.
- **Documents/forms:** SCSR inspection log; cache map; vendor service records.
- **Frequency:** Monthly inspection; per service-life schedule (typically 10-15 yr).
- **Hand-offs:** Safety → vendor (CSE, Drager, ELSA) → cache → miners.
- **State-specific:** State requirements parallel.
- **Pain points:** Inspection log gaps; expired units; replacement cost ($1K+ each).

### Communication & Tracking Systems (Post-MINER Act)
- **What it is:** Wireless two-way underground communication and electronic tracking of all underground personnel. Approved systems include leaky-feeder radios, mesh networks, RFID tracking.
- **Who performs it:** Communications technician; vendor (Strata, Innovative Wireless, Becker Mining).
- **Data captured:** System type, coverage map, personnel last-known location, system uptime.
- **Documents/forms:** Vendor maintenance log; coverage testing.
- **Frequency:** Continuous operation; periodic testing.
- **Hand-offs:** Comms tech → Safety → MSHA District during emergency.
- **State-specific:** State requires.
- **Pain points:** Coverage gaps in long entries; tracking handoffs across leases; node maintenance.

### Mine Rescue Team Coverage (§49)
- **What it is:** Each UG mine must arrange for two mine rescue teams within 1-hour ground travel time. Options: own team, neighboring operator team, contract service (Eastern Associated Mine Rescue, Mountaineer, Murray, etc.).
- **Who performs it:** Mine Safety Director; contracted team.
- **Data captured:** Team agreement, team roster, response time, equipment inventory, contract dates.
- **Documents/forms:** Mine rescue team agreement; roster filed with MSHA; equipment inventory.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; roster updates as members change.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety → contracted service → MSHA.
- **State-specific:** WV maintains state mine rescue program; KY active state program; VA reliant on commercial.
- **Pain points:** Contract pricing; verifying response times; member fitness.

### Mine Rescue Contest Participation
- **What it is:** Annual mine rescue contests (National Mine Rescue Contest, state contests) — teams compete on field problems and bench-test (apparatus); maintains skill currency.
- **Who performs it:** Team members + captain.
- **Data captured:** Contest, dates, problems, scores, team finish.
- **Documents/forms:** Contest entry; team scores.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Team → contest committee.
- **State-specific:** State-level contests in each.
- **Pain points:** Team time off; travel costs.

### Tabletop & Full-Scale Drills
- **What it is:** Required drills to test ERP — quarterly fire drills (some UG), annual full evacuation, tabletop emergencies, mine rescue team drills.
- **Who performs it:** Safety + Operations + contracted teams.
- **Data captured:** Drill type, date, scenario, participants, observations, corrective actions.
- **Documents/forms:** Drill report; corrective action tracker; ERP update.
- **Frequency:** Per ERP — quarterly to annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety → ERP update → MSHA.
- **State-specific:** State requires (WV particularly).
- **Pain points:** Production interruption; scenario realism.

---

## Incident Management

### Near-Miss Reporting
- **What it is:** Voluntary internal reporting of incidents that could have caused injury but did not; foundation of safety culture.
- **Who performs it:** Any miner; supervisor reviews.
- **Data captured:** Date, location, description, potential severity, contributing factors, corrective action.
- **Documents/forms:** Near-miss report form (internal); often integrated into safety mgmt system.
- **Frequency:** As they occur.
- **Hand-offs:** Reporter → supervisor → Safety → trending analysis.
- **State-specific:** Not regulated; internal program.
- **Pain points:** Underreporting; fear of blame; insufficient follow-through.

### First Aid / Recordable Injury / Lost-Time / Restricted Duty / Fatality
- **What it is:** Classification of injury severity drives reporting (Form 7000-1), workers comp, return-to-work, and KPIs.
- **Who performs it:** Safety + EMT + medical provider.
- **Data captured:** Injury class, treatment, work status (full duty / restricted / lost time / fatal), days lost, days restricted, RTW date.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 7000-1; OSHA 300 log (for non-MSHA areas like office/shop); workers comp first report (state-specific — WV-1, VA First Report of Injury, KY IA-1).
- **Frequency:** Per injury.
- **Hand-offs:** EMT → Safety → Workers Comp → HR → MSHA.
- **State-specific:** State workers comp forms differ.
- **Pain points:** Classification disputes (restricted vs lost time); RTW transitional duty programs; insurance interactions.

### Accident Investigation (Root Cause)
- **What it is:** Systematic investigation of any injury, near-miss, equipment damage, or §50.10 event; root cause analysis (5-Why, TapRooT, fishbone); corrective action.
- **Who performs it:** Safety Director + Operations + (for serious) MSHA + state agency.
- **Data captured:** Incident #, timeline, witnesses, photos, equipment data, contributing factors, root causes, corrective actions with owners/dates.
- **Documents/forms:** Internal investigation report; MSHA investigation report (for §50.10 events); state agency report.
- **Frequency:** Per event.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety → Operations → Engineering → corrective action tracker.
- **State-specific:** WV/VA/KY each have their own investigation processes for state-reportable events.
- **Pain points:** Multi-agency coordination; preserving scene; root cause discipline vs blame.

### Witness Statements
- **What it is:** Written statements from miners, supervisors, contractors who witnessed event; legal and investigative value.
- **Who performs it:** Safety + Legal; sometimes counsel-led.
- **Data captured:** Witness name, date, time, narrative, signature.
- **Documents/forms:** Statement template; recorded interviews.
- **Frequency:** Per investigation.
- **Hand-offs:** Witness → Safety → Legal → investigation file.
- **State-specific:** N/A.
- **Pain points:** Memory degradation; Garrity rights for supervisors; potential MSHA Special Investigation use.

### Accident Reconstruction
- **What it is:** Detailed reconstruction (often by third-party engineer or specialist) for serious accidents; physical evidence, sequence of events, contributing factors.
- **Who performs it:** Third-party engineer; MSHA Tech Support; state expert.
- **Data captured:** Scene measurements, equipment data, video, modeling.
- **Documents/forms:** Reconstruction report.
- **Frequency:** Per serious event.
- **Hand-offs:** Specialist → counsel → MSHA → public report.
- **State-specific:** State agencies do parallel.
- **Pain points:** Cost; scene preservation; discoverable in litigation.

### Reporting to MSHA / State / Insurance / Family
- **What it is:** Multi-stream notification — MSHA §50.10 within 15 min; state agency notification; workers comp carrier; family in fatality.
- **Who performs it:** Safety Director / Mine Manager / HR / Chaplain.
- **Data captured:** Notification recipient, time, person delivering.
- **Documents/forms:** Notification log; MSHA confirmation #; insurance claim #; family notification protocol.
- **Frequency:** Per event.
- **Hand-offs:** Across all parties.
- **State-specific:** State hotlines: WV 304-558-1425; VA 540-523-8208; KY 502-573-0140.
- **Pain points:** Family notification protocol; PR management; coordinating multiple notifications under stress.

---

## Occupational Health

### Black Lung Surveillance (NIOSH Coal Worker Health Surveillance Program)
- **What it is:** Free X-rays and spirometry offered to coal miners through NIOSH every 5 years; results in NIOSH B-reader review for pneumoconiosis classification (per ILO categories). Miners with 1/0 or higher classification can elect Part 90 transfer.
- **Who performs it:** NIOSH-approved facility; B-reader (radiologist); spirometry technician (NIOSH-certified).
- **Data captured:** Miner name, MSHA ID, exam date, X-ray result (ILO classification), spirometry result (FEV1, FVC), B-reader review.
- **Documents/forms:** NIOSH B-reader form; Part 90 transfer election letter.
- **Frequency:** Every 5 years (operator-funded mobile units common in WV/VA/KY).
- **Hand-offs:** Miner → NIOSH facility → MSHA (Part 90 eligibility) → operator (Part 90 transfer).
- **State-specific:** Federal; state occupational pneumoconiosis programs (WV particularly).
- **Pain points:** Participation rates; coordinating mobile units; Part 90 transfer assignments.

### Hearing Conservation (§62)
- **What it is:** Noise monitoring (dosimetry), audiograms (baseline + annual), hearing protectors, training; under 30 CFR Part 62 specifically for mining.
- **Who performs it:** Industrial Hygienist; CAOHC-certified audiometric technician.
- **Data captured:** Dosimetry results, miner audiograms, STS (standard threshold shift) status, hearing protector fit, training.
- **Documents/forms:** Audiogram records; dose results; STS log; OSHA-style 300 log for OSHA areas.
- **Frequency:** Annual audiograms; periodic dosimetry per occupation.
- **Hand-offs:** IH/Audio Tech → Safety → medical provider for STS evaluation.
- **State-specific:** Federal-driven.
- **Pain points:** STS confirmation; documentation across long careers; equipment-specific noise reduction tracking.

### Hand-Arm Vibration
- **What it is:** Assessment of hand-arm vibration exposure (rock drills, jacklegs, handheld equipment); medical surveillance for Raynaud's syndrome.
- **Who performs it:** Industrial Hygienist; occupational physician.
- **Data captured:** Tool inventory, vibration spectrum, exposure time, medical findings.
- **Documents/forms:** Vibration exposure log; medical surveillance records.
- **Frequency:** Periodic assessment.
- **Hand-offs:** IH → Safety → medical.
- **State-specific:** Limited regulatory.
- **Pain points:** Limited tools to mitigate; tracking individual exposure.

### Heat Stress Management (Haul Truck, Surface Crew)
- **What it is:** Heat stress program for outdoor crews (haul truck operators, surface workers) — hydration, work-rest cycles, monitoring of WBGT, heat illness response.
- **Who performs it:** Safety; supervisor; medical (heat illness).
- **Data captured:** Weather data, work-rest schedule, hydration provisions, heat illness incidents.
- **Documents/forms:** Heat stress plan; daily WBGT log; heat illness incident report.
- **Frequency:** During hot season; daily monitoring.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety → supervisor → field operations.
- **State-specific:** Not regulated specifically (yet — OSHA rule pending).
- **Pain points:** Cab heat in older trucks; sun exposure; tracking compliance.

### Bloodborne Pathogen Training (for EMTs and First Responders)
- **What it is:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 / state EMS bloodborne pathogen training for EMTs and designated first aid personnel.
- **Who performs it:** EMT trainer; Safety.
- **Data captured:** Trainee, date, topics, hepatitis B vaccine status.
- **Documents/forms:** Training cert; vaccine declination/acceptance.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Trainer → records.
- **State-specific:** State EMS rules.
- **Pain points:** Vaccine documentation; PPE inventory.

---

## Contractor Safety

### Pre-Qualification
- **What it is:** Vetting of contractors before on-site work — review of insurance, EMR, TRIR, OSHA/MSHA citation history, financial.
- **Who performs it:** Safety + Procurement + Legal.
- **Data captured:** Contractor name, MSHA contractor ID, NAICS, insurance certs (GL, WC, auto, umbrella), EMR last 3 yrs, TRIR last 3 yrs, citation history, contract scope.
- **Documents/forms:** Pre-qualification questionnaire (PICS, ISN, Avetta, internal); insurance COI; safety mgmt program review.
- **Frequency:** Initial; annual recert.
- **Hand-offs:** Procurement → Safety → approved vendor list.
- **State-specific:** State requires contractor registration in each.
- **Pain points:** Multiple pre-qual platforms (ISN, Avetta, Veriforce); insurance updates; small contractors lack documentation.

### Contractor Site-Specific Training & Sign-In
- **What it is:** Each contractor employee must complete site-specific hazard training (Part 46/48 hazard training); daily sign-in for accountability and exposure tracking.
- **Who performs it:** Safety + guard shack.
- **Data captured:** Contractor company, MSHA ID, employee name, training date, daily sign-in time.
- **Documents/forms:** Site-specific training log; daily sign-in sheet; visitor badge.
- **Frequency:** Per project; daily.
- **Hand-offs:** Guard → Safety → daily attendance.
- **State-specific:** State cards required for state-regulated tasks.
- **Pain points:** Volume of contractors during shutdowns; lost sign-in sheets; expired training cards.

### Contractor Incident Sharing
- **What it is:** Contractors must report their incidents to operator; operator must report contractor incidents under contractor ID on Form 7000-1; hours attributed to contractor ID for rate calculations.
- **Who performs it:** Contractor safety lead → mine Safety.
- **Data captured:** Contractor incident, MSHA contractor ID, hours.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 7000-1 (filed by contractor); contractor monthly safety report.
- **Frequency:** Per incident; monthly summary.
- **Hand-offs:** Contractor → mine → MSHA.
- **State-specific:** State reporting separately.
- **Pain points:** Verifying contractor compliance; concurrent jurisdiction on shared work.

---

## Workplace Safety (Non-MSHA / OSHA-Style)

### Job Safety Analyses (JSA / JHA)
- **What it is:** Pre-task written hazard analysis breaking job into steps, identifying hazards, controls.
- **Who performs it:** Supervisor + crew.
- **Data captured:** Task, steps, hazards, controls, PPE, sign-offs.
- **Documents/forms:** JSA template.
- **Frequency:** Per non-routine task.
- **Hand-offs:** Supervisor → crew → file.
- **State-specific:** Best practice.
- **Pain points:** Becoming pro-forma; not updated for conditions.

### Fall Protection (Non-MSHA areas: shop, office)
- **What it is:** OSHA 1910 fall protection at heights 4 ft+ (general industry); 6 ft (construction); harness/lanyard/anchorage.
- **Who performs it:** Worker + Safety; competent person.
- **Data captured:** Fall hazard areas, anchorage points, equipment inspection, training.
- **Documents/forms:** Fall protection plan; harness inspection log; training records.
- **Frequency:** Per task; daily inspection; annual training.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety → worker → records.
- **State-specific:** OSHA state plan in KY/VA differs slightly.
- **Pain points:** Defining MSHA vs OSHA jurisdiction at the line between mine area and shop/office.

### Confined Space Entries
- **What it is:** Entry into permit-required confined spaces (silos, tanks, bins) — atmospheric testing, ventilation, attendant, retrieval, rescue plan.
- **Who performs it:** Entry supervisor + attendant + entrants.
- **Data captured:** Permit #, space ID, hazards, atmospheric readings, entrants, duration.
- **Documents/forms:** Confined space entry permit; gas test log; rescue plan.
- **Frequency:** Per entry.
- **Hand-offs:** Supervisor → entrants → Safety.
- **State-specific:** OSHA jurisdiction at non-mine; MSHA §77.1900-1908 at mine.
- **Pain points:** Recognizing confined space; rescue capability; permit discipline.

### Hot Work Permits
- **What it is:** Permit for welding/cutting/grinding in non-routine locations — fire watch, fire suppression, atmospheric monitoring.
- **Who performs it:** Hot work coordinator + fire watch.
- **Data captured:** Permit #, location, work type, fire watch duration post-work, gas tests.
- **Documents/forms:** Hot work permit.
- **Frequency:** Per non-routine hot work.
- **Hand-offs:** Coordinator → workers → fire watch.
- **State-specific:** Best practice + insurance.
- **Pain points:** Underground hot work § 75.1106; methane checks; fire watch discipline.

### LOTO (Lockout/Tagout) Program
- **What it is:** Energy isolation program — locks, tags, verification before maintenance on equipment.
- **Who performs it:** Authorized employee.
- **Data captured:** Equipment, energy sources, lock #s, authorized employees, date.
- **Documents/forms:** LOTO procedures per equipment; lock log; training records.
- **Frequency:** Per maintenance task.
- **Hand-offs:** Authorized employee → operator → maintenance.
- **State-specific:** OSHA 1910.147 (general industry); MSHA §75.511 for UG electric.
- **Pain points:** Group lockouts; shift turnover; energy isolation verification.

### Crane & Rigging
- **What it is:** Crane operator certification (CCO or equivalent); rigging inspections; lift plans for critical lifts.
- **Who performs it:** Certified operator; rigger; lift director.
- **Data captured:** Crane inspections (daily/annual), operator cert, rigging inspection, load weights, lift plan.
- **Documents/forms:** Crane inspection log; lift plan; rigging inspection log.
- **Frequency:** Per use; annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Operator → rigger → director → Safety.
- **State-specific:** Cranes at mine fall under MSHA; non-mine under OSHA.
- **Pain points:** Operator turnover; rigging inventory.

### Ergonomic Assessments
- **What it is:** Workplace evaluation for musculoskeletal disorder risk — repetitive motion, lifting, posture (haul trucks, longwall, prep plant).
- **Who performs it:** Industrial Hygienist / Ergonomist; Safety.
- **Data captured:** Job analysis, hazard score, recommendations, implementations.
- **Documents/forms:** Ergonomic assessment report; corrective action.
- **Frequency:** Per request; periodic.
- **Hand-offs:** IH → operations → engineering.
- **State-specific:** Not regulated.
- **Pain points:** Equipment lifecycle; difficult-to-modify haul truck cabs.

---

## Key Data Points / KPIs

### TRIR (Total Recordable Injury Rate)
- **What it is:** (Recordable injuries × 200,000) / total hours worked. Compared to industry NAICS average.
- **Who performs it:** Safety; reported to MSHA quarterly via Form 7000-2 hours and 7000-1 injuries.
- **Data captured:** Recordables, hours, rate.
- **Frequency:** Monthly internal; quarterly external.
- **Pain points:** Hours allocation across mines; recordable classification.

### SR / Severity Rate (Lost-Time Days × 200,000) / Hours
- **What it is:** Severity metric for lost-time days.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.

### Fatality Rate
- **What it is:** Fatalities per 200,000 hours or per million hours; reported in MSHA Part 50 statistics.
- **Frequency:** Continuous (publicly reported).

### LTI Rate (Lost-Time Injury Rate)
- **What it is:** (Lost-time injuries × 200,000) / hours.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.

### Citation Rate / S&S Citation Rate
- **What it is:** Citations per 100 inspector-hours; S&S citations per 100 inspector-hours. Driver of POV screening.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly POV screen; monthly internal.

### Dollar Penalty (Proposed / Paid / Outstanding)
- **What it is:** Track of MSHA civil penalty assessments — proposed, contested, paid, outstanding.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.

### Days Since Last LTI / Days Since Last Fatality
- **What it is:** Visible safety culture metrics; posted at mine entrance.
- **Frequency:** Daily.

### Training Compliance %
- **What it is:** % of workforce current on annual refresher; % current on state retraining; % of contractors with valid training.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.

### Certification Expiration Calendar
- **What it is:** Forward-looking calendar of state cert expirations (foreman, electrician, EMT, blaster, MET) — typically 30/60/90 day alerts.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Pain points:** Multi-state, multi-cert per person, calendar maintenance.

---

## Cross-Cutting Pain Points (Summary for Product Scoping)

1. **Multi-jurisdiction overlap** — every event triggers federal MSHA + state agency (WV OMHST, VA DOE/Mines, KY OMSL) + state DEP (for impoundments) + workers comp + insurance + sometimes ATF (explosives). Single data entry must route to all.
2. **Time-sensitive clocks** — 15-min §50.10, 10-day Form 7000-1, 10-day informal conference, 30-day citation contest, 30-day Proposed Assessment payment, 12-month annual refresher, 5-yr VA renewal — all need automated alerts.
3. **Certification matrix complexity** — single miner may hold WV foreman + WV electrician + WV EMT-M + KY foreman + KY MET + federal SCSR trainer + Part 48 Blue Card with different expirations/retraining requirements.
4. **Examination book volume** — preshift, onshift, weekly, belt, electrical, fan, hoist, methane, permissibility, dust, impoundment — across multiple shifts and locations — paper or e-book.
5. **Citation litigation calendar** — many open cases concurrently across multiple ALJs.
6. **Contractor ID accountability** — every contractor work hour and incident must route to correct MSHA contractor ID for accident rate calc.
7. **Training records lost on hire/transfer** — miners arrive without prior 5000-3s; out-of-state experience not transferable.
8. **POV screening latency** — quarterly screening lags actual mine behavior; needs internal real-time POV-risk indicator.
9. **Multi-state inspector concurrency** — federal and state inspectors often on-site same week; double documentation burden.
10. **Form changes & PIB updates** — MSHA periodically updates forms, PIBs, and electronic-recordkeeping permissions; product must track.

---

# Domain 4: Equipment, Maintenance, Reliability & Procurement

# Equipment, Maintenance, Reliability & Procurement

Comprehensive domain inventory for Southern Coal Corporation operations across WV, VA, KY, AL, and TN. Covers surface and underground mining, prep plant, loadout, mobile maintenance, stationary plant, and all support equipment across the full asset lifecycle.

---

## 1. Asset Master / Equipment Inventory

### 1.1 Asset Register Creation & Master Data Setup
- **What it is:** Creating and maintaining a single source of truth for every piece of equipment owned, leased, or rented across all sites. Includes asset hierarchy (site → area → system → asset → component → sub-component), parent/child relationships, criticality classification, and replacement value.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer / maintenance planner / asset accountant / IT systems admin (CMMS administrator). Initial setup by capital project manager at commissioning.
- **Data captured:** Asset tag/number, OEM (CAT, Komatsu, Joy, Bucyrus/Caterpillar Global Mining, Hitachi, Liebherr, Fletcher, Sandvik), model (e.g., CAT 793F, Komatsu 930E-4, Joy 14CM27, Sandvik MB670-1, Bucyrus 49-R drill, Hitachi EX5600), serial number, year of manufacture, in-service date, location (mine/section), GPS coordinates for fixed assets, status (active/standby/idle/retired), criticality (A/B/C or 1-5), replacement value, original purchase cost, parent asset, manufacturer warranty expiry, MSHA approval numbers for permissible equipment.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM nameplate data, bill of sale, ISO 14224 (taxonomy/reliability data for petroleum/petrochemical/natural gas industries — widely adopted by mining for failure coding), ISO 55000 (asset management), MSHA approval plates (for UG permissible equipment per 30 CFR Part 18 / 19 / 20 / 22 / 23 / 27), commissioning checklists.
- **Frequency:** Initial at acquisition; updated whenever assets move, are rebuilt, scrapped, or change criticality. Continuous reconciliation against physical audit annually.
- **Hand-offs:** Procurement (PO data) → Receiving (commissioning) → Asset accounting (capitalization, depreciation start) → Maintenance (PM template assignment) → Operations (handed to operator). Fixed assets feed into general ledger (NetSuite, SAP, Sage, Viewpoint Vista, or Explorer Mine).
- **State-specific differences:** None for asset master itself, but MSHA ID number per mine drives asset location tagging. WV, VA, KY each have state mining boards that may require equipment lists for state permit applications and section/mine map filings.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Rebuilt components keep original serial but reset hours; idle/parked equipment falls off PM schedules; rental equipment co-mingled with owned; "ghost" assets (scrapped but still in CMMS); assets transferred between mines without tag updates; same physical asset has different IDs across CMMS, fixed asset ledger, fuel system, and telematics.

### 1.2 Asset Tagging & Identification
- **What it is:** Physical labeling of each asset with a durable tag (metal stamped, barcoded, RFID, or QR code) tied to the master record. Includes truck numbers painted on cab and unit numbers stenciled on equipment.
- **Who performs it:** Warehouse/asset clerk, mechanic at commissioning; reliability tech for re-tag.
- **Data captured:** Asset tag number, tag type (metal, barcode, RFID), tag location on asset, photo of tag, install date.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Internal numbering convention (e.g., "TRK-793-04" for truck 4 at a given pit; "CM-14CM-12" for continuous miner 12); barcode standards (Code 128, QR).
- **Frequency:** Once at commissioning; re-tag as needed after repaints or component swaps.
- **Hand-offs:** Tag → CMMS asset record; mobile devices scan to open work order.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Tags burn off in mine fires or are sandblasted during paint; rebuilt machines lose tags; multiple tags on same machine (owner, lender, MSHA approval plate, asset tag).

### 1.3 Surface Mobile Equipment Inventory
- **What it is:** Tracking every piece of surface mobile equipment by class and unit.
- **Who performs it:** Maintenance planner; operations superintendent confirms operational status.
- **Data captured:** Class (haul truck, dozer, loader, grader, water truck, fuel/lube truck, lowboy, articulated truck, scraper, drill, blade, pickup, mechanic truck, light plant), make/model (CAT 777F/G, 785C/D, 789C/D, 793F, 797F; Komatsu 830E-AC, 930E-4SE, HD785; CAT D8T/D9T/D10T/D11T; CAT 992K/993K wheel loader; Komatsu WA600/WA900; CAT 16M/24M motor grader; Bucyrus 49-R blasthole drill; Atlas Copco/Epiroc DM45/DM-M2/Pit Viper PV-235/PV-271; Sandvik DR412i; CAT MD6310/MD6420), hour meter, odometer, current operator assignment, last service hours, next PM due.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM operator manuals, OEM service manuals, lube charts, MSHA 30 CFR Part 77 (surface coal mine standards) for required equipment such as backup alarms, rollover protection (ROPS/FOPS), seatbelts.
- **Frequency:** Daily updates from telematics (CAT Product Link / VisionLink, Komatsu KOMTRAX, Modular Dispatch, Wenco, Hexagon Mining); hour meters synced hourly.
- **Hand-offs:** Telematics → CMMS → PM scheduler → Fuel system → Operations dispatch.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Hour meter rollover/replacement requires offset tracking; equipment moved between MSHA IDs requires re-registration of beacon/strobe inspections; pickup trucks rarely tracked in CMMS but accumulate big repair bills.

### 1.4 Underground Mobile Equipment Inventory (Permissible & Non-Permissible)
- **What it is:** Tracking UG production and support equipment, including MSHA-permissible classification and approval numbers.
- **Who performs it:** UG maintenance planner; outby maintenance foreman; MSHA approval tech.
