- **Data captured:** Equipment class (continuous miner, shuttle car, ram car, scoop, mantrip, jeep, supply car, roof bolter, feeder breaker, longwall shearer, AFC pan line, BSL, shields, stage loader, crusher), MSHA permissibility approval number (e.g., 2G-XXXX-X for continuous miners, 9C-XXXX for diesel power packages), make/model (Joy/Komatsu 14CM27, 14CM15, 14ED15, 12CM27; Sandvik MB670-1, MB710; Joy 10SC, 21SC shuttle cars; Stamler/Joy feeder breakers; Fletcher dual-head roof bolters DDR/HDDR; J.H. Fletcher RRII; Joy 4LS/5LS scoops; battery scoops; Damascus/MICO mantrips; Brookville mantrips), battery serial/cell config for battery equipment, diesel particulate filter (DPF) status for diesel UG units.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** MSHA approval certificates per 30 CFR Part 18 (electric equipment), Part 19 (permissible cap lamps), Part 20 (permissible motors), Part 22 (gas detectors), Part 23 (telephones), Part 27 (rebuilt equipment), Part 31 (diesel-powered equipment), Part 36 (mobile diesel for gassy mines), Part 75 (mandatory safety standards UG coal). Field modification approvals.
- **Frequency:** Daily updates; pre-shift permissibility exams per 30 CFR 75.512.
- **Hand-offs:** UG maintenance → mine examiner pre-shift book → CMMS → MSHA inspector during inspections.
- **State-specific differences:** WV state mine inspector additionally inspects per WV Code 22A; VA Department of Energy mine inspector per Title 45.2; KY Mine Safety and Licensing per KRS Chapter 351. Each may issue state-level violations on permissibility.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Permissibility-affecting modification done without MSHA field mod approval voids approval (citation 30 CFR 75.500); battery equipment with mixed-age cells fails capacity tests; DPF regeneration cycles not logged; serial numbers worn off MSHA plates.

### 1.5 Prep Plant Equipment Inventory
- **What it is:** All static and rotating equipment in the coal preparation plant from raw coal stockpile through clean coal stockpile and refuse disposal.
- **Who performs it:** Prep plant maintenance superintendent; plant reliability engineer.
- **Data captured:** Equipment list — raw coal feeders, rotary breaker (e.g., Pennsylvania Crusher), double-roll crusher, sizers (MMD), screen decks (sieve bends, deslime, drain & rinse, refuse, clean coal — primary OEMs Conn-Weld, Schenck Process, Derrick, Tabor, Polydeck), heavy media (HM) vessels / drum / bath (Daniels, McNally, Wemco), HM cyclones (Krebs, Multotec, Weir Cavex, Vorsyl), classifying cyclones, spirals (Multotec MX7/SC20, Mineral Technologies MG-series), flotation cells (Eriez column flotation, Outotec/Metso conventional cells), thickeners (WesTech, Outotec/Metso, EIMCO), filter presses (FLSmidth, Andritz, McLanahan), vacuum disc/drum filters, screen-bowl centrifuges (Decanter / Bird/Andritz, FLSmidth), basket centrifuges (CMI, Tema), magnetite recovery (LIMS — low intensity magnetic separators — Eriez/Multotec), demagnetizing coils, refuse conveyors, refuse pumps (Warman, GIW slurry pumps), sumps, slurry pumps, mainline conveyors, stacking conveyors, sample plant.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM P&IDs, equipment data sheets, ASME pressure vessel records for any pressurized vessels, ANSI conveyor standards (CEMA), OSHA 1910 general industry (some prep plants fall under OSHA where MSHA doesn't apply but mostly MSHA 30 CFR Part 77 Subpart F).
- **Frequency:** Continuous online status; PM schedules per OEM and reliability program.
- **Hand-offs:** Plant operator → maintenance work order; instrumentation → control system (PLCs: Allen-Bradley ControlLogix, Siemens; SCADA: Ignition, FactoryTalk, Wonderware/AVEVA System Platform).
- **State-specific differences:** State boiler/pressure vessel inspections (WV per WV Code 21-3D, VA per DPOR Boiler Safety, KY through Department of Housing). Air emission permits for thermal dryers (if any) trigger equipment-specific monitoring (rare in modern plants).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Old plants have mixed-vintage equipment with poor drawings; HM density and magnetite consumption tied to vessel/cyclone wear; spiral starts wear out and become impossible to source; vacuum filter cloths change frequency drives clean coal moisture; refurbished centrifuge baskets often have unknown rebuild histories.

### 1.6 Loadout & Stockpile Equipment Inventory
- **What it is:** Equipment from clean coal silo/stockpile through batch weigh and onto rail/barge/truck.
- **Who performs it:** Loadout supervisor / loadout maintenance.
- **Data captured:** Silo capacity (typically 1,500–10,000+ tons clean coal silo), batch weigh hopper capacity and weighbridge model (Thurman, Cardinal, Mettler-Toledo, Rice Lake), train loadout type (silo flood, batch, gravity), flop gates, telescoping chutes, stacker conveyors (radial, swing), reclaim feeders, dust suppression sprays, sampling system make (Heath & Sherwood, Metso, McLanahan, JBLCo sampling), railcar identification system (AEI tag readers), barge loadout extending booms.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** NTEP Certificate of Conformance for any commercial weighing devices; ASTM D2234 / D7430 for mechanical sampling; ASTM D6883 for stockpile sampling; railroad customer load specs (Norfolk Southern, CSX); barge loading plans for stability.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; tied to loadout schedule.
- **Hand-offs:** Loadout → Sales/contracts (tons by buyer), → Rail/barge logistics, → Lab (sample), → Royalty (tons by lease).
- **State-specific differences:** State Weights & Measures: WV Division of Labor, VA Office of Weights & Measures (VDACS), KY Department of Agriculture, AL Weights and Measures, TN Weights and Measures — each annually certifies the truck scale and batch weigh.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Batch weigh calibration drift; sampler cutter wear changes sample mass; train pull-throughs at incorrect speed; AEI tag misreads; flop gate hydraulic leaks; dust suppression frozen lines in winter.

### 1.7 Conveyor System Inventory
- **What it is:** Master list of every belt, conveyor structure, drive head, takeup, idler section, splice, and pulley by name.
- **Who performs it:** Belt mechanic / conveyor maintenance crew; belt foreman.
- **Data captured:** Belt name/number, length, width (typically 36"–72" UG, 60"–84" surface), belt rating (e.g., 600 PIW, 800 PIW, ST1000, ST1600 steel cord), belt manufacturer (Continental ContiTech, Fenner Dunlop, Bridgestone, Goodyear EPG/Veyance), splice type (vulcanized, mechanical Flexco/MLT/MS), splice locations, drive horsepower, drive type (CST, fluid coupling, variable frequency), takeup type (gravity, winch, hydraulic), idler counts (carry/return), troughing angle, head pulley diameter, scraper type (Martin, Flexco, ASGCO), belt scale present (Y/N — Thermo Ramsey, Schenck, Siemens Milltronics).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** CEMA conveyor standards, belt manufacturer data sheets, 30 CFR 75.1731 (UG belt maintenance), 30 CFR 75.1108 (flame-resistant belt), MSHA-approved belt certification numbers, ASTM D378 (belt rubber).
- **Frequency:** Continuous; physical belt walks per shift, weekly comprehensive.
- **Hand-offs:** Belt examiner → mine examiner book → CMMS work orders → belt splicing crew.
- **State-specific differences:** Flame-resistance requirements stricter for UG. State mine inspector also checks belt CO monitors per state regs paralleling 30 CFR 75.1103.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Belt slip / mistracking from worn idlers; splice failure root cause unclear (mechanical vs vulcanized vintage); belt rip detection systems false-trip; CO monitor calibration overdue; belt structure deformation hidden under coal spillage; conveyor belt fire risk (the 2006 Aracoma/Sago era reforms led to atmospheric monitoring systems — AMS — under 30 CFR 75.351).

### 1.8 Pumping Equipment Inventory
- **What it is:** Dewatering, slurry, sump, refuse, water supply, and potable water pumps.
- **Who performs it:** Mine electrician / pump mechanic.
- **Data captured:** Pump make/model (Flygt, Sulzer, KSB, Goulds/ITT, Tsurumi for sub pumps; Warman/Weir for slurry; GIW; Cornell; Gorman-Rupp), motor HP, voltage, impeller diameter, head/flow curve, location, discharge piping size, control panel.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM curves, NEMA motor standards, MSHA approval for any UG pumps in return air, hydrostatic test records for high-pressure mine pumps.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; pump house inspections per shift; submersible pump checks weekly.
- **Hand-offs:** Pump runner → maintenance → environmental (discharge to NPDES outfalls — see Environmental domain).
- **State-specific differences:** NPDES discharges from pump operations tracked per WV/VA/KY/AL/TN permits.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Submersible cable splice failures; impeller wear from high-solids slurry; pump runs dry; cavitation; check valves stuck; pump house power loss during storms (auto-start generators).

### 1.9 Crushing & Sizing Equipment Inventory
- **What it is:** Rotary breakers, roll crushers, sizers, and feeder breakers at face/outby/plant.
- **Who performs it:** Plant millwright; UG outby mechanic.
- **Data captured:** Make/model (Pennsylvania/Terex rotary breaker; McLanahan double-roll; MMD sizer; Stamler/Joy feeder breaker), tooth/picks count, segment wear measurements, throughput rating, motor HP, drive type (gearbox, hydraulic).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM rebuild manuals, pick supplier specs (Kennametal, Sandvik), MSHA approval for UG feeder breakers.
- **Frequency:** Pick changes weekly to monthly; segment changes quarterly to annually; major rebuild 5-10 years.
- **Hand-offs:** Crusher inspection → pick orders → outage planning.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Tramp metal damage; bearing temperature alarms; gearbox oil leaks; picks dulled by sandstone/rock partings.

### 1.10 Stationary Plant & Electrical Infrastructure
- **What it is:** All electrical, compressed air, generation, and substation equipment.
- **Who performs it:** Mine electrician (state licensed in WV/VA/KY/AL/TN); plant electrician; high-voltage tech.
- **Data captured:** Substations (incoming voltage 46kV/69kV/138kV from local utility — Appalachian Power/AEP, Kentucky Power, Dominion, TVA, Alabama Power), transformer kVA/winding configuration, switchgear (medium-voltage 5kV/15kV, low-voltage 480V MCCs — Allen-Bradley CENTERLINE, Eaton, Square D), VFDs (Allen-Bradley PowerFlex, ABB ACS, Yaskawa), motor list with kW ratings, ground monitors, ground checks (UG mandatory), air compressors (Atlas Copco, Ingersoll Rand, Sullair, Gardner Denver), receiver tanks, generators (CAT, Cummins, Kohler), fuel-day tanks, transfer switches, light plants.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** NEC (NFPA 70), MSHA 30 CFR 77 Subpart K (surface electrical), 30 CFR 75 Subpart F-J (UG electrical), arc flash labeling per NFPA 70E, NETA acceptance/maintenance testing standards, transformer oil tests (per ASTM D3613, D1816, D971).
- **Frequency:** Monthly electrical exams per 30 CFR 75.512 (UG) and 77.502 (surface); annual NETA testing on critical gear; oil sampling annually on transformers.
- **Hand-offs:** Electrician → mine examiner book → engineering for upgrades → utility coordination.
- **State-specific differences:** State electrician certifications: WV Mine Electrician card (issued by WV OMHST), VA mine electrician card (VA DOLP), KY mine electrician (KY OMSL). State mine inspector dual-certifies on electrical exams.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Trailing cable splice failures on UG equipment; ground-fault tripping on rainy days; substation lightning damage; PCB-containing legacy transformers requiring disposal; CT/PT calibration drift; arc flash incident energy recalcs after upgrades.

### 1.11 Ventilation Equipment Inventory
- **What it is:** Mine fans (main and booster), regulators, stoppings, line brattice, ventilation tubing, and atmospheric monitoring system (AMS) sensors.
- **Who performs it:** Mine ventilation engineer; outby maintenance; mine examiner.
- **Data captured:** Main fan make/model (Joy, Aerovent, Robinson, Spendrup), HP, RPM, fan curve, current operating point (CFM, water gauge), location, fan housing type (centrifugal, axial), AMS sensor locations (CO, CH4, smoke), regulator locations and settings, stopping construction (block, alternative material).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Approved ventilation plan per 30 CFR 75.370, fan certification per 30 CFR 75.310, weekly fan exams per 30 CFR 75.312.
- **Frequency:** Continuous monitoring; weekly fan inspection; quarterly fan tests; sensor calibration per manufacturer (usually quarterly).
- **Hand-offs:** Vent engineer → MSHA approval for plan changes → mine examiner pre-shift → CMMS for fan PMs.
- **State-specific differences:** State approval also required (WV ventilation plan to OMHST, VA to DMM, KY to OMSL). Booster fan use heavily restricted by state too.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Fan stopped = mine evacuation; calibration gas cylinder expiry; sensor coal-dust occlusion; tubing torn down by mantrips.

### 1.12 Shop, Warehouse & Office Equipment
- **What it is:** Buildings, cranes/hoists, welding equipment, vehicle lifts, tire handlers, light vehicles, copiers, computers, and office IT.
- **Who performs it:** Shop foreman; warehouse manager; IT.
- **Data captured:** Overhead crane capacity, last inspection date, jib cranes, gantry cranes, vehicle lifts (Stertil-Koni mobile column lifts for haul trucks), tire handlers (Stellar, IMT), welders (Miller, Lincoln, ESAB), plasma cutters, computers/laptops, printers.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OSHA 1910.179 (overhead cranes) — annual inspections; ASME B30.2 cranes; MSHA 30 CFR 77.205 work platforms.
- **Frequency:** Annual crane/hoist inspection; daily pre-use checks.
- **Hand-offs:** Inspections → corrective work orders → load test certifications.
- **State-specific differences:** None federal/state for crane inspection (federal OSHA/MSHA); IT inventory may tie to state-issued mobile devices.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Crane bridge wheel wear; hoist limit switch failures; missing inspection tags; rented vs owned welders mixed up.

## 2. Asset Lifecycle Management

### 2.1 Capital Need Identification & Replacement Forecasting
- **What it is:** Predicting when assets will need replacement, rebuild, or supplementing — based on hours, condition, production growth, or new mine plan.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer; mine engineering; equipment superintendent; CFO/controller for budget.
- **Data captured:** Asset hours, condition assessment, projected hours per year, expected useful life, replacement cost estimate, residual/salvage value, justification narrative.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Equipment replacement plan, life cycle cost model.
- **Frequency:** Annual capex planning cycle; rolling 3-5-year forecast updated quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** Replacement plan → AFE/CAR process → procurement.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Hours-driven replacement misses condition reality; spot market price spikes blow budgets; long lead-times (haul trucks 12-18+ months from order); used equipment dramatically cheaper but unknown history.

### 2.2 Capital Appropriation Request (AFE / CAR) Workflow
- **What it is:** Formal request for capital authorization — Authorization for Expenditure (AFE) or Capital Appropriation Request (CAR) — including business case, alternatives analysis, ROI/payback, and approvals.
- **Who performs it:** Originator (engineer/superintendent) → reviewer (operations manager) → controller → CFO → CEO/board (per dollar threshold).
- **Data captured:** AFE number, project description, total estimated cost, contingency, expected in-service date, NPV/IRR/payback, capex vs opex classification, alternatives evaluated, risk assessment, environmental review.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Company AFE form; FASB ASC 360 (PP&E) for capitalization; IRS MACRS class lives (mining equipment class 10.0 / 13.2 / 13.3); SEC disclosure if material.
- **Frequency:** As needed; cyclical in annual budget; emergency AFEs for failures.
- **Hand-offs:** AFE approved → procurement begins → accounting opens project code → engineering executes → fixed asset accounting capitalizes upon commissioning.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Scope creep blows AFE budget; AFE approved but project delayed eats contingency; capital vs expense disputes (rebuild vs replacement); multi-mine AFEs hard to allocate.

### 2.3 Equipment Specification & RFQ
- **What it is:** Writing technical specifications, sending Request for Quotation to OEMs/dealers, evaluating bids on technical and commercial terms.
- **Who performs it:** Maintenance engineer / mine engineer drafts spec; procurement runs RFQ; cross-functional bid review team.
- **Data captured:** Spec sheet, RFQ document, vendor responses (price, lead time, warranty, payment terms), commercial evaluation matrix, technical evaluation matrix, total cost of ownership analysis.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** RFQ template, vendor proposal templates, OEM spec sheets, MSHA approval requirements for UG.
- **Frequency:** Per capital project.
- **Hand-offs:** Spec → vendor → bid → award → PO.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Sole-source vs competitive; "or equal" disputes; freight INCOTERMS confusion (FOB origin vs destination); used equipment auctions (Ritchie Bros, IronPlanet) bypass formal RFQ.

### 2.4 Purchase Order Execution
- **What it is:** Issuing the PO to the awarded vendor, including terms, milestones, progress payments.
- **Who performs it:** Buyer / purchasing manager; legal review for large POs.
- **Data captured:** PO number, vendor, line items, prices, delivery date, terms (Net 30/45/60), freight terms, warranty, milestone payment schedule, change orders.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** PO terms & conditions; UCC for goods; OEM warranty terms.
- **Frequency:** Per acquisition.
- **Hand-offs:** Buyer → vendor → receiving when delivered.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Change orders not approved; progress payments without milestones met; lien rights on partial deliveries.

### 2.5 Receipt, Commissioning & Acceptance Testing
- **What it is:** Physical receipt of equipment, pre-operational checks, factory rep startup, performance testing, and formal acceptance.
- **Who performs it:** Maintenance superintendent; OEM factory rep; operations rep; safety; commissioning engineer.
- **Data captured:** Receiving report, inspection findings, punch list, performance test results, acceptance certificate, in-service date, training records, manuals delivered (paper/digital).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Commissioning plan, OEM acceptance test procedures, MSHA approval verification for UG, lockout/tagout plan for energization.
- **Frequency:** Per new asset.
- **Hand-offs:** Commissioning → asset accounting (start depreciation) → maintenance (load PM templates) → operations (operator training complete).
- **State-specific differences:** State mine inspector may inspect new permissible equipment before first use.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Equipment damaged in transit (insurance claims, OS&D reports); incomplete punch list released to production; manuals missing; OEM tech not available on commissioning day; warranty start date dispute.

### 2.6 In-Service Date & Capitalization Trigger
- **What it is:** Formal entry into service triggering depreciation, warranty start, insurance addition, and maintenance schedule activation.
- **Who performs it:** Fixed asset accountant; reliability engineer; risk manager.
- **Data captured:** In-service date, capitalized cost, depreciation method (typically MACRS), useful life, salvage value, insurance schedule update, warranty registration confirmation.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** FASB ASC 360; company capitalization policy threshold (commonly $5,000 minimum); insurance certificate.
- **Frequency:** Per asset commissioning.
- **Hand-offs:** Capital project → fixed asset register → general ledger → tax → insurance schedule.
- **State-specific differences:** State tangible personal property tax (e.g., WV personal property tax on mining equipment — counties assess; KY tangible personal property; VA business personal property assessed by locality; TN tangible personal property tax; AL business personal property assessed by counties).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Delayed capitalization while equipment idle pending commissioning; partial in-service for staged commissioning; capitalize-vs-expense judgment on installation costs.

### 2.7 Mid-Life Rebuild / Overhaul Scheduling
- **What it is:** Planning major component overhauls (engine in-frame, transmission rebuild, dragline gantry rebuild, longwall move, prep plant turnaround).
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer; planner; maintenance superintendent; OEM service for major rebuilds.
- **Data captured:** Component hours, condition data (oil samples, wear measurements), overhaul scope, estimated downtime, parts list, labor estimate, internal vs external (CAT Reman, Komatsu Reman, OEM dealer, third-party rebuilder), cost estimate, schedule.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM TBO (time between overhauls), CAT Component Mileage Targets, Komatsu Reman & Rebuild Service guides, Joy Global service bulletins.
- **Frequency:** Per OEM hours (e.g., CAT 793 engine in-frame ~18,000-22,000 hrs; transmission ~20,000-25,000 hrs).
- **Hand-offs:** Reliability → planner → outage schedule → procurement (long-lead parts) → execution crew → operations release.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Multiple component overhauls misaligned causes excessive downtime; rebuild creep adds scope; OEM Reman exchange short-supply forcing in-house rebuild; warranty disputes on rebuilt parts.

### 2.8 Equipment Transfer Between Sites
- **What it is:** Relocating equipment between mines/divisions/states, including transport, re-permitting, and asset record updates.
- **Who performs it:** Equipment manager; lowboy/heavy haul crew; permits coordinator; fixed asset accountant.
- **Data captured:** Source/destination location, transport date, hauler, escort permits, transferred asset cost basis, depreciation continuation, MSHA ID change (causes asset ID re-registration), state permit list updates.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** State DOT overweight/oversize permits (WV DOH, VA DMV, KY Transportation Cabinet, AL DOT, TN DOT); bill of lading.
- **Frequency:** As needed.
- **Hand-offs:** Originating site → transport → receiving site → asset records → permits.
- **State-specific differences:** Each state's oversize/overweight permit rules differ (lead-cars, weekend travel restrictions, bridge formula).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Disassembly required for road transport; equipment "lost in transit" not in either CMMS; MSHA ID confusion; insurance certificate gap.

### 2.9 Disposal / Scrap / Trade-In / Auction
- **What it is:** Ending the asset's life — selling, scrapping, trading in, parting out.
- **Who performs it:** Equipment manager; fixed asset accountant; environmental (for fluids drain).
- **Data captured:** Disposal date, method (auction — Ritchie Bros, IronPlanet, Yoder & Frey; trade-in; scrap; sale to other operator; part-out), proceeds, NBV, gain/loss, environmental clearance (oils/fuels drained, lead-acid batteries removed), title transfer (for licensed vehicles).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Disposal authorization form; bill of sale; auction listing; ASTM hazardous waste characterization for any fluid disposal; state DEP/DEQ paperwork for transformer/PCB; for vehicles state DMV title transfer.
- **Frequency:** Annual review of idle/obsolete; ad hoc.
- **Hand-offs:** Equipment manager → environmental → fixed asset → tax → property tax (delist).
- **State-specific differences:** State scrap metal sale reporting (some require recipient ID for theft prevention); DMV title transfers per state; hazmat transport for batteries/fluids per DOT.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Equipment scrapped in place at mine (still on books); "core" returned to OEM not properly credited; lost titles for old yellow iron; PCB transformer disposal costs exceed scrap value.

### 2.10 Salvage Value & Net Book Value Tracking
- **What it is:** Ongoing tracking of net book value, market value (per industry guides, recent auctions), and salvage value estimates for insurance, capital decisions, lender reporting.
- **Who performs it:** Fixed asset accountant; treasury (for collateral reporting); equipment manager (market estimates).
- **Data captured:** Original cost, accumulated depreciation, NBV, fair market value (FMV) estimate, source of FMV, lender reporting basis.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** FASB ASC 360 impairment testing; lender collateral schedules; insurance schedules.
- **Frequency:** Monthly NBV roll; quarterly FMV; annual impairment review.
- **Hand-offs:** Fixed asset → controller → treasury/lender → insurance.
- **State-specific differences:** Property tax assessors may use their own depreciation tables differing from book — appeal process per state/county.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Impairment trigger if mine idles; lender wants current FMV; insurance schedule lags acquisitions; coal market downturn craters FMV.

---

## 3. Maintenance Strategy & Work Management

### 3.1 Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) Program
- **What it is:** Systematic process to determine the right maintenance for each asset using failure modes & effects (FMEA), criticality, and economics.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer; cross-functional team (maintenance, operations, safety).
- **Data captured:** Asset criticality, failure modes, failure consequences (S/E/O), recommended maintenance task (PM, PdM, RTF), task interval, justification.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** SAE JA1011/JA1012 (RCM standard), ISO 14224 (taxonomy for failure data).
- **Frequency:** Initial RCM at commissioning; refresh every 3-5 years or after failures.
- **Hand-offs:** RCM output → PM templates in CMMS → planner → tradespeople.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** RCM done by consultant then ignored; PM templates not updated; criticality drift.

### 3.2 Preventive Maintenance (PM) Schedules
- **What it is:** Time-based, hours-based, or cycle-based recurring tasks (lube, filters, inspections).
- **Who performs it:** Maintenance planner builds; scheduler dispatches; mechanic executes.
- **Data captured:** PM template, frequency (e.g., 250/500/1000/2000/4000 hrs for CAT haul trucks; 100/250/500 hrs for dozers; daily/weekly/monthly for plant), tasks (lube points, filter changes, torque checks, inspection items), parts list, labor estimate, last performed, next due, compliance %.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM PM schedules (CAT Service Information System SIS, Komatsu CSS, Joy MineCare), MSHA pre-shift exam checklists (30 CFR 75.1914 UG diesel, 30 CFR 77.404 surface machinery).
- **Frequency:** Per asset class; continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** PM due → scheduler → crew → execution → closeout.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** PM compliance % politically managed; hour meter drift (telematics vs manual log); PM done but tasks skipped (signed-off without execution).

### 3.3 Predictive Maintenance (PdM) Program
- **What it is:** Condition-based maintenance using monitoring technologies to predict failure before it occurs.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability tech / PdM specialist; outside labs.
- **Data captured:** See specific dimensions below (oil, vibration, thermography, MCSA, ultrasonic).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ISO 17359 (condition monitoring general), ISO 18436 (vibration analyst cert), ASTM oil testing.
- **Frequency:** Sample frequencies per program.
- **Hand-offs:** PdM finding → reliability engineer review → corrective work order.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** "Sampled but never reviewed" lab reports; vibration data without baseline; thermal images filed but not analyzed.

### 3.4 Corrective Maintenance (CM) Work Orders
- **What it is:** Non-urgent work to repair a discovered defect — planned, scheduled, and executed.
- **Who performs it:** Originator (operator/inspector); planner; scheduler; mechanic/electrician.
- **Data captured:** Defect description, asset, priority, found-by, photos, parts/labor planned, parts/labor actual, root cause, failure code.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Work order template; ISO 14224 failure codes; LOTO procedure for energy isolation (per 30 CFR 75.511 UG / 77.501 surface — "no man shall perform electrical work on any equipment unless the disconnecting device has been locked out").
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Originator → planner → scheduler → crew → QA/QC → closeout.
- **State-specific differences:** State mine inspector LOTO regs largely parallel federal.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** "Quick fix" never followed by proper repair; LOTO not applied; parts unavailable so WO sits; same defect reopened repeatedly.

### 3.5 Emergency / Breakdown Maintenance
- **What it is:** Unplanned, reactive response to a sudden failure — maximum disruption.
- **Who performs it:** On-shift mechanic / electrician; maintenance foreman; call-in crew if after hours.
- **Data captured:** Breakdown time, response time, repair time, root cause, parts used, lost production estimate, callout hours (overtime).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Emergency work order; downtime coding standard.
- **Frequency:** Goal to minimize; track trend.
- **Hand-offs:** Operator radio → maintenance dispatch → field repair → operations release.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Diagnosis time exceeds repair time; same machine repeat-breaks; parts not in stock; running with known defects until fail.

### 3.6 Project Work & Capital Improvements
- **What it is:** Discrete projects to install new equipment, upgrade existing, or improve reliability — distinct from routine maintenance.
- **Who performs it:** Project engineer; in-house project crew; contracted construction (electricians, millwrights, riggers).
- **Data captured:** Project number/WBS, scope, budget, schedule, change orders, labor by trade, materials, contractor costs, capitalize-vs-expense allocation.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Project charter; AFE; engineering drawings; commissioning plan; contractor safety qualification (ISNetworld, Avetta).
- **Frequency:** Per project.
- **Hand-offs:** AFE → engineering → procurement → construction → commissioning → ops handover.
- **State-specific differences:** Contractor licensing per state (WV WV-1 / general contractor licenses; VA Class A/B/C; KY contractor licensing; AL Home Builders Licensure; TN contractor license over $25K).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Capex vs opex disputes (e.g., replacing the same conveyor belt — repair or capital improvement?); scope creep; commissioning delays.

### 3.7 Shutdown / Turnaround Planning (Prep Plant)
- **What it is:** Planned multi-day outage to perform major maintenance on plant — typically annually or semi-annually.
- **Who performs it:** Plant manager; reliability engineer; turnaround coordinator; contracted labor.
- **Data captured:** Turnaround date, duration, scope (job list), labor plan, contractor lineup, critical path schedule, daily progress, cost actuals vs budget.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Turnaround plan; critical path (MS Project / Primavera P6); job safety analyses (JSAs); contractor LOTO permits.
- **Frequency:** Annual / semi-annual (typically a 3-7 day plant outage).
- **Hand-offs:** Planning → procurement (long-lead) → site prep → execution → restart → post-turnaround review.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Scope explosion ("while we have it down..."); critical path slip; contractor no-show; restart failure means tons of slip; weather delays for outdoor work.

### 3.8 Maintenance Backlog Management
- **What it is:** All identified work not yet completed — categorized by priority, age, ready-to-schedule, waiting for parts.
- **Who performs it:** Planner; maintenance manager; weekly backlog review meeting.
- **Data captured:** Open work order count by priority, by status (planned, scheduled, waiting parts, waiting access), backlog hours by trade, aging buckets (0-30, 31-90, 91+).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Backlog report; ready-backlog metric (typically 2-4 weeks of crew hours).
- **Frequency:** Weekly review; daily for ready-backlog.
- **Hand-offs:** Backlog → weekly schedule meeting → assigned to crew.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Phantom backlog (work already done, never closed); zombie WOs (parts ordered, never received); growing backlog hidden by closing old non-essential items.

### 3.9 Equipment Inspection Programs (Pre-Shift, Daily, Weekly)
- **What it is:** Mandatory examinations of equipment before use — operator pre-op checks, weekly mechanical exams, monthly electrical exams.
- **Who performs it:** Equipment operator (pre-op); certified mine examiner (pre-shift mine exam); maintenance for weekly/monthly.
- **Data captured:** Inspection date/time, examiner ID, defects found, defects corrected, defects deferred, signature.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Pre-op inspection form (per OEM and MSHA), 30 CFR 75.1914 (UG diesel pre-shift), 30 CFR 75.512 (electrical exam weekly), 30 CFR 77.404 (surface machinery pre-shift), 30 CFR 75.360 (pre-shift mine exam), state-specific examination books (WV "Track Boss / Mine Foreman" exam books, KY pre-shift book).
- **Frequency:** Per shift; weekly; monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Inspection → defects to maintenance WO → mine examiner book retained for MSHA inspector review.
- **State-specific differences:** State examination books required to be available for state inspector — WV per WV Code 22A-2; VA per Title 45.2; KY per KRS 351.180.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** "Pencil whip" inspections; defects not transferred to CMMS; books water-damaged at face; electronic vs paper books debate (some states still require paper).

---

## 4. Work Order Lifecycle (Granular)

### 4.1 Work Identification & Notification
- **What it is:** Capturing maintenance needs from any source — operator radio, inspection finding, alarm, audit, planner-initiated.
- **Who performs it:** Anyone; logged into CMMS by dispatcher or originator.
- **Data captured:** Originator, date/time, asset, defect description, perceived priority, location, source (operator/inspection/alarm), photo/video, immediate hazard Y/N.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Notification template; defect tag (red/yellow); operator daily check sheet.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Notification → triage by maintenance foreman.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Verbal-only reports; duplicate notifications for same defect; defect found by inspector but not communicated; over-notification ("noise") drowning critical items.

### 4.2 Triage & Prioritization
- **What it is:** Assessing each notification for criticality, safety risk, production risk, and assigning priority.
- **Who performs it:** Maintenance foreman / planner / supervisor; safety for hazardous defects.
- **Data captured:** Priority (P1 emergency, P2 urgent within 24h, P3 within 7 days, P4 next outage, P5 deferred), criticality justification, target completion date, work order created.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Priority matrix; risk-based work selection criteria.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Triage → planner if scheduled; → immediate execution if emergency.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Priority inflation by operations ("everything is P1"); priority not re-evaluated as conditions change; defects parked at P4 indefinitely.

### 4.3 Work Order Planning
- **What it is:** Detailing the work — labor needed (trades and hours), parts and materials, tools, permits (confined space, hot work, electrical), LOTO, JSA, downtime estimate, scaffolding/rigging.
- **Who performs it:** Maintenance planner.
- **Data captured:** Task list with sequence, labor by trade and hours, parts list with stock checks, tools/equipment, special permits, JSA, isolation plan, drawing references, photos, predecessors/successors.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Planned WO package; JSA per MSHA Part 46/48 training; hot work permit; confined space entry permit; LOTO procedure per 30 CFR 75.511 / 77.501.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; ideally 2-4 weeks lead time before scheduling.
- **Hand-offs:** Planner → procurement (for non-stock parts) → scheduler.
- **State-specific differences:** State confined space and hot work paralleling OSHA 1910.146 / 1910.252.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Plans missing critical step; parts in stock-out at execution; permits expired; planner ratio insufficient (industry rule of thumb 1 planner per 15-20 craftspeople); poor planning = wrenching time below 30%.

### 4.4 Work Order Scheduling
- **What it is:** Assigning work to specific crews/days based on labor availability, asset availability, parts on hand, weather, production windows.
- **Who performs it:** Maintenance scheduler.
- **Data captured:** Weekly schedule with WOs assigned to days/crews; daily schedule with assigned individuals; compliance % (work scheduled vs work completed).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Weekly schedule meeting; daily schedule meeting; schedule compliance KPI.
- **Frequency:** Weekly schedule; daily refinement.
- **Hand-offs:** Schedule → crew supervisor → execution.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Schedule blown by emergencies; equipment not made available by operations; crew called off to other work; weather (especially storms causing power loss).

### 4.5 Work Execution & Time/Material Capture
- **What it is:** Mechanic/electrician performing the work, recording labor hours, parts consumed, tools used, downtime, deviations.
- **Who performs it:** Mechanic, electrician, welder, fitter, helper; supervised by foreman.
- **Data captured:** Hours by individual (regular, OT, double-time), parts issued (from warehouse or floor stock), additional parts consumed, downtime start/end with codes (mechanical / electrical / waiting parts / operational / scheduled), as-found / as-left photos, deviations from plan.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Time card; pick ticket; downtime log; as-built drawings if modified.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Execution → operations (equipment release) → planner (cost rollup).
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Labor recorded against wrong WO; parts pulled from floor stock not booked; downtime coded "operational" by maintenance and "mechanical" by operations (constant dispute); double-charging (LOTO permit holder time charged twice).

### 4.6 Quality Verification & Equipment Release
- **What it is:** Confirming the repair is complete and correct before returning equipment to service.
- **Who performs it:** Maintenance foreman; operations spot-check; for safety-critical work, second-person verification.
- **Data captured:** Test run results, operator acceptance, post-repair inspection.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Equipment release form; commissioning steps for major work.
- **Frequency:** Per WO.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance → operations → CMMS WO status to "ready to close."
- **State-specific differences:** Permissibility checks before UG equipment release.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** "It worked when we left" then fails on first shift; release without operator notified; permissibility check skipped.

### 4.7 Work Order Closeout
- **What it is:** Final documentation — work performed narrative, root cause, failure mode, failure code, total hours, total cost.
- **Who performs it:** Mechanic/foreman; planner reviews for completeness.
- **Data captured:** Work performed narrative, failure code (per ISO 14224), root cause if known, cost roll-up (labor + parts + contractor + overhead), downtime totals, photos.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ISO 14224 codes; failure mode taxonomy; company root cause analysis (RCA) for high-impact failures.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Closed WO → reliability for trend analysis → finance for cost allocation.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Narrative is "done" with no detail; failure code defaulted to "other"; no RCA on repeat failures; closed WOs missing cost data.

### 4.8 Failure Coding & RCM Data Capture
- **What it is:** Assigning standardized codes to failure events to enable trending, MTBF/MTTR calculation, and continuous improvement.
- **Who performs it:** Mechanic or planner; reliability engineer audits.
- **Data captured:** Failure mode (e.g., per ISO 14224 — wear, fatigue, corrosion, leakage, vibration, electrical short), failure mechanism, affected component, root cause category (design, manufacture, installation, operation, maintenance, environment), severity, detection method.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ISO 14224 (Petroleum/petrochemical/natural gas — but adopted across mining), SAE J1739 (FMEA), internal failure code library.
- **Frequency:** Per failure event.
- **Hand-offs:** Failure data → reliability dashboards → RCM updates → procurement (chronic-failure part replacements).
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Codes too generic; codes inconsistent across mechanics; reliability never reviews; no link from code to corrective design changes.

### 4.9 Cost Roll-Up & Allocation
- **What it is:** Total cost per work order — labor (regular, OT, benefits load), parts (from inventory at moving average), contractor services, overhead allocation — and rollup to asset, account, cost center, mine, division.
- **Who performs it:** Maintenance accountant; CMMS auto-rollup; controller validates.
- **Data captured:** Labor cost, parts cost, contractor cost, overhead, total cost, GL account, cost center, asset, mine site.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Chart of accounts mapping; maintenance cost per ton metric.
- **Frequency:** Daily; monthly close.
- **Hand-offs:** Cost data → controller → mine cost report → benchmark.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Inter-mine charges for shared crews; capital vs expense reclassifications; floor stock not allocated to specific assets.

## 5. Condition Monitoring Programs

### 5.1 Oil Sample Analysis (S·O·S / Fluid Analysis)
- **What it is:** Routine sampling of engine, hydraulic, transmission, final drive, gear case oils and lab analysis for wear metals, contaminants, viscosity, additive depletion.
- **Who performs it:** Lube tech / mechanic takes sample; lab analyzes (CAT S·O·S Services, Polaris Laboratories, Bureau Veritas, ALS Tribology, WearCheck/AveCheck, Eurofins TestOil).
- **Data captured:** Sample ID, asset, component, oil type, hours since last change, hours on component, wear metals (Fe, Cu, Cr, Pb, Sn, Al, Si — silicon indicates dirt), additive elements (Zn, P, Ca, Mg, B), contaminants (water, fuel, glycol, soot), viscosity, TBN/TAN, particle count (ISO 4406 cleanliness code).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ASTM D6595 (rotrode emission), ASTM D7416 (FTIR), ISO 4406 (particle count), ASTM D445 (viscosity), CAT S·O·S guidelines.
- **Frequency:** Engine oil every PM cycle (250-500 hrs); hydraulic every 500-1000 hrs; gear cases every 500 hrs; transformer oil annually.
- **Hand-offs:** Sample → lab → results to reliability → CMMS condition record → corrective work order if alarming.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Sample contamination at port (must flush first); wrong oil type listed; sample sent without info card; results delayed 5-10 days (CAT S·O·S "Same Day" is rare); "watch and wait" findings forgotten until failure.

### 5.2 Vibration Analysis
- **What it is:** Measuring vibration on rotating equipment to detect bearing wear, imbalance, misalignment, gear damage.
- **Who performs it:** PdM tech (Vibration Analyst Cat I-IV per ISO 18436-2 / Mobius / Vibration Institute certification).
- **Data captured:** Asset, measurement points, time waveform, FFT spectrum, overall vibration (ips/mm-s), bearing condition (acceleration, BPFO, BPFI, BSF, FTF), trend.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ISO 10816 / ISO 20816 (vibration severity), ISO 18436 (analyst certification), API 670 (machinery protection).
- **Frequency:** Monthly to quarterly for plant rotating equipment; continuous for critical (online systems — GE Bently Nevada 3500, Emerson AMS, SKF IMx).
- **Hand-offs:** PdM tech → reliability → corrective WO if alarms.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Wrong measurement point; sensor cable damage; baseline never established; alarms set wrong (always alarming or never alarming); online system not connected to CMMS.

### 5.3 Infrared Thermography
- **What it is:** Using thermal imaging cameras to detect overheating in electrical (loose connections, overloaded breakers), mechanical (bearings, couplings, belts), and steam/refractory systems.
- **Who performs it:** Certified thermographer (Level I-III per ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ISO 18436-7).
- **Data captured:** Thermal image, hottest spot temperature, reference temperature, ambient, load conditions, recommended action, severity.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** NETA MTS for electrical, NFPA 70B for electrical maintenance, ASTM E1934 (IR inspection of electrical), ISO 18436-7 (thermographer cert).
- **Frequency:** Annual for substations/MCCs; semi-annual for critical; monthly for outdoor switchgear.
- **Hand-offs:** Thermographer report → reliability → electrical WO for repair.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Equipment must be under load (often deenergized for maintenance window — defeats purpose); arc-flash PPE required to open panels; old aluminum connections constantly hot; report sits without action.

### 5.4 Motor Current Signature Analysis (MCSA)
- **What it is:** Analyzing motor current to detect broken rotor bars, eccentricity, stator faults without removing motor.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability tech with MCSA tool (PdMA MCEmax, AllTest IRIS, Emerson CSI).
- **Data captured:** Current spectrum, sideband frequencies, fault indicators, trend.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** IEEE 1415; EPRI testing guides.
- **Frequency:** Annual for critical motors; on alarm from vibration/thermal.
- **Hand-offs:** Tech → reliability → motor shop if rebuild needed.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Variable speed drives complicate analysis; coupling alignment masked; no baseline for new motors.

### 5.5 Ultrasonic Inspection
- **What it is:** Detecting high-frequency sound from leaks (air, steam, vacuum), electrical partial discharge, bearing faults early stage, valve passing.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability tech with ultrasonic device (UE Systems, SDT, Fluke).
- **Data captured:** dB level, location, leak rate estimate, recommended action.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ISO 18436-8 (UT for condition monitoring).
- **Frequency:** Quarterly air leak surveys (huge cost savings); annual electrical PD; bearing lube on-condition.
- **Hand-offs:** Tech report → corrective WO.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Background noise interferes; "we've always had leaks" culture; UT-guided lubrication abandoned for time-based.

### 5.6 Coolant Analysis
- **What it is:** Testing engine coolant for pH, conductivity, freeze point, additives, contaminants.
- **Who performs it:** Mechanic samples; CAT S·O·S Coolant Services / Polaris CoolCheck Plus / lab.
- **Data captured:** pH, glycol %, freeze point, nitrites, molybdate, conductivity, contamination.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ASTM D3306 / D6210 (coolant specifications); CAT ELC test kit.
- **Frequency:** Every PM cycle; level 1 dipstick check daily.
- **Hand-offs:** Sample → analysis → corrective WO if depleted.
- **State-specific differences:** Glycol disposal per RCRA (not hazardous unless contaminated with heavy metals).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Mixing ELC (extended life) with conventional coolant ruins additive package; cap-off-engine-running causes pressure release.

### 5.7 Fuel Quality / Particulate Checks
- **What it is:** Testing bulk fuel for water, sediment, biological growth, cloud point.
- **Who performs it:** Fuel tech; outside lab on quarterly samples.
- **Data captured:** Water content (ASTM D6304 Karl Fischer), sediment (ASTM D2276), microbial (ASTM D7978), cloud point (ASTM D2500), CFPP.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ASTM D975 (diesel fuel oil spec — Grade 1-D, 2-D, ULSD requirement EPA), tank water check daily.
- **Frequency:** Daily water bottom check; weekly filter check; quarterly lab sample.
- **Hand-offs:** Fuel quality → fuel system maintenance → potential fuel system overhaul.
- **State-specific differences:** State fuel quality standards (Weights & Measures); winter blends required in cold climates; biodiesel blend rules vary.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Microbial growth in tank bottom causes injector failures; condensation in tanks; tank-to-tank cross-contamination on multi-fuel systems.

### 5.8 Tire Pressure / Temperature Monitoring (TPMS)
- **What it is:** Continuous monitoring of haul truck tire pressure and temperature with onboard systems (PressurePro, Translogik, Bridgestone IntelliTire).
- **Who performs it:** Operator alerts; tire crew responds; reliability trends.
- **Data captured:** Tire position, pressure, temperature, alarm thresholds, alarm history.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM tire/wheel specs, TKPH/TMPH limits.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Alarm → operator → tire crew → CMMS WO.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Sensor battery failures; false alarms; operators ignoring; sensor swapped between tires without rebinding.

### 5.9 Battery Health (Lead-Acid / Lithium)
- **What it is:** Monitoring traction batteries for UG scoops, mantrips, supply cars — lead-acid traditional or increasing lithium-ion adoption.
- **Who performs it:** Battery tech / mechanic; battery shop personnel.
- **Data captured:** Specific gravity (lead-acid per cell), voltage per cell, capacity test (discharge load test per IEEE 450 / IEEE 1188), state of charge, cycle count, internal resistance, temperature.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** IEEE 450 (vented lead-acid), IEEE 1188 (VRLA), IEEE 1106 (Ni-Cd), OEM battery manuals, MSHA approval for battery equipment.
- **Frequency:** Per-shift voltage check; weekly specific gravity; annual capacity test.
- **Hand-offs:** Battery tech → CMMS → reorder cells / replace pack.
- **State-specific differences:** Lead-acid disposal per RCRA / state hazardous waste — universal waste exemption applies if recycled.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Mixing old/new cells damages pack; charger settings wrong; hydrogen ventilation in charging stations; lithium thermal runaway safety considerations (still emerging in coal UG).

### 5.10 Brake / Steering System Inspection
- **What it is:** Detailed inspection of safety-critical hydraulic systems on haul trucks, dozers, loaders.
- **Who performs it:** Mechanic; certified inspector for state safety inspections.
- **Data captured:** Brake pad/disc thickness, brake test (slope test, dyno), steering accumulator pressure, hydraulic leaks, hose age.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM brake test procedures (CAT, Komatsu), 30 CFR 77.1605 (loading and haulage equipment).
- **Frequency:** Per PM; functional brake test daily by operator.
- **Hand-offs:** Inspection → CMMS → repair WO.
- **State-specific differences:** State motor vehicle inspection for licensed on-road trucks (WV annual, VA annual, KY no annual, AL no annual, TN no annual).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Brake fade in long downhill hauls; accumulator pre-charge incorrect; hose age unknown.

## 6. Tire Management

### 6.1 Tire Procurement & Stock Management
- **What it is:** Ordering haul truck tires (major capex line item — single 59/80R63 tire can be $50,000-$70,000+) and managing on-hand stock.
- **Who performs it:** Equipment manager / tire program manager; buyer; tire OEM rep (Bridgestone, Michelin, Goodyear, Belshina, Maxam, Triangle).
- **Data captured:** Tire size (e.g., 24.00R35, 27.00R49, 33.00R51, 40.00R57, 46/90R57, 50/90R57, 53/80R63, 59/80R63, 59/80R63 XDR for haul trucks; smaller for loaders/graders/dozers), compound (E-3/E-4/L-4/L-5), application (haul, loader, grader), serial numbers (carcass tracking), purchase price, freight, mounting location upon installation.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** TRA (Tire & Rim Association) standards; OEM TKPH ratings.
- **Frequency:** Continuous ordering based on consumption.
- **Hand-offs:** Tire manager → procurement → receipt → tire shop → installation.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Lead times of 6-18 months for ultra-large; allocation systems during global shortages (2021-2023); price escalation; recyclers for end-of-life tires.

### 6.2 Tire Carcass Tracking (Serialization)
- **What it is:** Tracking each individual tire from new through scrap by serial — measurements, position history, hours/miles, repair history.
- **Who performs it:** Tire shop foreman; tire program engineer.
- **Data captured:** Tire serial, OEM, size/compound, initial tread depth, in-service date, installation events (position, machine, hours), tread depth at each rotation, repair history (cut, impact, separation), hours/miles accumulated, scrap date, scrap reason.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Tire history card; tire management software (Bridgestone TireMatics, Michelin Manager, Otraco).
- **Frequency:** At each tire move event; tread depth at PM intervals.
- **Hand-offs:** Tire shop → CMMS / tire management system → reliability for trends.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Serial illegible after time in service; tire moved without scan; double-stamped tires; lost history when changing software systems.

### 6.3 Tire Rotation & Position Management
- **What it is:** Moving tires across positions on truck (corner-to-corner) to even out wear, and managing TKPH/TMPH limits.
- **Who performs it:** Tire crew; tire program manager plans rotations.
- **Data captured:** Rotation event, from-position, to-position, tread depth before, reason, route TKPH/TMPH analysis.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM TKPH calculation (Ton-Kilometers Per Hour); haul road profile.
- **Frequency:** Per scheduled rotation interval (typically 2,000-4,000 hours).
- **Hand-offs:** Rotation plan → tire crew → CMMS.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Heat-stressed tires retained until catastrophic failure; rotation skipped because no spare; left-side vs right-side wear patterns.

### 6.4 Tire Repair vs Scrap Decision
- **What it is:** Evaluating damaged tires for repairability — sidewall, tread, or shoulder injury — and deciding repair vs scrap vs retread.
- **Who performs it:** Tire repair shop (Pomp's Tire, GCR, Purcell Tire, McCarthy, Snider Tire, OEM-authorized repair shops); tire program manager approves.
- **Data captured:** Damage type, location, depth, repair recommendation, repair cost, salvage value estimate, decision (repair/scrap/retread).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** TIA (Tire Industry Association) repair standards; OEM repair allowances.
- **Frequency:** Per damaged tire.
- **Hand-offs:** Tire shop → repair vendor → return → install.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Scrap value drops sharply with carcass damage; transport to repair shop expensive; repair warranty disputes.

### 6.5 Tire Failure & Damage Reporting
- **What it is:** Investigating tire failures — impact, cut, heat separation, tread separation — for road condition feedback to operations.
- **Who performs it:** Tire program manager; safety; operations.
- **Data captured:** Failure mode, location (road segment if known), operator, hours/miles on tire, suspected cause, photos, lost hours, replacement cost.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Tire incident report; haul road inspection.
- **Frequency:** Per failure.
- **Hand-offs:** Tire program → road maintenance crew → operations training feedback.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Repeated failures on same road segment indicating material/profile issue; operator over-speed; underinflation due to slow leaks.

### 6.6 Scrap Tire Disposal
- **What it is:** End-of-life tire disposal — recycling, on-site stockpile, or hauled to processor.
- **Who performs it:** Tire shop; environmental coordinator; waste hauler.
- **Data captured:** Scrap tire count, disposal method, hauler, manifests.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** State scrap tire regulations (most states regulate ≥10 tire piles); EPA RCRA; some states (KY tire pile cleanup, WV scrap tire law, VA waste tire program, AL scrap tire program, TN waste tire program) require permits/registrations; mining tires often have on-mine disposal allowance per surface mining permit reclamation plan.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Tire shop → environmental → waste hauler → recycler/landfill.
- **State-specific differences:** WV Scrap Tire Program under DEP; KY Department for Environmental Protection waste tire trust fund; VA Waste Tire Program in DEQ; AL Solid Waste Branch; TN Waste Tire Program.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Old tire piles legacy from former operations; mosquito breeding/fire risk; recycler capacity.

---

## 7. Rebuildable Component Tracking

### 7.1 Component Master & Serialization
- **What it is:** Tracking every rotatable, rebuildable component (engines, transmissions, final drives, wheel motors, hydraulic cylinders, pumps, motors, gearboxes, swing drives, dragline rigging) by unique serial across its lifetime.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability planner; warehouse; rebuild shop.
- **Data captured:** Component serial, OEM (CAT C175-16 engine, CAT C32 ACERT, CAT 3508/3512/3516, Komatsu SSDA16V160, SSDA18V170, Cummins QSK60/QSK78/QST30, Detroit MTU Series 4000, Allison transmissions, CAT 7G powertrain components), description, current asset assignment, current position on asset, install date, install hours, rebuild count, total hours since new, hours since last rebuild, next rebuild target hours.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Component register; OEM serial number plate; rebuild certificate.
- **Frequency:** Continuous as installed/removed.
- **Hand-offs:** Component master → rebuild shop → asset accounting (for rebuilt components capitalized separately).
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Internal components (cylinders, valves) within rebuildable not tracked; serial collision between same OEM/year; "core" returned wrong unit.

### 7.2 Engine Tracking
- **What it is:** Engine hours, oil samples, ECM data, in-frame rebuild planning, exchange engines.
- **Who performs it:** Engine rebuild specialist; CAT MARC tech; Komatsu service.
- **Data captured:** Engine serial, hours, ECM data download, S·O·S trend, fuel consumption per hour, blow-by readings, compression test (rare), top-end vs in-frame vs out-of-frame rebuild decision, exchange vs own-rebuild.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM engine manuals; CAT S·O·S Services; CAT Reman or Komatsu Reman exchange programs.
- **Frequency:** Continuous monitoring; rebuild at OEM TBO.
- **Hand-offs:** Engine shop / OEM rebuild center → install on machine.
- **State-specific differences:** None. EPA Tier 4 emissions impact engine choice for newer surface equipment (existing fleets often pre-Tier 4 or Tier 4 Final, regulated under 40 CFR Part 89 / 1039 nonroad).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** EPA non-road emissions tier compliance during rebuild (Tier 4 Final is current spec; emissions-modifying rebuilds prohibited per "tampering"); ECM lockouts on rebuilt engines.

### 7.3 Final Drive / Wheel Motor Tracking
- **What it is:** Haul truck final drives or AC drive system wheel motors (CAT, Komatsu, GE/Wabtec, Siemens for AC drive).
- **Who performs it:** Drive shop or OEM exchange.
- **Data captured:** Serial, position (LH/RH), hours, oil sample data, install date, rebuild history.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM rebuild specs.
- **Frequency:** Rebuild at OEM TBO (typically 18,000-25,000 hrs).
- **Hand-offs:** Removal → rebuild shop/OEM → install.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Diesel-electric vs mechanical drive trains have very different component lists; wheel motor regen on AC drives reduces brake wear but stresses cables/inverters.

### 7.4 Transmission Tracking
- **What it is:** Mechanical haul truck transmissions, dozer transmissions, motor grader transmissions.
- **Who performs it:** Powertrain shop / OEM rebuild.
- **Data captured:** Serial, hours, oil samples, gear engagement issues, install/removal history.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM rebuild guidelines.
- **Frequency:** Per OEM TBO.
- **Hand-offs:** Powertrain shop → install.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Operator gear-mashing accelerates wear; converter charge pump failures.

### 7.5 Hydraulic Cylinder Tracking
- **What it is:** Boom cylinders, stick cylinders, bucket cylinders, lift cylinders, dump cylinders, blade cylinders, hoist cylinders — all rebuildable.
- **Who performs it:** Hydraulic shop in-house or OEM dealer.
- **Data captured:** Serial, location, install/removal, seal kit changes, chrome rod condition, bore wear.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Hydraulic standards (NFPA), OEM specs.
- **Frequency:** Reseal as needed; rebuild at major component intervals.
- **Hand-offs:** Hydraulic shop → install.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Chrome plating contamination from hydraulic fluid degradation; rod scoring; pin/bushing wear sometimes mistaken for cylinder failure.

### 7.6 Major Mining-Specific Components
- **What it is:** Dragline rigging (boom point sheaves, drag rope, hoist rope, fairleads, dump blocks), shovel dipper handles, crowd drives, longwall shearer drum motors, AFC chain.
- **Who performs it:** Specialized riggers; OEM service.
- **Data captured:** Component-specific lifetime data — wire rope inspection per ASTM standards; shovel dipper teeth/lip changes; longwall chain stretch.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ASME B30 series (cranes/rigging); wire rope inspection per OEM; dragline maintenance per Bucyrus/Marion legacy specs and current CAT Mining service.
- **Frequency:** Per OEM, often daily inspections, weekly measurements.
- **Hand-offs:** Specialist crew → in-shop work; some require OEM-only.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Dragline rope "block-out" inspection; longwall move pace (typically 7-14 days for a complete move including shields, AFC, BSL, shearer) — major capital event.

### 7.7 Time Between Overhauls (TBO) Analysis
- **What it is:** Tracking actual hours achieved between rebuilds vs OEM targets and historical fleet averages.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer; OEM service.
- **Data captured:** Component, OEM TBO target, actual TBO achieved per event, variance reasons (early failure, conservative early rebuild, condition extended).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Reliability KPIs; benchmarking with industry (Society of Mining Engineers).
- **Frequency:** Per rebuild; quarterly trend.
- **Hand-offs:** Reliability → capital planning (timing of next major rebuild); → procurement (rebuild kits).
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Cost overruns on rebuilds with extensive damage; OEM warranty starts at exchange but installation problems claimed as install error.

---

## 8. Parts Inventory Management

### 8.1 Inventory Master Data (Item Master)
- **What it is:** Master record for every part — number, description, OEM cross-references, vendors, stocking class.
- **Who performs it:** Inventory analyst; warehouse manager; planner.
- **Data captured:** Item number, description, OEM part number, alternate/cross-reference part numbers (OEM, aftermarket, NAPA, Fastenal), unit of measure, weight, dimensions, hazmat class, shelf life, stocking class (A/B/C by velocity), critical flag, primary vendor, secondary vendor, lead time, manufacturer.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Inventory master form; UNSPSC codes; hazmat classification per DOT 49 CFR.
- **Frequency:** As new items added; cleansed periodically.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance/engineering → inventory analyst → warehouse → CMMS/ERP.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Duplicate item numbers for same part; OEM superseded part numbers; vendor part numbers vs OEM numbers mixed; "non-stock" items repeatedly purchased.

### 8.2 Stocking Level Management (Min/Max, ROP, EOQ)
- **What it is:** Determining how much of each item to keep on hand and at what point to reorder.
- **Who performs it:** Inventory analyst; planner; reliability for critical spares.
- **Data captured:** Min level (safety stock), max level, reorder point (ROP), economic order quantity (EOQ), lead time, demand history, demand variability (standard deviation), service level target (e.g., 95%, 99%).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** EOQ formula, statistical safety stock formulas, ABC analysis.
- **Frequency:** Annual review; on consumption-pattern change.
- **Hand-offs:** Analyst → procurement (replenishment POs); → finance (inventory carrying cost).
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Min/max set at "guess" not statistical; one-time consumption spike triggers permanent over-stocking; critical spare with zero demand history.

### 8.3 Critical Spares List (Insurance Spares)
- **What it is:** Identifying single-point-of-failure parts with long lead times that must be stocked despite low demand — gearbox assemblies, electric motors over X HP, specialty pumps, ECM/PLC modules.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer; maintenance superintendent; equipment manager.
- **Data captured:** Item, application asset, lead time, business impact of stockout (downtime $$, production loss), held quantity, alternative source.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Critical spare register.
- **Frequency:** Annual review; after major failures.
- **Hand-offs:** Reliability → procurement → warehouse "do not issue without approval" flag.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Insurance spares used for routine swap-out (then re-stocked late); accounting wants to write down "slow-moving" critical spares; spare goes bad in storage (motor bearings, batteries).

### 8.4 Cycle Counting & Annual Physical Inventory
- **What it is:** Regular counts of inventory to maintain accuracy.
- **Who performs it:** Warehouse staff; outside counters for annual; auditor observes annual.
- **Data captured:** Count date, location, items counted, system quantity, counted quantity, variance, adjustment value.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Cycle count procedure; SOX-compliant inventory procedures for public companies; FASB ASC 330 (inventory accounting).
- **Frequency:** Cycle count daily/weekly (A items most frequent); annual physical inventory.
- **Hand-offs:** Counter → warehouse manager → controller for adjustments → auditor for sign-off.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Adjustment write-offs hide theft / mis-issues; multiple bin locations for same item; "off-system" inventory (gang boxes, mechanic trucks); inventory in transit between mines.

### 8.5 Receiving & Put-Away
- **What it is:** Receiving parts against PO, inspection for quality, putting away to bin location.
- **Who performs it:** Receiver / warehouseman.
- **Data captured:** Receipt date, PO number, line item, quantity received, condition, packing slip, bin location, three-way match data.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Receiving report; packing slip; damaged goods report (OS&D — over/short/damaged).
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Receiver → AP (for invoice match) → put-away → CMMS bin update.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Receipt without inspection (defects discovered at issue); items received but not put away (lost on dock); back-orders without alert.

### 8.6 Picking, Issuing & Returns
- **What it is:** Issuing parts from warehouse to work orders or mechanics; returning unused.
- **Who performs it:** Warehouseman; mechanic at self-serve windows.
- **Data captured:** Issue date, WO number, requestor, item, quantity, bin, value; for returns date returned, quantity, condition.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Pick ticket; issue/return form.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Issue → WO cost; returns → recheck condition → back to bin or scrap.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Issues without WO ("just give me a hose fitting"); returns put back without inspection; off-shift self-serve not tracked.

### 8.7 Slow-Moving & Obsolete Inventory Identification
- **What it is:** Identifying parts with no issues in X months/years — candidates for scrap, return, or write-down.
- **Who performs it:** Inventory analyst; controller.
- **Data captured:** Item, last issue date, on-hand qty, value, age, reason for stocking (if known), retired equipment Y/N.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Slow-mover report; obsolete inventory write-down per FASB ASC 330.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** Analyst → reliability for retention decision → controller for write-down → warehouse for disposal.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Parts for retired equipment kept "just in case"; resold to other operators; donated; scrapped.

### 8.8 Tool Cribs & Special Tools
- **What it is:** Sub-inventory of tools, gauges, alignment equipment, specialty pullers, OEM service tools.
- **Who performs it:** Tool crib attendant; shop foreman.
- **Data captured:** Tool number, description, last calibration (if applicable), current holder, checkout date.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Tool crib checkout log.
- **Frequency:** Per checkout/return.
- **Hand-offs:** Mechanic → tool crib → return.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Lost tools (especially specialty OEM service tools that cost $1,000s); tool calibration overdue; "permanent loaner" tools.

### 8.9 Floor Stock / Free Issue Items
- **What it is:** Low-value, high-volume items (nuts, bolts, washers, rags, gloves) issued without WO charge.
- **Who performs it:** Warehouse stocks; mechanics self-serve.
- **Data captured:** Bulk consumption by month; periodic replenishment counts.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Floor stock list; Vending Machine Inventory (CribMaster, AutoCrib, Fastenal vending).
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Vendor managed inventory (VMI) replenishment by Fastenal/MSC/Grainger.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Theft / waste from open access; VMI vendor over-stocks; floor stock category creep into expensive items.

### 8.10 Hazardous Materials Storage & Inventory
- **What it is:** Inventory and storage of oils, greases, fuel additives, paints, solvents, batteries, aerosols, gas cylinders.
- **Who performs it:** Warehouse with safety oversight; SDS librarian.
- **Data captured:** SDS on file, quantity on hand, storage location, secondary containment, fire rating, segregation per compatibility.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OSHA HazCom 29 CFR 1910.1200 / MSHA 30 CFR 47 (HazCom for mines); EPA SPCC Plan for oil storage ≥1,320 gallons aggregate (40 CFR 112); flammable storage per NFPA 30; compressed gas per NFPA 55.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; SDS update annually.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety/environmental review; emergency response plan link.
- **State-specific differences:** State chemical inventory reporting EPCRA Tier II (filed with State Emergency Response Commission and Local Emergency Planning Committee) — varies by state in submission process; AST registration: WV ASTs under WV DEP per WV ASTA, KY ASTs in some cases under KY DEP, AL ABC Above Ground Storage Tank Trust Fund / ADEM, TN ASTs not generally registered, VA DEQ AST program for ≥1,320 gallons.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** SDS not updated; incompatible storage (oxidizer near flammable); aerosol cans piled up; lead-acid battery storage with no neutralizing kit.
