## 9. Procurement & Vendor Management

### 9.1 Vendor Master
- **What it is:** Central record of every approved vendor with contact, terms, payment data, certifications, and performance.
- **Who performs it:** Procurement; AP for payment data; risk/compliance for vendor qualification.
- **Data captured:** Vendor name, TIN/EIN (W-9 on file), DUNS, addresses, contacts, payment terms, payment method (check, ACH, wire), 1099 status, insurance certificates, safety qualification (ISNetworld, Avetta, PEC Premier), diversity (MBE/WBE/SDVOSB/DBE), bank info, sanctioned-party screening (OFAC SDN).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Vendor onboarding form; W-9; ACH authorization; certificate of insurance with required coverages; certifications.
- **Frequency:** New vendor as needed; annual reverification of key data.
- **Hand-offs:** Procurement → AP → ERP master file.
- **State-specific differences:** State sales tax exemption certificates (per buyer's exemption status for mining production inputs — varies WV/VA/KY/AL/TN); state contractor licensing checks.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Duplicate vendors (variations on name); inactive vendors not archived; ACH fraud (impostor change of bank instructions); certificates of insurance expired; sanctioned vendor onboarding before screening.

### 9.2 Requisition → PO Workflow
- **What it is:** Internal request for goods/services → approval → conversion to PO.
- **Who performs it:** Requestor (planner/mechanic/foreman); approver per dollar threshold; buyer.
- **Data captured:** Requisition number, requestor, line items, quantity, suggested vendor, charge code, approvals (timestamp by each approver), conversion to PO.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Requisition form; approval matrix (e.g., < $1,000 supervisor; < $10K manager; < $50K superintendent; < $250K mine GM; < $1M COO; > $1M CEO/board).
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Requestor → approvers → buyer → vendor.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Split orders to avoid approval thresholds; emergency POs created after goods received ("after-the-fact" PO); requisitions sitting in approval queues during travel/leave.

### 9.3 Request for Quotation (RFQ)
- **What it is:** Formal solicitation of bids from multiple vendors for non-blanket purchases.
- **Who performs it:** Buyer; engineer for technical evaluation.
- **Data captured:** RFQ document, vendor list, response date, responses (price, lead time, terms), evaluation, award decision.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** RFQ template; bid tabulation; award memo.
- **Frequency:** Per significant purchase (per policy, often >$25K).
- **Hand-offs:** Buyer → vendors → bid analysis → PO.
- **State-specific differences:** None (private company; not subject to public bidding).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Specs written around single vendor; informal "phone quotes" without paper trail; rushed RFQs with inadequate response time.

### 9.4 Blanket POs & Call-Out Agreements
- **What it is:** Pre-approved POs for recurring purchases (lubricants, common consumables, contracted services) where releases are made against the blanket.
- **Who performs it:** Buyer; warehouse releases.
- **Data captured:** Blanket PO number, vendor, agreement terms (price, term, max value), releases against blanket, balance remaining.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Blanket PO terms; master service agreement (MSA) for services.
- **Frequency:** Annual blanket; releases as needed.
- **Hand-offs:** Buyer → warehouse for release → vendor.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Releases exceeding blanket value; pricing changes without amendment; blanket expired but releases continue; spend by blanket not visible.

### 9.5 Three-Way Match (PO / Receipt / Invoice)
- **What it is:** AP matching invoice to PO and receipt before payment.
- **Who performs it:** AP clerk; ERP automation.
- **Data captured:** Match status, variance, hold reason.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Three-way match procedure; vendor invoice; goods receipt; PO.
- **Frequency:** Per invoice.
- **Hand-offs:** AP → resolves mismatches with buyer/warehouse → payment.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Receipt not entered (invoice on hold); quantity variance within tolerance; price variance escalations; freight billed separately from goods.

### 9.6 Goods Receipt & Service Receipt
- **What it is:** Confirming goods received or services delivered, triggering inventory entry or expense recognition.
- **Who performs it:** Warehouse for goods; service receiver (foreman) for services.
- **Data captured:** Date, PO line, quantity, condition; for services description of work done.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Goods receipt note (GRN); service receipt; signed service ticket.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Receiver → AP for invoice match.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Service work signed-off without verification; double receipt; partial receipts not aggregated.

### 9.7 Returns & Credit Memos
- **What it is:** Returning defective, wrong, or excess goods to vendor; tracking credit memos.
- **Who performs it:** Warehouse / buyer; AP for credit application.
- **Data captured:** RMA number, return reason, return date, credit memo number, value.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** RMA from vendor; shipping documents; credit memo.
- **Frequency:** As needed.
- **Hand-offs:** Warehouse → vendor → AP for credit.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Restocking fees; freight back to vendor disputes; vendor never issuing credit; partial credits.

### 9.8 Vendor Performance Scorecard
- **What it is:** Tracking vendor KPIs — on-time delivery, quality, price competitiveness, responsiveness.
- **Who performs it:** Procurement; quality (for defects); operations (for service feedback).
- **Data captured:** OTD %, quality defects, price variance, response time, safety record (TRIR for service contractors).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Vendor scorecard template; quarterly business review.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly for top vendors.
- **Hand-offs:** Procurement → vendor for review → contract renewal decisions.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Scorecards generated but not shared/reviewed; subjective performance ratings.

### 9.9 Supplier Qualification & Audit
- **What it is:** Onboarding due diligence on new suppliers, periodic audits of critical suppliers (financial health, safety, quality).
- **Who performs it:** Procurement; safety (ISN/Avetta verification); quality; finance.
- **Data captured:** Qualification questionnaire, financial review (D&B), insurance certificates, safety stats (TRIR/LTIR/EMR), references, site audit if applicable.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Supplier qualification packet; safety prequalification (ISNetworld grade A/B/C, Avetta scorecards).
- **Frequency:** New supplier; annual renewal.
- **Hand-offs:** Procurement → qualification → approved vendor list.
- **State-specific differences:** State contractor licensing checks (WV WV-1, VA Class A/B/C, KY contractor license, AL Home Builders Licensure Board, TN contractor license).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Expired insurance certs go unnoticed; subcontractor not separately qualified; financial distress missed until late.

### 9.10 Contract Management
- **What it is:** Managing master service agreements, supply agreements, equipment leases, OEM service contracts.
- **Who performs it:** Legal; procurement; contract administrator.
- **Data captured:** Contract number, parties, scope, term, value, key terms (warranty, indemnity, insurance, IP, termination), renewal date.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Master agreements; contract management system.
- **Frequency:** As executed; renewal reviewed 90-120 days pre-expiry.
- **Hand-offs:** Legal → procurement → AP → operations.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Auto-renewal traps; "evergreen" contracts; price escalator clauses missed; contracts in legal's drawer not in procurement system.

### 9.11 Diversity & Small Business Reporting
- **What it is:** Tracking spend by MBE/WBE/SDVOSB/HUBZone/DBE if relevant for corporate or customer commitments.
- **Who performs it:** Procurement reporting.
- **Data captured:** Vendor diversity classification, spend, certifications.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Certifications from SBA, state agencies; supplier diversity reports.
- **Frequency:** Annual or quarterly per customer requirements.
- **Hand-offs:** Procurement → customers requesting reports.
- **State-specific differences:** State certification programs (WV Department of Administration; VA SWaM; KY MWBE; AL SBOR; TN GoDBE).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Outdated certifications; mis-classified vendors.

## 10. Fuel Management

### 10.1 Bulk Fuel Tank Inventory & Regulation
- **What it is:** Managing on-site diesel storage in above-ground or underground tanks.
- **Who performs it:** Fuel attendant; environmental coordinator; tank inspector.
- **Data captured:** Tank ID, capacity (gallons), location, GPS, fuel type (off-road diesel #2, on-road ULSD, gasoline, DEF), construction (single-wall, double-wall, fiberglass, steel), age, overfill protection, secondary containment, leak detection method.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** EPA SPCC Plan (40 CFR 112) for aggregate ≥1,320 gal AST or ≥42,000 gal UST oil; UST regulations under 40 CFR 280; state AST/UST registration: WV Aboveground Storage Tank Act (WV-ASTA) and UST registration under DEP; VA DEQ AST/UST programs; KY DEP UST program; AL ADEM AST/UST; TN DEC UST. Annual SPCC training; monthly visual inspection; annual SPCC review with PE certification for facilities >10K gal.
- **Frequency:** Monthly visual; annual integrity; periodic state inspection.
- **Hand-offs:** Fuel attendant → environmental → state agency.
- **State-specific differences:** WV-ASTA Tier 1 (>50K gal or near water) requires PE-certified plans and frequent inspections; KY UST and AST programs distinct; VA TR-1 / TR-1S forms; AL Tank Trust Fund. UST regs (federal) common to all.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Aged tanks failing integrity test; SPCC plan not updated post-modification; spills triggering Tier II reporting; leak detection alarms ignored.

### 10.2 Bulk Fuel Receipts (Deliveries)
- **What it is:** Receiving fuel delivered by truck or rail.
- **Who performs it:** Fuel attendant / receiver.
- **Data captured:** Delivery date, vendor, fuel type, gallons gross, gallons net (temperature corrected), BOL/ticket number, before/after tank level (manual stick or ATG — automatic tank gauge), seal numbers, density/API.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Bill of lading (BOL); shipping ticket; carrier invoice; ATG report (Veeder-Root TLS, OPW SiteSentinel); ASTM D4057 (manual sampling).
- **Frequency:** Per delivery.
- **Hand-offs:** Receiver → fuel system → AP for invoice.
- **State-specific differences:** State motor fuel tax: most states tax dyed diesel separately from undyed; off-road exemption applies to mining equipment but documentation must be retained (refund or exemption certificates).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Temperature-correction disputes; shrinkage between BOL and tank; mixed loads (gasoline contamination); meter calibration drift on delivery trucks.

### 10.3 Daily Fuel Issues (Dispensing to Equipment)
- **What it is:** Pumping fuel to mobile equipment by hour meter.
- **Who performs it:** Fuel attendant; some sites self-serve via card/key fob (FuelMaster, Multiforce/Banlaw, Gilbarco FuelTrak).
- **Data captured:** Date/time, asset, hour meter, gallons dispensed, attendant.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Daily fuel log; automated fuel management system (AFMS).
- **Frequency:** Per equipment fueling event (typically per shift for haul trucks).
- **Hand-offs:** Fuel system → CMMS (for hours capture) → fuel reconciliation → cost allocation.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Wrong asset selected (fuel charged to wrong unit); pump malfunction overshoot; bypass mode usage; fuel theft (cans / drums).

### 10.4 Fuel Reconciliation (Book vs Physical)
- **What it is:** Comparing tank readings, receipts, and issues to find variance — losses indicate leaks, theft, or measurement error.
- **Who performs it:** Fuel attendant / accountant; environmental on losses.
- **Data captured:** Opening tank level, plus receipts, minus issues, minus expected temperature-corrected loss, vs closing tank level; variance.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Daily reconciliation; SIR (Statistical Inventory Reconciliation) per 40 CFR 280.43(d); monthly UST reconciliation per UST rules.
- **Frequency:** Daily; SIR monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Fuel reconciliation → environmental for trigger losses → maintenance for leak investigation.
- **State-specific differences:** UST regs require leak detection method (SIR, ATG, manual tank gauging, statistical methods). State UST programs may have additional reporting.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Phantom losses (water bottom expansion, ATG calibration); chronic small losses ignored; large overnight loss = leak (potential release reportable to state within 24 hours per 40 CFR 280.50).

### 10.5 Fuel Quality Program
- **What it is:** Maintaining fuel quality through filtration, water removal, periodic lab testing.
- **Who performs it:** Fuel attendant; outside lab quarterly samples.
- **Data captured:** Water bottom level, filter differential pressure, lab results (water content, particulate, microbial, viscosity, distillation, cetane).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ASTM D975 (diesel spec), ASTM D6217 (filtration), ASTM D7978 (microbial); Worldwide Fuel Charter.
- **Frequency:** Daily water check; weekly filter check; quarterly lab.
- **Hand-offs:** Fuel attendant → environmental for water disposal → maintenance for engine impacts.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Tank moisture in summer-winter cycles; microbial growth biocide treatment; bulk fuel sitting >6 months degrades.

### 10.6 Fuel Card Programs (On-Road Fleet)
- **What it is:** Cards for over-the-road pickups, lowboys, service trucks at retail/commercial stations (WEX, Comdata, FleetCor/Fuelman).
- **Who performs it:** Drivers; fleet manager; AP.
- **Data captured:** Card number, vehicle assigned, transaction (date, station, gallons, price, odometer), unique driver PIN.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Card issuance log; monthly statement; suspect transactions report.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Card vendor → fleet manager → AP → fuel tax accounting.
- **State-specific differences:** State motor fuel tax included; IFTA reporting for vehicles ≥26,001 lbs or 3+ axles crossing state lines.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Card theft / personal use; PIN sharing; lost cards; out-of-fleet vehicle fueled.

### 10.7 Fuel Tax — Off-Road Diesel & IFTA
- **What it is:** Distinguishing off-road dyed diesel (no federal/state highway tax) from on-road, and reporting interstate motor fuel tax via IFTA.
- **Who performs it:** Tax accountant; fleet manager.
- **Data captured:** Off-road dyed consumption (mining equipment), on-road consumption by jurisdiction, IFTA quarterly returns, miles by state, fuel by state.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** IRS Form 4136 (Credit for Federal Tax Paid on Fuels — for refund if on-road fuel used off-road); state off-road refund programs; IFTA Quarterly Tax Return; IRS Publication 510.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly IFTA; annual fuel tax refunds.
- **Hand-offs:** Fuel system data → tax accounting → IFTA filing → IRS/state refunds.
- **State-specific differences:** Each state's motor fuel tax rate and exemptions differ; AL, KY, TN, VA, WV all IFTA member jurisdictions. Off-road refund rules vary (e.g., KY allows refund for off-road; WV permits dyed diesel direct purchase exempt). State surface mining severance tax may include credit for fuel.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Dyed fuel used in on-road vehicle = federal penalty ($1,000+/day or $10/gal whichever greater); IFTA audit risk; bulk plant transfers not properly categorized.

### 10.8 DEF (Diesel Exhaust Fluid) Management
- **What it is:** Storing and dispensing DEF for Tier 4 Final diesel engines with SCR (Selective Catalytic Reduction).
- **Who performs it:** Fuel attendant.
- **Data captured:** DEF tank levels, dispensing logs, quality tests (refractometer per ISO 22241).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ISO 22241 (DEF quality); API DEF supplier program.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Fuel system → engine maintenance → emissions compliance.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** DEF freezes at -11°C / 12°F (heated tank needed); contamination ruins SCR catalyst ($$$); operators top off engine DEF wrong tank.

---

## 11. Lubricants & Fluids Management

### 11.1 Bulk Lube Inventory (Oil, Grease, Coolant, Hydraulic, Gear)
- **What it is:** Managing bulk storage and dispensing of all lubricants and process fluids.
- **Who performs it:** Lube tech / warehouse.
- **Data captured:** Product (engine oil 15W-40, hydraulic ISO 46/68, gear oil 80W-140, multipurpose grease NLGI 2, EP grease, transmission TDTO, coolant ELC, brake fluid), bulk tank levels, dispense records, totes/drums/pails inventory.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Lube chart per machine (OEM-specified), SDS, ISO viscosity standards, API SP/SN/CK-4/FA-4 engine oil categories, OEM approval lists.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Lube inventory → lube routes / dispensing → equipment.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Wrong oil in wrong tank (cross-contamination); mixed grease types; expired open drums; outdated SDSs.

### 11.2 Lube Routes & Scheduled Lubrication
- **What it is:** Pre-defined routes for greasing equipment per OEM lube charts.
- **Who performs it:** Lube tech with grease cart or auto-lube refill.
- **Data captured:** Route ID, equipment, lube points, lube type, quantity per point, last performed, next due.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Lube chart; auto-lube system (Lincoln/SKF Lincoln Quicklub, Graco, Beka, Bijur Delimon) reservoir level.
- **Frequency:** Daily/weekly/per PM hours.
- **Hand-offs:** Lube tech → CMMS PM compliance → reliability for trend.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Missed grease points hidden inside guarding; auto-lube system pump failures unnoticed; wrong grease for high-temp application.

### 11.3 Used Oil Collection & Disposal
- **What it is:** Collecting drained used motor oil, hydraulic oil, gear oil for recycling or disposal.
- **Who performs it:** Lube tech; environmental; waste oil hauler (Safety-Kleen, Heritage-Crystal Clean, regional haulers).
- **Data captured:** Used oil tank levels, hauler manifests, gallons recycled.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** 40 CFR 279 (used oil management standards); manifest if classified hazardous (uncommon — used oil typically not hazardous unless mixed); state used oil programs.
- **Frequency:** Continuous collection; periodic pickup.
- **Hand-offs:** Lube tech → used oil tank → hauler.
- **State-specific differences:** All states adopt 40 CFR 279 with some variations; used oil registration may be required for generators/transporters.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Hazardous waste mixed in (solvents, paint) reclassifies whole tank; on-site burner permits if burning used oil for heat; spill cleanup costs.

### 11.4 Reclaimed Oil / Oil Reclamation
- **What it is:** On-site filtering/centrifuging of oil to extend service life (large UG and surface fleets economically justify).
- **Who performs it:** Lube specialist; oil reclamation vendor (RelaDyne, OilFiltrationSystems).
- **Data captured:** Volume reclaimed, quality before/after, equipment treated.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Oil cleanliness ISO 4406; service life extension data.
- **Frequency:** Continuous on critical equipment.
- **Hand-offs:** Reclamation → oil sample lab to verify.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Insufficient filtration creates false sense of cleanliness; reclaimed oil mixed with new tracking.

### 11.5 Spill Kit Inventory & Response
- **What it is:** Pre-positioned spill kits at fuel/lube areas, equipment, and shops.
- **Who performs it:** Environmental coordinator; first responders.
- **Data captured:** Kit locations, contents inventory, last inspection.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** SPCC plan kit list; OSHA HAZWOPER per 29 CFR 1910.120 / MSHA 30 CFR 56/57.4106 hazardous spill cleanup.
- **Frequency:** Monthly inspection.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance → environmental on use → restock.
- **State-specific differences:** State spill reporting thresholds: any release reaching waters of state typically reportable immediately (within hours).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Kits raided for routine cleanup; absorbent used up before restock; no kit at remote sites.

---

## 12. Explosives & Drilling Supplies (Surface Mines)

### 12.1 Explosives Storage & Magazine Operations
- **What it is:** On-site magazines storing detonators, primers/boosters, and emulsion or ANFO components — typically done by contracted blaster (Austin Powder, Dyno Nobel, ICI/Orica, Maine Drilling & Blasting) but mine may own/store.
- **Who performs it:** Licensed blaster/powderman; magazine keeper; ATF registrant.
- **Data captured:** Magazine inventory by item (detonators by type: electric, nonel, electronic; boosters; emulsion; ANFO; cap & fuse), daily inventory count, receipts, issues to blast pattern, destruction logs.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ATF Form 5400.5 (Limited Permit / Permit holder) for explosives importation/distribution/use; 27 CFR 555 (Commerce in Explosives); MSHA 30 CFR 77.1300 (surface explosives handling); IME (Institute of Makers of Explosives) recommendations; magazine specifications per ATF 5400.13 (Type 1-4 magazines).
- **Frequency:** Daily inventory by ATF rule (theft/loss reportable within 24 hours per 27 CFR 555.30).
- **Hand-offs:** Magazine keeper → blaster → blast pattern → ATF on incident.
- **State-specific differences:** State blaster licensing required in addition to ATF: WV blaster certification through OMHST (per WV Code 22-3-13 surface blasting and per 30 CFR 850 explosives requirements for SMCRA); KY blaster certification through KY OMSL; VA blaster certification through DMM; TN blaster certification (TDEC); AL blaster certification (ASMC). Each state's surface mining program also has blasting plans and pre-blast survey requirements.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Theft (immediate ATF/FBI notification); magazine break-ins; expired detonators; mixed lots; pre-blast survey of nearby structures (homes, wells, churches) mandatory in many states; blast vibration/airblast monitoring; neighbor blast claims.

### 12.2 Daily Blast Pattern & Explosives Use
- **What it is:** Blasting individual benches/patterns and recording quantities, hole counts, vibrations.
- **Who performs it:** Blaster-in-charge; drill operator; ATF magazine keeper.
- **Data captured:** Blast pattern ID, hole count, depth, diameter, hole spacing, burden, charge per hole, total powder, stemming, initiation sequence, delay times, vibration monitor readings (peak particle velocity, airblast dB), wind, weather.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Blasting plan per state SMCRA program (30 CFR 816.61-816.68 surface mining blasting and 30 CFR 850); MSHA blasting record per 30 CFR 77.1303; OSMRE rules; vibration limits per OSMRE 30 CFR 816.67 (scaled distance equation or 0.5"-2.0" PPV depending on frequency).
- **Frequency:** Per blast (typically daily on active mine).
- **Hand-offs:** Blaster → mine engineering → environmental (vibration reports) → state agency.
- **State-specific differences:** WV/VA/KY all have detailed state blasting rules under their SMCRA programs (e.g., WV 38 CSR 2; KY 405 KAR 16:120; VA 4VAC25); state blasting log requirements; neighbor notification rules.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Misfire (charged hole that didn't detonate — 24-hour wait per MSHA); flyrock incidents; vibration complaints requiring claim adjustment; wet holes affecting product choice.

### 12.3 Drill Bits, Steel, Hammers Inventory
- **What it is:** Consumable drilling supplies for rotary, percussive, and blasthole drills.
- **Who performs it:** Drill foreman; warehouse.
- **Data captured:** Bit type (tricone rotary, button bit, DTH hammer), bit size, OEM (Sandvik, Atlas Copco/Epiroc Secoroc, Numa, Mincon), serial, feet drilled, hours, current asset, return-for-rebuild Y/N.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Drill bit logs.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Drill foreman → warehouse → drill operators.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Tracking feet-per-bit; bit rebuilds vs disposal; rotation in/out of drills.

---

## 13. Shop, Welding, PPE & Calibration

### 13.1 Shop Bay Assignment & Scheduling
- **What it is:** Managing limited shop space — bays assigned to equipment in for repair, sequence and dwell time.
- **Who performs it:** Shop foreman; planner; scheduler.
- **Data captured:** Bay number, occupant equipment, in-date, out-date, blocking equipment behind, crane availability.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Shop board (whiteboard, CMMS scheduling).
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Planner → shop foreman → release to ops.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Equipment parked in bay with mechanic re-assigned; mechanic theft of tools; bay occupied longer than planned blocks others.

### 13.2 Overhead Crane / Hoist Inspections
- **What it is:** Inspection and load testing of cranes, hoists, jibs, gantries.
- **Who performs it:** Qualified crane inspector; in-house operator daily; outside inspector annual.
- **Data captured:** Crane ID, capacity, last inspection date, findings, load test results, certification.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OSHA 1910.179 / MSHA 30 CFR 77.205 (work platforms); ASME B30.2 (overhead and gantry cranes), B30.16 (overhead hoists), B30.21 (lever hoists); annual inspection.
- **Frequency:** Daily pre-use; monthly periodic; annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Inspector → maintenance for repairs → certification posted.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Failed brake test removing crane from service; missing inspection sticker citation; chain falls and lever hoists overlooked.

### 13.3 Welding Equipment & Consumables
- **What it is:** Welders, plasma cutters, gouging equipment, welding rod, MIG wire, flux core wire, gas cylinders.
- **Who performs it:** Welders (CWI-certified for some critical work); welding foreman.
- **Data captured:** Welder ID, last calibration, consumables inventory (rod types — E7018, E11018, hardfacing rod; wire types), gas cylinder inventory (argon, CO2, oxygen, acetylene).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** AWS D1.1 (structural steel), AWS D14.3 (earthmoving construction), CWI certification, MSHA 30 CFR 77.408 (welding around combustible materials), gas cylinder storage per NFPA 55.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Welder → warehouse for consumables → safety for hot work permits.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Rod oven for low-hydrogen rods; certified welder lapsed cert; gas cylinder restraints (chain, cap); hot work near combustibles requires permit and fire watch.

### 13.4 PPE Inventory & Issue Tracking
- **What it is:** Issuing required PPE — hard hats, safety glasses, hearing protection, FR clothing, boots (steel/composite toe, metatarsal), gloves, fall protection, respirators, dust masks, methane detectors.
- **Who performs it:** Warehouse; safety; HR for new hires.
- **Data captured:** Employee, item issued, date, size, replacement cycle, sign-off.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OSHA 1910 Subpart I PPE / MSHA 30 CFR 56/57/72 (UG dust) / 30 CFR 75 (UG safety equipment); ANSI Z89.1 hard hats; ANSI Z87 safety glasses; ASTM F2412/F2413 footwear; NFPA 70E arc-rated for electrical work; respiratory protection per 30 CFR Part 72 and 42 CFR 84.
- **Frequency:** New hire issue; replacement on damage/wear; annual issue of certain items.
- **Hand-offs:** HR → warehouse → safety for fit-testing (respirators).
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Contractor PPE compliance; FR clothing laundering; respirator fit-test (annual); fall protection inspection (per use and periodic per OSHA / MSHA).

### 13.5 Methane Detector / Multi-Gas Meter Management
- **What it is:** Calibration and assignment of personal methane detectors (single gas methanometers) and multi-gas meters (LEL, O2, CO, H2S) for UG.
- **Who performs it:** Mine examiner; safety department; instrument tech.
- **Data captured:** Meter serial, model (MSA Altair, BW GasAlert, Industrial Scientific, RKI Instruments), assigned person, daily bump test results, calibration history, alarm history.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** 30 CFR 75.323 (methane action levels), 30 CFR 75.317/.323/.342 (methane monitors), MSHA Program Information Bulletin on gas detectors; ISA 12 series for hazardous location instruments.
- **Frequency:** Daily bump test (functional test); periodic full calibration (typically monthly).
- **Hand-offs:** Instrument tech → daily issue to mine examiner → return → calibration log.
- **State-specific differences:** State mine inspection examiners require working meters during exam; some states have additional methane meter requirements.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Sensor degradation (typically 2-year life); calibration gas expiry; failure to bump test (cited regularly); battery failures mid-shift.

### 13.6 Truck Scale & Belt Scale Calibration
- **What it is:** Annual certification of truck scales and ongoing calibration of belt scales used for billing tons.
- **Who performs it:** State Weights & Measures; certified scale company (Mettler-Toledo, Cardinal, Fairbanks, Rice Lake, B-TEK); belt scale specialist.
- **Data captured:** Scale ID, last certification date, certifier, accuracy, repair history, test weight or test chain reference.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** NIST Handbook 44; NTEP Certificate of Conformance; state W&M certification; belt scale ASTM E2629 / OIML R107 / state Class III approval.
- **Frequency:** Truck scale annually; belt scale per OEM (monthly material tests typical).
- **Hand-offs:** Certifier → scale operator → loadout/sales billing.
- **State-specific differences:** WV W&M Division; VA VDACS; KY Department of Agriculture W&M; AL W&M; TN Department of Agriculture W&M. Each state's annual seal must be visible.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Cert lapse halts commercial transactions; calibration drift triggers customer billing disputes; belt scale tonnage off pulls revenue.

### 13.7 Calibrated Tool Management (Torque, Pressure, Test Equipment)
- **What it is:** Inventory and calibration of all measurement tools that affect product quality, safety, or compliance.
- **Who performs it:** Calibration tech; outside lab (NIST-traceable).
- **Data captured:** Tool ID, type, range, accuracy, last calibration, next due, calibration certificate.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ISO/IEC 17025 (calibration lab); ANSI/NCSL Z540; NIST traceability.
- **Frequency:** Annual typical; per OEM specs.
- **Hand-offs:** Cal tech → tool users → recall when due.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Out-of-cal tools in use (causes torque-related failures); cal lab turnaround time; in-house cal vs outside cal cost trade-off.

### 13.8 Lab Instrument Calibration
- **What it is:** Calibration of in-house coal quality lab instruments (proximate/ultimate analyzers, calorimeter, ash analyzer, sulfur analyzer, fluorescence, moisture oven, riffler, drying oven balances). See Coal Quality & Lab domain for detail.
- **Who performs it:** Lab manager; instrument vendor service.
- **Data captured:** Instrument, last cal, next cal, control sample results, drift.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ASTM methods (D3172 proximate, D5865 calorimeter, D4239 sulfur, etc.).
- **Frequency:** Per ASTM/OEM.
- **Hand-offs:** Lab → maintenance/vendor for repair.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Linked to Coal Quality domain.

---

## 14. Capital Planning & OEM Relationships

### 14.1 Long-Range Capital Plan (1/3/5 Year)
- **What it is:** Multi-year capital plan covering equipment replacement, major rebuilds, capital improvements, new equipment, capacity expansion.
- **Who performs it:** Engineering; reliability; operations leadership; CFO.
- **Data captured:** Asset, planned year, scope, estimated cost, source of funds, ROI/payback, dependency on other projects, mine plan alignment.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Capital plan; mine plan; LOM (Life of Mine) plan.
- **Frequency:** Annual full update; quarterly review.
- **Hand-offs:** Capital plan → annual budget → AFE process → procurement.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Coal market volatility (capex cancelled / delayed); mine life uncertainty (reserves vs market); long lead times.

### 14.2 Lease vs Buy Analysis
- **What it is:** Evaluating lease (operating or capital) vs purchase for major equipment.
- **Who performs it:** Treasury; CFO; equipment manager.
- **Data captured:** Lease vs buy NPV, tax implications (Section 179, bonus depreciation), cash flow, balance sheet impact (ASC 842), lender covenants.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** FASB ASC 842 (leases — operating and finance distinction); IRS Section 179 and 168(k) bonus depreciation.
- **Frequency:** Per acquisition.
- **Hand-offs:** Treasury → CFO → procurement.
- **State-specific differences:** State personal property tax may differ on leased vs owned.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Operating lease conversion to balance sheet under ASC 842; lessor restrictions on usage; buy-out provisions at end of lease.

### 14.3 OEM Service Contracts (CAT MARC, Komatsu CMMS, Joy Lifecycle)
- **What it is:** Maintenance and Repair Contracts with OEM/dealer providing parts and labor at fixed cost per hour.
- **Who performs it:** Equipment manager; OEM rep; contract admin.
- **Data captured:** Contract terms, included assets, covered scope, fixed price per hour, exclusions, performance guarantees, true-up provisions.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** CAT MARC (Maintenance and Repair Contract); Komatsu KCMS / Komatsu Care; Joy Global / now Komatsu Mining Lifecycle services.
- **Frequency:** Multi-year contract.
- **Hand-offs:** Contract admin → OEM/dealer for service; → AP for monthly invoice.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Scope disputes (covered vs excluded repairs); operator damage claims excluded; OEM tech availability gaps.

### 14.4 Warranty Registration & Claims
- **What it is:** Registering equipment for warranty and managing claims for failures within warranty.
- **Who performs it:** Equipment manager; OEM dealer.
- **Data captured:** Warranty registration date, term (e.g., 2,000 hours or 1 year), failed component, claim submitted, status, settlement.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Warranty terms; warranty claim form per OEM.
- **Frequency:** As needed.
- **Hand-offs:** Equipment manager → OEM dealer → AP credit on settlement.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Warranty denied for operator abuse / lack of PM compliance; claim back-and-forth delays repair; rebuilt component re-warranty disputes.

### 14.5 OEM Technical Bulletins / Recalls / Safety Alerts
- **What it is:** Receiving and acting on OEM-issued technical service bulletins (TSBs), product improvement programs (PIPs), and safety alerts.
- **Who performs it:** Equipment manager / reliability; OEM dealer pushes notifications.
- **Data captured:** Bulletin number, affected models/serials, action required, completion deadline, completion status per asset.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** CAT SIMS (Service Information Management System), Komatsu SiteCare / KomTrax notifications, OEM service bulletin systems.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** OEM → equipment manager → reliability → CMMS WO → execution → record in service history.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Bulletins missed in email; serial-specific applicability confusion; failure to comply voids warranty / liability.

### 14.6 ECM / Firmware / Software Updates
- **What it is:** Updates to engine ECM, machine control software, telematics, drive systems, plant PLCs/SCADA.
- **Who performs it:** OEM tech for engine ECM; in-house controls engineer for plant.
- **Data captured:** Equipment, current firmware version, target version, update date, regression test results.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM software change procedures; plant change management; cyber security (NERC-CIP for utility-connected, ISA-99/IEC 62443 emerging).
- **Frequency:** As released by OEM; major plant updates during turnaround.
- **Hand-offs:** Controls engineer → operations → reliability for performance verification.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Engine ECM updates that change emissions calibration; PLC update causes integration issues; lost backups making rollback impossible; cyber security on internet-connected telematics.

### 14.7 Operator Training (OEM-Led, In-House, Simulator)
- **What it is:** Training operators on new equipment, refreshing skills, simulator training for complex equipment.
- **Who performs it:** OEM trainer; in-house training; simulator vendor (Immersive Technologies, ThoroughTec/CYBERMINE, 5DT).
- **Data captured:** Operator, equipment trained on, training date, OEM-cert / company-cert, refresher due.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** OEM training certificates; MSHA Part 48 (UG and surface miner training) — 8-hour annual refresher; new task training before assignment; MSHA Part 46 for surface mines (less prescriptive than Part 48).
- **Frequency:** New hire; new equipment; annual refresher; after-incident retraining.
- **Hand-offs:** Training → HR records → MSHA 5000-23 forms.
- **State-specific differences:** State annual mine foreman / examiner certification requires CE hours (WV, VA, KY each have specific CE rules for certified persons).
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Operator certified on one model running another; Part 48 vs Part 46 confusion at sites with both; documentation lapses cited.

---

## 15. Downtime Analysis & Reliability Reporting

### 15.1 Downtime Capture & Coding
- **What it is:** Recording every event where equipment is not available, with start/end times and reason codes.
- **Who performs it:** Dispatcher / production foreman; mechanic; operator.
- **Data captured:** Asset, start time, end time, duration, downtime category (scheduled vs unscheduled), cause code (mechanical, electrical, operational, weather, no operator, no haul, fuel/lube, lunch/break, idle).
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Internal downtime taxonomy; some align with industry SMU/AAU/MARC time accounting standards; ASTM E2500/E2700; longwall benchmarking through Coal Age / mining productivity studies.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Downtime log → reliability dashboards → operations reports.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** "Operational" vs "mechanical" disputes between ops and maint; mantrip downtime not captured; downtime overlap on multi-component failures.

### 15.2 MTBF / MTTR Calculation
- **What it is:** Mean Time Between Failures (reliability) and Mean Time To Repair (maintainability) per asset/component.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer.
- **Data captured:** Failure events, time between failures, time to repair.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** ISO 14224; reliability KPIs.
- **Frequency:** Monthly trending.
- **Hand-offs:** Reliability → maintenance management.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Censored data (machine not yet failed); planned vs unplanned commingling; multi-failure events.

### 15.3 Availability, Utilization, Productivity Metrics
- **What it is:** Calendar-based productivity and availability metrics — typically Physical Availability, Use of Availability, Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer; operations analyst.
- **Data captured:** Calendar hours, scheduled hours, available hours, operating hours, productive hours; physical availability = (calendar - mechanical/electrical downtime) / calendar; use of availability = operating / available.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Industry benchmarks (typically 80-90% availability for haul trucks; 90%+ for plant); SMR Inc., Bucyrus availability standards; CAT Performance Handbook.
- **Frequency:** Daily/weekly/monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Reliability → operations → executive reporting.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Definition wars (which buckets count); "delay" coding bias.

### 15.4 Top 10 Bad Actors / Pareto Analysis
- **What it is:** Ranking assets or failure modes by downtime/cost to focus reliability improvement efforts.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer; cross-functional reliability team.
- **Data captured:** Asset/component, total downtime, total cost, count of events, % of total.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Pareto chart; root cause analysis (RCA — 5 Whys, Fishbone, Apollo, TapRoot).
- **Frequency:** Monthly review.
- **Hand-offs:** Reliability → improvement project portfolio.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Same bad actor for years (no real improvement); fixing the wrong thing because data is poor.

### 15.5 Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
- **What it is:** Investigation of significant failures to find root cause and prevent recurrence.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer leads; mechanic, operator, supervisor participate; outside expert for catastrophic.
- **Data captured:** Event description, evidence, timeline, contributing factors, root cause (physical, human, latent), corrective actions, completion verification.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** RCA methodology (5-Why, Apollo, TapRoot, Kepner-Tregoe); company RCA template.
- **Frequency:** Per qualifying event (defined by cost / downtime threshold or any safety-related).
- **Hand-offs:** RCA → corrective actions → tracking to completion.
- **State-specific differences:** Required for any incident involving MSHA reportable injury/fatality.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Stops at "operator error" without deeper why; corrective actions not implemented; RCA report not shared across mines (same failure happens elsewhere).

### 15.6 Cost Per Operating Hour / Cost Per Ton
- **What it is:** Maintenance and total operating cost per hour and per ton mined / processed / loaded.
- **Who performs it:** Cost accountant; reliability engineer.
- **Data captured:** Labor cost, parts cost, contractor cost, fuel cost, tire cost, total cost; operating hours; tons produced; cost/hr and cost/ton.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** Cost report; mine benchmark studies; AME, Wood Mackenzie cost curves.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Cost report → executive → benchmark.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Allocations of shared resources; capital vs expense allocations; "managed" cost reports for executive consumption.

### 15.7 Reliability KPI Dashboards
- **What it is:** Centralized dashboards for maintenance/reliability KPIs.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer; IT (BI tool — Power BI, Tableau, Spotfire, Pi Vision).
- **Data captured:** PM compliance %, schedule compliance %, backlog hours, work type distribution (PM/PdM/CM/Emergency %), MTBF, MTTR, availability, % proactive vs reactive, % planned vs unplanned, % wrench time.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** SMRP best practice metrics (Society for Maintenance & Reliability Professionals); EAM (Enterprise Asset Management) standards.
- **Frequency:** Real-time dashboards; weekly/monthly review.
- **Hand-offs:** Reliability → maintenance leadership → executives.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Dashboards without owners; metrics gamed; targets set politically not statistically.

### 15.8 Benchmarking & External Reporting
- **What it is:** Comparing performance to industry peers via consortia, OEM benchmark programs, SMRP, NMA studies.
- **Who performs it:** Reliability engineer; equipment manager; SMRP/NMA membership.
- **Data captured:** Anonymized fleet metrics submitted; received industry quartile data.
- **Documents / forms / standards:** SMRP body of knowledge; National Mining Association safety/productivity reports.
- **Frequency:** Annual submission and benchmark report.
- **Hand-offs:** Reliability → benchmark provider → executive presentation.
- **State-specific differences:** None.
- **Common edge cases / pain points:** Apples-to-apples definitions; data quality concerns from peers.

---

## 16. Cross-Functional Hand-Offs & Integration Points

### 16.1 Integration: Equipment ↔ Production Reporting
- Hour meter → production system (tons per hour); availability data → production planning; equipment assignment → operator allocation.

### 16.2 Integration: Equipment ↔ Coal Quality & Lab
- Drill chip samples by hole; conveyor sampler equipment in QA; bath density tied to plant equipment performance.

### 16.3 Integration: Equipment ↔ Finance / Fixed Assets
- Capital projects to fixed asset register; depreciation rolls; maintenance expense to GL by asset and cost center; capital vs expense classification.

### 16.4 Integration: Equipment ↔ Safety
- Pre-shift exam findings; defects affecting safety; LOTO permits; lift plans; permits to work; incident investigation tied to equipment history.

### 16.5 Integration: Equipment ↔ Environmental
- Spill reporting tied to fuel/lube; air emissions equipment (engines, dust collectors) tied to permit conditions; equipment used at NPDES outfalls; explosives/blasting tied to vibration monitoring.

### 16.6 Integration: Equipment ↔ HR / Training
- Operator certifications, MSHA training records, mine examiner certifications, electrician certifications, blaster certifications, simulator training.

### 16.7 Integration: Equipment ↔ Permitting / Engineering
- Equipment included in mine plan; vehicles included in haul road design; mainline conveyor in mine plan; ventilation equipment in vent plan.

### 16.8 Integration: Equipment ↔ Procurement
- Item master, vendor master, blanket POs, contract pricing, RFQ-to-PO.

### 16.9 Integration: Equipment ↔ IT / OT
- Telematics, fuel system, plant PLC/SCADA/Historian (Pi, Ignition), CMMS, ERP, BI; cybersecurity.

---

## 17. Common Cross-Cutting Pain Points

1. **Multiple disconnected systems** — CMMS, ERP, fuel system, telematics, fixed asset ledger, scale system, lab LIMS — same equipment has different IDs.
2. **Data quality** — incomplete WO closeouts, generic failure codes, missing oil sample asset info.
3. **Tribal knowledge dependence** — experienced mechanics' know-how never captured.
4. **Hour meter / odometer integrity** — drift, replacement, manual override, telematics outages.
5. **Operations vs Maintenance friction** — equipment release, downtime coding, priority disputes.
6. **MSHA / state inspector readiness** — books current, defects timely corrected, electrical exams complete.
7. **Contractor management** — qualification, insurance, work permits, downtime/cost attribution.
8. **Long lead times** — major components (engines, transmissions, tires), mid-life rebuild planning.
9. **Idle equipment** — falls off PM schedules, deteriorates faster than running equipment.
10. **Fleet vintage diversity** — same role, different OEMs, different ages, different parts.
11. **State variation** — blaster licensing, electrician licensing, tank registrations, scale certifications, severance tax fuel exemptions.
12. **Cost allocation politics** — capital vs expense, inter-mine charges, allocated overhead.
13. **Sustainability / emissions creep** — Tier 4 Final engines, electric/battery UG equipment, methane/GHG reporting.
14. **Cybersecurity of OT** — internet-connected telematics, PLC vulnerabilities, ransomware risk to mine operations.
15. **Workforce shortage** — diesel mechanics, certified mine electricians, longwall millwrights all in shortage; succession planning weak.
