# Domain 5: Finance, Accounting, Tax, Treasury & Audit

# Finance, Accounting, Tax, Treasury & Audit

Scope: Southern Coal Corporation, a privately held multi-entity coal producer operating in WV, VA, KY (and AL/TN), affiliated with the broader Justice family of companies (timber, agriculture, hospitality/Greenbrier). This domain covers the full GL-to-disclosure stack plus the coal-specific layers: severance and AML compliance, ARO/reclamation accrual, depletion, royalty distribution, hedging, bonding, multi-state apportionment, UMWA exposure, and Black Lung Excise Tax.

Verified statutory citations and rates used throughout:
- WV Coal Severance Tax: WV Code Chapter 11, Article 13A; CST-200CU monthly return; standard 5% (4.65% State + 0.35% Local); thin-seam reduced rates 2% (37"-45") and 1% (<37"); WV minimum severance $0.75/ton (W. Va. Code §11-12B-3); Special Reclamation Tax per WV Code §22-3-11.
- KY Coal Severance & Processing Tax: KRS Chapter 143; Form 55A100, monthly, due within 20 days; 4.5% of gross value or $0.50/ton minimum.
- VA Coal Severance: state under §58.1-439 (now repealed for state portion — current rates 1% / 0.75% small mine apply to LOCAL Coal Severance License Tax under §58.1-3741 and Local Coal & Gas Road Improvement Tax under §58.1-3712/3713 imposed by counties).
- Federal AML Reclamation Fee (post-IIJA, FY2022-2034): Surface 22.4¢/ton, Underground 9.6¢/ton, Lignite 6.4¢/ton (or 10% / 10% / 2% of value, whichever less); reported monthly on Form OSM-1.
- Federal Black Lung Excise Tax (IRC §4121, post-IRA 2022 permanent rates): Underground lesser of $1.10/ton or 4.4% of sales price; Surface lesser of $0.55/ton or 4.4%; reported on IRS Form 720 quarterly.

---

## 1. General Ledger & Controllership

### 1.1 Multi-Entity Chart of Accounts (COA)
- **What it is:** Master account structure spanning every Southern Coal legal entity — holding company (typically a Delaware LLC/Inc parent), state operating subsidiaries (separate per state for severance/income tax planning), mine-level LLCs per permit, services entity (equipment rental, labor pooling), land-holding entities, and family-pass-through entities tied to Justice ownership.
- **Who performs:** Corporate Controller (owner); Assistant Controller (mine/site books); Accounting Manager (intercompany).
- **Data captured:** Account number, account name, entity code, mine cost center, department, project/AFE, account type, FS line, tax-line mapping (UltraTax/CCH/Lacerte), eliminations flag, intercompany flag, statutory mapping (GAAP vs tax vs lender), inactive date.
- **Documents/forms:** COA master, account add/change request, COA mapping crosswalk (entity-to-consolidation), entity legal-structure diagram, EIN register.
- **Frequency:** Continuous maintenance; full annual review at Q4 close.
- **Hand-offs:** Tax (apportionment), Treasury (bank-to-entity map), IT (ERP setup), Legal (entity registry).
- **State differences:** Each state mine often sits in its own LLC because (a) WV severance & B&O tax compute at entity level, (b) KY county distributions track per-entity, (c) VA local severance is by county/city, requiring per-mine entity for clean local reporting.
- **Edge cases:** Mid-year entity mergers (post-acquisition), pass-through allocations to multiple Justice family members (K-1 splits), reactivation of dormant permit entities, intercompany shared services charged at "cost-plus" requiring transfer pricing documentation.

### 1.2 Mine Cost Center Structure
- **What it is:** Hierarchy capturing each producing mine, prep plant, loadout, refuse area, support shop, and admin function as a discrete cost center for production cost-per-ton reporting.
- **Who performs:** Cost Accounting Manager; Mine Accountant per site.
- **Data captured:** Cost center code, mine ID, permit number, MSHA Mine ID, prep plant ID, loadout ID, status (active/idle/reclaim), GL roll-up, FERC/permit linkage.
- **Documents/forms:** Cost center master, mine operating plan, monthly cost-per-ton report.
- **Frequency:** Set up at mine commissioning, updated on idle/reactivate events, reviewed at budget.
- **Hand-offs:** Operations (production data tie-out), Engineering (mine plan), Tax (severance by mine), Royalty (lease-to-cost-center map).
- **State differences:** WV per-mine cost separation needed for thin-seam severance certification; KY per-mine needed for county distribution; VA per-mine needed for local severance.
- **Edge cases:** Multi-seam mines mining both severance-rate brackets concurrently (must split tons by seam and cost center), shared prep plant feeding multiple permits.

### 1.3 Job Cost / Activity Cost Accounting
- **What it is:** Tracking labor, materials, equipment burden, contractor cost, and overhead by activity (development, mining, hauling, prep, loadout, reclamation in progress).
- **Who performs:** Cost Accountant; Mine Foreman (time charging).
- **Data captured:** Job code, activity code, MSHA section ID, shift, employee ID, equipment ID, fuel gallons, supplies issued, contractor invoice tag.
- **Documents/forms:** Daily production report (DPR), shift labor distribution, activity time sheets, equipment hour cards.
- **Frequency:** Daily capture; monthly close; quarterly variance.
- **Hand-offs:** Payroll (labor distribution), AP (vendor charges to job), FP&A (variance analysis), Operations.
- **State differences:** None directly; differences flow through severance and royalty.
- **Edge cases:** Contract miner cost (full turnkey vs cost-plus), capitalized vs expensed development at long-life UG mines, idle mine carrying-cost capitalization rules.

### 1.4 Intercompany Transactions
- **What it is:** Shared services billings, intercompany loans, transfer pricing for equipment/leases between SC entities and to/from Justice-affiliated entities (timber, ag, Greenbrier).
- **Who performs:** Accounting Manager — Intercompany; Controller.
- **Data captured:** Originating entity, receiving entity, IC GL pair, service description, basis (cost, cost-plus markup, market), interest rate on IC notes, IC AR/AP aging, settlement schedule.
- **Documents/forms:** IC service agreements, IC promissory notes, transfer pricing study (IRC §482), IC settlement journal.
- **Frequency:** Monthly billing and settlement; transfer pricing study annual refresh.
- **Hand-offs:** Tax (apportionment, §482), Audit, Treasury (cash settlement), Legal.
- **State differences:** WV add-back rules for intercompany interest/royalty; KY and VA combined-reporting impact; mining services charged across state lines create nexus questions.
- **Edge cases:** Cross-industry IC (coal entity buys lumber from Justice timber entity), zero-interest IC loans triggering IRC §7872 imputed interest, related-party reclamation surety indemnity.

### 1.5 Eliminations
- **What it is:** Removal of IC P&L and B/S balances on consolidation, including IC profit in inventory.
- **Who performs:** Consolidation Accountant; Controller (review).
- **Data captured:** Elimination JE detail, IC balance tie-out grid, IC profit in inventory calc.
- **Documents/forms:** Elimination workbook, consolidation worksheet, intercompany matching report.
- **Frequency:** Monthly with close.
- **Hand-offs:** Audit, FP&A, Lender reporting.
- **State differences:** WV and KY require separate-entity returns despite federal consolidation, so elims appear only in consolidated lender package.
- **Edge cases:** IC equipment transfers where book vs tax basis diverge, IC coal sales (mine entity sells to sales entity that resells to customer), services entity Cost-of-Sales true-ups.

### 1.6 Consolidated Reporting (GAAP / Modified-GAAP / Lender)
- **What it is:** Preparation of consolidated FS — Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Cash Flows, Equity, Notes — under US GAAP plus parallel views (cash-basis for owners, modified-GAAP for lender covenants, EBITDA bridge).
- **Who performs:** Controller; External auditor (review/audit).
- **Data captured:** Trial balance per entity, FX (rare), eliminations, consolidating adjustments, ARO movement, depletion, depreciation, hedge OCI, deferred tax, UMWA contingent liability disclosures.
- **Documents/forms:** Consolidated FS package, footnote disclosures (ASC 410-20 ARO, ASC 815 hedging, ASC 280 segments, ASC 842 leases, ASC 715/715-80 multiemployer pension, ASC 606 revenue, going-concern memo if applicable), MD&A for lender.
- **Frequency:** Monthly internal, quarterly full package, annual audit.
- **Hand-offs:** Bank/lender, Surety, Tax (book-to-tax), Owners.
- **State differences:** N/A at consolidated level; per-entity FS required for state filings.
- **Edge cases:** Pushdown accounting on acquisitions, fresh-start accounting (post-bankruptcy of certain affiliates), going-concern qualifications during price downturns, related-party transactions disclosure across Justice family.

### 1.7 Monthly Close (Calendar)
- **What it is:** Structured close calendar typically WD-5 to WD-10 for coal companies given production cutoff timing.
- **Who performs:** Controller (owner); all accounting subteams.
- **Data captured:** Close checklist status, JE list, account reconciliations, flux analysis, sign-offs.
- **Documents/forms:** Close calendar, JE log, recon binder, flux memo, balance-sheet review, management close package.
- **Frequency:** Monthly; abbreviated mid-quarter; expanded at quarter and year-end.
- **Hand-offs:** All departments feed in; FP&A consumes for reporting.
- **State differences:** Severance return due dates pull severance accruals into pre-close; KY 20-day deadline on 55A100 most aggressive.
- **Edge cases:** Production cutoff mismatch (last shift of month spans into new month), in-transit coal title transfer timing, prep plant yield true-ups, mine idled mid-month.

### 1.8 Bank Reconciliations
- **What it is:** Tie GL cash to bank statement for every account (operating, payroll, lockbox, escrow, reclamation trust, captive insurance).
- **Who performs:** Staff Accountant or Treasury Analyst.
- **Data captured:** Outstanding checks, deposits in transit, bank fees, interest, NSF, wire memo posting, positive pay exceptions.
- **Documents/forms:** Bank statement, GL cash detail, recon workpaper, stale-check report.
- **Frequency:** Monthly minimum; daily for primary operating.
- **Hand-offs:** AP (stale checks → escheat), Treasury (sweep), Audit.
- **State differences:** Reclamation trust accounts in KY (KY Bond Pool) and other state-mandated trusts must be reconciled and reported to state.
- **Edge cases:** Lockbox timing differences, multi-bank cash pooling, ZBA child accounts, dormant accounts at idled mines.

### 1.9 Inventory Reconciliations (Coal Inventory)
- **What it is:** Reconcile perpetual coal tons (raw, clean, refuse) at each location (mine stockpile, prep feed, prep clean, loadout, in-transit rail/barge) to physical surveys and to sales/production.
- **Who performs:** Cost Accountant; Surveyor (third-party stockpile surveys).
- **Data captured:** Tons by location and product, BTU/quality grade, ash, sulfur, moisture, survey date, density factor, GL value at production cost.
- **Documents/forms:** Stockpile survey report (drone/LiDAR/GPS), perpetual inventory ledger, yield reconciliation, shrinkage/loss journal.
- **Frequency:** Daily perpetual; monthly book-to-perpetual; quarterly or semiannual physical survey.
- **Hand-offs:** Tax (severance is at first point of sale — inventory timing matters), Operations, Sales (specs).
- **State differences:** WV severance taxes coal at "value at first point of sale" — stockpile aging until sale defers severance liability. KY similar. VA local severance assessed similarly.
- **Edge cases:** Refuse re-mining/coal recovery, wash-plant yield drift, weather-related moisture swings, mid-month price moves affecting LCM/NRV write-down.

### 1.10 Fixed Asset Reconciliation
- **What it is:** Sub-ledger tie to GL for mining equipment (continuous miners, longwalls, shuttle cars, draglines, shovels, haul trucks, prep plant equipment, conveyors, rail loadout) plus capitalized mine development.
- **Who performs:** Fixed Asset Accountant; Plant Engineer (asset tagging).
- **Data captured:** Asset ID, serial, location/mine, in-service date, useful life, salvage, depreciation method (book vs tax), accumulated depreciation, disposals, transfers, impairment indicators.
- **Documents/forms:** FA roll-forward, depreciation report, CIP (construction-in-progress) detail, AFE close-out, gain/loss on disposal.
- **Frequency:** Monthly roll-forward; annual physical inventory.
- **Hand-offs:** Tax (179/bonus/MACRS), Insurance (property values for COPE statement), Operations (asset transfers), Audit.
- **State differences:** Personal property tax filings (WV, KY, VA) all county-level using cost or trended-cost — FA register feeds returns; KY has special unmined minerals separate from FA.
- **Edge cases:** Componentization of longwall systems, mine-specific tooling (cutters, bits) expensed vs capitalized, equipment moves between states (apportionment), idle equipment held for sale, repair vs improvement determination under TPR §1.263(a)-3.

### 1.11 Lessor Royalty Payable Reconciliation
- **What it is:** Tie royalty sub-ledger (per lease, per lessor) to GL accrued royalties and to actual payments made.
- **Who performs:** Royalty Accountant.
- **Data captured:** Lease ID, lessor party, royalty rate, tons mined per lease, gross value, allowed deductions, severance pass-through, net royalty owed, suspense balance.
- **Documents/forms:** Royalty statement, suspense ledger, lease abstract.
- **Frequency:** Monthly accrual; monthly or quarterly payments per lease terms.
- **Hand-offs:** AP (payment), Tax (1099 box 2), Land/Lease module.
- **State differences:** WV severance often passed-through to lessor (lease specifies "of value before severance" or "net of severance"); KY allows similar; VA leases vary; federal coal under ONRR has its own royalty regime.
- **Edge cases:** Heir splits (single lessor estate now 40+ heirs), undivided interest leases, escheated/unclaimed royalty, lessor audit demands, minimum/advance royalty recoupment.

### 1.12 Severance Tax Payable Reconciliation
- **What it is:** Tie severance accrual GL to filed returns (WV CST-200CU, KY 55A100, VA local 800-series, AML OSM-1, BLET 720).
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; Controller (review).
- **Data captured:** Tons by state, by mine, by seam (thin-seam flag), gross value, deductions, tax rates applied, payments, late-fee/interest.
- **Documents/forms:** Tax accrual workbook, return copies, payment confirmations, prior-period adjustments.
- **Frequency:** Monthly accrual and reconciliation.
- **Hand-offs:** Tax filing team, Treasury (payment), Operations (tonnage).
- **State differences:** WV CST-200CU monthly with annual reconciliation; KY 55A100 monthly within 20 days; VA local taxes filed county-by-county; AML OSM-1 monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Thin-seam certification retroactive adjustments, gross-value disputes with auditor, tax incentive (e.g., waste-coal credit) timing, refund claims from federal off-road diesel.

### 1.13 Cutoff Procedures
- **What it is:** Ensure production tons, sales tons, royalty, severance, and AP align to correct period.
- **Who performs:** Controller; Cost Accountant; Sales Accountant.
- **Data captured:** Last shift production timestamp, last shipment BOL date, last invoice date, in-transit title cutoff, cutoff JEs.
- **Documents/forms:** Cutoff testing checklist, post-close adjustment log.
- **Frequency:** Monthly at close.
- **Hand-offs:** Audit, Tax.
- **Edge cases:** FOB origin shipments crossing midnight, demurrage starting in prior month, quality samples not yet returned at cutoff (estimated price adjustments).

---

## 2. Accounts Payable

### 2.1 Vendor Master Maintenance
- **What it is:** Onboarding and ongoing maintenance of vendors with W-9 collection, 1099 flag, ACH banking, COI status, tax-id verification (TIN match).
- **Who performs:** AP Supervisor; Vendor Master Analyst.
- **Data captured:** Legal name, DBA, TIN, address, contact, payment terms, default GL, 1099 type, ACH/check, banking, COI expiry, MSHA Part 45 contractor ID for mine-site contractors, OFAC/sanction check.
- **Documents/forms:** Form W-9, ACH authorization, COI, Vendor Add Form, banking change validation (callback).
- **Frequency:** On add; annual review.
- **Hand-offs:** Tax (1099), Safety (contractor MSHA compliance), Risk (COI), Treasury (ACH).
- **State differences:** WV/KY/VA non-resident lessor withholding rules may trigger different tax-flag setup.
- **Edge cases:** Sole-proprietor royalty payees, deceased lessors paid through estate, vendor banking-change fraud attempts.

### 2.2 Invoice Receipt
- **What it is:** Capture of invoices from paper mail, vendor email, vendor portal, EDI, OCR.
- **Who performs:** AP Clerk; AP Automation (OCR/IDP system).
- **Data captured:** Vendor, invoice #, date, PO #, amount, tax, line detail, GL coding.
- **Documents/forms:** Invoice image, OCR extract, exception queue.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Three-way match, approval routing.
- **Edge cases:** Multi-PO invoices, freight-only invoices, mine-site direct invoices (no PO), parts ordered to support stock vs job-charged.

### 2.3 Three-Way Match
- **What it is:** PO + Goods Receipt + Invoice match within tolerance for price and quantity.
- **Who performs:** AP Clerk (auto-match), Buyer (resolve exceptions).
- **Data captured:** PO header, line, receipt, invoice, match status, variance reason.
- **Documents/forms:** Match exception report.
- **Frequency:** Daily.
- **Hand-offs:** Purchasing (PO correction), Receiving, AP.
- **Edge cases:** Partial receipts, blanket POs with releases, freight added to invoice not on PO, rebill on warranty replacement.

### 2.4 Approval Workflow (DOA — Delegation of Authority)
- **What it is:** Routing of invoices and POs through approvers based on amount, category, GL/cost center, AFE.
- **Who performs:** Approvers per DOA; AP Supervisor (queue management).
- **Data captured:** Approver, approval timestamp, amount, escalation trail.
- **Documents/forms:** DOA matrix, approval audit log.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Controller (out-of-policy escalation).
- **Edge cases:** Delegated approval during PTO, emergency parts approval at mine site outside policy, AFE-related vs run-rate categorization.

### 2.5 Discount Capture
- **What it is:** Take vendor early-pay discounts (2/10 net 30) where capital cost permits.
- **Who performs:** AP Manager; Treasury (cash position decision).
- **Data captured:** Discount terms, eligible date, captured/missed.
- **Frequency:** Each pay run.
- **Hand-offs:** Treasury.
- **Edge cases:** Forced cash conservation during downturn means missing discounts intentionally.

### 2.6 Payment Runs (ACH, Check, Wire)
- **What it is:** Scheduled disbursement runs by method; large/urgent payments via wire.
- **Who performs:** AP Manager (queue); Treasury (release/wire approval).
- **Data captured:** Payment batch, vendor, amount, GL hit, bank account, reference.
- **Documents/forms:** Positive pay file, ACH file (NACHA format), wire approval form (dual-control).
- **Frequency:** Weekly checks/ACH; daily wires as needed.
- **Hand-offs:** Bank.
- **Edge cases:** Same-day wire for surety/bonding posting, royalty checks needing physical printing for heirs, joint payee on liens.

### 2.7 Positive Pay File Generation (Fraud Control)
- **What it is:** Transmit issued-check file to bank daily so bank pays only matching items.
- **Who performs:** AP Manager; Treasury.
- **Frequency:** Daily after print.
- **Edge cases:** Voids after transmit, manual checks issued at mine site needing add-on file.

### 2.8 Vendor Statement Reconciliation
- **What it is:** Compare vendor statement to AP open items quarterly for major vendors.
- **Who performs:** AP Clerk; AP Supervisor.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly / on dispute.
- **Edge cases:** Mining-supply distributor with multiple ship-to mines, fuel supplier with daily deliveries.

### 2.9 1099-MISC / 1099-NEC Year-End
- **What it is:** Issue 1099-NEC (contractors), 1099-MISC (royalty box 2, attorney box 10, rents box 1) annually.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; AP Manager.
- **Data captured:** TIN, name, address, total payments by box, withholding (if backup or non-resident).
- **Documents/forms:** 1099-NEC, 1099-MISC, 1096 transmittal, IRS FIRE/IRIS electronic filing, state copies.
- **Frequency:** Annual; Jan 31 (NEC) / Mar 31 (MISC e-file).
- **State differences:** WV, KY, VA all participate in CF/SF or require separate state file; KY non-resident lessor 6% withholding (KRS 141.206 for partners; lease-specific for royalty); WV non-resident withholding considerations.
- **Edge cases:** Royalty paid to estate vs heir, attorney settlements box 10, payments split between NEC and MISC for same payee, TIN mismatch (B-Notice).

### 2.10 Escheatment / Unclaimed Property
- **What it is:** Identify, due-diligence, and report unclaimed checks (royalty, vendor, payroll) to states.
- **Who performs:** AP/Royalty Accountant; Tax (filing).
- **Data captured:** Owner name, last address, amount, date issued, due-diligence letter sent, escheat year.
- **Documents/forms:** State unclaimed property reports (WV, KY, VA); due-diligence letters.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **State differences:** WV (3-year dormancy typical), KY (3-year), VA (3-year for wages, 5 for general intangibles); reporting deadlines vary (Nov 1 for KY, etc.).
- **Edge cases:** Royalty held in suspense vs escheatable, heir trace before escheat, multi-state lessors (state of last known address controls).

### 2.11 Non-Resident Lessor Withholding
- **What it is:** Withhold and remit income tax on royalty paid to non-resident individuals/entities in producing state.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; AP.
- **Data captured:** Lessor residency, withholding rate, amount withheld, remittance.
- **Documents/forms:** State withholding returns; year-end 1099 with state withholding box; W-8 or W-9.
- **Frequency:** Monthly or quarterly remit; annual reconciliation.
- **State differences:** KY pass-through withholding under KRS 141.206; WV non-resident composite considerations; VA similar.
- **Edge cases:** Treaty claims, partnership-tier withholding cascades, election to file composite return covering all non-residents.

---

## 3. Accounts Receivable

### 3.1 Customer Master, Credit Applications, Credit Limits
- **What it is:** Onboard customer with credit application, financial review, set credit limit and terms.
- **Who performs:** Credit Manager; Sales (intake); Controller (high-limit approval).
- **Data captured:** Customer legal entity, DUNS, credit score (D&B), trade references, financial statements, parent guarantee, credit limit, payment terms, ship-to locations.
- **Documents/forms:** Credit app, credit memo, customer master form.
- **Frequency:** On onboarding; annual review; ad hoc on payment events.
- **Edge cases:** Foreign customer (met coal export), utility with state-regulated rates, customer in financial distress (Murray-type bankruptcy precedent).

### 3.2 Sales Contract → Shipment → Invoice Generation
- **What it is:** Take signed contract, schedule shipments, generate invoice on each shipment unit (railcar, barge, vessel) at contract pricing.
- **Who performs:** AR Billing Clerk; Sales Admin (contract entry); Logistics (BOL).
- **Data captured:** Contract #, customer, product (compliance/PCI/etc.), specs, base price, escalators/de-escalators, ship date, BOL, tons by car/barge, FOB point, freight terms.
- **Documents/forms:** Sales contract, BOL, weight certificate (railroad scale or barge survey), quality certificate, customer invoice, freight invoice.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; per shipment unit.
- **Hand-offs:** Logistics, Quality (sample lab), Tax (severance value calc).
- **State differences:** Severance base derives from invoice value; lower invoice (lower-grade coal) = lower severance.
- **Edge cases:** Spot vs term contracts, take-or-pay contracts, met vs thermal mix, blended product, export FOB vessel pricing tied to API2/Newcastle.

### 3.3 Quality Adjustments to Invoice
- **What it is:** Premium/penalty on each shipment vs contract spec for BTU, ash, sulfur, moisture, volatile matter, HGI, FSI (met).
- **Who performs:** AR Billing; Quality/Lab Manager (results); Sales.
- **Data captured:** Contract spec, actual analysis (proximate + ultimate + ash fusion), penalty/premium formula, adjustment $/ton, dispute status (umpire sample).
- **Documents/forms:** Lab certificate of analysis, umpire/referee sample report, credit/debit memo, quality settlement.
- **Frequency:** Per shipment; trued up monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Sample dispute → umpire lab; multi-month rolling average specs (steel mill contracts); rejection rights if outside outer limit; variable consideration estimate at recognition under ASC 606.

### 3.4 Demurrage / Detention Billings to Customer
- **What it is:** Bill customer for railcar/barge/vessel hold time beyond contract free time.
- **Who performs:** Logistics; AR Billing.
- **Data captured:** Equipment ID, free time start/end, demurrage rate, charges.
- **Documents/forms:** Demurrage invoice, supporting rail/barge timeline.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Carrier vs customer fault, force majeure, weather, joint demurrage where multiple parties contribute.

### 3.5 Collections Workflow, Aging, Dunning
- **What it is:** Active collections via aging cycle, dunning letters, holds on shipments.
- **Who performs:** Collections Specialist; Credit Manager.
- **Data captured:** Aging buckets (current, 30, 60, 90+), call notes, promise-to-pay, hold flag.
- **Documents/forms:** Aging report, dunning letters, collection log.
- **Frequency:** Weekly review; monthly aging.
- **Edge cases:** Customer dispute over quality, freight, demurrage; net-settlement against penalty refund; bankruptcy filing.

### 3.6 Customer Concentration Tracking
- **What it is:** Monitor % of revenue and AR from top customers for risk and lender reporting.
- **Who performs:** Credit Manager; Controller; FP&A.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Lender covenant on concentration, customer parent rollups, customer-specific reclamation indemnity exposure.

### 3.7 Bad Debt / Write-Off / Allowance
- **What it is:** Estimate allowance for doubtful accounts (CECL post-ASC 326) and write-off uncollectible.
- **Who performs:** Controller; Credit Manager.
- **Documents/forms:** Allowance computation, write-off memo with approvals, bankruptcy claim file.
- **Frequency:** Monthly allowance; ad hoc write-off.
- **Edge cases:** Customer bankruptcy preference clawback, reclamation indemnity offset, factor recourse.

### 3.8 Letters of Credit / Parent Guarantees from Customers
- **What it is:** Credit support from weaker customers — bank LC or corporate guarantee.
- **Who performs:** Credit Manager; Treasury.
- **Documents/forms:** Customer LC, guarantee agreement, LC expiration tracker.
- **Frequency:** Annual renewal.
- **Edge cases:** LC draw mechanics, evergreen vs fixed term, guarantor credit deterioration mid-term.

### 3.9 Factoring / AR Financing
- **What it is:** Sell AR to factor for cash; common in stressed coal periods.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; Controller.
- **Data captured:** Factored receivables, advance rate, fee, recourse vs non-recourse, true-sale opinion.
- **Frequency:** As funded.
- **Edge cases:** ABL borrowing-base interaction (factored AR usually excluded), customer notification ("notice" factoring), repurchase of disputed AR.

---

## 4. Payroll (PEO / Provider Interface)

### 4.1 Classification (Hourly / Salary / Union / Non-Union)
- **What it is:** Maintain classification, pay rate, union local, work location, mine ID for every employee.
- **Who performs:** Payroll Manager; HR.
- **Data captured:** Employee ID, classification, MSHA Part 50 reportable flag, mine ID, hourly rate, salary, union local code, CBA wage scale tier.
- **Frequency:** On hire; per CBA wage step.
- **Edge cases:** Salaried employee working underground triggers MSHA Part 48 training tracking; pattern crew vs production crew distinctions.

### 4.2 Mine-By-Mine Payroll
- **What it is:** Distribute labor by mine for severance/cost reporting and multi-state withholding.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Cost Accounting.
- **Data captured:** Hours by mine, by activity, by shift; work state for withholding.
- **Documents/forms:** Time card, labor distribution report.
- **Frequency:** Per pay cycle.
- **State differences:** WV/KY/VA all have reciprocity nuances; KY and WV have full reciprocity for residents working in the other state (file in resident state only) with appropriate exemption certificates (KY form 42A809; WV/KY/VA reciprocal agreements).
- **Edge cases:** Employee working at mines in multiple states in one pay period, work-from-home admin employee in different state.

### 4.3 Union vs Non-Union Pay and Benefits
- **What it is:** Apply CBA wage scale, vacation, sick, pension contribution, H&W contribution.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Union Relations / HR.
- **Data captured:** CBA classification, hours worked, hours toward benefit accrual, pension contribution per hour worked.
- **Documents/forms:** CBA wage scale, UMWA benefit reports.
- **Frequency:** Each pay cycle; monthly fund remittance.
- **Edge cases:** Successor obligations on acquired union mines, partial-withdrawal liability triggers when union headcount drops.

### 4.4 Overtime / Sunday / Holiday / Call-Out Premiums
- **What it is:** Apply premium pay per CBA or FLSA.
- **Who performs:** Payroll.
- **Edge cases:** 8/80 rule, Sunday premium per CBA, FLSA overtime calc on production bonus, on-call vs call-out distinctions.

### 4.5 Per Diem
- **What it is:** Non-taxable per diem for travel to remote mines or training.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; AP (if reimbursement).
- **Documents/forms:** Travel auth, per-diem schedule (IRS or GSA).
- **Edge cases:** Long-term assignment (>1 year) becomes taxable.

### 4.6 Bonus Accruals
- **What it is:** Production bonus (tons/yield), safety bonus (accident-free hours), retention bonus.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Operations (calc data); HR.
- **Frequency:** Accrued monthly, paid per plan.
- **Edge cases:** Safety bonus clawback on MSHA citation, production bonus FLSA recalc.

### 4.7 401(k), HSA, FSA Contributions
- **What it is:** Pre-tax deductions remitted to record-keepers.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Benefits.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 5500 (annual), nondiscrimination testing.
- **Edge cases:** Union vs non-union plan separation.

### 4.8 Workers Comp Class Code Mapping
- **What it is:** Map each employee to NCCI/state class code for premium calc.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Risk.
- **Documents/forms:** NCCI class code list (1005 UG mining, 1016 surface, others), state rate sheets.
- **Frequency:** On hire / role change; annual premium audit.
- **State differences:** WV (BrickStreet/Encova privatized but state retains residual), KY (KEMI or commercial), VA (commercial market).
- **Edge cases:** Misclassification audit findings, multi-state employee split coding.

### 4.9 Multi-State SUI Experience Rates
- **What it is:** Track and apply each state's SUI rate to wages up to that state's wage base.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Tax.
- **Documents/forms:** Annual rate notices (WV Workforce, KY OUI, VA VEC).
- **Frequency:** Annual rate update.
- **Edge cases:** SUTA dumping rules on entity restructuring, joint account elections.

### 4.10 Multi-State Withholding (Residency vs Work Location)
- **What it is:** Apply correct state income tax withholding based on residence/work and reciprocal agreements.
- **Who performs:** Payroll.
- **State differences:** KY-WV-VA-IN-OH reciprocal agreement combinations; KY and WV have reciprocity (KY 42A809; WV WV/IT-104R); VA has reciprocity with KY, WV, PA, DC, MD; resident must file exemption form to avoid work-state withholding.
- **Edge cases:** Mid-year residency change, dual-state work (engineer travels among mines).

### 4.11 Garnishments / Child Support
- **What it is:** Process court-ordered withholdings.
- **Who performs:** Payroll.
- **Documents/forms:** Income Withholding Order (IWO), state disbursement unit remit.
- **Edge cases:** Multiple orders priority, CCPA limits, multi-state child support enforcement.

### 4.12 Direct Deposit / Pay Cards
- **What it is:** Distribute net pay electronically.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Treasury.
- **Edge cases:** State pay-card consent rules, prenote failures, fraudulent banking change attempts.

### 4.13 W-2 Year-End
- **What it is:** Annual wage statement to employees and SSA.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Tax.
- **Documents/forms:** W-2, W-3, state W-2 copies; due Jan 31.
- **Edge cases:** Box 12 codes (DD healthcare cost, D 401k), Box 14 union dues, multi-state W-2 splits.

### 4.14 ACA Reporting (1095-C)
- **What it is:** Report offers of MEC to ALEs' employees.
- **Who performs:** Benefits; Payroll.
- **Documents/forms:** 1094-C, 1095-C; due March 2 to employees, March 31 e-file IRS.
- **Edge cases:** Variable-hour miners (long-cycle measurement), COBRA coding, retiree-only plan exclusion.

---

## 5. Treasury / Cash Management

### 5.1 Multi-Bank Account Map
- **What it is:** Inventory of every bank account by entity, purpose (operating, payroll, lockbox, escrow, reclamation trust, captive), authorized signers, online banking access.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; Treasury Analyst.
- **Data captured:** Bank, account #, entity, purpose, signers, balance, fees, sweep target.
- **Documents/forms:** Bank account inventory; signature cards; KYC packages.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly review.
- **Edge cases:** Reclamation trust accounts held by surety/state; captive insurance trust; UMWA H&W payable accounts.

### 5.2 Daily Cash Position
- **What it is:** Consolidate prior-day balances and project today's net cash.
- **Who performs:** Treasury Analyst.
- **Data captured:** Beginning balance, expected receipts (lockbox, ACH), expected disbursements (AP run, payroll, tax, royalty), revolver borrowing decision.
- **Documents/forms:** Daily cash report; revolver borrowing/paydown instruction.
- **Frequency:** Daily AM.
- **Edge cases:** Wire cutoff timing, customer wire arrival window, month-end royalty + severance + AP convergence.

### 5.3 Cash Forecasting (13-Week Rolling)
- **What it is:** Weekly direct-method cash forecast for next 13 weeks.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; FP&A.
- **Data captured:** AR receipts by customer/contract, AP by vendor category, payroll, taxes (federal payroll, AML monthly, severance monthly), royalty, debt service, capex, hedge margin.
- **Documents/forms:** 13-week forecast model; variance to actuals.
- **Frequency:** Weekly.
- **Edge cases:** Customer slow-pay events, surety collateral calls, hedge margin calls in volatile periods.

### 5.4 Borrowing Base Certificate (ABL Revolver)
- **What it is:** Calculate eligible AR + eligible inventory * advance rates to determine revolver availability.
- **Who performs:** Treasury; Controller.
- **Data captured:** Eligible AR (excl >90d, foreign, concentration, intercompany), eligible coal inventory (with NRV cap), reserves (priority payables, royalties, severance, rent, in-transit), advance rates, current borrowings, availability.
- **Documents/forms:** Borrowing Base Certificate (BBC) per credit agreement; supporting schedules; field exam findings.
- **Frequency:** Monthly (some weekly during downturn).
- **Edge cases:** Customer dispute reduces eligibility, in-transit coal under FOB origin still counts as inventory, surety bonding reserves, dilution roll-rate adjustments.

### 5.5 Letters of Credit
- **What it is:** Issued LCs for surety collateral, utility deposits, customer requirements; tracked for expiry and exposure.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer.
- **Data captured:** LC #, beneficiary, amount, expiry, issuing bank, collateral, fee.
- **Frequency:** Annual renewal.
- **Edge cases:** Auto-renewal vs expiry, draw mechanics, replacement with cash collateral.

### 5.6 Foreign Exchange
- **What it is:** FX management for export met coal proceeds (often USD-denominated FOB origin, but freight/vessel sometimes in other currency) and equipment imports (German/Polish longwall).
- **Who performs:** Treasurer.
- **Edge cases:** EUR/USD on Caterpillar/Eickhoff equipment, GBP on insurance, hedging via forwards.

### 5.7 Investment of Excess Cash
- **What it is:** Sweep balances to MMF, treasuries, repo.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer.
- **Documents/forms:** Investment policy, broker statements.
- **Edge cases:** Insurance company captive cash investment under domiciliary regulator rules; restricted cash in reclamation trust.

### 5.8 Bank Fee Analysis
- **What it is:** Review monthly account analysis statements (AFP service codes) for fee accuracy and optimization.
- **Who performs:** Treasury Analyst.
- **Frequency:** Monthly; annual benchmarking.

### 5.9 Banking Relationships / KYC
- **What it is:** Annual KYC refresh, beneficial ownership reporting (BOI under CTA — though enforcement evolving), bank relationship reviews.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; Legal.
- **Documents/forms:** KYC questionnaire, beneficial owner list, corporate authority resolutions.
- **Edge cases:** Justice family ownership complexity; CTA reporting changes; FinCEN inquiries.

---

## 6. Debt / Capital Structure

### 6.1 Revolver Tracking
- **What it is:** Track drawn balance, available, interest accrual on ABL revolver.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer.
- **Data captured:** Borrowings, paydowns, SOFR base + spread, LC sublimit, swing line, undrawn fee.
- **Frequency:** Daily.
- **Edge cases:** SOFR transition mechanics, cash-dominion triggers, springing lockbox events.

### 6.2 Term Loans / Notes / Equipment Financing
- **What it is:** Amortization schedule maintenance, interest accrual, payment processing for term debt and equipment loans.
- **Who performs:** Treasury Accountant.
- **Data captured:** Original principal, balance, rate, payment schedule, lender, security, prepayment terms.
- **Documents/forms:** Loan agreements, amortization schedules.
- **Edge cases:** Equipment lease vs loan classification (ASC 842 vs ASC 840 legacy), refinancing modification accounting (ASC 470-50 / TDR).

### 6.3 Capital Lease / Operating Lease Obligations (ASC 842)
- **What it is:** Right-of-use asset and lease liability for equipment leases.
- **Who performs:** Lease Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Lease abstract, ROU rollforward, discount rate file.
- **Edge cases:** Mining leases generally excluded from ASC 842 scope as leases of mineral rights; minimum royalties may need separate analysis.

### 6.4 Reclamation Surety / Bonding Lines
- **What it is:** Surety credit facility separate from operating debt for posting reclamation bonds.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; Risk Manager; Surety relationship.
- **Documents/forms:** Surety facility agreement, indemnity agreement, collateral pledges, bond schedule.
- **Edge cases:** Surety collateral step-up demands during downturn, replacement surety on cancellation.

### 6.5 Covenant Compliance
- **What it is:** Calculate and certify financial covenants (Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio, Leverage Ratio, EBITDA, minimum liquidity, capex limits, springing covenants).
- **Who performs:** Controller; CFO; Treasurer.
- **Documents/forms:** Compliance Certificate, supporting calc workbook, board package.
- **Frequency:** Monthly (springing FCCR), quarterly (full covenant).
- **Edge cases:** Add-backs (ARO accretion, stock comp, non-cash hedge MTM, restructuring), pro-forma EBITDA for acquisitions, waiver requests, equity cure.

### 6.6 Interest Accruals / Payments
- **What it is:** Accrue interest at month-end and process scheduled payments.
- **Who performs:** Treasury Accountant.
- **Frequency:** Monthly accrual; per debt instrument.

### 6.7 Refinancing Tracking
- **What it is:** Manage refinancing process — engagement, lender outreach, DD data room, commitment, closing.
- **Who performs:** CFO; Treasurer; outside counsel; investment banker.
- **Edge cases:** Debt modification vs extinguishment accounting, original issue discount, prepayment premium.

---

## 7. Hedging / Risk

### 7.1 Coal Price Hedges
- **What it is:** Financial swaps on coal indices (CSX Domestic Hot-Rolled-style indices for met; API2 ARA, FOB Newcastle for thermal export proxies; CAPP/NAPP OTC bilateral for domestic thermal) to lock margins.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; Risk Committee; outside broker (ICE / OTC counterparty).
- **Data captured:** Trade ticket (counterparty, index, notional tons, fixed price, period, settlement), MTM value, ISDA reference.
- **Documents/forms:** ISDA Master + Schedule + CSA, trade confirmations, hedge designation memo (ASC 815), hedge effectiveness test.
- **Frequency:** Per trade; monthly MTM; quarterly effectiveness.
- **Edge cases:** Index discontinuation, basis risk (location/quality), cleared vs bilateral margin, novation.

### 7.2 Diesel Price Hedges
- **What it is:** NYMEX ULSD heating oil cross-hedge or physical fixed-price contracts with fuel suppliers for off-road diesel consumed on-site.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer / Procurement.
- **Edge cases:** Cross-hedge ineffectiveness (NY Harbor ULSD vs Appalachian off-road), refund interaction with federal excise off-road exemption.

### 7.3 Steel / Roof Bolt / Supply Hedges
- **What it is:** Forward fixed-price purchase commitments with major suppliers (steel rope, roof bolts, belt, conveyor structure).
- **Who performs:** Procurement; Treasurer.
- **Edge cases:** Hedge accounting generally not pursued — treated as normal purchase exception (ASC 815-10-15-22).

### 7.4 Power Hedges
- **What it is:** Fixed-price PPA or financial swap on PJM/MISO for prep plant and longwall electric consumption.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; Energy procurement.
- **Edge cases:** Capacity vs energy, RTO basis, renewable energy credit overlay.

### 7.5 Mark-to-Market Accounting (ASC 815)
- **What it is:** Record derivative at fair value each period.
- **Who performs:** Treasury Accountant; Controller; valuation specialist.
- **Documents/forms:** MTM workbook, broker statement, level-2/level-3 fair value hierarchy memo.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Level-3 OTC met coal swaps with thin price discovery.

### 7.6 Cash Flow Hedge Designation / Documentation
- **What it is:** Formal hedge documentation at inception per ASC 815-20-25-3 to qualify for cash flow hedge accounting.
- **Who performs:** Treasury; Controller.
- **Documents/forms:** Hedge documentation memo (hedged item, hedging instrument, risk, method of assessing effectiveness).
- **Edge cases:** Late designation = ineligible for hedge accounting until re-designated; partial-month coverage.

### 7.7 Hedge Effectiveness Testing
- **What it is:** Quantitative test (regression / dollar-offset) at inception and ongoing per ASC 815.
- **Who performs:** Controller; outside accounting advisor.
- **Frequency:** Initial + quarterly.
- **Edge cases:** Failed effectiveness → de-designate and recognize in P&L; critical-terms-match simplification.

### 7.8 OCI Tracking and Reclassification
- **What it is:** Track effective portion of cash flow hedges in OCI and reclass to P&L on hedged transaction.
- **Who performs:** Controller.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Forecast no longer probable triggers OCI reclass to P&L (ASC 815-30-40).

### 7.9 Counterparty Exposure / ISDA Management
- **What it is:** Monitor concentration to each hedge counterparty; manage CSA collateral exchange.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer.
- **Frequency:** Daily collateral; monthly exposure.
- **Edge cases:** Counterparty downgrade triggers, set-off across multiple swap exposures.

### 7.10 Margin Calls on Cleared Hedges
- **What it is:** Daily margin posting to clearing broker for futures and cleared swaps.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; Treasury Operations.
- **Frequency:** Daily.
- **Edge cases:** Variation margin spike in volatility periods; initial-margin model changes.

---

## 8. Insurance / Captive

### 8.1 Property All-Risk (Mining Equipment, Prep Plant, Mine Improvements)
- **What it is:** First-party property coverage on above-ground equipment, prep plant, loadout, surface buildings; underground equipment typically a separate manuscript form.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; Insurance Broker (commercial); Carrier.
- **Data captured:** Statement of Values (COPE), values by location, deductibles per peril, sublimits, BI/EE.
- **Documents/forms:** Policy declarations, SOV, COPE narrative, schedule of equipment with serials.
- **Frequency:** Annual renewal.
- **Edge cases:** Underground equipment exclusion debate; flood/mine subsidence sublimit; BI from prep-plant fire.

### 8.2 Difference In Conditions / Mine Subsidence
- **What it is:** Catastrophic perils gap-fill (flood, earthquake, subsidence) outside primary all-risk.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager.
- **Edge cases:** Long-term subsidence claims years after mining ceased; pre-existing condition exclusion.

### 8.3 General Liability
- **What it is:** Third-party BI/PD; usually excludes pollution and mining-operations-specific (carved into separate policies).
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager.
- **Documents/forms:** CGL policy, additional-insured endorsements to customers/lessors.
- **Edge cases:** "Care, custody, control" exclusions on customer coal in stockpile.

### 8.4 Commercial Auto
- **What it is:** Auto liability/physical damage for on-road fleet; mine-roads and haul trucks excluded (covered under mobile equipment in property or via MOL).
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager.
- **Edge cases:** Hired/non-owned auto for contractors, livery exposures for crew bus.

### 8.5 Workers Compensation
- **What it is:** Statutory WC coverage in each state; often combines large-deductible primary, SIR, captive layer, excess.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; TPA (claims); Actuary (reserve).
- **Documents/forms:** Policy per state, payroll audit, loss runs, IBNR study.
- **State differences:** WV — formerly monopolistic, now competitive (Encova/BrickStreet primary, others); KY — competitive (KEMI common); VA — competitive (commercial market with VWC oversight). Second-injury fund participation: WV abolished its fund; KY has Subsequent Claims Fund; VA still has Uninsured Employer's Fund.
- **Edge cases:** Cumulative trauma claims, occupational disease (silica) outside Black Lung, large-deductible collateral, claims handling on reorganization.

### 8.6 Black Lung Coverage (State & Federal)
- **What it is:** Federal Black Lung Benefits Act (BLBA) coverage for pneumoconiosis claims by miners; states may have parallel programs (KY, WV historically). Can be insured or self-insured (with DOL authorization).
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; Black Lung Administrator; outside counsel for contests.
- **Documents/forms:** DOL CM-2017a/2017b self-insurance application, claimant file, medical evidence, IME reports, ALJ decisions, BLBA-specific surety bond.
- **Frequency:** Per claim; annual self-insurance recert; quarterly trust funding.
- **Edge cases:** Successor liability on acquired mines, ARB/court appeals, "responsible operator" determinations, lifetime claimant medical, federal Trust Fund offset.

### 8.7 Federal Mine Safety & Health Act Civil Penalty Coverage
- **What it is:** Defense cost coverage for MSHA citations and S&S contest; indemnity for penalties NOT INSURABLE under public-policy.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; outside MSHA counsel.
- **Documents/forms:** MSHA assessment letters, contest filings (FMSHRC), settlement agreements.
- **Edge cases:** Pattern-of-violations notices, individual agent liability (104(d)), criminal referrals.

### 8.8 Employment Practices Liability
- **What it is:** Coverage for EEOC, FMLA, ADA, wage-hour claims.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager.
- **Edge cases:** Union-related claims often excluded.

### 8.9 D&O
- **What it is:** Directors & Officers coverage including Side A (no indemnity), B (corporate reimbursement), C (entity).
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; CFO; Legal.
- **Edge cases:** Private-company D&O includes "entity vs employee" suits; investigation cost coverage; bankruptcy creditor claims against officers (very real coal-sector risk).

### 8.10 Cyber
- **What it is:** First-party (BI, extortion, restoration) and third-party (privacy) cyber coverage.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; IT/CISO.
- **Edge cases:** OT/ICS exposure at prep plants, ransomware exclusions tightening.

### 8.11 Environmental Impairment Liability (EIL) / Pollution Legal Liability (PLL)
- **What it is:** Site-specific pollution coverage including historic conditions and on-site cleanup.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; Environmental Counsel.
- **Documents/forms:** PLL policy with named locations, environmental reports (Phase I/II), retro date.
- **Edge cases:** Reclamation excluded (covered by surety/ARO), CERCLA designation areas, NPDES exceedance event.

### 8.12 Surety Bonds (Reclamation, Performance, Payment, IRS, Court)
- **What it is:** Bonds posted to states for reclamation per SMCRA, performance bonds to customers, payment bonds to vendors, IRS bonds on tax disputes, court bonds.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager / Treasurer; Surety underwriter.
- **Documents/forms:** Bond form, indemnity agreement, collateral pledge, bond schedule, rider history.
- **State differences:** WV (DEP-bonded with state Special Reclamation Fund backstop); KY (Bond Pool program option vs full surety); VA (DMME-bonded); each state has its own form and acceptable collateral.
- **Edge cases:** Self-bonding eligibility (largely phased out post-2015-16 bankruptcies — Alpha, Patriot, Arch, Peabody — though still permitted in some statutes); 100% collateralization demands; bond replacement on permit transfer.

### 8.13 Captive Insurance / Risk Retention Group
- **What it is:** Wholly-owned or industry-pooled captive insurance company to retain risk and access reinsurance.
- **Who performs:** CFO; Captive Manager (domicile); Captive Board.
- **Documents/forms:** Captive financial statements, regulator filings (Vermont, Cayman, etc.), reinsurance treaties, premium tax filings.
- **Edge cases:** IRS recharacterization risk (831(b) "micro-captive"), domiciliary regulator audit, fronting carrier collateral.

### 8.14 Premium Audits
- **What it is:** Year-end audits by WC and GL carriers of payroll/sales for true-up premium.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; Payroll; Accounting (audit response).
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Edge cases:** Misclassified payroll surcharges, subcontractor uninsured exposure pulled into premium.

### 8.15 Claims Management
- **What it is:** Coordinate claim handling with TPA — incident report, medical management, return-to-work, reserve setting, litigation.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; TPA; Safety; HR.
- **Documents/forms:** First Report of Injury (FROI), MSHA 7000-1, medical reports, reserve worksheets.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; monthly claims review.
- **Edge cases:** Mod factor management, cumulative trauma, third-party recovery, return-to-work refusal.

### 8.16 Loss Runs
- **What it is:** Carrier-produced claim history reports used in renewal and analytics.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly + at renewal.

### 8.17 COI Issuance to Customers, Lessors, Agencies
- **What it is:** Issue ACORD 25/27/28 to evidence coverage.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager / Broker.
- **Frequency:** On request; annual renewal.

### 8.18 COI Receipt and Tracking from Contractors
- **What it is:** Maintain contractor COI library to ensure mine-site contractors meet insurance requirements.
- **Who performs:** Risk Manager; Procurement; Safety.
- **Documents/forms:** ACORD certs, additional-insured endorsements, waiver of subrogation.
- **Frequency:** Continuous monitoring; on contractor entry to site.
- **Edge cases:** MSHA Part 45 contractor IDs separate from insurance; expired certs blocking site access.

---

## 9. Bonding

### 9.1 Reclamation Bonds (Per Permit, Per State)
- **What it is:** Surety bond (or alternative — collateral, self-bond) posted with state regulator covering estimated reclamation cost of disturbed acreage per SMCRA.
- **Who performs:** Permit Manager; Risk Manager; Surety.
- **Data captured:** Permit #, bond amount, surety company, bond #, effective date, acreage covered, rider history.
- **Documents/forms:** Bond form per state, rider amendments, indemnity agreement.
- **State differences:**
  - **WV** — Bonds to WVDEP under WV Code §22-3-11; backed by WV Special Reclamation Fund (per-ton tax-funded) to address forfeited sites.
  - **KY** — Two options: surety bond OR Bond Pool program (KRS 350.700 series); KY Energy & Environment Cabinet administers.
  - **VA** — Bonds to VA DMME (DEQ since 2024 reorganization).
- **Edge cases:** Bond release acreage stuck in Phase I/II/III status; surety insolvency mid-permit; permit transfer.

### 9.2 Bond Rider Amendments
- **What it is:** Increase/decrease bond as acreage disturbed changes.
- **Who performs:** Permit Manager; Surety.
- **Frequency:** Per disturbance event; annual review.
- **Edge cases:** Bond shortfall triggers cessation order.

### 9.3 Bond Release Applications and Tracking
- **What it is:** Phase I (backfilling/grading), II (revegetation), III (final after 5-year liability) release applications.
- **Who performs:** Permit Manager; Engineering; Environmental Consultant.
- **Documents/forms:** Bond release application, public notice, inspection reports.
- **Frequency:** Per phase as triggered.
- **Edge cases:** Citizen objection, Selenium / TDS NPDES open at site blocking Phase III.

### 9.4 Self-Bonding Eligibility
- **What it is:** Demonstrate creditworthiness to post unsecured bond (mostly phased out).
- **Who performs:** CFO; outside auditor.
- **State differences:** WV, KY, VA all technically allow under specific creditworthiness tests, but post-2015 cycle few operators qualify.
- **Edge cases:** Loss of self-bond status mid-cycle requires immediate replacement surety/collateral.

### 9.5 Indemnity Agreements with Surety
- **What it is:** General Agreement of Indemnity (GAI) signed by SC entities and often Justice-family guarantors.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; CFO; Legal; Surety.
- **Documents/forms:** GAI, collateral side letter.
- **Edge cases:** Cross-default between sureties, joint-and-several liability across affiliates.

### 9.6 Collateral Pledges
- **What it is:** Cash, LCs, or securities pledged to surety in lieu of full credit reliance.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer.
- **Frequency:** At demand.
- **Edge cases:** Step-up demands during downturn.

### 9.7 Reclamation Trust Funds
- **What it is:** State-mandated trust accounts.
- **State differences:**
  - **WV** — Special Reclamation Tax per ton (currently 27.9¢/ton total — 15¢ Special Reclamation Fund + 12.9¢ Special Reclamation Water Trust Fund per WV Code §22-3-11), pooled funding for forfeited site cleanup.
  - **KY** — Bond Pool program allows entity to participate in pooled bonding with deposit + per-ton premium.
  - **VA** — Reclamation fund similar concept.
- **Edge cases:** Trust contribution timing aligns with severance; insufficient pool triggers per-ton increase by regulator.

### 9.8 AML (Abandoned Mine Land) Fee
- **What it is:** Federal per-ton fee on coal production paid monthly to ONRR per SMCRA §402 / IRC §4121 cross-reference.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; Tonnage Reporter (Operations).
- **Data captured:** Tons by mine, by method (UG / surface / lignite), by month.
- **Documents/forms:** Form OSM-1 "Coal Reclamation Fee Report"; payment via Pay.gov.
- **Frequency:** Monthly; due last day of month following production month.
- **Rates (FY2022-2034 per BIL):** Surface 22.4¢/ton or 10% of value; Underground 9.6¢/ton or 10% of value; Lignite 6.4¢/ton or 2% of value (whichever lower).
- **Edge cases:** Coal sold vs used vs transferred timing; refuse coal recovery treatment; tonnage reconciliation to severance returns.
