## 10. Tax — Federal

### 10.1 C-Corp Income Tax / Pass-Through
- **What it is:** Federal income tax — entity-level for C-corps, pass-through for S-corps/partnerships/LLCs taxed as partnership.
- **Who performs:** Tax Director; outside CPA.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 1120 (C-corp), 1120S (S-corp), 1065 (partnership), K-1s, state composite returns.
- **Frequency:** Annual; quarterly estimates.
- **Edge cases:** Justice family ownership structure may use mix; consolidated 1120 for sub-group; basis tracking at owner level; §163(j) interest limitation; CAMT (corporate AMT post-IRA — generally only $1B+ AFSI but watch family aggregation rules).

### 10.2 Percentage Depletion
- **What it is:** Statutory 10% depletion on gross income from coal property, limited to 50% of taxable income from the property (IRC §613(b)(4)).
- **Who performs:** Tax Director; Tax Manager.
- **Data captured:** Gross income per property, allocable expenses, taxable income per property, prior-year depletion.
- **Documents/forms:** Depletion schedule per property (Form 4562 supporting), Form 1120 line.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Edge cases:** Percentage-depletion limitation by property, related-party royalty allocation, statutory carve-outs.

### 10.3 Cost Depletion
- **What it is:** Recovery of property basis * (tons mined / recoverable tons).
- **Who performs:** Tax Director; Reserve Engineer (recoverable tons).
- **Documents/forms:** Basis schedule, reserve report, depletion computation.
- **Frequency:** Annual; recompute on reserve revision.
- **Edge cases:** Reserve write-down increases per-ton depletion; basis from acquisitions allocated under §1060; bonus depreciation interplay.

### 10.4 §179 / Bonus Depreciation
- **What it is:** Immediate expensing of qualifying mining equipment.
- **Who performs:** Tax Director; Fixed Asset Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 4562; bonus elections; ADS elections.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Edge cases:** Bonus phase-down schedule (80% 2023, 60% 2024, 40% 2025, 20% 2026 absent reinstatement); §179 cap and phase-out; used property eligibility post-TCJA.

### 10.5 IDC-Analog Mine Development Cost
- **What it is:** Coal exploration (§617) and development (§616) cost election to expense vs capitalize and deplete.
- **Who performs:** Tax Director.
- **Edge cases:** §291 30% reduction for C-corps; recapture on disposition.

### 10.6 Federal Black Lung Excise Tax (IRC §4121)
- **What it is:** Excise tax on first sale or use of domestic coal by producer to fund Black Lung Disability Trust Fund.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; Excise Tax Manager.
- **Data captured:** Tons sold/used (UG vs Surface), sales price per ton, calculated tax per row.
- **Documents/forms:** IRS Form 720 (quarterly excise return); Schedule A; deposits via EFTPS semimonthly.
- **Frequency:** Semimonthly deposits; quarterly return.
- **Rates (current, IRA permanent):** Underground — lesser of $1.10/ton or 4.4% of sales price; Surface — lesser of $0.55/ton or 4.4% of sales price.
- **Edge cases:** Tons "used" (mine consumption) treatment; lignite exemption; export exemption (Ranger Fuel v. US line of cases); related-party sale valuation.

### 10.7 Federal AML Reclamation Fee
- **What it is:** Covered in §9.8.

### 10.8 Federal Excise Tax on Diesel — Off-Road Refund
- **What it is:** Federal motor fuel tax (24.4¢/gal diesel) paid at pump on off-road diesel; eligible for refund/credit when used in mining (off-highway business use).
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; Operations (gallons by use).
- **Documents/forms:** Form 4136 (income tax credit) or Form 8849 Schedule 1 (refund); fuel logs.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly Form 8849 or annual Form 4136.
- **Edge cases:** Dyed-diesel deliveries vs clear diesel paid-then-refunded; LUST tax not refundable; on-road haul truck use not eligible.

### 10.9 R&D Credits
- **What it is:** §41 credit for qualified research in process / technology improvements (longwall automation, prep-plant optimization).
- **Who performs:** Tax Director; outside R&D study firm.
- **Documents/forms:** R&D study, Form 6765, §174 amortization schedule.
- **Edge cases:** §174 mandatory capitalization/amortization (5-yr domestic) — significant cash impact.

### 10.10 Federal Coal Royalty (ONRR)
- **What it is:** Royalty on federal coal leases (8% UG, 12.5% surface typically) paid to ONRR.
- **Who performs:** Royalty Accountant; Land.
- **Documents/forms:** ONRR Form 4430 (Solid Minerals Production and Royalty Report); SMP-2010.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Federal coal limited in WV/KY/VA (most coal is private); valuation disputes; transportation/processing allowance.

### 10.11 Estimated Tax Payments
- **What it is:** Quarterly federal income tax estimates.
- **Who performs:** Tax Director.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 1120-W; EFTPS payments.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly (4/15, 6/15, 9/15, 12/15 for C-corp).

### 10.12 FUTA
- **What it is:** Federal Unemployment 6% on first $7,000 wages (net 0.6% after state credit).
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Tax.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 940 annual; Form 940 deposits quarterly when exceed $500.
- **Edge cases:** Credit-reduction states (rare in WV/KY/VA recent years).

---

## 11. Tax — State Income, Severance & Special

### 11.1 WV Coal Severance Tax (WV Code Ch 11 Art 13A)
- **What it is:** 5% combined severance on gross value of coal at first point of sale (4.65% to State + 0.35% to local). Reduced rates for thin-seam: 2% (37"-45"), 1% (<37"). Minimum tax $0.75/ton applies broadly but NOT to thin-seam reduced coal.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; Controller (review).
- **Data captured:** Tons by mine and seam, gross value, deductions (transportation outside state if applicable per rule), thin-seam certification.
- **Documents/forms:** WV/CST-200CU (Combined Sales/Severance Monthly Return); WV/CST-200CU annual reconciliation; Thin-Seam Certification.
- **Frequency:** Monthly (due 20th of following month).
- **Edge cases:** Thin-seam engineer certification timing; minimum-tax computation interplay; refund claims; intercompany sales at non-arm's-length pricing.

### 11.2 WV Minimum Severance Tax
- **What it is:** $0.75/ton floor when 5% computation yields less (W. Va. Code §11-12B-3); waste-coal credit interplay.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.
- **Edge cases:** Distressed low-price periods trigger minimum on most production; thin-seam exempt.

### 11.3 WV Special Reclamation Tax
- **What it is:** Per-ton tax dedicated to Special Reclamation Fund and Water Trust Fund per WV Code §22-3-11 (currently 27.9¢/ton combined).
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Filed with CST-200CU.
- **Edge cases:** Rate set by DEP/Legislature periodically based on fund actuarial.

### 11.4 WV Workers Comp Debt Reduction Tax
- **What it is:** Historically a per-ton surcharge to pay down former WC fund deficit (largely sunset but verify each year).
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.

### 11.5 WV B&O Tax
- **What it is:** State Business & Occupation gross-receipts tax on certain activities; coal sales generally now under severance not B&O, but other entity activities (electric, services) may be subject.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.

### 11.6 VA Coal Severance — Local Coal Road Improvement Tax (§58.1-3713)
- **What it is:** Local tax on coal severed in producing counties; up to 1% on gross receipts (0.75% small mine), proceeds to county for road improvement/economic development.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Local coal severance return (per county — typically Form CG-1 or county-specific).
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Each Wise/Buchanan/Dickenson/Lee/Russell/Tazewell/Scott county has own ordinance; rates and allocations differ.

### 11.7 VA Local Coal Severance License Tax (§58.1-3741)
- **What it is:** Additional local severance up to 1% (0.75% small mine) per county adoption.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Per-county local severance return.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Distribution formulas by Wise County etc. with town allocations; small-mine definition tracking.

### 11.8 VA Coal Surface Mining Reclamation Tax / Pool
- **What it is:** Funding for state reclamation programs; rate per ton.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.

### 11.9 KY Coal Severance & Processing Tax (KRS Ch 143)
- **What it is:** 4.5% of gross value of coal severed AND of coal processed (separate calc), minimum $0.50/ton on severance.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Form 55A100 "Coal Severance Tax Return"; supporting Form 55A101 (instructions); Schedule for purchased-processed coal.
- **Frequency:** Monthly; due within 20 days of month end.
- **Edge cases:** Coal severed in KY and processed in KY taxed only once at higher of two; coal severed in KY but processed elsewhere = severance only; coal severed elsewhere processed in KY = processing only; minimum $0.50/ton severance still required; exported-coal refund per KRS 143.022.

### 11.10 KY Coal Severance Distribution (LGEAF / LGEDF)
- **What it is:** Distribution mechanism — state retains portion, balance allocated to coal-producing counties via Local Government Economic Assistance Fund and Local Government Economic Development Fund.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; County tracking.
- **Edge cases:** SC counties (Pike, Letcher, Harlan, Bell, etc.) get distributions tied to where coal severed.

### 11.11 Multi-State Apportionment for Income Tax
- **What it is:** Apportion taxable income by formula (single-sales factor in WV (now), three-factor variants elsewhere) across states where SC has nexus.
- **Who performs:** Tax Director.
- **Documents/forms:** Apportionment schedule per state, throwback/throwout analysis.
- **State differences:**
  - **WV** — Single-sales factor (post-2022 phase-in for many taxpayers).
  - **KY** — Single-sales factor (post-2018).
  - **VA** — Single-sales factor manufacturing election; otherwise three-factor with double-weighted sales.
- **Edge cases:** Coal sold FOB origin sourced to origin state; sales of services sourced under cost-of-performance vs market; combined vs separate reporting.

### 11.12 Multi-State SUTA and SIT
- **What it is:** State unemployment and income tax withholding per state.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Tax.
- **Documents/forms:** WV WV/IT-103, KY K-1 / K-3, VA VA-5/VA-6.
- **Edge cases:** Wage base and rate differences; reciprocal agreement combinations.

### 11.13 Sales & Use Tax (Mining Machinery Exemptions)
- **What it is:** State sales tax on tangible personal property purchases; mining machinery exemptions narrow and frequently contested.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; Procurement (exemption certs).
- **Documents/forms:** Resale/exemption certs (WV F0003 SST, KY 51A111, VA ST-11); sales/use tax returns per state.
- **State differences:**
  - **WV** — §11-15-9 exemption for direct-use mining machinery; refund claims via WV Code procedures.
  - **KY** — KRS 139.480 "machinery for new and expanded industry" exemption; narrow per Stoll Keenon Ogden analysis — must be first installation, not replacement.
  - **VA** — §58.1-609.3(2)(iii) "used directly in mining" exemption (mining included with manufacturing); per VA Tax Ruling 15-106 and others — equipment must be integral to mining process, not ancillary.
- **Edge cases:** Out-of-state purchase use-tax accrual; consumables (bits, bolts, lube); reclamation activity equipment (VA includes reclamation as "used directly"); repair parts treatment varies; lease of mining equipment.

### 11.14 Personal Property Tax / Business Tangible
- **What it is:** County-level annual tax on business personal property (equipment, fixtures, inventory in some states).
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Per-county returns (WV Form STC-12:32-I; KY Form 62A500; VA county-specific).
- **Frequency:** Annual (typically Jan-May deadlines).
- **State differences:**
  - **WV** — Industrial property valued by State Tax Commissioner per WV Code §11-1C-10, then assessor multiplies by 60% (assessment ratio).
  - **KY** — State Form 62A500; rate per county; mining machinery may qualify for reduced state rate.
  - **VA** — Wise, Buchanan, etc. each have own rates; "Machinery & Tools" tax (separate from BPP) at separate rate per locality.
- **Edge cases:** Idle equipment valuation; pollution control exemption; manufacturer's machinery & tools (VA only).

### 11.15 Real Property Tax Including Unmined Coal Valuation
- **What it is:** County tax on real property including separately valued unmined coal/mineral interests.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant; Land Department.
- **State differences:**
  - **WV** — Unmined coal valued by State Tax Commissioner per §11-1C-10 using statutory methodology (DCF on recoverable tons); appeal mechanisms via county Board of Equalization and Office of Tax Appeals.
  - **KY** — Unmined minerals assessed separately by Department of Revenue (Property Tax Branch) under KRS 132.820; per-acre or per-ton methods; appealable.
  - **VA** — Mineral lands generally locally assessed; coal interests separately listed.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Edge cases:** Surface vs mineral ownership splits, royalty-burden adjustments to value, reserve depletion downward revisions, undeveloped reserve valuation disputes (very common appeal driver).

### 11.16 Coal License / Privilege Taxes (County-Specific in Some KY Counties)
- **What it is:** Per-ton occupational/license tax adopted by some KY coal counties.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.
- **Frequency:** Monthly/quarterly per county.

### 11.17 Local Occupational License Taxes (KY)
- **What it is:** KY counties and cities impose payroll occupational tax (typically 0.5-2.5% of wages).
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Tax.
- **Documents/forms:** Per-county quarterly return.
- **Edge cases:** Net-profits add-on at year-end (some jurisdictions tax both payroll and net profits).

---

## 12. Tax Filings Calendar

### 12.1 Monthly Filings
- **What it is:** Recurring monthly returns and remittances.
- **Detail:**
  - Federal: AML OSM-1 (last day of next month); Form 720 semimonthly excise deposits.
  - WV: CST-200CU (20th).
  - KY: 55A100 (20 days post-month-end); occupational license per county.
  - VA: Local coal severance per county (typically 30 days).
  - State sales/use returns per state.
  - Royalty remittances per lease.
- **Who performs:** Tax Compliance Manager; Tax Accountant per filing.

### 12.2 Quarterly Filings
- **What it is:** Estimated income tax (federal and state), payroll 941 / state withholding, FUTA deposits, excise return.
- **Frequency:** Per calendar quarter.

### 12.3 Annual Filings
- **What it is:** Federal income tax, state income tax (multi-state), property tax returns, unmined coal returns, W-2/W-3, 1099/1096, ACA 1094-C/1095-C, K-1s, 940 FUTA, captive insurance returns, BOI updates.
- **Frequency:** Annual; calendar set with deadlines.

---

## 13. Depletion / Reclamation Accounting

### 13.1 Cost Depletion Calculation
- **What it is:** Basis / recoverable tons * tons mined = cost depletion expense per period.
- **Who performs:** Tax Director; Reserve Engineer; Fixed Asset Accountant.
- **Frequency:** Annual; revised on reserve update.
- **Edge cases:** Acquisition-allocated basis under §1060, downward reserve revisions accelerate per-ton, undeveloped reserves excluded.

### 13.2 Percentage Depletion Calculation
- **What it is:** 10% of gross income from coal property subject to 50% of taxable-income-from-property limit (IRC §613).
- **Who performs:** Tax Director.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Edge cases:** "Property" definition (each tract, lease, mine) drives result; aggregation elections; §291 30% reduction for C-corp.

### 13.3 Reserves & Resources Tracking
- **What it is:** Maintain proved/probable reserves and measured/indicated resources as denominator for depletion and for lender/disclosure.
- **Who performs:** Reserve Engineer; Geology.
- **Documents/forms:** Reserve report (third-party annually); JORC/SEC SK-1300 style report.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Edge cases:** Reclassification on geologic update; economic test changes with price.

### 13.4 Asset Retirement Obligation (ARO) — ASC 410-20
- **What it is:** Fair-value liability recorded at inception of obligating event (mine/permit creation, equipment installation) for estimated reclamation cost; accreted at credit-adjusted risk-free rate over life of mine.
- **Who performs:** Controller; Environmental/Reclamation Engineer (cost estimate); Treasurer (discount rate).
- **Data captured:** Estimate by component (regrade, revegetate, water treatment perpetual, structure removal), inflation rate, settlement date, discount rate, ARC asset.
- **Documents/forms:** ARO model per mine, accretion schedule, ARC depreciation schedule, revaluation memo on revision.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly review; annual full update; on triggering events.
- **Edge cases:** Long-term water treatment with no defined end date (perpetual treatment of selenium-bearing seeps), upward revision discounted at current rate but downward at original rate (layered), interaction with bond posting (different basis), reclamation acceleration credit on settled work.

### 13.5 Discount Rate Selection
- **What it is:** Credit-adjusted risk-free rate by tenor; entity-specific based on credit profile.
- **Who performs:** Treasurer; Controller; external valuation specialist.
- **Edge cases:** Justice-family credit profile uncertainty; rate update annually.

### 13.6 ARO Settlement / Revision Accounting
- **What it is:** Compare actual reclamation spend to liability; gain/loss on settlement; revisions adjust liability and asset.
- **Who performs:** Controller; Reclamation Engineer.
- **Edge cases:** Significant timing changes from regulatory bond release delays.

### 13.7 Underwater Asset Impairment (ASC 360)
- **What it is:** Mining asset group impairment when undiscounted cash flows < carrying value.
- **Who performs:** Controller; FP&A; external valuation.
- **Edge cases:** Mine-level asset grouping vs entity-level; ARC and ARO interplay in carrying value; price-deck assumptions; ceiling test analog (though not formal as in O&G).

---

## 14. Lease Accounting (Lessee — ASC 842)

### 14.1 Equipment Lease Accounting (Operating vs Finance)
- **What it is:** Classify equipment leases (haul trucks, draglines, loaders, conveyors) per ASC 842; record ROU asset and lease liability.
- **Who performs:** Lease Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Lease abstract, classification memo, ROU/liability schedule.
- **Frequency:** On commencement; remeasure on modification/index change.
- **Edge cases:** Embedded leases in mining services contracts (e.g., contract miner "owns" but exclusively serves SC), short-term lease exception (<12 mo), index-linked rents.

### 14.2 Coal Mining (Royalty) Lease Accounting
- **What it is:** Mineral rights leases generally outside scope of ASC 842 — but minimum/advance royalties and surface-use components may need separate treatment.
- **Who performs:** Lease Accountant; Land.
- **Edge cases:** Recoupable advance royalty creates asset; non-recoupable expensed; surface-rights piggybacking on mineral lease.

---

## 15. Revenue Recognition (ASC 606)

### 15.1 Point-in-Time Recognition at Title Transfer
- **What it is:** Revenue recognized at transfer of control — typically FOB mine, FOB rail loadout, FOB barge dock, FOB vessel rail.
- **Who performs:** Controller; Sales Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Contract review memo per ASC 606 5-step, FOB term mapping.
- **Edge cases:** "FOB destination" rare but exists; bill-and-hold criteria when stockpiled but invoiced.

### 15.2 Quality Adjustments as Variable Consideration
- **What it is:** Estimate quality-based premium/penalty at recognition (expected value or most-likely-amount), true-up to actual.
- **Who performs:** Sales Accountant.
- **Edge cases:** Constraint on estimate, umpire-sample disputes, rolling-month adjustments.

### 15.3 Demurrage / Freight as Separate Performance Obligation
- **What it is:** Evaluate whether freight billed to customer is a distinct performance obligation or fulfillment activity.
- **Who performs:** Controller; Sales Accountant.
- **Edge cases:** FOB origin freight prepaid-and-add typically fulfillment; FOB destination freight separate POB.

### 15.4 Take-or-Pay Contracts
- **What it is:** Customer obligation to take minimum volume; if not taken, pays anyway.
- **Who performs:** Sales Accountant; Controller.
- **Edge cases:** Make-up rights, revenue recognition timing on unfilled obligation, breakage on expiration.

### 15.5 Bill-and-Hold
- **What it is:** Customer purchases coal but requests it remain in SC stockpile for later shipment.
- **Who performs:** Controller.
- **Edge cases:** ASC 606-10-55-83 4-criteria test (substantive reason, identified, ready, not available to SC).

---

## 16. Inventory Valuation

### 16.1 Lower of Cost or NRV
- **What it is:** Coal inventory at lower of cost or net realizable value (selling price – completion – disposal).
- **Who performs:** Cost Accountant; Controller.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Falling spot price triggers write-down; spec-specific NRV vs blended; refuse coal NRV typically zero.

### 16.2 Production Cost Build-Up
- **What it is:** Roll mining, prep, loadout, royalty, severance, depreciation into per-ton cost basis.
- **Who performs:** Cost Accountant.
- **Edge cases:** Capitalized overhead allocation, mid-month rate changes, idle-capacity exclusion (period cost not inventoriable).

### 16.3 Inventory By Location
- **What it is:** Track tons at mine raw, prep feed, prep clean, loadout, in-transit.
- **Who performs:** Cost Accountant; Logistics.
- **Edge cases:** In-transit title (FOB origin = sold; FOB dest = owned), cross-mine blending.

### 16.4 Periodic vs Perpetual
- **What it is:** Most coal operations perpetual with periodic survey reconciliation.
- **Who performs:** Cost Accountant.

### 16.5 Physical Inventory / Stockpile Survey Reconciliation
- **What it is:** Drone/LiDAR/GPS survey of stockpiles compared to book.
- **Who performs:** Surveyor; Cost Accountant.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly or semiannual.
- **Edge cases:** Density factor, moisture, compaction, geometry assumptions.

---

## 17. Capital Budgeting / AFE

### 17.1 AFE Workflow
- **What it is:** Authorization for Expenditure document for any capital project above threshold; pre-AFE estimate, formal AFE with approval routing per DOA, supplemental AFE for overruns.
- **Who performs:** Project Sponsor (mine engineer); Engineering; Cost Estimator; Controller; CFO/CEO depending on threshold.
- **Documents/forms:** AFE form, scope, schedule, budget, justification (IRR, NPV, payback), approval routing, supplemental AFE.
- **Frequency:** Per project.
- **Edge cases:** Equipment trade-in netting, contingency usage tracking, scope change governance.

### 17.2 Project Tracking
- **What it is:** Track commitments (POs), accruals, actuals against AFE; in-service date for cap-vs-expense.
- **Who performs:** Project Accountant.

### 17.3 In-Service Date and Depreciation Commencement
- **What it is:** Date asset placed in service triggers depreciation, ARC accretion, property tax inclusion.
- **Who performs:** Fixed Asset Accountant; Engineering (sign-off).

### 17.4 Capitalization vs Expensing Thresholds
- **What it is:** De minimis safe harbor ($2,500 typically), capitalization policy threshold.
- **Who performs:** Controller; Tax.

### 17.5 Repair vs Improvement (TPR §1.263(a)-3)
- **What it is:** Tangible Property Regulations analysis for capitalize vs deduct on equipment work.
- **Who performs:** Tax Director; Fixed Asset Accountant.
- **Edge cases:** Major component replacement vs routine maintenance; UOP analysis on integrated equipment (longwall as single UOP).

---

## 18. Joint Interest Billing / Joint Ventures

### 18.1 JV Agreement Administration
- **What it is:** Manage joint operating agreements where SC operates property jointly with timber, ORRI partner, or contract miner.
- **Who performs:** JV Accountant; Land; Legal.
- **Documents/forms:** JOA, JV agreement, ORRI/NPI conveyance.

### 18.2 JIB Statements
- **What it is:** Joint Interest Billing — operator bills non-operating partners their working-interest share of costs.
- **Who performs:** JV Accountant.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Edge cases:** Audit rights (typically 24 months), AFE approval thresholds requiring partner consent.

### 18.3 Operator vs Non-Operator
- **What it is:** Role determines whether SC reports gross or net of partner share.
- **Who performs:** Controller.

### 18.4 Cash Calls
- **What it is:** Operator requests funds from partners for upcoming costs.
- **Who performs:** JV Accountant; Treasury.

---

## 19. Royalty Accounting (Interfaces with Land/Lease Module)

### 19.1 Per-Ton Calculation Engine
- **What it is:** For each ton shipped, apply lease royalty rate (% of value, $/ton, or sliding scale).
- **Who performs:** Royalty Accountant.
- **Edge cases:** Tiered rates by price, per-seam splits.

### 19.2 Allowed Deductions
- **What it is:** Per-lease allowed deductions (transportation, preparation, marketing, severance pass-through).
- **Who performs:** Royalty Accountant.
- **Edge cases:** Lease interpretation disputes ("at the mine" vs "at the point of sale").

### 19.3 Suspense Management
- **What it is:** Hold royalty payments in suspense pending title clearance, heir identification, address resolution, division-order signature.
- **Who performs:** Royalty Accountant; Land.
- **Edge cases:** Aged suspense converts to escheat after dormancy period.

### 19.4 Statement Generation
- **What it is:** Monthly/quarterly royalty statement to lessor.
- **Who performs:** Royalty Accountant.

### 19.5 Check / ACH Issuance
- **What it is:** Disburse royalty per lease schedule.
- **Who performs:** AP.

### 19.6 1099-MISC Box 2 (Royalty)
- **What it is:** Year-end reporting of royalties paid.
- **Who performs:** Tax Accountant.
- **Edge cases:** Foreign lessor 1042-S instead of 1099.

### 19.7 Severance Pass-Through vs Hold-Out
- **What it is:** Per lease, severance either grosses up calc or is netted from lessor share.
- **Who performs:** Royalty Accountant.

### 19.8 Heir Splits
- **What it is:** Sub-divide royalty among multiple heirs per probate-determined fractions.
- **Who performs:** Royalty Accountant; Land.
- **Edge cases:** 30+ heir lessor groups, partial title curative needed before payment.

### 19.9 Audit Defense (Lessor Audits)
- **What it is:** Respond to lessor or lessor-CPA audit of royalty calculations.
- **Who performs:** Royalty Accountant; Controller; Counsel.
- **Frequency:** Per audit request (typically 24-mo lookback).
- **Edge cases:** Class action royalty cases; underpayment + interest + attorney fees exposure.

---

## 20. Post-Retirement Benefits

### 20.1 UMWA Health & Retirement Funds Participation
- **What it is:** Where operations are unionized — contribute to UMWA Combined Benefit Fund, 1992 Benefit Plan, 1993 Benefit Plan, 2011 Retiree Bonus Account, 1974 Pension Plan.
- **Who performs:** Payroll; Union Relations; Benefits.
- **Documents/forms:** Monthly contribution reports per CBA; Coal Act Combined Fund per-beneficiary premium statements.
- **Frequency:** Monthly contributions.
- **Edge cases:** SC's union footprint determines exposure; coverage under Coal Industry Retiree Health Benefit Act of 1992 (Coal Act) creates lifetime obligations regardless of current operations.

### 20.2 Multiemployer Pension Withdrawal Liability (1974 Pension Plan)
- **What it is:** Contingent liability for proportionate share of unfunded vested benefits triggered on complete or partial withdrawal from UMWA 1974 Pension Plan.
- **Who performs:** CFO; Actuary; Outside Counsel; Auditor (disclosure).
- **Data captured:** Contribution base units (hours worked), allocation method (presumptive 20-year), estimated WL per latest plan statement.
- **Documents/forms:** Annual WL estimate from plan administrator; ASC 715-80 footnote disclosure (Schedule of Significant Multiemployer Plans).
- **Frequency:** Annual estimate request; on triggering event.
- **Edge cases:** Partial withdrawal (70% decline test, 3-year contribution test), free-look rule, sale of assets §4204 election to avoid WL trigger, related-party group treatment, Supreme Court guidance pending on discount-rate methodology (Energy West case), insolvency / mass withdrawal scenarios.

### 20.3 Multi-Employer Pension Plan Disclosures
- **What it is:** ASC 715-80 footnote — plan name, EIN, plan number, contributions, zone status (green/yellow/red), funded status, SC's % of total contributions.
- **Who performs:** Controller; Auditor.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Edge cases:** "Critical" zone status for 1974 Plan; PBGC mass withdrawal risk disclosure.

### 20.4 OPEB (Retiree Medical) — ASC 715
- **What it is:** Actuarial liability for promised retiree medical (non-union legacy programs, supplemental promises).
- **Who performs:** Actuary; Controller.
- **Edge cases:** Caps on benefits, Medicare integration, retiree contribution increases.

### 20.5 Coal Industry Retiree Health Benefit Act (Coal Act) Obligations
- **What it is:** Per-beneficiary monthly premium to Combined Fund and assignments to 1992 Plan for assigned operators.
- **Who performs:** Benefits; Tax.
- **Documents/forms:** SSA assignment notices; monthly premium billings.
- **Edge cases:** Successor liability, "related person" joint liability, IRS Tax Court disputes over assignments.

### 20.6 Federal Black Lung Benefits (Claimant-by-Claimant)
- **What it is:** Pay monthly benefits to qualifying claimants and their dependents/survivors under BLBA; medical bills lifetime.
- **Who performs:** Black Lung Administrator; TPA.
- **Documents/forms:** Per-claimant ledger; monthly DOL reporting; Form CM-911 et al.
- **Frequency:** Monthly per claimant.
- **Edge cases:** Survivor benefits, modification requests, augmentation for dependents, Trust Fund interim payments.

---

## 21. Audit

### 21.1 External Financial Audit
- **What it is:** GAAP audit of consolidated financial statements per lender/surety requirement.
- **Who performs:** External CPA firm; Controller / CFO coordinate.
- **Documents/forms:** PBC list, audit workpapers, management rep letter, audit report, audit committee deliverables.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Edge cases:** Going-concern evaluation in downturn; ARO and UMWA WL critical audit matters; related-party transaction testing (Justice family).

### 21.2 Lender Compliance Audit
- **What it is:** Lender-directed field exam (typically by third-party — Wells, Hilco, Carl Marks) of AR, inventory, borrowing base, payables priority.
- **Who performs:** External field exam firm; Treasurer / Controller host.
- **Documents/forms:** Field exam report, BBC reconciliation, ineligibility findings, advance-rate reset.
- **Frequency:** Annual or semiannual; more frequent during stress.
- **Edge cases:** Concentration adjustments, in-transit eligibility, foreign AR ineligibility, royalty/severance priority reserves.

### 21.3 Insurance Premium Audits
- **What it is:** Carrier audit of payroll/sales for WC/GL true-up.
- **Who performs:** Carrier auditor; Payroll/Accounting respond.
- **Frequency:** Annual.

### 21.4 Workers Comp Audit (State and Carrier)
- **What it is:** State or carrier verifies class codes and payroll.
- **Who performs:** WC auditor; Risk Manager.

### 21.5 Sales Tax Audits
- **What it is:** State sales/use tax audits — coal companies frequent targets given mining-exemption complexity.
- **Who performs:** State auditor; Tax Director; outside tax counsel.
- **Frequency:** Per audit cycle (typically 3-4 yr lookback).
- **Edge cases:** Use-tax accrual on out-of-state equipment purchases; exemption-cert validity at point of sale; bobtail/consumables.

### 21.6 Severance Tax Audits
- **What it is:** State severance audits — verify tons, value, deductions, seam classifications.
- **Who performs:** State auditor; Tax Director.
- **Frequency:** Per state cycle.
- **Edge cases:** Thin-seam recertification challenges, intercompany sale valuation, "first point of sale" disputes.

### 21.7 Federal Income Tax Audit
- **What it is:** IRS examination of 1120/1065.
- **Who performs:** IRS RA; Tax Director; outside tax counsel.
- **Edge cases:** Percentage depletion property aggregation; §174 R&D; captive insurance §831(b); transfer pricing §482.

### 21.8 Property Tax Appeals
- **What it is:** Annual appeal of assessor valuations — significant cost driver, especially unmined coal.
- **Who performs:** Tax Director; Land; outside property tax counsel; appraiser.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **State differences:** WV Board of Equalization → Office of Tax Appeals → Circuit Court; KY Local Board → KBTA → Circuit; VA Board of Equalization → Circuit.
- **Edge cases:** Unmined coal DCF input disputes (price deck, recovery factor); manufacturer M&T classification (VA); pollution-control exemptions.

### 21.9 Royalty Audits by Lessors
- **What it is:** Lessors / their CPAs audit royalty calculations.
- **Who performs:** Lessor auditor; Royalty Accountant; Counsel.
- **Edge cases:** Class actions, gas/coal underpayment cases, multi-lessor pooling disputes.

### 21.10 ONRR Audits of Federal Coal Royalty
- **What it is:** ONRR (Office of Natural Resources Revenue) audits federal coal royalty filings.
- **Who performs:** ONRR auditor; Royalty Accountant.
- **Edge cases:** Limited applicability if no federal coal; transportation allowance contests.

### 21.11 Internal Audit
- **What it is:** Internal SOX-style controls testing where mature; risk-based audit plan.
- **Who performs:** Internal Audit (if function exists); often outsourced.
- **Frequency:** Per IA plan.

### 21.12 SOX-Like Controls
- **What it is:** Internal control framework where required by lenders or in anticipation of public-debt issuance.
- **Who performs:** Controller; IA; external advisor.
- **Documents/forms:** Risk and control matrix (RCM), control testing workpapers, deficiency log, management response.

---

## 22. Forecasting / FP&A

### 22.1 Annual Budget By Mine, By Cost Center
- **What it is:** Bottoms-up budget per mine and cost center — production, cost per ton, capex, headcount.
- **Who performs:** FP&A Manager; Mine GMs; Cost Accountant.
- **Documents/forms:** Budget package, ops plan, mine plan integration, AFE plan, board approval deck.
- **Frequency:** Annual (typically Q4 prior year); reforecast at mid-year.

### 22.2 Monthly Forecast Updates
- **What it is:** Rolling forecast — actual + remaining-year + outyear with current price/cost assumptions.
- **Who performs:** FP&A.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.

### 22.3 Long-Range Plan (5-Year)
- **What it is:** Integration of mine plan, reserve life, customer contracts, capex into 5-yr financial plan.
- **Who performs:** FP&A; Operations Planning; Reserve Engineer.
- **Frequency:** Annual; major refresh on M&A or major contract.

### 22.4 Cost Per Ton Modeling
- **What it is:** Decompose total cost into per-ton drivers — labor, supplies, royalties, severance, freight, prep, capex amortization.
- **Who performs:** Cost Accountant; FP&A.
- **Frequency:** Monthly review; budget update.

### 22.5 Sensitivity Analysis
- **What it is:** Test EBITDA / cash sensitivity to price, volume, mix, diesel, FX, interest rates.
- **Who performs:** FP&A; CFO.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly; before lender meeting; before hedge decisions.

### 22.6 Scenario Planning
- **What it is:** Discrete scenarios — base / downside / upside — with full P&L, BS, CF.
- **Who performs:** FP&A; CFO.
- **Frequency:** Annual; ad hoc on macro events (price collapse, regulatory shock).

# Domain 6: Land, Mineral Rights, Lease, Royalty & Title

# Land, Mineral Rights, Lease, Royalty & Title

Scope: every land, surface, mineral, lease, royalty, easement, water, timber, title, and lessor-relations activity for a multi-state Appalachian coal operator (Southern Coal Corporation; WV/VA/KY plus AL/TN). Appalachian coal land tenure is uniquely complex: surface and mineral estates are routinely severed by pre-1900 deeds; coal can be severed seam-by-seam; ORRIs and NPIs stack; fractional heirs are scattered across the country; broad-form deed jurisprudence differs sharply by state; and unmined coal is taxed as a distinct interest in real property in WV and KY. The functions below assume a full landman + title attorney + royalty accountant + lessor relations team.

Roles referenced (abbreviations used throughout):
- LM = Land Manager / VP Land
- LMAN = Landman (in-house or contract)
- TA = Title Attorney (in-house General Counsel or outside coal title firm)
- RA = Royalty Accountant
- LRC = Lessor Relations Clerk / Owner Relations
- SUR = Surveyor (licensed PLS)
- CFO = Finance
- ENV = Environmental / Permitting
- OPS = Mine Operations / Engineering
- HSE = Safety
- HR = Human Resources (for MEPP / UMWA exposure on acquisitions)
- IT-GIS = GIS Analyst (land/parcel mapping)

---

## 1. Land & Mineral Estate Inventory (Master Records)

### 1.1 Fee Land Owned (Surface in Fee)
- **What**: Maintain a register of every tract of surface land Southern Coal Corp. owns outright (in fee simple), separate from mineral ownership. Includes mine sites, prep plant sites, loadouts, refuse impoundment footprints, headquarters/shop parcels, recreational/buffer land, and post-mining "legacy" parcels.
- **Who**: LM (record owner), LMAN (field verification), IT-GIS (mapping), TA (chain of title curative).
- **Data captured**: Parcel ID (county tax map / district / map / parcel), grantor, grantee (current titleholder entity), deed book/page, recording date, acreage (deeded vs surveyed), legal description (metes & bounds), use classification (active mine / inactive / legacy / HQ / buffer), purchase price + closing date, basis for tax, post-mining land use designation, encumbrances (mortgages, liens, leases out).
- **Documents**: Deed (warranty, special warranty, quitclaim), title opinion, survey plat, ALTA survey if commercial, closing statement, mortgage/deed of trust if financed.
- **Frequency**: Continuous; reconciled to county tax bills annually; full audit every 3–5 years.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (property tax payment, fixed-asset register, depletion basis), ENV (permit boundary verification), OPS (mine plan footprint).
- **State-specific**: WV — surface estate routinely severed from minerals; tax billed in "land book" by district/map/parcel. KY — recorded by deed book/page in county clerk's office; PVA (Property Valuation Administrator) maintains parcel data. VA — recorded with circuit court clerk; some counties use "tax map ID" + "GPIN". AL/TN — probate judge offices record (AL); register of deeds (TN).
- **Edge cases**: Surface owned but minerals severed away decades ago; orphan parcels (tax-delinquent acquired at sheriff's sale); fractional interests inherited through multi-generation chain; parcels straddling county or state lines.

### 1.2 Leased Surface (Surface Use Only, No Ownership)
- **What**: Register of every tract where SC has a surface use right via lease, license, or surface use agreement but does not own the surface fee. Includes haul roads on neighbors' surface, prep plant pads on leased ground, refuse area surface leases.
- **Who**: LM, LMAN, TA.
- **Data captured**: Lessor name, lease/agreement number, acreage, term, renewal terms, surface rental rate, restoration obligation, indemnity language reference, permitted uses.
- **Documents**: Surface lease, Surface Use Agreement (SUA), license, easement deed.
- **Frequency**: Continuous; calendar of expirations reviewed monthly.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (rental payment schedule), ENV (permit boundary), OPS (operational planning).
- **State-specific**: WV — surface owner consent required for surface mining of severed coal under WV Code §22-3; KY — Broad Form Deed Amendment (KY Const. §19(2), 1988) requires surface owner consent for any extraction method not contemplated at deed execution; VA — Code of Virginia §45.2 requires surface owner written consent or express grant for surface mining of severed minerals.
- **Edge cases**: Implied surface easement under severance deed; expired surface lease still being used (creates tenancy at sufferance); overlapping surface leases from same lessor to multiple operators.

### 1.3 Mineral Estate Owned in Fee
- **What**: Tracts where SC owns the minerals (coal, oil/gas, other), whether or not it also owns the surface. The "mineral estate" can include all minerals, only coal, only specific seams, or all minerals except oil/gas.
- **Who**: LM, LMAN, TA.
- **Data captured**: Parcel ID, mineral interest description ("all coal", "Pittsburgh #8 only", "all coal below Pocahontas #4"), grantor source deed, recording reference, fractional interest %, NRI after burdens, severance date.
- **Documents**: Mineral deed, severance deed (often pre-1900), title opinion, mineral reservation in surface deed.
- **Frequency**: Continuous.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (mineral permit boundary), OPS (mineable reserve calc), CFO (depletion, unmined coal tax in WV/KY).
- **State-specific**: WV — coal "in place" is taxed as separate real property under WV Code §11-1C, valued by Tax Commissioner using statutory methodology; unmineable seams valued at $5/deed acre per 110 CSR 1I. KY — KRS 132.820 assesses unmined coal as a distinct interest in real property at fair market value in place, returned on Form 62A200(P), filed Jan 1, with Office of Property Valuation Division of Minerals Taxation. VA — varies by locality; many counties assess minerals separately.
- **Edge cases**: Mineral ownership severed seam-by-seam (Pittsburgh #8 owner ≠ Sewell owner); after-acquired-title issues; mineral interest "lost" due to never being separately taxed; dormant mineral interest statutes (none in WV/KY/VA but Pennsylvania-style dormant mineral statutes have been proposed).

### 1.4 Coal Estate by Seam
- **What**: For each tract with coal, identify which seams SC owns or controls and which are owned/leased separately. Critical because Appalachian operators often own/lease only specific seams.
- **Who**: LMAN, TA, OPS (geology).
- **Data captured**: Tract ID; for each named seam — ownership type (fee / leased / not owned), source deed/lease, depth interval, geologic correlation, mineable status, reserve tons (P&P/M&I).
- **Named seams (north→south, illustrative)**:
  - WV northern: Pittsburgh #8, Sewickley, Redstone, Waynesburg
  - WV southern: Eagle, Cedar Grove, Coalburg, Stockton, Powellton, Sewell, Beckley, Fire Creek, Pocahontas #3, #4, #6
  - VA: Imboden, Splashdam, Lower Banner, Upper Banner, Jawbone, Tiller, Raven, Pocahontas #3
  - KY eastern: Hazard #4, #5, #5A, #7, #8, #9, Fire Clay, Amburgy, Elkhorn
  - KY western: Davis (W. KY #9), Kentucky #11, #12, #13, #14
  - AL: Black Creek, Mary Lee, Blue Creek, Pratt
  - TN: Sewanee, Richland, Vowell
- **Documents**: Seam-coded deed/lease abstract, geologic cross-section, reserve report.
- **Frequency**: Continuous; reconciled to reserve report annually.
- **Hand-offs**: OPS (mine plan), ENV (permit MR boundary by seam), CFO (depletion by seam, reserve report for SEC if public).
- **State-specific**: All Appalachian states recognize seam-by-seam ownership; WV deeds frequently name specific seams; KY deeds often grant "all coal" with reservations.
- **Edge cases**: Two operators in same tract on different seams (subjacent support disputes); "coal below the [named seam]" reservations creating ambiguity on intermediate seams; coal blending across seams owned by different lessors triggers complex royalty splits.

### 1.5 Other Mineral Estates (Oil/Gas, Limestone, Timber, Hard Minerals)
- **What**: Register of non-coal minerals owned or controlled — oil & gas, sandstone/limestone, sand/gravel, hard minerals, methane (CBM). Important because oil/gas drilling overlying SC's coal can damage workings and trigger coal-owner notice rights.
- **Who**: LM, LMAN, TA, OPS.
- **Data captured**: Tract, mineral type, ownership/lease status, lessee (if leased out), royalty rate, depth interval.
- **Documents**: Oil/gas lease, CBM lease, timber deed, limestone lease.
- **Frequency**: Continuous.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (frac/drill notice), OPS (avoid drilling within mine workings), Legal.
- **State-specific**: WV recognizes implied coal-owner right to require plugging of overlying gas wells (Wendt v. WV Land Resources); KY/VA have separate CBM ownership statutes; VA Gas & Oil Act creates the Virginia Gas and Oil Board with conservation jurisdiction over CBM disputes.
- **Edge cases**: CBM ownership disputed between coal and gas estate owners (settled by VA legislation, less clear in WV); fracking on adjacent tract communicating with mine workings.

### 1.6 Title Chain (Chain of Title)
- **What**: Documented chain of conveyances from the present owner back to a "root of title" (in MRTA states) or to original sovereign grant (in non-MRTA states). For Appalachian coal, often back to original Virginia/Kentucky/Crown grants of late 1700s.
- **Who**: TA, LMAN (title runner), title abstract company.
- **Data captured**: For each link — grantor, grantee, instrument type, date executed, date recorded, deed book/page, consideration, acreage conveyed, exceptions/reservations.
- **Documents**: Abstract of title, title opinion (preliminary, supplemental, division order), runsheets, certified copies of deeds.
- **Frequency**: New chain at acquisition; supplemental opinions as needed (every new lease, every assignment).
- **Hand-offs**: TA → LM → CFO (for acquisition closing).
- **State-specific**: WV — Uniform Marketable Title Act (WV Code §36-11) provides 30-year root-of-title cleansing, but does not cut off mineral rights "of record". KY — no general MRTA; full chain to sovereign required for marketable title (most rigorous of the three). VA — limited MRTA-style relief under Va. Code §55.1-307; full chain typically required for coal title. AL — Ala. Code §35-4-71 thirty-year title act. TN — no MRTA.
- **Edge cases**: Burned courthouse counties (WV — Logan, Mingo, Boone all had courthouse fires; KY — multiple); pre-statehood KY/WV grants from VA; overlapping or conflicting sovereign grants ("Pasley grant" vs "Welch grant" overlaps).

### 1.7 Broad-Form Deed Analysis
- **What**: For severed-estate tracts, analyze whether SC's mineral title comes through a "broad form" deed (granting coal + right to use surface "by any means necessary or convenient") and whether modern mining methods (strip, MTR, longwall) are authorized.
- **Who**: TA, LM.
- **Data captured**: Source deed citation, deed language (grant + appurtenances), date executed, mining methods at execution, mining methods proposed, governing jurisprudence.
- **Documents**: Source severance deed, title opinion section on permitted mining methods, litigation file if contested.
- **Frequency**: Once per tract; revisited if new method proposed.
- **Hand-offs**: OPS (method selection), Legal (litigation risk).
- **State-specific**:
  - **KY**: Section 19(2) of KY Constitution (1988 amendment, "Broad Form Deed Amendment", approved by 82% of voters) — extraction methods presumed limited to those commonly in use when deed executed unless deed expressly authorizes otherwise. Effectively prohibits strip mining under broad-form deeds without surface owner consent.
  - **WV**: No constitutional amendment; case law uses "contemplation" doctrine — methods not contemplated at severance (e.g., longwall, MTR) not authorized by silence. *Schoene v. McElroy Coal Co.* (4th Cir. 2016) voided 1902 severance-deed subsidence waiver because longwall was not contemplated. WV Code §22-7 (Surface Owner Protection / subsidence) provides additional statutory protection.
  - **VA**: VA Code §45.2 requires written surface owner consent or express grant for surface coal extraction where estates are severed.
- **Edge cases**: Deed expressly grants "all methods now known or hereafter discovered" — usually upheld; deed reserves "right to enter and take" without method specifics — strictly construed against grantee in modern courts; longwall subsidence under broad-form deeds.

### 1.8 Boundary Survey & Plats
- **What**: Licensed survey of tract boundaries; required for new acquisitions, mining permit applications, lease negotiations, and boundary dispute resolution.
- **Who**: SUR (licensed PLS), LM.
- **Data captured**: Bearings/distances, monuments found/set, acreage by deed vs by survey, encroachments, adjoining owners, certified surveyor's signature.
- **Documents**: Survey plat, surveyor's report, field notes, recorded boundary line agreements (if disputes).
- **Frequency**: At acquisition, lease, permit, or dispute.
- **Hand-offs**: TA (title curative), ENV (permit boundary), OPS (mine planning), IT-GIS.
- **State-specific**: WV — surveyor's seal and certification per WV Board of Professional Surveyors; KY — KRS 322; VA — § 54.1-400; all require licensed PLS.
- **Edge cases**: Senior/junior survey conflicts (older patent prevails in KY/VA); senior calls overrunning junior; lost corners requiring proportionate reconstruction; "hanging" boundaries with no monuments.

### 1.9 Tax Map / Parcel ID Reconciliation
- **What**: Continuous reconciliation between SC's internal land records and county tax maps / PVA records / GIS layers.
- **Who**: LM, LMAN, IT-GIS.
- **Data captured**: County map/parcel ID, internal tract ID, acreage per tax map, acreage per deed, assessed value, billing address on file at county.
- **Documents**: County tax map, tax bill, PVA print-out.
- **Frequency**: Annually before tax bill cycle.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (tax payment), LM (assessment appeals).
- **State-specific**: KY — PVA in each county; tax bills issued by sheriff. WV — assessor in each county; tax bills issued by sheriff; "land book" published annually. VA — Commissioner of Revenue; treasurer collects. AL — revenue commissioner. TN — assessor + trustee.
- **Edge cases**: County splits a parcel without notice; parcel double-billed (assessed to two owners); parcel never on tax roll (escape assessment exposure).

---

## 2. Lease Inventory (Coal Mining Leases)

### 2.1 Coal Mining Lease Master Record
- **What**: One record per active or recently-expired coal lease. The lease abstract is the single source of truth.
- **Who**: LM (owner), LMAN (abstracting), RA (royalty fields).
- **Data captured**:
  - **Identification**: Lease number, lease name, region, primary lessor, primary lessee (SC entity).
  - **Parties**: Lessor(s) with NRI %, lessee, assignees, original lessee if assigned.
  - **Dates**: Execution, effective, primary term expiry, secondary term trigger ("so long as coal is being mined in paying quantities"), recording date, recording office, deed book/page.
  - **Premises**: Acreage, seams covered, depth restrictions, surface use rights, county/district.
  - **Royalty terms**: See §6.
  - **Operational rights**: Mining methods permitted (UG continuous, UG longwall, surface contour, mountaintop, auger, highwall miner), surface use grant, wheelage rights, tipple/loadout rights, water use rights, timber use rights.
  - **Lessor protections**: Audit rights, default/cure provisions, force majeure scope, indemnity, MFN clauses, surrender provisions, anti-assignment clauses.
  - **Reclamation allocation**: Who bonds, who reclaims, who indemnifies.
- **Documents**: Original recorded lease, all amendments/modifications/extensions, lease abstract (internal), title opinion on leasehold, surveyor's plat.
- **Frequency**: Maintained continuously; full re-abstracting at amendment.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (royalty calc, minimums calendar), OPS (mining method, permitted uses), ENV (reclamation allocation), RA (royalty engine setup), TA (curative).
- **State-specific**: WV — recording in county clerk's office of county where land lies (multiple recordings if multi-county); KY — recording in county clerk's office; some KY counties require deed-style acknowledgments. VA — circuit court clerk recording.
- **Edge cases**: Lease covers tracts in multiple counties (record in each); lease silent on a seam SC wants to mine; "head lease" with subleases creating chain of obligations; lease executed by deceased lessor's predecessor with disputed heirship.

### 2.2 Lease Abstract Generation
- **What**: Distill the lease into a structured one-page (or multi-page) abstract used by Accounting, Operations, and Legal.
- **Who**: LMAN, with TA review.
- **Data captured**: Same fields as 2.1 but in condensed structured form; cross-references to lease section/paragraph; "alerts" for nonstandard clauses (MFN, anti-Mountaintop, no longwall, etc.).
- **Documents**: Abstract form (standard template).
- **Frequency**: Once per lease; refresh on amendment.
- **Hand-offs**: All downstream consumers — RA, OPS, ENV, CFO.
- **Edge cases**: Lease "incorporates by reference" prior agreements not in SC's files; lease executed in two parts (separate surface and mineral instruments).

### 2.3 Seams Leased per Lease
- **What**: For each lease, enumerate which named coal seams are within the grant and which are reserved/excluded.
- **Who**: LMAN, OPS geology.
- **Data captured**: Lease ID, seam name, depth interval (where defined), mining method permitted by seam, royalty rate by seam (where rates differ).
- **Documents**: Lease excerpt, geologic correlation map.
- **Frequency**: Continuous.
- **Hand-offs**: RA (royalty by seam), OPS (mine plan).
- **State-specific**: WV/VA leases commonly identify seams by historic local names; KY leases often use Hazard or Western KY numbering; reconciling stratigraphy across leases is essential.
- **Edge cases**: Seam identified by old/colloquial name no longer in geologic literature; lease grants "Pittsburgh and lower seams" — what's the floor?

### 2.4 Mining Methods Permitted
- **What**: Catalog of permitted methods per lease (room-and-pillar UG, longwall, surface contour, MTR, auger, highwall miner, refuse reprocessing).
- **Who**: LMAN, OPS, TA.
- **Data captured**: Lease ID, methods permitted, methods prohibited, subsidence waiver scope, MTR/cross-ridge mining authorization.
- **Documents**: Lease section on operations; supplemental method authorizations.
- **Frequency**: At lease execution; revisited at every change of method.
- **Hand-offs**: OPS, ENV.
- **State-specific**: KY Broad Form Deed Amendment may invalidate strip rights even if granted in old broad-form deed without express surface consent; WV "contemplation" doctrine similar effect on longwall under old deeds.
- **Edge cases**: Lease silent — courts split; "any method now or hereafter known" — generally upheld; written modification to authorize MTR/longwall on existing UG-only lease.

---

## 3. Lease Maintenance Calendar

### 3.1 Minimum Royalty / Advance Royalty Schedule
- **What**: Calendar of all minimum royalty, advance royalty, and delay rental payments by lease.
- **Who**: RA, LRC.
- **Data captured**: Lease ID, payment type, amount, due date, frequency, recoupable Y/N, recoupment period, paid date, check #, lessor.
- **Documents**: Lease excerpt; payment confirmation; recoupment schedule.
- **Frequency**: Monthly review; payments per lease terms (often Jan 1 or anniversary).
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (cash out), RA (accrual booking), LRC (1099 reporting).
- **Edge cases**: Lease with "recoupable up to 5 prior years' production" — must track running recoupment balance; minimum waived during force majeure; advance royalty paid on UG lease but coal mined from different seam.

### 3.2 Renewal / Extension Options
- **What**: Track all renewal/extension windows and the notice provisions required to exercise.
- **Who**: LM, LMAN.
- **Data captured**: Lease ID, option type, exercise window (start/end), notice form required, decision deadline, decision maker, rationale documented.
- **Documents**: Notice of intent to renew/extend; cover letter; certified mail receipt.
- **Frequency**: Reviewed quarterly; alerts 180/90/30 days before window closes.
- **Hand-offs**: LM, CFO (financial decision), OPS (mine plan dependency).
- **Edge cases**: Notice sent to old address (lessor moved); option requires lessor counter-signature; option expired during pandemic — equitable tolling argument.

### 3.3 Notice of Expiration / Surrender / Release
- **What**: Manage surrender of expiring or uneconomic leases; record releases in courthouse to clear title.
- **Who**: LM, LMAN, TA.
- **Data captured**: Lease ID, surrender date, reason, release recorded Y/N, recording reference.
- **Documents**: Notice of surrender, Release of Lease (recordable form), recording cover sheet.
- **Frequency**: Per lease lifecycle.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (permit retirement, bond release), CFO (lease asset/ARO retirement), TA (recording).
- **State-specific**: Recording recommended in all three primary states to clear title and stop minimum royalty obligations.
- **Edge cases**: Lessor refuses to acknowledge surrender; unrecorded surrender leaves cloud on title; surrender of mined-out tract with un-reclaimed acreage triggers reclamation dispute.

### 3.4 Default / Cure Notices
- **What**: Track defaults asserted by lessors and cure deadlines.
- **Who**: LM, LRC, Legal.
- **Data captured**: Lease ID, default alleged, notice date, cure window, cure actions taken, status.
- **Documents**: Lessor's default letter, SC response, cure evidence.
- **Frequency**: Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs**: Legal (litigation risk), CFO (settlement reserves).
- **Edge cases**: Alleged default in royalty calc → triggers full lookback audit; default for failure to mine in "paying quantities" — fact-intensive defense.

---

## 4. Sub-Leases / Assignments

### 4.1 Sub-Lease Out (SC as Sub-Lessor to Contract Miner)
- **What**: When SC sub-leases all or part of its leasehold to a contract miner.
- **Who**: LM, TA.
- **Data captured**: Sub-lease ID, head lease ID, sublessee, term, royalty back to SC, indemnity, bond replacement, permit transfer commitment.
- **Documents**: Sub-lease agreement, head-lessor consent letter, recorded memorandum.
- **Frequency**: Per transaction.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (permit transfer), CFO (royalty income), Legal.
- **State-specific**: Many head leases require head-lessor written consent for sub-lease; recording of memorandum in county.
- **Edge cases**: Sublessee defaults → SC remains liable to head lessor (privity of contract); sublessee bankruptcy.

### 4.2 Assignment In (SC as Assignee from Prior Operator)
- **What**: When SC takes assignment of an existing lease from another operator.
- **Who**: LM, LMAN, TA, ENV.
- **Data captured**: Lease ID, assignor, assignment effective date, consideration, lessor consent obtained Y/N, recorded reference, indemnity for prior conduct.
- **Documents**: Assignment & Assumption Agreement, lessor consent, recorded assignment.
- **Frequency**: Per transaction.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (permit transfer / SMCRA permit revision), HSE (latent liabilities), CFO (consideration accounting).
- **State-specific**: SMCRA permit transfer requires regulatory approval (WV DEP, KY EEC DMRE, VA DMRE); takes 60–180 days typical. Lessor consent required by most modern leases.
- **Edge cases**: Assumed indemnity for pre-assignment environmental conditions; pre-existing reclamation deficiency; unfunded MEPP/UMWA contribution liability follows the operator under ERISA §4204 sale-of-assets safe harbor (must structure carefully).

### 4.3 Assignment Out (SC Assigns to Buyer)
- **What**: SC assigns one or more leases to a buyer (typically as part of asset sale).
- **Who**: LM, TA, CFO.
- **Data captured**: Assignee, assignment date, consideration, lessor consent, indemnification, tail-liability allocation.
- **Documents**: Assignment & Assumption, lessor consent, recorded instrument.
- **Frequency**: Per divestiture.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (permit transfer), CFO (gain/loss on sale), HR (MEPP withdrawal liability analysis).
- **Edge cases**: Without lessor consent, assignment voidable; ERISA §4204 unfunded vested benefit ("UVB") liability if UMWA participant — requires bond/escrow.

### 4.4 Consent-to-Assign Tracking
- **What**: For every consent required, document request, response, conditions, and recording.
- **Who**: LMAN, TA.
- **Data captured**: Lease ID, party to consent, request date, response date, conditions imposed, fee paid.
- **Documents**: Consent letter, fee invoice.
- **Frequency**: Per transaction.
- **Edge cases**: Lessor demands "consent fee" not contemplated by lease; lessor refuses consent unreasonably → potential litigation.

---

## 5. Overriding Royalty Interests (ORRI) & Net Profits Interests (NPI)

### 5.1 ORRI Register
- **What**: Register of all ORRIs burdening SC's leasehold interests and any ORRIs SC owns in others' leases.
- **Who**: RA, LM, TA.
- **Data captured**: Lease ID, ORRI holder, ORRI %, basis (gross sales / net sales / per-ton fixed), carve-outs (specific seams, specific mining methods), term (life of lease vs term-of-years), payment frequency, source instrument (assignment, conveyance), recording reference, 1099 status.
- **Documents**: ORRI assignment, conveyance, recorded memorandum, W-9, 1099-MISC/NEC.
- **Frequency**: Continuous; reconciled monthly to royalty payments.
- **Hand-offs**: RA (royalty calc), CFO (cash out / 1099), LRC (owner relations).
- **State-specific**: WV/KY/VA all recognize ORRI as a real property interest; assignment must satisfy statute of frauds and recording statutes.
- **Edge cases**: ORRI carved out of expired or surrendered lease — does it survive on new lease (depends on "extension or renewal" clause)? Stacking ORRIs reducing NRI below economic threshold; ORRI on coal blended with non-burdened coal at prep plant.

### 5.2 NPI (Net Profits Interest)
- **What**: NPI calculation engine — share of net profits after deductions defined in the NPI conveyance.
- **Who**: RA, CFO.
- **Data captured**: NPI %, defined deductions (capital cost recovery, operating cost, transportation, marketing, sustaining capital), payment frequency, audit rights.
- **Documents**: NPI conveyance, periodic NPI statement.
- **Frequency**: Quarterly typical.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (cost accounting), Legal (audit defense).
- **Edge cases**: NPI never pays because costs exceed revenue; deduction disputes; "payout" trigger for working-interest reversion.

---

## 6. Royalty Calculation Engine

### 6.1 Royalty Setup per Lease
- **What**: Configure the royalty engine per lease — formula, rate, minimums, deductions allowed, ORRI/NPI stack.
- **Who**: RA (setup), LM (lease term confirmation), CFO (review), TA (legal review).
- **Data captured**:
  - Royalty type (% of gross sales / % of net sales / $ per ton fixed / sliding scale / hybrid)
  - Rate or rate table (e.g., 5% of gross; or $1.50/ton; or 8% if price ≤ $60, 10% if $60–$80, 12% if > $80)
  - Heating-value adjustment (Btu per pound base, escalator/de-escalator)
  - Quality penalties/premiums (sulfur, ash, moisture)
  - Allowed deductions (washing, drying, transportation to first sale point, severance pass-through, marketing fee cap, ad valorem pass-through)
  - Minimum royalty (annual amount, recoupment terms)
  - Advance royalty (recoupable Y/N, recoupment window)
  - ORRI/NPI stack
  - Take-in-kind option Y/N
  - Market value vs actual sale price (arms-length sale clause)
  - Affiliate-sale anti-abuse clause (use posted price or market index)
  - Payment frequency (monthly, quarterly)
  - Payment due date (e.g., last day of month following production)
  - Statement format requirements
- **Documents**: Lease, royalty setup worksheet, RA's reviewer sign-off.
- **Frequency**: Once per lease; refresh on amendment.
- **Hand-offs**: RA, CFO, Audit.
- **Edge cases**: Lease formula references a price index that no longer publishes (e.g., Platts coal index discontinued for region); sliding scale crossing tax brackets; deduction "uncapped" → margin compression.

### 6.2 Monthly Royalty Calculation
- **What**: Compute monthly royalty per lease using production, sales, and deductions data.
- **Who**: RA.
- **Inputs**: Tons sold by lease (from OPS / Sales), gross sale proceeds, allowed deductions (washing yield loss, transportation, severance tax pass-through, marketing fee), heating value, quality data.
- **Outputs**: Gross royalty, ORRI/NPI splits, withholding (state non-resident), net check.
- **Documents**: Royalty calculation worksheet, royalty statement to lessor, check/ACH advice, 1099 accumulator.
- **Frequency**: Monthly (typical) or quarterly per lease.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (cash out), LRC (statement mail/email), Tax (1099/state withholding).
- **State-specific withholding**:
  - WV — non-resident withholding on royalty income to non-resident payees (WV State Tax §11-21-71a); 6.5% rate currently
  - KY — KRS 141.206 partnership/pass-through entity withholding for non-resident partners; for ORRI/royalty individual non-residents, generally no withholding on simple lessor royalties but check annually
  - VA — Va. Code §58.1-486.2 non-resident pass-through withholding 5%
- **Edge cases**: Coal blended from multiple leases — apportion sale proceeds by tons; lessor's tract produced reject only; royalty paid in advance and now recoupment is exhausted; lessor disputes Btu adjustment.

### 6.3 Royalty Suspense Management
- **What**: Royalties not paid out due to title defects, heir issues, address unknown, escheat dormancy approaching, etc.
- **Who**: RA, LRC, TA.
- **Data captured**: Lessor ID, suspense reason, suspense start date, suspense amount running total, dormancy clock, action required to release, last contact attempt.
- **Documents**: Suspense register, due diligence letters, certified mail tracking.
- **Frequency**: Monthly review.
- **Hand-offs**: TA (heirship / curative), LRC (owner search), Unclaimed Property officer (compliance).
- **State-specific (unclaimed property dormancy)**:
  - WV — 3 years for most property types (WV Code §36-8); due diligence notice required at $50+ between 60–120 days before report; annual report due before November 1
  - KY — 3 years for most intangibles (KRS 393A); annual report due Nov 1; due diligence letter required
  - VA — generally 5 years for royalties (Va. Code §55.1-2500 et seq.); report due Nov 1
  - AL — 3 years (Ala. Code §35-12); TN — generally 3-5 years depending on type
- **Edge cases**: Lessor died without estate filing; heirs scattered across multiple states; lessor address returned mail repeatedly; lessor disputes amount and refuses to cash check (escheat clock running).

### 6.4 Royalty Statement Generation
- **What**: Produce lessor-readable royalty statements per lease per period.
- **Who**: RA, LRC.
- **Data captured per statement**: Lease, period, tract, seam, tons produced/sold, gross sale price/ton, gross sales $, deductions itemized, royalty rate, gross royalty, ORRI/NPI splits, withholding, net amount, payment method, payment date, check#/ACH ref.
- **Documents**: Royalty statement (PDF, mailed and/or owner portal).
- **Frequency**: Monthly/quarterly per lease.
- **Hand-offs**: LRC (mail/portal upload), CFO (cash disbursement).
- **Edge cases**: Lessor wants statement re-cut to correct prior period; statement triggers audit request.

### 6.5 1099 Generation
- **What**: Annual 1099-MISC (or 1099-NEC where applicable) for royalty paid.
- **Who**: RA, CFO/Tax.
- **Data captured**: Lessor TIN/SSN, address, total royalty paid (Box 2 — Royalties), state withholding by state.
- **Documents**: 1099-MISC, 1096 transmittal, state copies, lessor copy.
- **Frequency**: Annually; mailed by Jan 31; IRS-filed by Feb 28 (paper) / Mar 31 (e-file).
- **Hand-offs**: CFO/Tax, LRC.
- **Edge cases**: Lessor refuses to provide W-9 → 24% backup withholding required; ITIN vs SSN issue; estate/trust requires EIN; foreign lessor — 1042-S not 1099.

### 6.6 Royalty Audit Defense
- **What**: Defend audits brought by lessors (most leases grant audit rights to lessor).
- **Who**: RA (data), CFO (oversight), Legal.
- **Data captured**: Audit notice, scope, period, auditor, status, findings, settlements.
- **Documents**: Audit notice, document production log, audit report, settlement agreement.
- **Frequency**: Event-driven (typically every 2–5 years per major lease).
- **Hand-offs**: Legal, CFO.
- **Edge cases**: Audit reveals systemic underpayment → multi-lease lookback; auditor demands access to affiliate sales data; "marketing fee" deduction challenged.

### 6.7 Federal Coal Royalty Reporting (ONRR Form ONRR-4430)
- **What**: For any federal coal leases (BLM-administered) — monthly production and royalty reporting to ONRR.
- **Who**: RA, CFO.
- **Data captured per form**: Lease number (federal), product code, sales type code, transaction code, sales volume, sales value, royalty value, allowance deductions, royalty rate.
- **Documents**: Form ONRR-4430 (electronic submission required unless exempt), production records, sales invoices.
- **Frequency**: Monthly — due by 4:00 PM Mountain Time on the last day of the month following the production month, per 30 CFR §1210.201.
- **Federal coal royalty rates**: 8% UG, 12.5% surface (Mineral Leasing Act default); some leases issued under royalty relief at reduced rates.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (cash out to ONRR), Legal (LMU/diligent development compliance).
- **State-specific**: Federal leases not common in WV/VA/KY (largely private land); more relevant for any AL/TN federal acreage.
- **Edge cases**: Late filing penalties ($10/day or more); valuation challenges (arm's-length vs index); LMU diligent development not met → potential lease termination.

---

## 7. Federal Coal Leases (BLM)

### 7.1 Federal Lease Bid Tracking (LBA / Competitive Sale)
- **What**: Tracking Lease-by-Application (LBA) submissions and competitive lease sale participation.
- **Who**: LM, CFO, Legal.
- **Data captured**: LBA filing date, tract description, fair market value estimate, bonus bid, bid result, lease number issued.
- **Documents**: LBA application, Form 3400-12, sale notice, bid sheet, lease instrument.
- **Frequency**: Per opportunity (rare in Appalachia).
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (bonus payment), ENV (NEPA / EIS participation), Legal.

### 7.2 Diligent Development & LMU Designation
- **What**: Federal leases must produce coal within a defined period or be subject to cancellation; Logical Mining Unit (LMU) designations consolidate multiple leases for diligence.
- **Who**: LM, OPS.
- **Data captured**: Lease term, diligence deadline, production threshold, LMU designation, LMU production rollup.
- **Documents**: BLM diligence reports, LMU designation order.
- **Frequency**: Annual diligence certification.
- **Hand-offs**: OPS (production planning), CFO.

### 7.3 ONRR Royalty Payment & Reporting
- See §6.7 above.

---

## 8. Surface Owner / Surface Use Agreements

### 8.1 Surface Owner Master
- **What**: For every tract where SC mines under severed minerals, maintain a record of the surface owner(s) and surface owner agreement (SOA).
- **Who**: LM, LMAN, LRC.
- **Data captured**: Tract ID, surface owner(s), contact, payment terms, notice address, recorded consent (if any), historic dealings, complaint history.
- **Documents**: Severance deed showing the split, SOA, surface damage release, photos.
- **Frequency**: Continuous.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (notice & permitting), HSE (blast notice), Legal (complaints/litigation).
- **State-specific**:
  - **WV**: Surface owner protections under WV Code §22-3 (SMCRA) and case law (Buffalo Mining doctrine). Specific surface owner consent required for surface mining of severed coal in many circumstances. Subsidence claims under WV Code §22-3-25 et seq.
  - **KY**: Section 19(2) Constitution (1988 Broad Form Deed Amendment) — explicit written surface owner consent required for any method not contemplated when deed was executed. Pre-mining notice per 405 KAR (general permit notice 30 days; specific notice provisions in various sections).
  - **VA**: VA Code §45.2-1010 et seq. — written surface owner consent required, or express grant of surface mining rights in the conveyance.
- **Edge cases**: Surface owner deceased / heirs unknown; multiple surface owners (joint tenants); surface owner is also coal lessor (combined SOA + lease); surface owner is anti-mining activist; absentee surface owner.

### 8.2 Surface Owner Pre-Mining Notice
- **What**: Statutory notice to surface owner before mining commences.
- **Who**: ENV, LMAN, LRC.
- **Data captured**: Notice date, method (certified mail / personal service), recipient, mining start date noticed, response received Y/N.
- **Documents**: Notice letter, certified mail receipt, affidavit of service.
- **Frequency**: Per permit / per mine start.
- **State-specific**:
  - **WV**: SMCRA permit application includes notice provisions; adjacent surface owners and owners of structures within ½ mile must be noticed of blasting plans
  - **KY**: Pre-blast notice within 1/2 mile (405 KAR 16:120 / 18:120); permit application public notice in newspaper
  - **VA**: Pre-blast notices required to dwellings within 1/2 mile; SMCRA permit notice requirements
- **Edge cases**: New homeowner moves in after notice given — must SC re-notice? Notice sent to property address rather than legal mailing address.

### 8.3 Surface Damage Settlement
- **What**: Process and settle claims for surface damage (subsidence cracks, blast damage, well loss, spring loss, slipped slopes, road damage, livestock loss).
- **Who**: LRC, Legal, Insurance/Risk Manager, HSE (blasting).
- **Data captured**: Claim ID, claimant, property address, damage type, claim date, investigation result, settlement amount, release executed Y/N.
- **Documents**: Claim form, pre-blast survey, post-damage inspection report, photos, repair estimates, release of claims, payment record.
- **Frequency**: Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs**: HSE (blast records), Insurance (excess coverage), Legal.
- **State-specific**:
  - **WV**: Water supply replacement obligation under WV Code §22-3-24 (coal operator must replace contaminated/diminished water supply); subsidence damage rebuttable presumption under §22-3-25
  - **KY**: 405 KAR water replacement; subsidence damage similar presumption
  - **VA**: §45.2 water replacement; subsidence damage provisions
  - **Federal**: SMCRA §720 — water replacement and subsidence repair obligations apply nationally
- **Edge cases**: Damage cause disputed (mining vs natural settlement); claimant filed years later (statute of limitations); pre-blast survey shows pre-existing damage; alleged blast damage from operation miles away.

### 8.4 Surface Owner Buyouts (MTR / Large-Footprint Operations)
- **What**: Acquisition of surface in fee from owner who does not want to live near operations.
- **Who**: LM, LMAN, TA, CFO.
- **Data captured**: Owner, parcel, appraisal, offer, accepted price, closing date.
- **Documents**: Appraisal, purchase agreement, deed, settlement statement, relocation assistance documentation.
- **Frequency**: Per project.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (capital), TA (deed, recording), HR if employee assistance.
- **Edge cases**: Owner refuses sale → continue mining with severed-mineral rights subject to surface protections; relocation assistance required if displacement is federally funded (Uniform Relocation Act).

---

## 9. Easements & Rights of Way (ROW)

### 9.1 Haul Road Easements
- **What**: Easement to construct, use, and maintain coal haul roads across third-party surface.
- **Who**: LMAN, TA, ENV (permit), OPS.
- **Data captured**: Easement ID, grantor, grantee, length, width, term, per-ton wheelage / lump-sum fee, recording reference, maintenance obligations, reversion provisions.
- **Documents**: Easement deed, recorded memorandum, survey/centerline plat, maintenance agreement.
- **Frequency**: Per ROW.
- **Hand-offs**: OPS, ENV (DOT/road permits), CFO (payment).
- **Edge cases**: Easement expires while haul road still needed; easement grantor sells underlying land — successor unhappy; bonded/improved condition for return.

### 9.2 Conveyor / Belt / Slurry Pipeline Easements
- **What**: Linear easements for overland conveyors, refuse slurry pipelines.
- **Who**: LMAN, TA, ENV.
- **Data captured**: Same as 9.1 plus pipeline diameter/pressure, electrical clearances, secondary containment.
- **Documents**: Easement deed, plan/profile sheets.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (spill prevention plan), OPS.
- **Edge cases**: Slurry release across easement creates third-party CERCLA exposure.

### 9.3 Power Line, Water Line, Gas Line Easements
- **What**: Utility easements both granted to SC and granted by SC to utilities.
- **Who**: LMAN, TA.
- **Data captured**: Easement holder, voltage / pressure, encroachment provisions, indemnity.
- **Documents**: Utility easement form, recorded.
- **Hand-offs**: OPS, Maintenance.
- **Edge cases**: Buried gas line crossing planned strip pit — relocation cost allocation.

### 9.4 Rail Spur / Loadout ROW
- **What**: Easement or fee strip for rail spur access to loadout.
- **Who**: LM, Rail Engineering.
- **Data captured**: ROW width, switch ownership, rail carrier (CSX / NS), per-car loading fee.
- **Documents**: Spur agreement with railroad, ROW deed/easement.
- **Hand-offs**: OPS, Rail logistics, CFO.
- **Edge cases**: STB (Surface Transportation Board) abandonment; railroad reversion clauses.

### 9.5 Drainage / Sediment Pond Easements
- **What**: Easement for off-permit drainage features, ponds, NPDES outfalls on third-party surface.
- **Who**: ENV, LMAN.
- **Data captured**: Pond ID, outfall ID, easement, monitoring obligations, post-mining transfer.
- **Documents**: Easement, NPDES permit, monitoring records.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (NPDES), OPS.
- **Edge cases**: Post-mining drainage continues — perpetual easement needed.

### 9.6 ROW Recording & Reversion Tracking
- **What**: Ensure all ROWs are recorded; track reversion triggers.
- **Who**: TA, LMAN.
- **Data captured**: Recording reference, reversion trigger (e.g., 1 year of non-use), notice obligation to revert.
- **Documents**: Recorded easement, release upon reversion.
- **Frequency**: Annual ROW audit.
- **Edge cases**: ROW abandoned without formal release — cloud on title.
