## 10. Water Rights

### 10.1 Water Withdrawal Permits / Registrations
- **What**: Authorization to withdraw surface or groundwater for mine use (dust suppression, processing, potable, slurry transport).
- **Who**: ENV, LM.
- **Data captured**: Source (stream, well, mine pool), permitted volume, actual usage, reporting frequency.
- **Documents**: Withdrawal permit/registration, monthly use logs, annual report.
- **Frequency**: Annual reporting; permit renewal per term.
- **State-specific**:
  - **WV**: WV Code §22-26 Water Resources Protection Act — large-quantity users (>300,000 gallons/month) must register with DEP; coal mine water diverted but not used and not affecting low-flow is exempt from "withdrawal" definition
  - **VA**: Virginia Water Withdrawal Reporting (VWUDS) per §62.1-44.38; >10,000 GPD must report annually
  - **KY**: Division of Water (DOW) withdrawal permits per KRS 151 / 401 KAR 4; >10,000 GPD generally requires permit
  - **AL/TN**: AL Office of Water Resources Capacity Use Areas; TN DEC withdrawal registration
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (NPDES coordination), OPS (mine water management).
- **Edge cases**: Withdrawal exceeds permit → enforcement; downstream user complaints about flow reduction; mine pool water rights disputed between adjacent operators.

### 10.2 Riparian Rights
- **What**: Common-law riparian rights of SC as upstream/downstream owner.
- **Who**: TA, LM.
- **Data captured**: Stream, frontage, ownership.
- **Documents**: Deeds.
- **State-specific**: WV/KY/VA are riparian states (modified); reasonable use doctrine.
- **Edge cases**: Riparian downstream user sues for diversion / pollution.

### 10.3 Mine Pool Water Rights & Sales
- **What**: Rights to water accumulated in inactive UG workings; potential for water sale to industrial or municipal users.
- **Who**: ENV, LM, CFO.
- **Data captured**: Pool ID, volume, quality, sale contracts, treatment cost.
- **Documents**: Mine pool study, water sale agreement, treatment records, NPDES discharge permit if treated and discharged.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV, OPS.
- **Edge cases**: Pool ownership disputed between SC and surface owner / state; AMD treatment costs exceed sale revenue.

---

## 11. Timber Rights

### 11.1 Pre-Mining Timber Inventory & Sale
- **What**: Inventory and harvest of merchantable timber before surface disturbance.
- **Who**: LM, forester (contract typical), LMAN.
- **Data captured**: Tract, species, BDFT/cords, cruise date, sale terms, contractor, stumpage rate.
- **Documents**: Timber cruise report, timber sale contract, slash agreement, harvest map.
- **Frequency**: Pre-mining per tract.
- **Hand-offs**: OPS (clearing schedule), ENV (E&S after harvest), CFO (timber revenue, separately depleted).
- **State-specific**: WV — Logging Sediment Control Act §19-1B; KY — KRS Chapter 149 (Forest Conservation Act / Master Logger required); VA — silviculture BMPs.
- **Edge cases**: Lease silent on timber — most coal leases grant timber for mining use; standalone timber deeds; landowner reserved timber.

### 11.2 Stumpage Payments to Timber Owner
- **What**: Payment for timber to landowner where timber is reserved.
- **Who**: RA, LRC, LM.
- **Data captured**: Volume harvested, stumpage rate, payee, payment date.
- **Documents**: Stumpage statement, payment record.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO, Tax (1099 if applicable).

### 11.3 Replanting / Post-Mining Forestry
- **What**: Tree replanting under FRA (Forestry Reclamation Approach) post-mining; replanting obligations under permit.
- **Who**: ENV, contractor.
- **Data captured**: Acres planted, species, survival counts.
- **Documents**: Planting plan, contractor invoice, survival surveys.
- **Frequency**: Per permit area, multi-year monitoring.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (bond release), Legal.
- **Edge cases**: Survival fails → replant; ARRI guidelines compliance.

## 12. Lessor Relations

### 12.1 Lessor Master Record
- **What**: Master record per lessor / royalty payee.
- **Who**: LRC, RA.
- **Data captured**: Lessor name, type (individual/trust/estate/LLC/govt), TIN/SSN/EIN, mailing address, physical address, phone, email, payment method (check/ACH), bank info, W-9 on file Y/N, W-9 date, backup withholding Y/N, communications preference, do-not-contact flag.
- **Documents**: W-9, W-8 (foreign), ACH authorization, voided check.
- **Frequency**: Continuous; annual refresh.
- **Hand-offs**: RA (royalty payment), CFO (vendor master sync), Tax (1099).
- **State-specific**: Non-resident state withholding setup per §6.2.
- **Edge cases**: Lessor changes name (marriage, divorce); business entity dissolved; lessor demands all-email communications.

### 12.2 Heirship Tree Maintenance
- **What**: For deceased original lessors, build and maintain heirship tree showing fractional shares of each heir.
- **Who**: TA, LMAN, LRC.
- **Data captured**: Original lessor, date of death, probate court, will/intestate, each heir with share %, address, contact info, status (active / suspense / unknown).
- **Documents**: Death certificate, will, affidavit of heirship, probate court order, family tree chart, genealogist report.
- **Frequency**: Updated on each death, marriage, birth notification.
- **Hand-offs**: RA (royalty split update), TA (curative if disputed), LRC.
- **State-specific**: WV, KY, VA all recognize affidavits of heirship; KY also allows "small estate" procedures; intestate share rules differ by state (KRS 391; WV Code §42-1; Va. Code §64.2-200 et seq.).
- **Edge cases**: Heir whose interest is < 1/1,000,000; predeceased heir with own descendants (per stirpes vs per capita); adopted-out heirs; non-marital children with paternity issues; missing/unknown heirs (force partition / interpleader).

### 12.3 Curative Work for Lessors
- **What**: Legal work to clear lessor's title issues so royalties can be paid without risk to SC.
- **Who**: TA, outside curative counsel, LMAN.
- **Data captured**: Issue type (missing heir, conflicting deed, recorded but never indexed instrument, forged signature claim, etc.), action plan, status, cost, resolution date.
- **Documents**: Heirship affidavit, quitclaim deed, partition order, quiet title judgment, ratification of lease.
- **Frequency**: Per issue.
- **Hand-offs**: TA, Legal, RA (release of suspense).
- **State-specific**: KY allows partition by sale (KRS Chapter 381); WV similar (WV Code §37-4); VA (Va. Code §8.01-83); all allow quiet title actions.
- **Edge cases**: Heir refuses to sign ratification → interpleader / partition; "lost" heir located via genealogist after 30 years.

### 12.4 Power of Attorney / Guardianship Tracking
- **What**: Track POAs, trusts, conservatorships affecting lessor's right to receive payment.
- **Who**: LRC, TA.
- **Data captured**: POA/trustee/guardian name, scope, expiration, court of appointment.
- **Documents**: POA instrument, trust agreement, letters of guardianship.
- **Frequency**: Continuous.
- **Hand-offs**: RA (payee per POA), Legal.
- **Edge cases**: POA challenged by another family member; trustee replaced mid-period.

### 12.5 Lessor Portal / Owner Relations
- **What**: Self-serve portal for lessors to view statements, update contact info, request payment history.
- **Who**: LRC, IT.
- **Data captured**: Portal login, last login, address change requests, document downloads, support tickets.
- **Documents**: Portal records.
- **Hand-offs**: RA, IT.

## 13. Title & Courthouse Work

### 13.1 Recording Deeds, Leases, Modifications, Releases
- **What**: Physically (or electronically) record instruments in county clerk / circuit court clerk / probate judge office.
- **Who**: TA, LMAN (runner), title company.
- **Data captured**: Instrument type, parties, date executed, date recorded, recording reference (book/page or instrument#), recording fees, transfer tax paid.
- **Documents**: Original/certified copy of recorded instrument.
- **Frequency**: Continuous.
- **Hand-offs**: LM (update master), CFO (recording fees), TA (chain).
- **State-specific**:
  - WV — recording in county clerk; transfer tax $1.10/$500 of consideration (county) + $1.65/$500 (state, deeds only)
  - KY — county clerk; transfer tax $0.50/$500
  - VA — circuit court clerk; recording fees + grantor tax + local tax
  - AL — probate judge; deed tax $0.50/$500
  - TN — register of deeds; transfer tax $0.37/$100
- **Edge cases**: Instrument rejected at recording (notary defect, wrong county); e-recording not available in rural county; consideration affidavit required (KY).

### 13.2 Title Search & Examination for Acquisitions
- **What**: Full title search and opinion on tracts being acquired or new leases being taken.
- **Who**: TA, outside coal title counsel, title runner.
- **Data captured**: Search date, examiner, period searched, root of title, exceptions, requirements.
- **Documents**: Runsheet, abstract, title opinion (preliminary, supplemental, division order).
- **Frequency**: Per acquisition / lease.
- **Hand-offs**: LM (decision), CFO (closing), Insurance (title insurance).
- **State-specific**: WV requires "good and marketable title"; KY also; VA "marketable" standard; depth of search varies by transaction risk.
- **Edge cases**: Burned-courthouse counties — secondary sources (tax rolls, surveyor's books, US Census, mineral atlas).

### 13.3 Curative Title Actions (Partition, Quiet Title, Slander)
- **What**: Litigation to clear title defects (partition fractional interests, quiet adverse claims, recover from slander).
- **Who**: TA, outside litigation counsel.
- **Data captured**: Case caption, court, filing date, parties, issues, status, cost, outcome.
- **Documents**: Complaint, lis pendens, judgment, recorded final order.
- **Frequency**: Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs**: LM (asset value impact), CFO (cost), Legal.
- **State-specific**: Partition by sale generally available in all three; quiet title statutes — WV §51-2-2 / Code §55-12A; KY §411.120; Va. Code §55.1-119.
- **Edge cases**: Adverse possession claim by surface owner against severed minerals — generally NOT permitted post-severance under most Appalachian case law (severed minerals not subject to AP without actual mining adverse to record owner).

### 13.4 Property Tax Delinquency Monitoring
- **What**: Monitor tax delinquency lists for tracts of interest — potential acquisition opportunity at sheriff's sale.
- **Who**: LM, LMAN.
- **Data captured**: Parcel, owner of record, year delinquent, amount, redemption period, sale date.
- **Documents**: Sheriff's delinquent list, sale notice, certificate of purchase, deed.
- **Frequency**: Annual.
- **Hand-offs**: LM, CFO.
- **State-specific**:
  - WV — tax sale by sheriff; certificate of sale; 17-month redemption; deed by State Auditor (§11A)
  - KY — third-party purchaser certificates of delinquency (KRS 134); priority lien
  - VA — judicial tax sales (§58.1-3965 et seq.)
- **Edge cases**: Tract of severed minerals never separately assessed; redemption right exercised after planning purchase.

## 14. Acquisitions

### 14.1 Acquisition Title Due Diligence
- **What**: Full title diligence on acquisition target — leases, fee, ORRIs, easements, water/timber.
- **Who**: TA, outside counsel, LM.
- **Data captured**: Asset schedule, title status per asset, requirements, exceptions, indemnity needs.
- **Documents**: DD memorandum, asset schedules, exception schedules.
- **Frequency**: Per acquisition.
- **Hand-offs**: LM (purchase agreement), CFO (PPA), Legal.
- **Edge cases**: Seller has unrecorded leases; lessor consents needed before closing.

### 14.2 Environmental & Permit DD
- **What**: SMCRA permit status, AVS (Applicant Violator System) check, bond status, NPDES status, AMD liability.
- **Who**: ENV, Legal.
- **Data captured**: Permits + status, bonds posted, outstanding NOVs, OSMRE/state issues.
- **Documents**: Permit files, AVS report, ECOS database, bond pool reports.
- **Hand-offs**: LM, CFO.

### 14.3 Reclamation Liability Assumption
- **What**: Quantify and allocate reclamation obligations.
- **Who**: ENV, CFO, Legal.
- **Data captured**: Estimated reclamation cost per permit, ARO, bond replacement cost, indemnity from seller.
- **Documents**: Reclamation cost estimate, ARO calc, indemnity agreement.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO, ENV.

### 14.4 Bond Replacement at Closing
- **What**: Replace seller's reclamation bonds with SC bonds at closing.
- **Who**: ENV, CFO, surety broker.
- **Data captured**: Permit, bond amount, bond type (surety / collateral / SOSO), surety carrier, premium.
- **Documents**: New bonds, bond release for seller, regulatory acceptance.
- **Hand-offs**: ENV, CFO, Legal.
- **State-specific**: WV self-bonding eliminated; SOSO (Special Reclamation) tax + alternative bonding systems vary by state.

### 14.5 Permit Transfer Application
- **What**: Formal application to state regulator (WV DEP DMR, KY EEC DMRE, VA DMRE) to transfer SMCRA permit.
- **Who**: ENV, Legal.
- **Data captured**: Permit#, application date, public notice date, regulator approval date.
- **Documents**: Permit transfer application, public notice, decision letter.
- **Frequency**: Per acquisition.
- **State-specific timing**: Often 60–180 days; public comment period; pre-existing violations on AVS can block transfer.

### 14.6 Lease Assignment / Lessor Consent
- See §4.

### 14.7 MEPP / UMWA Withdrawal Liability DD
- **What**: Determine SC's potential withdrawal liability if acquired business is a UMWA 1974 Pension Plan / 1993 Benefit Plan contributor.
- **Who**: HR/Benefits, Actuary, Legal.
- **Data captured**: Hours worked covered, UVB share, §4204 sale-of-assets safe harbor structure.
- **Documents**: Actuarial estimate, sale agreement structuring, §4204 bond/escrow.
- **Hand-offs**: HR, CFO, Legal.

## 15. Divestitures

### 15.1 Asset Sale Structuring
- **What**: Decide stock vs asset sale, structuring to minimize tail liability.
- **Who**: CFO, Legal, LM.
- **Data captured**: Deal structure, tax treatment, tail-liability allocation.
- **Documents**: Letter of intent, purchase agreement.
- **Hand-offs**: All.

### 15.2 Bond Release / Replacement
- **What**: Coordinate bond release upon buyer posting replacement.
- **Who**: ENV, CFO.
- **Data captured**: Bond release amount, buyer bond posted, regulator approval.
- **Documents**: Bond release request, regulatory order.
- **State-specific**: Phased release in three increments under SMCRA (Phase I after backfill/regrading; Phase II after revegetation; Phase III after final liability period — 5 years east of 100th meridian).

### 15.3 Permit Transfer (Outbound)
- **What**: Transfer SMCRA permit to buyer.
- **Who**: ENV, Legal.
- **Data captured**: Permit, transfer application, regulator approval.
- **Documents**: Transfer application, public notice, approval.

### 15.4 Tail Liability Management
- **What**: Identify CERCLA, CWA, ERISA-MEPP, OSMRE, surface owner tail liabilities.
- **Who**: Legal, ENV, HR, CFO.
- **Data captured**: Indemnity scope, escrow, insurance.
- **Documents**: Indemnity agreement, escrow agreement, tail insurance.
- **Edge cases**: CERCLA "owner or operator" liability survives sale; CWA citizen suits against former owner; UMWA partial withdrawal triggered by sale.

---

## 16. Property Tax Assessment & Appeals

### 16.1 Annual Assessment Review
- **What**: Review of all assessments — fee land, unmined coal, equipment.
- **Who**: LM, CFO, outside tax consultant.
- **Data captured**: Assessed value, prior year, change %, methodology, taxes due.
- **Documents**: Assessment notice, tax bill.
- **Frequency**: Annual.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (payment), LM (appeals).

### 16.2 Unmined Coal Tax (WV)
- **What**: WV Tax Commissioner appraises coal in place under WV Code §11-1C and Coal Rule 110 CSR 1I; county assessor multiplies by 60% assessment ratio and adds to land book.
- **Who**: LM, outside tax counsel.
- **Data captured**: Tract, seam, reserve tons, FMV, assessed value, tax.
- **Documents**: Coal Property Tax Return (WV), assessment notice, tax bill.
- **Frequency**: Annual; methodology review every 5 years per §11-1C-10.
- **State-specific**: WV — active/reserve coal valued using DCF/income approach with statutory parameters; unmineable seams $5/deed acre.
- **Edge cases**: Reserves overstated → over-assessment; mine plan change reduces mineable tons; new technology recovery reassessment.

### 16.3 Unmined Coal Tax (KY)
- **What**: KY DOR Office of Property Valuation Division of Minerals Taxation values coal as distinct interest in real property under KRS 132.820 at fair market value in place; assessment date Jan 1; Form 62A200(P) due.
- **Who**: LM, outside tax counsel.
- **Data captured**: Per-tract reserve data, taxpayer's value where insufficient technical data.
- **Documents**: Form 62A200(P), KY assessment notice.
- **Frequency**: Annual.
- **State-specific**: Separate from surface assessment; KY DOR central valuation.
- **Edge cases**: Coal interest controlled but not owned — still taxable to controller; reserves below mineable threshold.

### 16.4 Unmined Coal Tax (VA & Others)
- **What**: VA — coal taxation varies by locality; some counties assess minerals separately, some include in surface assessment; "minerals and mineral lands" can be classified differently under Va. Code §58.1-3712 (severance tax) and §58.1-3713 (coal/gas road improvement tax).
- **Who**: LM, CFO.
- **Data captured**: Per-locality assessment & tax.
- **Documents**: Locality assessment notices.
- **Edge cases**: County reassessment cycle differences.

### 16.5 Equipment / Personal Property Tax
- **What**: Tangible personal property assessment on mining equipment, shop, office.
- **Who**: CFO, Plant Accounting.
- **Data captured**: Equipment list, book value, depreciation, assessed value, tax.
- **Documents**: Personal property return.
- **Frequency**: Annual.

### 16.6 Assessment Appeals
- **What**: Formal appeal of overstated assessments.
- **Who**: LM, tax counsel.
- **Data captured**: Appeal year, basis, hearing date, decision, refund.
- **Documents**: Petition for appeal, hearing record, decision.
- **State-specific**: WV — county Board of Equalization & Review (Feb), then Office of Tax Appeals; KY — county PVA appeal, then KBTA; VA — Board of Equalization, then circuit court.
- **Frequency**: As needed; annually for high-value properties.

- **What**: Centralized intake of community complaints (blast, dust, noise, water, structures, traffic).
- **Who**: HSE, LRC, ENV.

- **Data captured**: Investigation findings, root cause, corrective action, settlement, release.
- **Documents**: Investigation report, blast records, monitoring data, settlement agreement, release of claims.
- **Hand-offs**: Insurance, Legal, CFO.

### 17.3 Long-Term Monitoring of Impacted Properties
- **What**: Ongoing monitoring of springs, wells, structures with established history.
- **Who**: ENV, LRC.
- **Data captured**: Property, monitoring schedule, results, payment to owner.
- **Documents**: Monitoring records, sampling reports.
- **Frequency**: Quarterly / semi-annual / annual per agreement.

## 18. Property Management (Non-Mining Land Use)

### 18.1 Hunting Club Leases
- **What**: Lease idle land to hunting clubs / individuals.
- **Who**: LM.
- **Data captured**: Lessee club, acreage, term, fee, insurance certificate, liability waiver.
- **Documents**: Hunting lease, COI, waiver.
- **Frequency**: Annual.
- **Hand-offs**: Insurance/Risk, CFO.
- **Edge cases**: Hunter injury claim; trespass on adjacent landowner; concurrent mining operations safety.

### 18.2 Cell Tower / Communications Leases
- **What**: Lease ridge tops to wireless carriers / tower companies.
- **Who**: LM.
- **Data captured**: Lessee, tower location, rent (monthly, escalator), term, RF safety zone.
- **Documents**: Tower lease, recorded memorandum, easement for access.
- **Frequency**: Long-term (often 25 years + options).
- **Hand-offs**: CFO.

### 18.3 Pipeline Cross-Easements (Granted)
- **What**: Easements granted to pipeline / utility operators across SC land.
- **Who**: LM, TA.
- **Data captured**: Grantee, route, term, payment.
- **Documents**: Easement deed.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO.

### 18.4 Post-Reclamation Timber Sales
- **What**: Timber sales on reclaimed forestry-PMLU acres after rotation.
- **Who**: LM, forester.
- **Data captured**: Tract, harvest plan, stumpage.
- **Documents**: Timber sale contract.
- **Frequency**: Per rotation (decades).

### 18.5 Renewable Energy Leases (Solar / Wind on Reclaimed Land)
- **What**: Lease reclaimed mountaintop or flat-bench reclaimed land to renewable developers.
- **Who**: LM, Legal, CFO.
- **Data captured**: Lessee, acreage, term, rent (per MW or per acre), construction timeline, decommissioning bond.
- **Documents**: Solar/wind ground lease, decommissioning agreement, interconnection rights.
- **Frequency**: Long-term (25–35 years).
- **Hand-offs**: ENV (PMLU consistency), CFO, Legal.
- **State-specific**: WV has incentivized brownfield/mineland solar; KY similar emerging program; PMLU change may require SMCRA permit revision.
- **Edge cases**: Solar lessee's foundations interfere with future mining (subjacent coal); decommissioning bond insufficient.

---

## 19. GIS & Spatial Data

### 19.1 Land/Lease GIS Layer
- **What**: GIS layers for tracts, leases, surface ownership, mineral ownership, easements, permits.
- **Who**: IT-GIS, LMAN.
- **Data captured**: Spatial geometry + attribute joins to lease, deed, permit records.
- **Documents**: GIS database, map atlases.
- **Frequency**: Continuous.
- **Hand-offs**: All teams.
- **Edge cases**: Spatial discrepancy vs deed acreage; overlapping leases; state-line tracts; lat/long vs PLSS in metes-and-bounds states.

### 19.2 Reserve Mapping by Seam
- **What**: Reserve polygons per seam tied to ownership/lease overlays for NRI calc.
- **Who**: OPS geology, IT-GIS.
- **Data captured**: Reserve tons, seam, owner/lessor split, mineable/non-mineable.
- **Documents**: Reserve report, reserve maps.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO (depletion, SEC reserves), LM (lease economics).

---

## 20. Cross-Functional Integrations & Reporting

### 20.1 Royalty-Production Reconciliation
- **What**: Monthly reconciliation between mine production records, sales, and royalty calculations.
- **Who**: RA, OPS, CFO.
- **Data captured**: Tons produced vs sold vs paid royalty on; allocation by lease/tract/seam.
- **Documents**: Reconciliation worksheet.
- **Frequency**: Monthly.
- **Hand-offs**: CFO close.
- **Edge cases**: Blended coal across leases; inventory timing differences; quality adjustments.

### 20.2 Lessor Reporting Pack
- **What**: Periodic packet to lessor — statement, production, sales, deductions, ORRI/NPI splits.
- **Who**: LRC, RA.
- **Frequency**: Per lease cycle.

### 20.3 Land/Lease Reporting to Lenders, Reserve-Based Lenders, SEC
- **What**: Compliance reporting on reserves, leases, encumbrances.
- **Who**: CFO, LM, Legal.
- **Documents**: Reserve report, lease schedule, encumbrance schedule.
- **Frequency**: Quarterly / annual.

### 20.4 ESG / Stakeholder Reporting (Surface Owner Relations Metrics)
- **What**: Track surface owner relations metrics for ESG reporting.
- **Who**: LM, ESG/Sustainability lead.
- **Data captured**: Complaints opened/closed, settlements paid, water replacements, community grants.
- **Documents**: ESG report.
- **Frequency**: Annual.

## 22. Common Edge Cases (Cross-Cutting)

- Fractional heir located in CA/TX after 30 years of suspense; demands lookback with interest
- Royalty audit reveals affiliate sale at below-market price → multi-year underpayment + interest
- Lessor refuses ACH; check returned undeliverable → escheat clock ticks
- Surface owner builds new dwelling within 1/2-mile blast radius after permit issued — pre-blast survey obligation refreshed?
- Old broad-form deed silent on surface mining — strip permit applied → KY constitutional amendment blocks; WV "contemplation" defense
- Title chain runs through burned-courthouse county (e.g., Logan WV) — reconstruct from tax rolls and adjacent deeds
- ORRI holder defunct corporation — payments held in suspense indefinitely; potential interpleader
- Mine pool water sale across state line triggers second-state jurisdiction
- Permit transfer to buyer blocked by AVS hit on buyer's affiliate
- Lessor demands MFN-clause recalculation back to lease inception after learning of higher rate on a different lease
- Solar lease over reclaimed land conflicts with coal lease on deep seam under same surface — subjacent support negotiation
- Coal blended at prep plant from 12 leases with different royalty rates — allocation methodology audit
- Heir designates a trust as payee; trust dissolves; payments suspended pending trustee succession
- WV non-resident lessor moves to FL; state withholding rules change mid-year
- Unrecorded surface lease used as basis for SC's operation; lessor's successor disputes use
- Sub-lessee defaults on royalty to head lessor; SC liable as middle party
- Adverse possession claim against surface where SC owns minerals only — generally not valid against severed minerals
- Federal coal LMU diligent development failed in shoulder year — risk of lease cancellation
- Cell tower lease over haul road corridor — relocate or compensate
- Hunting lessee shoots a contract miner — liability allocation
- Lessor dies intestate with 8 children and 23 grandchildren scattered across 14 states — heirship affidavit + curative
- Pre-1900 severance deed reserves "all coal in the Pittsburgh seam and beneath" — what about Sewickley above? (Coal owner only)

# Domain 7: Coal Marketing, Sales, Customer, Transportation & Logistics

# Coal Marketing, Sales, Customer, Transportation & Logistics

Scope: Every function from price discovery through cash collection — market intelligence, product/quality management, customer master, contracts, shipment planning, rail/barge/truck/vessel logistics, loadouts, quality documentation, shipment visibility, invoicing, demurrage, export compliance, customer service, marketing, regulatory marketing, document flow, and EDI integration. Built for Southern Coal Corporation operations across WV, VA, KY, AL, TN producing both metallurgical (HCC/SHCC/PCI/Mid-Vol/Low-Vol) and steam coal sold to domestic utilities, integrated steel and coke producers, international met buyers, and industrial customers via rail, barge, truck, and ocean vessel.

Each function below lists 8 dimensions: (1) What it is, (2) Who performs it, (3) Data captured, (4) Documents/forms, (5) Frequency, (6) Hand-offs, (7) State-specific differences, (8) Common edge cases.

---

## 1. Market Intelligence

### 1.1 Domestic Steam Coal Price Benchmark Tracking (CAPP / NAPP / ILB / PRB / Uinta)
1. **What it is:** Daily/weekly capture of US thermal coal spot and forward prices for Central Appalachian (CAPP — 12,500 BTU 1.2 SO₂), Northern Appalachian (NAPP — Pittsburgh #8 13,000 BTU 3.0 lb SO₂), Illinois Basin (ILB), Powder River Basin (PRB 8,800/8,400), and Uinta — used to price spot tons, validate contract indexed prices, and inform forward sales.
2. **Who performs it:** Coal marketing analyst; VP Sales & Marketing; Trading desk (where SC trades).
3. **Data captured:** Index name, sulfur tier, BTU spec, $/ton, publication date, lag (front month / prompt / forward strip), provider (Argus/McCloskey, Platts, OPIS).
4. **Documents/forms:** Daily price sheet, weekly index summary email, internal price deck PDF, forward curve snapshot.
5. **Frequency:** Daily (settlement prices); weekly published indexes (Friday); monthly close prices used for indexed contract settlement.
6. **Hand-offs:** Contracts team (for monthly true-ups on indexed deals), Finance (revenue recognition), Sales (spot quotes), Risk/Hedging.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV/VA/KY mines feed CAPP and NAPP markets; western SC properties (AL/TN) bridge between CAPP and ILB pricing — bidirectional arbitrage opportunities. CAPP compliance coal (low-S, high-BTU) commands premium increasingly rare from CAPP supply.
8. **Edge cases:** Index methodology changes (new specs, BTU/sulfur tier shifts); single-day prints with very thin liquidity skewing indexes; index pauses for holidays creating settlement disputes; provider data correction (republished prices) impacting prior month invoices.

### 1.2 Seaborne Thermal Coal Index Tracking (API2 / API4 / Newcastle)
1. **What it is:** Tracking of Argus/McCloskey API2 (CIF ARA — Northwest Europe delivered), API4 (FOB Richards Bay — South Africa), API5/API8 (Asia), Newcastle 6000 NAR (FOB Australia) as global benchmarks for any export thermal moves. 85%+ of global coal derivatives settle against API2/API4.
2. **Who performs it:** Export marketing manager; broker-dealer relationships.
3. **Data captured:** Index value, calorific value basis (NAR vs GAR), Mt traded volume reported in assessment, FX (USD/EUR).
4. **Documents/forms:** Argus/McCloskey Coal Price Index Report (Friday), Platts Coal Daily, CME/ICE forward curve screenshots.
5. **Frequency:** Daily (Platts MOC at 5:30pm Singapore), weekly (Argus/McCloskey Friday close).
6. **Hand-offs:** Export sales, treasury (FX hedging), Vessel chartering desk.
7. **State-specific differences:** Tidewater proximity (VA/MD terminals) drives netback math relative to Newcastle benchmark; SC's Newport News/Norfolk/Baltimore terminal options determine FOB realization.
8. **Edge cases:** Index methodology shifts (e.g., 2025 PLV physical timing structure launch); Russian/Iran/North Korea-sourced cargoes excluded from price assessments; cargo "wash" routings affecting reported tonnage.

### 1.3 Metallurgical Coal Benchmark Tracking (PLV HCC, US East Coast HCC, Low-Vol, Mid-Vol, PCI)
1. **What it is:** Tracking Platts Premium Low Vol (PLV) FOB Australia — flagship met benchmark (21.5% VM, 71% CSR baseline); HCC FOB Australia (TSI/Platts) futures on CME/SGX; US East Coast HCC FOB Hampton Roads; PCI (Pulverized Coal Injection) and Semi-Soft (SSCC). The reference for SC's met coal sales to integrated steel and export customers.
2. **Who performs it:** Met coal marketing manager; Senior sales reps.
3. **Data captured:** PLV $/mt, US ECC HCC $/st, low-vol/mid-vol differentials, PCI $/mt, Semi-Soft discount, quarterly benchmark (legacy JSM "QBR"), spot premium/discount.
4. **Documents/forms:** Platts Metals Alert real-time feed; Argus Metallurgical Coal report; broker quote sheets (Tullett Prebon, GFI, Marex); customer-specific bid forms.
5. **Frequency:** Daily spot, monthly average for indexed contracts, quarterly (where legacy quarterly benchmark structure still applies in Asia).
6. **Hand-offs:** Production planning (which met mines fed which buyer), Mine quality control, Vessel ops, Settlement.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV/VA produce dominant US east-coast HCC supply (Pocahontas seams; Buchanan, Pittston, Eagle); KY produces mid-vol; AL produces SHCC (Blue Creek). PCI/Mid-Vol pricing differs by basin.
8. **Edge cases:** PLV market structure becoming illiquid causes index distortion; quarterly benchmark negotiation breakdowns; customer rejection on CSR/CRI miss invokes spec-rerate not penalty; force majeure-driven spot premium spikes; trade flow disruption (China import ban swing).

### 1.4 Forward Curve and Derivatives Mark
1. **What it is:** Daily mark-to-market on CME (API2, API4, NYMEX coal), ICE (API2, Newcastle, HCC), SGX (Australian coking coal) and any OTC swaps held; used to value forward sales and hedges.
2. **Who performs it:** Trading/risk manager; Treasury.
3. **Data captured:** Contract month, settlement price, open interest, position size, MTM gain/loss, margin call.
4. **Documents/forms:** Broker confirms, FCM margin statements, trade tickets.
5. **Frequency:** Daily mark; intraday on volatile days.
6. **Hand-offs:** Finance (hedge accounting under ASC 815), risk committee.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A (derivatives are commodity-level).
8. **Edge cases:** Hedge ineffectiveness if physical product differs materially from index; margin spike during volatility (March 2022 PLV $670 spike); broker default risk.

### 1.5 Competitor Production and Earnings Monitoring
1. **What it is:** Track publicly disclosed production, sales tons, ASP, costs, and guidance from Arch Resources, Peabody, Consol, Warrior Met, Alpha Met Resources, Ramaco, CORSA, Hallador, Foresight, Wolverine, Coronado, Whitehaven, Glencore, etc. Used to anticipate supply changes and price direction.
2. **Who performs it:** Marketing analyst; CEO/CFO for board reporting.
3. **Data captured:** Quarterly production (st), realized price ($/st), unit cost, guidance ranges, capex, mine startups/idlings.
4. **Documents/forms:** 10-Q/10-K extracts, earnings call transcripts, investor decks.
5. **Frequency:** Quarterly (full); monthly (operational updates).
6. **Hand-offs:** CEO/board strategy, Capital allocation, Mine planning.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV competitors (Consol NAPP; Met division; Arch in W. Elk; Warrior in AL); KY competitors (Foresight/Hallador ILB-adjacent); VA met competitors.
8. **Edge cases:** Bankruptcy filings altering market (Murray, Foresight, Cleveland Cliffs spinoffs); MA&A movement; competitor force majeure events tightening supply.

### 1.6 Utility Demand Signal Tracking
1. **What it is:** Monitor EIA weekly coal stockpile (Form EIA-923 derived), monthly days-of-burn (bituminous units ~120 days Feb 2026), Henry Hub natural gas price (coal-to-gas switching threshold), weather degree-day forecasts (NOAA HDD/CDD), and unit retirement notices.
2. **Who performs it:** Domestic utility sales team; Market analyst.
3. **Data captured:** Per-plant stockpile (tons, days-of-burn), monthly burn (tons), forecast HDD/CDD by NERC region, gas storage (Bcf — 3,579 Bcf Dec 2025), retirement date by unit.
4. **Documents/forms:** EIA Electricity Monthly Update — Coal Stocks page; Weekly NG Storage Report (Thursday 10:30am EST); plant-level monthly burn from EIA-923.
5. **Frequency:** Weekly NG storage; monthly EIA-923 (60-90 day lag); seasonally for weather forecast.
6. **Hand-offs:** Domestic sales (positioning spot offers), Production planning, Contract renewal calendar.
7. **State-specific differences:** PJM (NAPP/CAPP customers — AEP, Duke, Dominion, FirstEnergy); SERC (TVA, Duke, Southern Co — TN/AL/KY); MISO (some KY exposure).
8. **Edge cases:** Plant unexpected outage drops demand; coal-to-gas switching when HH < $2.50 makes gas dispatch ahead of coal in NAPP/ILB; data center demand surge (2026) lifting baseload coal duration.

### 1.7 Metallurgical Coal Demand Signal Tracking
1. **What it is:** Global crude steel production (worldsteel monthly), blast furnace utilization rates by region, hot metal production, China coke export volumes, India coking coal import volumes, EU steel output (EUROFER), Japan/Korea steel, ex-China seaborne flows.
2. **Who performs it:** Met coal marketing manager; Export sales lead.
3. **Data captured:** Monthly crude steel (Mt) by country, BF utilization %, hot metal (Mt), coke production, EAF share, scrap price (HMS 1/2), iron ore price (62% Fe CFR China).
4. **Documents/forms:** worldsteel monthly report; Mysteel data; CISA China weekly; Argus monthly met coal report.
5. **Frequency:** Monthly (steel data); weekly (China data); daily (iron ore correlation).
6. **Hand-offs:** Met sales, Export shipping schedule, Vessel chartering.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV/VA met heavily sold to NA integrated mills (Cleveland Cliffs, US Steel, Stelco/ArcelorMittal Dofasco) — NA blast furnace count and utilization is the primary domestic driver.
8. **Edge cases:** Sudden Chinese met coal import policy change; BF reline timing affecting customer specific buying patterns; EAF transition reducing met coal pool of buyers.

### 1.8 Export Terminal Stockpile and Vessel Queue Monitoring
1. **What it is:** Real-time monitoring of stockpile and ship queue at Lambert's Point (Norfolk Southern, Norfolk VA — largest in N. hemisphere, 5,700 tph dumpers, 130 mine origins), DTA (Dominion Terminal Associates, Newport News VA), Pier IX (Kinder Morgan, Newport News VA — 16 Mt/yr capacity), CNX Marine Terminal (Baltimore, 16 Mst capacity, owned by Consol), Curtis Bay Coal Piers (Baltimore, CSX-owned).
2. **Who performs it:** Vessel/marine ops manager; Terminal coordinator.
3. **Data captured:** Stockpile tons by quality grade per terminal, vessel arrival queue (ships in roads, alongside, loaded, sailed), berth occupancy, weather holds.
4. **Documents/forms:** Terminal stockpile reports (NS/CSX customer portal, KM portal, DTA portal); vessel queue spreadsheets; Marine Exchange position reports.
5. **Frequency:** Daily; per-vessel update.
6. **Hand-offs:** Vessel charter desk, Rail dispatch, Mine production cadence.
7. **State-specific differences:** VA terminals (Lambert's Point, DTA, Pier IX) — closest to CAPP met production. MD terminals (CNX Marine, Curtis Bay) — exposed to Baltimore Key Bridge collapse (2024) and channel restrictions.
8. **Edge cases:** Bridge collapse closures (Baltimore Key Bridge); hurricane evacuation (Hampton Roads); terminal dumper breakdown; vessel queue backup during peak shipping season.

### 1.9 Baltic Dry / Ocean Freight Tracking
1. **What it is:** Monitor BDI/BCI (Baltic Capesize Index — primary for coal cargoes), Panamax (BPTI), Supramax (BSI), Handysize (BHSI), Capesize T/C average rates, and key route assessments (C5 W. Australia–Qingdao; C3 Tubarão–Qingdao; voyage rates from Hampton Roads to ARA/Rotterdam, to India ECoast, to China).
2. **Who performs it:** Vessel chartering manager; broker (Howe Robinson, Clarksons, Braemar, SSY, Banchero Costa).
3. **Data captured:** BDI, BCI 5TC avg, voyage rate $/ton from Hampton Roads to discharge port, bunker price (VLSFO Rotterdam/Singapore).
4. **Documents/forms:** Baltic Exchange daily reports, broker circulars.
5. **Frequency:** Daily.
6. **Hand-offs:** Export pricing (FOB vs CFR netback), Charter party negotiation.
7. **State-specific differences:** Hampton Roads (VA) is most active US east coast loading; Baltimore (MD) secondary.
8. **Edge cases:** Bunker price spikes (Russia/Ukraine 2022); Suez/Panama Canal restrictions (Panama drought 2023-24); IMO 2020 scrubber economics; piracy or geopolitical re-routing.

### 1.10 Currency Tracking (FX)
1. **What it is:** Monitor USD/EUR (European customer pricing), USD/INR (Indian buyers), USD/CNY (Chinese), USD/AUD (competitor pricing input), USD/BRL (Brazilian steel).
2. **Who performs it:** Treasury; Export sales.
3. **Data captured:** Spot, forward 1M/3M/6M, implied vols.
4. **Documents/forms:** Bloomberg FX terminal screenshot, treasury daily report.
5. **Frequency:** Daily; intraday for active deals.
6. **Hand-offs:** Treasury hedging, Export pricing committee.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Sharp currency devaluations (Turkish lira affecting Erdemir-type buyers); CNY band shifts.

### 1.11 Geopolitical and Trade Policy Monitoring
1. **What it is:** Track sanctions (Russia coal Aug 2022 EU ban, OFAC SDN updates), US Section 232 tariffs, China import duties/quotas, India coking coal duty changes, Indonesian export policy, EU CBAM phase-in.
2. **Who performs it:** Senior commercial counsel; Marketing manager; Compliance.
3. **Data captured:** Sanctions list update date, tariff rate % by HTS, quota effective dates.
4. **Documents/forms:** OFAC SDN updates, USTR notices, Federal Register filings, EU Official Journal.
5. **Frequency:** As-events occur; weekly compliance sweep.
6. **Hand-offs:** Legal, Compliance, Export operations, Customer relations.
7. **State-specific differences:** Federal level — uniform.
8. **Edge cases:** Mid-voyage sanctions change forcing re-routing; customer becoming sanctioned post-contract; CBAM cost passthrough disputes.

### 1.12 Coal Coke Production / Steel-Adjacent Tracking
1. **What it is:** Track global merchant coke output (China dominant), coke export licenses, coke price (FOB China, CFR India), met coke and PCI substitution dynamics.
2. **Who performs it:** Met coal marketing analyst.
3. **Data captured:** Coke production (Mt), coke price $/mt FOB North China, China export quota.
4. **Documents/forms:** Mysteel coke report, SBB/Platts coke assessment.
5. **Frequency:** Weekly.
6. **Hand-offs:** Met sales (informs HCC vs PCI mix), Strategy.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** China cuts coke export creating HCC demand pull; merchant coke price collapse signals soft steel.

### 1.13 Coal-to-Gas Switching Dynamics
1. **What it is:** Track Henry Hub gas price vs delivered coal cost (CAPP, NAPP, ILB delivered to PJM/MISO/SERC); model the heat rate cutoff where gas dispatches ahead of coal.
2. **Who performs it:** Market analyst; Utility sales rep.
3. **Data captured:** HH spot, regional basis, delivered coal $/MMBtu, coal vs gas dispatch cost.
4. **Documents/forms:** Internal switching model spreadsheet/dashboard.
5. **Frequency:** Daily.
6. **Hand-offs:** Domestic sales, Spot quote desk.
7. **State-specific differences:** PJM AEP-Dayton zone (NAPP customers most exposed); SERC TVA (more diverse fuel mix).
8. **Edge cases:** Gas storage emergency forcing forced coal dispatch ignoring economics; localized basis blowouts (Permian Waha negatives).

### 1.14 Carbon Policy / Coal Retirement Tracking
1. **What it is:** Track utility integrated resource plans (IRPs) for coal retirement dates by unit; IRA/Section 45X impacts; EPA effluent limit guidelines (ELG); EPA Coal Combustion Residuals (CCR) rule; state carbon rules.
2. **Who performs it:** Strategy & external affairs; sales account managers.
3. **Data captured:** Unit retirement date (announced vs filed), capacity (MW), associated annual coal burn (st/yr).
4. **Documents/forms:** Utility IRP filings, state PUC dockets.
5. **Frequency:** Quarterly; ad-hoc on IRP filing.
6. **Hand-offs:** Sales (account life-cycle), Strategy, M&A.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV PSC, KY PSC, VA SCC have different retirement-approval timelines and rate recovery rules.
8. **Edge cases:** Retirement deferral due to grid reliability concerns (NERC); IRA tax credit changes; data center load growth reversing retirement plans (2026 wave).

---

## 2. Product / Quality Management

### 2.1 Product Catalog (by Mine, Seam, Wash Spec)
1. **What it is:** Master catalog of every sellable product: mine/complex, seam, raw vs washed, BTU range, sulfur, ash, moisture, met vs steam classification, customer-suitable markets.
2. **Who performs it:** Quality/Geology team; Marketing.
3. **Data captured:** Product SKU, mine, seam (Pocahontas #3, Eagle, Pittsburgh #8, Pratt, Blue Creek), wash plant feed/clean spec, sellable BTU range, typical S/ash/moisture, target market.
4. **Documents/forms:** Product spec card (one-pager per SKU), reserve maps, wash circuit diagrams.
5. **Frequency:** Quarterly review; updates on new pit, new seam access, or wash circuit reconfig.
6. **Hand-offs:** Geology/Reserve engineering, Mine ops, Sales (offering sheet), Lab.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV/VA — Pocahontas, Eagle, Sewell, Beckley met seams; KY — Elkhorn, Hazard #4/#5/#7/#8; AL — Blue Creek (Mary Lee, Black Creek); TN — limited remaining seams.
8. **Edge cases:** Discovery that a seam produces off-spec mid-mining (geological transition); decision to add a new wash circuit changes product mix; permit limits on certain pits affecting SKU availability.

### 2.2 Quality Spec Sheet Maintenance — Steam Coal
1. **What it is:** Maintain per-product spec sheet with proximate (moisture, ash, VM, fixed carbon), ultimate (C/H/N/S/O), BTU (gross and net, AR/DRY/DAF basis), HGI (Hardgrove Grindability), ash fusion temps (IDT/ST/HT/FT, reducing and oxidizing), trace elements (Hg, Cl, As, Se).
2. **Who performs it:** Quality manager; Geology technical services.
3. **Data captured:** Each parameter — typical, range, guarantee.
4. **Documents/forms:** Spec sheet PDF, ASTM-referenced methods table (D3173 moisture, D3174 ash, D3175 VM, D5865 BTU, D3177/D4239 sulfur, D409 HGI, D1857 ash fusion).
5. **Frequency:** Per-product annual review; updated when mine seam shifts.
6. **Hand-offs:** Sales, Contracts (used in spec sections), Lab, Customer technical service.
7. **State-specific differences:** PRB low-S/low-BTU/high-moisture vs CAPP high-BTU/low-moisture — different test method emphasis.
8. **Edge cases:** Customer demanding a new trace element (e.g., mercury continuous monitoring); lab method version changes between ASTM revisions causing trend breaks.

### 2.3 Quality Spec Sheet Maintenance — Metallurgical Coal
1. **What it is:** Maintain met spec: VM, ash, S, P, moisture, Fluidity (ddpm log scale), FSI/CSN (Free Swelling Index / Crucible Swelling Number 0–9), Gieseler max fluidity, dilatation, vitrinite reflectance Romax, maceral composition, CSR (Coke Strength after Reaction), CRI (Coke Reactivity Index), Hardgrove, ash composition (SiO2, Al2O3, Fe2O3, basic/acid ratio), alkalis.
3. **Who performs it:** Met coal quality manager; Carbonization lab.
4. **Data captured:** Each parameter typical/range/guarantee, plus pilot oven coke quality testing (40 lb test oven, 1000 kg sole-heated oven).
5. **Documents/forms:** Met spec sheet PDF; pilot oven test report; petrographic report.
6. **Frequency:** Per product semi-annual; sample retained on every shipment.
7. **Hand-offs:** Sales, Contracts, Lab, Customer technical contact (often a metallurgist).
8. **State-specific differences:** WV/VA — premium low-vol HCC (Pocahontas); KY — mid-vol; AL — Blue Creek SHCC. Different VM/fluidity targets per seam.
9. **Edge cases:** CSR/CRI miss on a single shipment triggering full lot resample; Romax shift between bench levels indicating roof/floor cutting; high P (>0.080 dry) rejecting cargo.

### 2.4 Quality Forecast (by Mine, by Month)
1. **What it is:** 3-12 month forward forecast of quality output by mine/seam based on mine plan, expected ply mix, wash plant performance.
2. **Who performs it:** Geology/Quality engineering; Mine planners.
3. **Data captured:** Forecast quality (with confidence band), expected tons, blend availability.
4. **Documents/forms:** Quality forecast spreadsheet; monthly S&OP deck.
5. **Frequency:** Monthly rolling forecast.
6. **Hand-offs:** Sales (commitment-making), Production scheduling, Blending coordinator.
7. **State-specific differences:** Seam transitions specific to geology (WV Pocahontas roll, KY Elkhorn transition zones, AL Blue Creek inclusions).
8. **Edge cases:** Geological surprise (washout, roll, intrusion); wash plant performance degradation; equipment outage shifting which face is mined.

### 2.5 Customer-Specific Quality Spec Management
1. **What it is:** Per-customer (per-contract) target spec, rejection limits, penalty schedules, premium schedules; tracked vs actual shipments.
2. **Who performs it:** Contract administrator; Quality manager.
3. **Data captured:** Customer ID, contract ID, parameter, target, rejection threshold, penalty $/ton per unit deviation (e.g., $0.40/ton per 100 BTU below target), premium structure.
4. **Documents/forms:** Contract spec exhibit; customer-specific COA template.
5. **Frequency:** Per contract; reviewed at each shipment vs spec.
6. **Hand-offs:** Loadout (blend to spec), Lab (COA generation), Invoicing (penalty calculation), Quality dispute resolution.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A (driven by customer plant requirements).
8. **Edge cases:** Customer changes spec mid-contract (newer SO2 scrubber adjustment); rejection vs penalty dispute on a single shipment; rolling-average vs per-shipment basis for penalty (rolling-30 BTU vs per-load).

### 2.6 Blending Strategy and Execution
1. **What it is:** Determining the mine/stockpile/seam mix to load to hit a customer's spec — including back-blending where needed (e.g., high-S NAPP + low-S CAPP for utility spec).
2. **Who performs it:** Blending coordinator; Loadout operator; Quality engineer.
3. **Data captured:** Recipe (source A % + source B % + ...), batch tons, target spec, predicted spec.
4. **Documents/forms:** Blend recipe / batch sheet; loadout batch log.
5. **Frequency:** Per shipment / per train.
6. **Hand-offs:** Mine operations (delivering to right stockpile), Lab (verifying as-loaded sample matches prediction), Loadout operator.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV/VA preparation plants often blend from multiple seams within complex; KY similar; AL Blue Creek often single-source.
8. **Edge cases:** Source stockpile contamination; pad limits exceeded forcing recipe change; loadout silo mixing without proper splitter setting.

### 2.7 Reserve Allocation (Which Seams Back Which Sales)
1. **What it is:** Strategic mapping of remaining recoverable reserve to long-term contracts to ensure deliverability across contract life.
2. **Who performs it:** VP Marketing + VP Engineering + Reserves engineer; CFO.
3. **Data captured:** Mine/seam, recoverable reserves (st), contract-committed tonnage, free uncommitted reserves.
4. **Documents/forms:** Reserve allocation memo; contract-to-reserve mapping spreadsheet; SK-1300 reserve report.
5. **Frequency:** Annually; on each new long-term contract.
6. **Hand-offs:** Mine planning, Sales (deliverability assurance), Finance (DD&A), Investor relations.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV/VA/KY seam thinness and complexity drives more conservative allocation; AL Blue Creek thick seams allow more aggressive commitments.
8. **Edge cases:** Permit denial reducing available reserve mid-contract; reserve write-down via independent engineer; bankrupt customer freeing committed reserve.

### 2.8 Compliance Coal Management
1. **What it is:** Tracking and selling coal that meets a customer's clean-air requirements (low sulfur, specific BTU). Historically PRB sub-bituminous; CAPP low-S compliance coal is increasingly rare and commands premium.
2. **Who performs it:** Domestic utility sales; Quality engineer.
3. **Data captured:** SO₂ basis (lb/MMBtu), Hg content, Cl content.
4. **Documents/forms:** Compliance coal certification per shipment.
5. **Frequency:** Per shipment.
6. **Hand-offs:** Customer's environmental compliance team; CEMS/CAMD reporting feed.
7. **State-specific differences:** PRB low-S coal is a different supply chain entirely; CAPP compliance coal (under 1.2 lb SO₂/MMBtu) tighter and tighter supply.
8. **Edge cases:** Customer's scrubber upgrade reducing need for compliance grade; allowance market changes (CSAPR/Acid Rain) affecting demand.

## 3. Customer Master

### 3.1 Customer Profile and Segmentation
1. **What it is:** Customer master record with segment classification (regulated investor-owned utility / municipal utility / co-op / industrial / integrated steel / merchant coke / broker-trader / export end-user / cement).
2. **Who performs it:** Sales operations; Account manager.
3. **Data captured:** Legal entity name, DUNS, parent, segment, country, plant(s) served, annual coal usage estimate, current/competitor share.
4. **Documents/forms:** Customer master record (CRM), KYC packet, W-9.
5. **Frequency:** On onboarding; annual refresh; on M&A events.
6. **Hand-offs:** Credit, Compliance (OFAC), Sales.
7. **State-specific differences:** State-regulated utilities (PSC-approved coal purchases) vs merchant power (free contracting) — different process for contract approval.
8. **Edge cases:** Customer merger creating new entity (e.g., Cleveland Cliffs absorbing AK Steel/ArcelorMittal USA); ownership change triggering re-KYC.

### 3.2 Decision-Maker / Stakeholder Mapping
1. **What it is:** For each customer, map fuel buyer, contract administrator, plant manager, fuel handling supervisor, logistics contact, quality manager, finance/AP, engineering, environmental.
2. **Who performs it:** Account manager.
3. **Data captured:** Name, role, phone, email, location, decision authority, primary/backup.
4. **Documents/forms:** Account map / org chart in CRM; relationship grid.
5. **Frequency:** Continuous update; quarterly review.
6. **Hand-offs:** Marketing (industry events targeting), Customer service, Quality.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Buyer rotation/promotion; outsourced fuel procurement to a consultant (DR-WG, Innio); buyer leaving for competitor or supplier.

### 3.3 Plant Location and Unloading Capability Records
1. **What it is:** For each customer destination, record physical address, rail-served (which railroad, junction), barge-served (river, dock), truck-served, unloading equipment (rotary dumper, bottom-dump, clamshell, conveyor, stacker-reclaimer), max rate, restrictions (length, weight, draft).
2. **Who performs it:** Logistics manager; Customer service.
3. **Data captured:** Plant ID, address, lat/long, modes accepted, max train length, dump rate (cars/hour), draft restriction, hours of operation.
4. **Documents/forms:** Plant data card; unloading agreement; site survey notes.
5. **Frequency:** On new account; updated annually or when equipment changed.
6. **Hand-offs:** Rail/barge/truck dispatch, Sales (delivered pricing).
7. **State-specific differences:** Eastern US plants typically rail or barge served; AL plants often barge (Black Warrior / Tombigbee).
8. **Edge cases:** Plant adds/removes rotary capability changing freight cost; dock dredging affecting draft.

### 3.4 Specifications Customer Buys (Multi-spec)
1. **What it is:** Catalog of which SC products each customer purchases — some buy one spec, integrated steel buys 2-4 grades concurrently (HCC, mid-vol, PCI).
2. **Who performs it:** Account manager.
3. **Data captured:** Customer × product matrix, current annual tons by product.
4. **Documents/forms:** Customer-product matrix; offer sheet.
5. **Frequency:** Quarterly review.
6. **Hand-offs:** Quality forecast, Sales planning.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Customer's BF coal blend recipe change.

### 3.5 Historical Purchase Volume Tracking
1. **What it is:** Year-over-year tonnage by customer; share of wallet calculation.
2. **Who performs it:** Sales operations.
3. **Data captured:** Annual tons by customer, by product, by year (5-10 year history); total customer fuel spend; SC share %.
4. **Documents/forms:** Customer scorecard.
5. **Frequency:** Quarterly.
6. **Hand-offs:** Account manager (renewal strategy), Finance.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Plant retirement event eliminating future tons; data restating of past tons due to error correction.

### 3.6 Payment Terms / Credit Management
1. **What it is:** Credit limit, payment terms (N/10, N/30), security (LOC, parent guaranty, prepayment), payment history scoring.
2. **Who performs it:** Treasury / Credit manager; CFO sign-off above threshold.
3. **Data captured:** Credit limit $, terms, days-sales-outstanding actual, last payment, default events.
4. **Documents/forms:** Credit application, D&B report, financial statements, credit memo.
5. **Frequency:** Annual review; on credit limit increase request; on missed payment.
6. **Hand-offs:** Finance, Legal (if guaranty), Sales (notify when on hold).
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Customer Chapter 11 (Murray Energy 2019; Hibbing Taconite mid-customer events); LOC bank failure; force majeure event extending payment terms.

### 3.7 Customer Documentation Requirements
1. **What it is:** Track per-customer required documentation: CO2/Scope 3 emissions data, sustainability reporting (TCFD, GRI), force majeure protocols, anti-corruption certifications, coal seam/origin certification, MSHA mine ID disclosure.
2. **Who performs it:** Sales operations + Sustainability / ESG manager.
3. **Data captured:** Required document type, due frequency, last submitted date, format, recipient.
4. **Documents/forms:** ESG questionnaires, CDP reports, supplier compliance attestations.
5. **Frequency:** Annual; on customer audit.
6. **Hand-offs:** ESG team, Legal, Operations.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Customer mid-year ESG framework switch; missing prior-year data; CBAM coal scope inclusion for EU buyers.

### 3.8 Customer Satisfaction / Scorecard Management
1. **What it is:** Track customer-issued scorecards (quality, on-time, responsiveness, sustainability); proactively run internal NPS-style review.
2. **Who performs it:** Account manager; VP Sales.
3. **Data captured:** Scorecard period, score by dimension, issues flagged, remediation actions, follow-up date.
4. **Documents/forms:** Customer scorecard PDF; internal QBR deck.
5. **Frequency:** Quarterly per major account.
6. **Hand-offs:** Quality, Operations, Logistics for improvement actions.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Repeated quality miss triggers customer audit; scorecard not received (customer not running formal program).

## 4. Contracts

### 4.1 Term Contract Origination (Utility Multi-Year)
1. **What it is:** Negotiation and execution of 1-, 3-, 5-, or 10-year supply contracts with utilities — typical structure: annual tonnage with monthly delivery program, base price + indexation, quality spec + adjustments, FOB origin or delivered.
2. **Who performs it:** VP Marketing + Senior sales rep + Commercial counsel.
3. **Data captured:** Customer, term, total tons, monthly delivery, price formula, base price, indexes referenced, quality spec, FOB point, freight responsibility.
4. **Documents/forms:** Coal Supply Agreement (CSA); term sheet; pricing schedule exhibit; spec exhibit; freight exhibit; force majeure exhibit.
5. **Frequency:** Periodic — RFP cycle from utility (often annual buy round in Aug-Oct for next year).
6. **Hand-offs:** Legal (review), Reserve engineering (deliverability), Operations (production plan), Logistics (rate confirmation), Finance (credit approval).
7. **State-specific differences:** Some state utilities require PUC approval for fuel contracts above threshold; WV PSC, KY PSC, VA SCC each have different filing requirements.
8. **Edge cases:** RFP re-bid; bilateral negotiation under master agreement; standby/option tons; opt-out triggers tied to environmental regulation changes; co-burn requirements (biomass).

### 4.2 Spot Transaction Booking
1. **What it is:** Single-cargo or short-duration deal (1-3 months) at fixed or indexed price; often broker-intermediated.
2. **Who performs it:** Sales trader/representative.
3. **Data captured:** Customer, tons, price, delivery period, FOB point, quality, mode, payment terms.
4. **Documents/forms:** Confirmation letter or short-form sale and purchase agreement; broker confirm if applicable.
5. **Frequency:** As-occurs; can be daily during active markets.
6. **Hand-offs:** Operations (loadout slot), Logistics (rail/barge order), Credit (approval).
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Broker conflict (same lot offered to two buyers); price drop between trade date and confirmation; customer reneges before fixture.

### 4.3 Tonnage Scheduling (Monthly/Quarterly Nominations)
1. **What it is:** Customer or seller nominates monthly delivery quantity within contract bands (min/max); SC commits to load.
2. **Who performs it:** Contract administrator + Customer fuel buyer.
3. **Data captured:** Nominated tons, accepted tons, ratable rate, allowable variance.
4. **Documents/forms:** Monthly nomination letter or portal entry; quarterly schedule.
5. **Frequency:** Monthly; quarterly review.
6. **Hand-offs:** Production planning, Loadout scheduling, Rail/barge requisitioning.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Customer overlift/underlift triggering true-up; nomination missed forcing fallback to schedule; force majeure mid-month.

### 4.4 Pricing Mechanism Implementation
1. **What it is:** Implementation of contract pricing — fixed, indexed (e.g., Argus McCloskey API2 + premium), base-plus-adjustment, formula (linked to natural gas, electricity, or steel indexes), two-tier (firm tons fixed + flex tons indexed), or PRB-style cents-per-million-Btu.
2. **Who performs it:** Contract administrator; Settlement analyst.
3. **Data captured:** Index name and publication, lag (e.g., previous month average), formula coefficients, floor/ceiling, escalator (CPI, PPI fuel, labor).
4. **Documents/forms:** Pricing schedule exhibit; monthly invoice with calculation backup.
5. **Frequency:** Per shipment (invoiced); monthly index lookup.
6. **Hand-offs:** Finance (revenue recognition), Customer settlement.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Index pause/suspension forcing fallback formula; index methodology change; FX or freight pass-through dispute; out-of-range index reading (limit-up/down).

### 4.5 Quality Adjustment Schedules
1. **What it is:** Codified $/ton penalty/premium for deviation from target BTU, ash, sulfur, moisture, VM, etc. — e.g., -$0.40/ton per 100 BTU below target down to 11,500 BTU floor, then rejection.
2. **Who performs it:** Contract administrator; Quality manager.
3. **Data captured:** Parameter, target, premium/penalty curve, rejection limit, calculation basis (per-shipment or rolling).
4. **Documents/forms:** Quality adjustment exhibit; settlement statement showing per-shipment adjustment.
5. **Frequency:** Every shipment.
6. **Hand-offs:** Lab (COA), Invoicing, Customer.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Rejection-vs-penalty dispute; rolling-average vs per-shipment basis mismatch; mid-contract spec amendment.

### 4.6 Delivery Point and Mode Provisions
1. **What it is:** Specification of FOB mine, FOB rail loadout, FOB barge dock, delivered customer plant, CIF, CFR, DES, DDP; mode-specific terms (rail only, barge only, dual mode).
2. **Who performs it:** Commercial counsel; Logistics manager.
3. **Data captured:** Title transfer point, risk transfer point, mode required, alternative mode allowance.
4. **Documents/forms:** Delivery exhibit; INCOTERMS 2020 reference (export).
5. **Frequency:** Per contract.
6. **Hand-offs:** Logistics (rate development), Finance (revenue recognition timing per ASC 606).
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Dual-mode contract with mode-arbitrage by buyer; force majeure on primary mode; cross-modal cost dispute.

### 4.7 Take-or-Pay Obligations
1. **What it is:** Customer commitment to pay for minimum tonnage even if not lifted; SC obligation to make available; reciprocal commitment language.
2. **Who performs it:** Commercial counsel; Contract administrator.
3. **Data captured:** Minimum tons, makeup right, deficiency price, cure period.
4. **Documents/forms:** Take-or-pay exhibit; deficiency notice.
5. **Frequency:** Annual reconciliation.
6. **Hand-offs:** Finance (revenue recognition / deficiency invoice), Legal.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Force majeure excusing performance; makeup year extending; bankrupt buyer's deficiency claim as unsecured.

### 4.8 Force Majeure Provisions
1. **What it is:** Contractual excuse from performance for events outside reasonable control — strike, mine accident, geological event, severe weather, war, sanctions, transport disruption, lock outage, vessel casualty.
2. **Who performs it:** Commercial counsel; Operations leadership; Account manager (notification).
3. **Data captured:** FM event date, scope, expected duration, tonnage affected, allocation methodology (pro rata across customers).
4. **Documents/forms:** Force majeure notice (written, time-sensitive — typically 5-10 days); allocation schedule; termination notice if FM extends beyond cure period.
5. **Frequency:** Event-driven.
6. **Hand-offs:** Legal, all affected customers, Operations.
7. **State-specific differences:** Permit suspension by WVDEP/VADMME/KYDEP/AL ADEM can be a FM event under most contracts.
8. **Edge cases:** Disputed FM (transport vs production); FM declaration to one customer triggering rights of others; "complete force majeure" definition disputes; price differential between original schedule and make-up delivery.

### 4.9 Hardship / Material Adverse Change Clauses
1. **What it is:** Re-opener clauses allowing renegotiation if specific economic conditions trigger (cost spike, regulatory change).
2. **Who performs it:** Commercial counsel.
3. **Data captured:** Trigger events, trigger thresholds, renegotiation procedure, baseball arbitration fallback.
4. **Documents/forms:** Hardship exhibit; trigger notification.
5. **Frequency:** As-occurs.
6. **Hand-offs:** Legal; senior management.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Trigger dispute (was it material?); deadlock leading to arbitration.

### 4.10 Audit Rights Administration
1. **What it is:** Customer's right to audit SC's books and records related to quality, weight, freight, invoicing — typically 1-3 year lookback, designated auditor.
2. **Who performs it:** Contract administrator; Internal audit; CFO.
3. **Data captured:** Audit requests, scope, records produced, findings, remediation.
4. **Documents/forms:** Audit request letter; data room manifest; audit report; remediation log.
5. **Frequency:** Customer-driven; 1-3 per year typical.
6. **Hand-offs:** Lab (sample retention), Finance, Logistics, Quality.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Auditor demands records beyond contract scope; finding triggering credit/debit memo.

### 4.11 Confidentiality and NDA Tracking
1. **What it is:** NDA in place before commercial discussions; per-contract confidentiality; bid-process confidentiality.
2. **Who performs it:** Commercial counsel; Sales operations.
3. **Data captured:** NDA expiry, scope, mutual/one-way, exceptions.
4. **Documents/forms:** Mutual NDA; specific contract confidentiality clause.
5. **Frequency:** Pre-engagement; renewed periodically.
6. **Hand-offs:** Legal.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Leak; sub-processor (broker) sharing with multiple sellers; NDA expiry mid-deal.

### 4.12 Term Sheet Management
1. **What it is:** Pre-contract summary of commercial terms used for both parties to align before drafting.
2. **Who performs it:** Senior sales rep.
3. **Data captured:** Tons, price, delivery, quality, FOB, term, FM, options, conditionality.
4. **Documents/forms:** Term sheet PDF / portal entry.
5. **Frequency:** Pre-execution.
6. **Hand-offs:** Legal (drafting), Customer (countersign).
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Term sheet binding vs non-binding ambiguity; term sheet escalation to definitive without complete drafting.

### 4.13 Amendment / Change Order Management
1. **What it is:** Formal contract amendment process — tonnage flex, quality flex, term extension, price re-open.
2. **Who performs it:** Contract administrator; Commercial counsel.
3. **Data captured:** Amendment number, effective date, sections amended, signature.
4. **Documents/forms:** Amendment document; tracked-changes redline; signed amendment.
5. **Frequency:** As-needed.
6. **Hand-offs:** Legal; Finance (revenue effect); Operations.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Verbal agreement not papered; conflicting amendments; cross-default if amendment fails.

### 4.14 Renewal Calendar / Option Exercise
1. **What it is:** Tracking of evergreen renewal dates, option windows (volume call, term extension, price re-open), notice periods.
2. **Who performs it:** Contract administrator; VP Marketing.
3. **Data captured:** Date, option type, notice period, exercise/lapse status.
4. **Documents/forms:** Renewal/option calendar; exercise notice letter.
5. **Frequency:** Monthly review; pre-deadline alert.
6. **Hand-offs:** Sales (decision), Legal (notice service).
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Notice missed (auto-renew); notice timing dispute; market change favoring/disfavoring exercise.

### 4.15 Optionality Management (Volume Calls, Quality Bands)
1. **What it is:** Tracking and valuing buyer's optional rights — volume call (buy up to X% more), quality band optionality (sub vs super spec).
2. **Who performs it:** Commercial counsel; Marketing analyst.
3. **Data captured:** Option type, strike, expiry, current market value vs strike.
4. **Documents/forms:** Option valuation memo; exercise notice.
5. **Frequency:** Monthly valuation; on exercise.
6. **Hand-offs:** Finance (fair value), Operations (capacity to deliver).
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Customer trying to call into a tight supply environment; option exercise during force majeure.

### 4.16 Contract Performance Dashboard
1. **What it is:** Per-contract dashboard of nominated vs delivered tons, quality performance vs spec, demurrage incurred, penalty/premium balance, financial vs forecast.
2. **Who performs it:** Sales operations; Account manager.
3. **Data captured:** Tons MTD/YTD, $/ton realized, quality, on-time %, demurrage $, penalty $.
4. **Documents/forms:** Dashboard PDF or Power BI.
5. **Frequency:** Weekly internal; monthly external (customer QBR).
6. **Hand-offs:** Account manager (corrective actions).
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Data lag from logistics; mid-period correction; missing customer-side data.

### 4.17 Settlement and True-Up
1. **What it is:** End-of-period reconciliation for indexed contracts — calculate true-up payment between provisional and final indexed price; reconcile quality adjustments; reconcile take-or-pay.
2. **Who performs it:** Settlement analyst.
3. **Data captured:** Provisional vs final price per shipment, difference $/ton, total true-up $.
4. **Documents/forms:** Settlement statement; credit memo / debit memo.
5. **Frequency:** Monthly or quarterly; annual for take-or-pay.
6. **Hand-offs:** Finance, Customer AP.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Index dispute; lookback over multi-month period; FX or freight pass-through retro.

## 5. Shipment Planning

### 5.1 Monthly Sales Plan by Customer/Product
1. **What it is:** S&OP-driven monthly plan integrating contract obligations + spot opportunities + production capability + transportation capacity.
2. **Who performs it:** S&OP lead; Sales; Production planning.
3. **Data captured:** Customer × product × month tons, by mode, by terminal.
4. **Documents/forms:** Monthly S&OP deck; constraint analysis.
5. **Frequency:** Monthly; bi-weekly during peak.
6. **Hand-offs:** Production (mine plan), Quality (blend plan), Logistics (mode capacity), Finance (forecast).
7. **State-specific differences:** WV/VA/KY met production typically routed through Lambert's Point/DTA/Pier IX; AL through Mobile/McDuffie; western SC properties may stockpile or rail-direct.
8. **Edge cases:** Plan-actual gap; mine slip; customer reschedule; rail dispatch shortfall.

### 5.2 Daily Loadout Schedule (Per Loadout / Per Hour)
1. **What it is:** Hour-by-hour schedule of train/barge/truck loads at each loadout; sequencing of stockpile-to-silo blend setup.
2. **Who performs it:** Loadout dispatcher; Plant superintendent.
3. **Data captured:** Loadout, train/barge ID, scheduled start/end, tons, product, customer.
4. **Documents/forms:** Loadout daily schedule; shift turnover log.
5. **Frequency:** Daily; updated intraday.
6. **Hand-offs:** Plant ops, Rail dispatch, Lab (sampling), QC.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV/VA/KY loadouts typically rail-served (NS or CSX); AL loadouts may include barge.
8. **Edge cases:** Rail late arrival; mechanical breakdown of dumper/silo; weather closure; stockpile shortage.

### 5.3 Truck Dispatch Schedule (In-Haul and Customer Delivery)
1. **What it is:** Dispatch list of trucks moving raw coal from mine to prep plant, clean coal to loadout, or direct to customer (for short-haul utility deliveries).
2. **Who performs it:** Truck dispatcher.
3. **Data captured:** Truck ID, driver, origin, destination, tons, time, route.
4. **Documents/forms:** Daily dispatch sheet; ELD log; bill of lading per load.
5. **Frequency:** Daily / per-shift.
6. **Hand-offs:** Mine ops, Prep plant, Customer receiving.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV — coal trucks subject to county weight permits; VA — Coal & Gas Road Improvement Tax up to 1% of gross receipts funds road repair; KY — coal haul roads; AL — varying county rules.
8. **Edge cases:** Driver out-of-hours; weather closure; truck overweight ticket; haul road damage assessment.

### 5.4 Rail Car Request / Order
1. **What it is:** Ordering rail cars from NS, CSX, BNSF, UP, CPKC, or short lines (R.J. Corman, Buckingham Branch, Watco subsidiaries, Genesee & Wyoming subsidiaries); using EDI 204 or carrier portal.
2. **Who performs it:** Rail logistics coordinator.
3. **Data captured:** Number of cars, car type, origin, destination, load date, customer reference.
4. **Documents/forms:** Car order request (EDI 204 / portal); car placement confirmation.
5. **Frequency:** Daily; per shipment.
6. **Hand-offs:** Railroad customer service, Loadout, Customer (notice of arrival).
7. **State-specific differences:** NS dominant in CAPP (VA/WV); CSX in NAPP and parts of CAPP; CSX in AL Black Warrior. Short line: Buckingham Branch (VA), R.J. Corman (KY), Watco (multiple).
8. **Edge cases:** Car shortage; bad-order cars; misrouted cars; embargo declared by railroad.

### 5.5 Barge Tow Schedule (Ohio, Big Sandy, Kanawha, Tennessee, Cumberland, Black Warrior, Tombigbee)
1. **What it is:** Booking barges and tow service from Ingram Barge, ACBL (American Commercial Barge Line), Marathon Petroleum, Marquette Transportation, Crounse Corporation, McKinney Towing, Amherst Madison (Kanawha/Ohio specialist), Campbell Transportation.
2. **Who performs it:** Marine logistics coordinator.
3. **Data captured:** Barge ID, tow operator, load dock, destination, tow window, draft, tons.
4. **Documents/forms:** Barge nomination; tow confirmation; barge BOL.
5. **Frequency:** Per cargo; weekly tow line-up review.
6. **Hand-offs:** Loadout dock, Tow operator, Receiving dock.
7. **State-specific differences:** WV Kanawha — Amherst Madison dominant; Big Sandy — multi-operator; Ohio River trunkline — Ingram/ACBL/Marathon/Marquette/Crounse; Black Warrior/Tombigbee (AL) — different operator pool (Parker Towing, Mobile Bar Pilot).
8. **Edge cases:** River high/low water; lock outage; tow operator strike; barge sinking incidents.

### 5.6 Vessel Loading Nomination
1. **What it is:** Nominate vessel to terminal — laycan window (canceling date / arrival date), vessel name, size (Panamax 65-80kt, Capesize 150-180kt, Newcastlemax), discharge port, charterer.
2. **Who performs it:** Marine ops; Vessel chartering.
3. **Data captured:** Vessel name/IMO, laycan, tonnage, grade, terminal, ETA, charterer.
4. **Documents/forms:** Vessel nomination letter; terminal acceptance; pre-fixture inspection.
5. **Frequency:** Per cargo.
6. **Hand-offs:** Terminal operations, Rail planning (deliver cargo ahead of laycan), Customer (notice of fixture).
7. **State-specific differences:** Hampton Roads VA terminals (Lambert's Point, DTA, Pier IX) vs Baltimore MD (CNX, Curtis Bay) — different draft restrictions, channel rules.
8. **Edge cases:** Vessel arrival outside laycan (cancel or accept under protest); vessel substitution; demurrage clock running on early/late vessel.

### 5.7 Sales-Operations Coordination (S&OP)
1. **What it is:** Cross-functional meetings reconciling production plan against sales plan, with logistics constraint analysis.
2. **Who performs it:** S&OP lead; VP Sales; VP Operations; CFO.
3. **Data captured:** Production forecast, sales plan, inventory positions, transport capacity, financial outlook.
4. **Documents/forms:** S&OP deck; constraint list; action items.
5. **Frequency:** Monthly main; weekly tactical.
6. **Hand-offs:** All functions.
7. **State-specific differences:** N/A.
8. **Edge cases:** Mine production slip mid-month; customer cancellation freeing capacity; price shift triggering re-prioritization.

### 5.8 Inventory Positioning (Stockpile-to-Loadout)
1. **What it is:** Decisions on which mine inventory feeds which loadout/dock; railing or trucking between sites; pad management.
2. **Who performs it:** Logistics coordinator; Plant superintendent.
3. **Data captured:** Stockpile location, tons, quality, intended customer, age.
4. **Documents/forms:** Stockpile map; transfer order.
5. **Frequency:** Daily.
6. **Hand-offs:** Plant, Trucking, Quality.
7. **State-specific differences:** Permit constraints on stockpile capacity at WV/VA/KY surface sites.
8. **Edge cases:** Pad overflow forcing flush sales; mismatched quality assigned to customer.
