# Domain 8: HR, Workforce, Labor, Benefits & Wellness

# HR, Workforce, Labor, Benefits & Wellness

Domain inventory for Southern Coal Corporation (WV, VA, KY, AL, TN; ~300–1,200 employees; mixed union/non-union; surface and underground operations; HR-side workforce processes including those that hand off to the Mine Safety domain for MSHA training, miner certifications, and OSHA/MSHA inspections).

Each function lists: (1) What it is, (2) Who performs it, (3) Data captured, (4) Documents/forms, (5) Frequency, (6) Hand-offs, (7) State-specific differences, (8) Common edge cases.

---

## Workforce Planning

### Headcount Budget by Mine and Craft
1. Annual budget of FTE counts by mine, by craft family (production face crew, maintenance, electrical, supervision, technical/engineering, administrative, surface), and by shift.
2. HR Director with VP Operations, Mine Superintendents, Controller/CFO; reviewed by President.
3. Budgeted FTE by mine/craft/shift; loaded hourly cost (wage + benefits + workers comp + payroll tax loaders); attrition assumption; over/under to plan monthly.
4. Annual Headcount Plan worksheet (internal); reconciles to Production Plan tons-per-employee assumptions; feeds Labor section of operating budget.
5. Built annually (Q4 for next year); refreshed quarterly; reforecast on permit changes, idling, or new sections.
6. Hands off to Payroll (cost loaders), Finance (labor budget rollup), Operations (crewing model), Mine Safety (MSHA training capacity to absorb hires).
7. WV/VA/KY: state UI experience rates and workers comp base rates differ by state — load factor varies; KY adds coal-specific assessments. AL/TN crews much smaller.
8. Edge cases: idling a section but holding crew on payroll to retain experienced miners; "ghost" positions kept budgeted for political reasons; contractor offload that hides true headcount.

### Position Control (Budgeted vs Filled vs Open)
1. Live ledger of every approved position with status: budgeted, filled, open, frozen, eliminated.
2. HR Generalist owns the ledger; Superintendents approve fills; HR Director approves new positions; CFO approves headcount adds.
3. Position ID, title, classification/pay grade, FLSA status, cost center/mine, reporting manager, status, last incumbent, days open, requisition number.
4. Position Authorization Form (PAF); Personnel Action Form (also PAF, distinct); requisition record in ATS or paper.
5. Continuous; reconciled monthly to payroll active roster.
6. Hands off to Finance (open positions accrual decisions), Recruiting (requisition queue), Payroll (active roster reconciliation).
7. No direct state variation; UMWA mines layer in NBCWA job classifications and panel order.
8. Edge cases: position filled "out of class" pending bid; position carrying a person on workers comp / FMLA who may not return; double-fill during knowledge transfer.

### Succession Planning
1. Identification of successors for foreman, section foreman, mine foreman, superintendent, chief electrician, master mechanic, preparation plant superintendent, chief engineer, controller, and other key roles.
2. HR Director, VP Operations, GM per complex; reviewed annually with President.
3. Successor name, readiness (ready now / 1-2 years / 3-5 years), development gap, certifications held vs needed (Mine Foreman papers, EE-1, Surface Foreman, etc.), retention risk.
4. 9-Box grid; Succession Slate by Position; Individual Development Plan (IDP).
5. Annual full review; quarterly updates on movement.
6. Hands off to Mine Safety (foreman/superintendent certifications and continuing ed coordination), Training (development plan delivery), Compensation (retention pay where warranted).
7. WV, VA, KY each issue their own state mine foreman/EE certifications — successor must be certified in the operating state; cross-state movement requires reciprocity or re-test.
8. Edge cases: "bench" person retires before incumbent; identified successor leaves; family-business loyalty vs best-qualified candidate tension.

### Workforce Demographics & Retirement Forecasting
1. Age, tenure, certification-eligibility tracking to forecast retirement waves. Coal workforce is aging — median age often 45+; experienced miners (20+ years) carry irreplaceable tacit knowledge.
2. HR Generalist runs the analytics; HR Director presents to Operations.
3. DOB, hire date, length of service, last anniversary, eligibility for pension/401(k) full vesting, eligibility for UMWA Health & Retirement Funds (where applicable), self-declared planned retirement date.
4. Age/tenure pivot, "retirement-eligible in next 24/36/60 months" lists by mine/craft.
5. Refreshed quarterly; deep-dive annually.
6. Hands off to Workforce Planning (replacement pipeline), Benefits (retiree medical/OPEB liability projections), Finance (UMWA H&R Funds contribution projection, MPPAA exposure modeling).
7. UMWA-covered mines drive multi-employer plan exposure that varies by historical participation, not state.
8. Edge cases: retirement wave triggered by NBCWA reopener or rumored mine closure; key foreman delays retirement for an unvested grant or to hit 30-year bonus; "phantom retirees" who keep coming back as contractors.

### Critical Role Identification & Pipeline Development
1. Defining roles where vacancy halts production (mine foreman, certified electrician EE-1, chief electrician, longwall coordinator if applicable, prep plant operator, dragline operator on surface), and building feeder pipelines (apprentices, second-shift backups).
2. Operations leadership with HR; Training Coordinator owns pipeline build.
3. Role criticality score, current bench depth, time-to-replace, apprenticeship slots, registered apprenticeship roster.
4. Critical Role Register; Apprenticeship Standards (if state-registered with WV/VA/KY DOL apprenticeship offices); Mentor Assignment.
5. Annual register update; pipeline reviewed quarterly.
6. Hands off to Mine Safety (newly-certified miners need MSHA new-miner training, then experienced-miner status), Training (development), Recruiting (external sourcing where pipeline is dry).
7. WV apprenticeship: WV Office of Apprenticeship/USDOL; VA: Virginia Department of Labor and Industry Registered Apprenticeship; KY: Kentucky Department of Workforce Investment.
8. Edge cases: certified electrician retires with no qualified backup — operating illegally until replaced; apprentice fails state cert exam; rural labor market with zero candidates.

---

## Recruiting

### Job Requisition Workflow
1. Approval workflow from hiring manager request to posted requisition.
2. Hiring Manager (Superintendent/Foreman) initiates; HR Director and CFO approve; Recruiter posts.
3. Requisition number, mine/cost center, title, classification, pay range, justification (replacement vs new), target start, certifications required.
4. Requisition Authorization Form; backfill checklist (terminated employee name, end date).
5. As-needed.
6. Hands off to Recruiting (sourcing), Position Control, Finance (budget check).
7. UMWA mines: bargaining-unit vacancies must first be posted internally per NBCWA bidding rules before external posting.
8. Edge cases: hiring manager bypasses requisition by hiring a contractor; "temporary" hire that becomes permanent without re-requisition; promotion-from-within that creates a cascade of req's.

### Sourcing Channels
1. Channels used to attract coal mining candidates.
2. Recruiter; Operations referrals.
3. Source code per applicant, cost-per-hire, yield by source, time-to-fill.
4. Source list: New River CTC, Southern WV CTC, Mountwest CTC, Bluefield State, Eastern KY University, Big Sandy Community & Technical College, Hazard Community & Technical College, Mountain Empire Community College (VA), miner relocation networks, Indeed mining segment, NBCWA panel recall, internal employee referral, military veteran outreach (USERRA hires; Hire Vets Medallion programs), former-employee rehire list.
5. Continuous; intensifies during expansion.
6. Hands off to Mine Safety (verification that new hires can complete required MSHA new-miner training within 90 days).
7. WV/VA/KY have strong vocational mining programs; AL/TN draw more from general industrial labor pools.
8. Edge cases: poaching from a competitor mine where the candidate brings an active workers comp claim; rehire of a former employee who was previously discharged for safety violations; candidate who is on a competitor's UMWA panel.

### Application Intake
1. Receipt of applications — paper applications still common in coal country given uneven broadband.
2. HR Clerk/Mine Clerk at site; Recruiter at HQ.
3. Applicant data, prior mines worked, prior MSHA certifications, prior workers comp claims (where lawful to ask, generally only post-offer), references, "applied for what position" tracking.
4. Standard Employment Application (state-compliant — must avoid disallowed questions: salary history is restricted in some VA municipalities; criminal-history "ban the box" varies); Voluntary EEO Self-Identification; Voluntary Veteran/Disability Self-ID; ATS record.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Screening, EEO recordkeeping.
7. WV: no statewide salary-history ban. VA: state-level ban on salary-history retaliation but not asking. KY: no statewide ban-the-box for private employers.
8. Edge cases: paper apps lost between site and HQ; applicant unwilling to disclose SSN until offer; same applicant applying at multiple mines.

### Pre-Employment Screening
1. Background check, drug test, MMR (medical/physical capability), check of prior MSHA citations issued against the individual via MSHA's Mine Data Retrieval System.
2. Recruiter coordinates; Background vendor; Occupational health clinic; Medical Review Officer (MRO) for drug results.
3. Criminal history hits, MVR for drivers, drug test result (negative/positive/dilute/refused), physical fitness for the essential functions of mining (lifting, climbing, respirator fit), MSHA individual citation history.
4. FCRA Disclosure & Authorization (separate document); FCRA Pre-Adverse / Adverse Action Notice; consent for drug test; physical capability evaluation form; respirator medical clearance (OSHA 1910.134 Appendix C).
5. Pre-hire; periodically for drivers (annual MVR).
6. Hands off to Onboarding, Mine Safety (respirator fit testing, hearing baseline), Legal (adverse action handling).
7. WV: medical marijuana law passed 2017; mining is safety-sensitive — positive THC test still disqualifying. VA: medical cannabis broader, still safety-sensitive carve-out for mining. KY: no recreational, narrow medical; positive THC disqualifying. Some states protect off-duty lawful use, but safety-sensitive coal mining is exempt.
8. Edge cases: applicant with expunged record that still appears; positive THC with valid medical card in WV/VA — still rejected for safety-sensitive role but file adverse action carefully; dilute specimen requiring re-test; applicant with chronic MSHA citation history at prior employer.

### Reference Checking
1. Validation of prior employment, eligibility for rehire, and (lawful) performance comments.
2. Recruiter; senior HR for executive hires.
3. Dates of employment, last position, eligibility for rehire (most former employers will only confirm name/dates/title).
4. Reference Check Worksheet.
5. Per offer.
6. Hands off to Hiring Manager and Offer.
7. Defamation risk varies; KY and WV have qualified-privilege protection for good-faith references; VA similar.
8. Edge cases: former supervisor at competitor refuses contact; "boomerang" rehire of prior employee — internal HR record is the reference.

### Interview Scheduling
1. Logistics for phone, on-site, and panel interviews.
2. Recruiter; Hiring Manager.
3. Interview date, interviewers, structured interview scores.
4. Structured Interview Guide; Interview Scorecard; Travel reimbursement form for distant candidates.
5. Per requisition.
6. Hands off to Offer.
7. None significant.
8. Edge cases: candidate no-shows because shift work makes scheduling hard; candidate touring an underground mine for "realistic job preview" creates non-employee MSHA training/escort questions.

### Job Offer, Negotiation
1. Written offer with all conditions (drug test, background, physical, I-9, references, MSHA new-miner training completion within 90 days).
2. Recruiter drafts; Hiring Manager and HR Director approve; sent to candidate.
3. Offered wage/salary, sign-on, relocation, start date, classification, mine assignment, shift, supervisor, contingencies.
4. Contingent Offer Letter; if union — letter notes that the position is in the bargaining unit and subject to NBCWA; relocation agreement (repay if leaving within X months); confidentiality/non-disclosure; arbitration agreement (where used).
5. Per accepted candidate.
6. Hands off to Onboarding, Payroll.
7. WV: non-competes generally enforceable if reasonable. VA: in 2026, "low-wage" employees (avg weekly wage <$1,507.01) cannot be subject to non-competes; effective July 1, 2026 per SB 170, non-competes are void against employees discharged without cause unless severance is paid. KY: non-competes enforceable if reasonable; per Charles T. Creech, Inc. v. Brown (KY S. Ct. 2014) continued employment alone is NOT consideration to bind an existing employee — must accompany promotion, pay raise, or new benefit.
8. Edge cases: candidate accepts then "ghosts" before start; offered wage below union scale for a misclassified union position; relocation package abused by serial relocators.

### Onboarding Paperwork
1. Forms package for first day.
2. HR Generalist with Mine Clerk for site forms.
3. Personal data, withholdings, banking, beneficiaries, policy acknowledgements.
4. Federal: I-9, W-4, Direct Deposit authorization, Form 8850 (WOTC), New Hire Reporting (federal new-hire database). State W-4 equivalents: WV/IT-104, VA-4, K-4. State new-hire reporting: WV New Hire Reporting Center; VA New Hire Reporting Center; KY New Hire Reporting Center. Plus internal: handbook acknowledgement, substance abuse policy acknowledgement, PPE issue sheet, confidentiality, code of conduct, harassment policy acknowledgement, electronic communications policy.
5. Per hire.
6. Hands off to Payroll, IT (system access), Mine Safety (training enrollment), Benefits (eligibility countdown).
7. WV/VA/KY each require state new-hire reporting within 20 days. WV-IT-104, VA-4, K-4 are state withholding forms.
8. Edge cases: SSN no-match; new hire works in WV but lives in KY — multi-state withholding setup; rehire whose I-9 may be reverified vs re-completed.

### Apprenticeship / New Miner Ramp-Up
1. Structured ramp of inexperienced miners — paid training, mentor pairing, progressive job duties.
2. Training Coordinator (HR-side coordination with Mine Safety MSHA trainer who delivers Part 46/48 instruction).
3. Apprentice ID, hours per task, mentor name, evaluation milestones, target full-craft date.
4. Apprenticeship Standards (if registered with USDOL Office of Apprenticeship or state apprenticeship agency); New Miner Training records held by Safety per 30 CFR Part 48 (handed off).
5. Continuous per cohort.
6. Hands off to Mine Safety (delivery of MSHA new-miner 40-hr underground / 24-hr surface, 8-hr annual refresher, task training); to Operations (productivity).
7. Registered apprenticeship reciprocity varies by state; WV/VA/KY all have apprenticeship offices.
8. Edge cases: apprentice fails MSHA black hat-to-red hat progression; mentor changes shift; apprentice claims unsafe assignment.

---

## Onboarding

### I-9 Verification
1. Federal employment eligibility verification.
2. HR Generalist or trained Mine Clerk.
3. Document list A or B+C, document number, expiration, completion dates.
4. Form I-9 (2023 revised version); E-Verify case (if enrolled).
5. Within 3 business days of hire.
6. Hands off to Personnel File (I-9 stored separately from personnel file).
7. WV: no E-Verify mandate for private employers. VA: E-Verify mandatory for state contractors with 50+ employees on contracts >$50K. KY: no general E-Verify mandate. AL/TN: AL mandates E-Verify for all employers; TN E-Verify required for employers with 35+ employees.
8. Edge cases: receipt for replacement document; remote hire I-9 (post-2023 alternative procedure for E-Verify employers); expiring work authorization reverification (Supplement B).

### Federal & State Tax Forms
1. W-4 federal and state equivalent.
2. HR Generalist; Payroll Administrator.
3. Filing status, allowances/credits, additional withholding, state of residence vs work state.
4. IRS Form W-4 (2026 version); WV/IT-104; VA-4; K-4; AL A-4; TN has no state income tax — no form.
5. At hire and on employee change.
6. Hands off to Payroll.
7. Multi-state miners: WV resident working at KY mine — KY withholding plus WV resident reconciliation; no reciprocity between WV and KY. VA-KY reciprocity exists (Form VA-4 + K-4).
8. Edge cases: undeliverable W-2 due to address change; employee claims exempt and earns too much; resident state changes mid-year.

### Direct Deposit Setup
1. ACH banking for net pay.
2. HR Generalist; Payroll Administrator.
3. Routing, account, account type, % or $ allocation across accounts.
4. Direct Deposit Authorization with voided check or bank letter.
5. At hire and on change.
6. Hands off to Payroll bank.
7. WV/VA/KY allow electronic-only pay only if certain conditions (employee consent or paycard option provided).
8. Edge cases: closed account; pre-note rejection; split deposits across multiple banks.

### Benefits Enrollment
1. Initial enrollment in medical/dental/vision/FSA/HSA/401(k)/life/disability.
2. Benefits Coordinator.
3. Plan elections, dependents, coverage tiers, beneficiary designations, evidence of insurability where required.
4. Plan-specific enrollment forms or ben admin platform record; HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices; Summary of Benefits and Coverage (SBC); Marketplace Notice (ACA Section 18B); CHIPRA notice; Medicare Part D Creditable Coverage Notice.
5. At hire (within waiting period — commonly 30/60/90 days), at qualifying life events, at annual open enrollment.
6. Hands off to Carriers, Payroll (deduction setup).
7. Marketplace Notice required nationwide; state-specific continuation coverage where state mini-COBRA applies (WV mini-COBRA for groups <20; VA Continuation; KY has limited).
8. Edge cases: missed enrollment window; QLE evidence missing; dependent over age; domestic partner coverage tax treatment.

### Confidentiality / Non-Compete / Restrictive Covenants
1. Restrictive-covenant package signed at hire (or promotion).
2. HR Director; Legal review for executives.
3. Scope (geography, time, activity), consideration, choice of law.
4. Confidentiality / NDA, Non-Compete (where lawful and reasonable), Non-Solicitation, Invention Assignment.
5. At hire or promotion.
6. Hands off to Personnel File; Legal vault.
7. Critical state variation: VA strict low-wage ban + new July 1, 2026 SB 170 restrictions (void if discharged without cause unless severance paid; up to $10,000 per violation penalties). KY requires fresh consideration for mid-employment non-competes. WV generally enforces reasonable restrictions; FTC's non-compete ban remains tied up in litigation as of 2026 — treat as still-evolving.
8. Edge cases: choice-of-law clauses to evade VA restrictions (often unenforceable); enforcing against a long-tenured miner with no fresh consideration in KY; "garden leave" alternative for executives.

### Substance Abuse Policy Acknowledgement
1. Signed acknowledgement that employee will submit to pre-employment, random, post-accident, reasonable suspicion, return-to-duty, and follow-up testing.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Acknowledgement date, witness, copy of policy received.
4. Drug & Alcohol Policy; Consent to Test; Notice of Random Selection Process; rights under WV drug-free workplace law (where claimed).
5. At hire; re-acknowledge on material policy change.
6. Hands off to D&A Coordinator, Mine Safety (post-accident protocol coordination).
7. WV §22A-1A (Drug Free Workplace Act for coal mines): mandatory program covering all safety-sensitive employees; specific panel of substances; SAMHSA-certified lab; safe-harbor from wrongful termination if program followed. VA/KY: no mining-specific drug-free workplace statute; employer policy governs but mining recognized as safety-sensitive.
8. Edge cases: employee claims they didn't understand policy; medical marijuana cardholder asking for accommodation.

### Drug Test (Pre-Employment)
1. Pre-employment drug screen; SAMHSA panel typically 5- or 10-panel.
2. Recruiter coordinates; Collection site; MRO reviews.
3. Specimen ID, chain of custody, result, MRO verification.
4. Federal Custody and Control Form (CCF) or state-specific equivalent; MRO letter.
5. Pre-hire.
6. Hands off to HR (negative = clear to start; non-negative = adverse action workflow).
7. WV mining: panel includes alcohol, amphetamines, cannabinoids (THC), cocaine, opiates, phencyclidine per WV Code §22A-1A. VA/KY apply employer policy.
8. Edge cases: dilute specimen → re-test; positive with valid prescription → MRO verification; refusal (shy bladder protocols).

### Equipment / PPE Issue
1. Issue of hard hat, cap lamp, self-rescuer assignment, steel-toe boots reimbursement, FR clothing, safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, belt, kneepads.
2. Mine Clerk; Warehouse.
3. PPE issued, serial numbers (cap lamp, SCSR), size, reissue dates.
4. PPE Issue Sheet; Boot Reimbursement form; SCSR assignment log (also tracked by Mine Safety).
5. At hire; replacement as needed.
6. Hands off to Mine Safety (SCSR is MSHA-required and tracked under 30 CFR), Warehouse.
7. None state-specific.
8. Edge cases: PPE not returned at termination → wage deduction limits vary; allergy to FR fabric needs accommodation; ill-fitting respirator → re-fit.

### ID Badge / Access Credentials
1. Photo ID, mine site access badge, IT account.
2. HR Generalist; IT; Mine Clerk for site badges; Site Security.
3. Badge number, access levels, IT account, MFA device, email.
4. Badge Issue Form; IT Provisioning Ticket.
5. At hire; deactivation at termination.
6. Hands off to IT, Security, Time & Attendance (badge feeds clock).
7. None.
8. Edge cases: shared badges (a discipline issue); badge active after termination — security gap.

### Coal Mining-Specific Orientation & Site Safety
1. HR-side onboarding modules — handbook, harassment, EEO, IT acceptable use, ethics, drug-free workplace — distinct from MSHA new-miner safety training delivered by Mine Safety.
2. HR Generalist or Training Coordinator delivers HR modules; Mine Safety delivers MSHA modules.
3. Topics completed, date, signed acknowledgements, test scores.
4. Orientation Checklist; Handbook Acknowledgement.
5. Within first 1–2 weeks.
6. Hand off the MSHA training requirements to Mine Safety (5000-23 forms maintained there).
7. State sexual harassment training mandates differ — none of WV/VA/KY currently mandate annual sexual harassment training for private employers, but VA state contractors and certain industries have requirements.
8. Edge cases: contractor employee mistakenly given full-employee orientation; remote/clerical hire who never goes underground but still receives surface orientation.

### Light-Duty / Restricted Assignment at Hire
1. Rare — but if a new hire arrives with a pre-existing restriction from a prior employer, accommodate or rescind.
2. HR with Site Safety, Operations.
3. Restriction description, source (physician note), expected duration.
4. Functional Capacity Evaluation; ADA Accommodation Request log.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to Workers Comp/ADA tracker.
7. None state-specific.
8. Edge cases: restriction not disclosed at offer → potential rescission with legal review; restriction permanent → essential-function analysis.

## Employee Master / HRIS

### Personnel File (Digital + Paper)
1. Single source of record for each employee.
2. HR Generalist; HR Director custodian.
3. All hiring docs, pay history, performance, discipline, training rosters (non-MSHA), separation docs.
4. Personnel file folder structure; access log.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Legal on litigation hold; to Payroll for payroll change packets.
7. State right-to-inspect varies — WV (no statute, common practice), VA (no statute), KY (no statute). Many companies grant access by policy anyway.
8. Edge cases: medical info accidentally placed in main file (HIPAA/ADA violation); union grievance discovery scope; subpoena response.

### Hire Date, Anniversaries, Service
1. Tracking of hire date, adjusted service date (rehires, union service credit), and milestones.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Original hire, rehire dates, total credited service, vacation accrual tier, vesting date, retirement eligibility date.
4. Service Computation Worksheet; for NBCWA-covered, panel/seniority date.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Benefits (vesting), Payroll (accruals), Union (panel/seniority).
7. UMWA service crediting under NBCWA rules; UMWA H&R Funds credit signatory hours specifically.
8. Edge cases: bridge of prior service across an acquisition; military service credit (USERRA); break-in-service rules.

### Position / Classification / Pay Grade
1. Position metadata.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Job code, FLSA status, EEO-1 category, pay grade.
4. Job Description; Position Authorization.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Comp, Payroll, Union (classification disputes).
7. None state-specific.
8. Edge cases: misclassification of exempt/non-exempt → FLSA exposure; "working out of class" grievance.

### Reporting Structure
1. Manager-of-record chain.
2. HR Generalist; Org Design owner.
3. Direct manager, dotted-line, mine GM, segment VP.
4. Org chart; manager assignment in HRIS.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to all systems that route by manager (timecards, performance, approvals).
7. None.
8. Edge cases: dotted-line for technical roles; acting/interim manager; orphan employees after a manager terminates.

### Cost Center / Mine Assignment
1. Where the labor cost lands.
2. HR; Payroll; Cost Accounting.
3. Cost center, mine ID, work unit, GL account.
4. Cost Center Change Form.
5. On hire and change.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Cost Accounting, Production reporting.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: split assignment across mines on the same day; loaner crew between sites.

### Demographic Data (EEO)
1. Race/ethnicity, gender, veteran, disability for EEO reporting.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Self-identified data, refusal noted.
4. EEO Self-ID Form; Veteran Self-ID; Disability Self-ID (OFCCP form if federal contractor).
5. At hire; periodic re-survey.
6. Hands off to EEO compliance.
7. EEO-1 filing required at federal contractor thresholds or 100+ employees private; Southern Coal likely meets the threshold.
8. Edge cases: refusal to self-identify (visual identification permitted at hire for race/gender under EEOC rules); recategorization of multi-race; change in gender identity.

### Emergency Contacts & Beneficiary Designations
1. Who to call; who gets life insurance/401(k).
2. HR Generalist; Benefits Coordinator.
3. Contact name, relationship, phone; beneficiary % allocation.
4. Emergency Contact Form; Beneficiary Designation per plan.
5. At hire; encouraged annual review.
6. Hands off to Operations (incident response), Carriers.
7. Spousal consent rules for 401(k) per ERISA — same nationally; UMWA H&R Funds have their own beneficiary rules.
8. Edge cases: divorced employee never updated beneficiary; minor beneficiaries (guardianship); estranged spouse claim.

### Address / Phone / Email
1. Current contact info — critical in coal communities with limited connectivity.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Mailing address, physical, primary phone, alternate, personal email.
4. Address Change Form.
5. On change; annual confirmation.
6. Hands off to Payroll (W-2 mailing, multi-state withholding triggers), Benefits (carrier address).
7. State residence change can trigger multi-state withholding setup (WV ↔ KY: no reciprocity; KY ↔ VA: reciprocity).
8. Edge cases: rural addresses without USPS delivery; PO Box only — affects garnishment service.

---

## Payroll Administration

### Time Clock Data Collection
1. Capture of hours worked per mine, per shift.
2. Mine Clerk; Supervisor; Payroll Administrator.
3. In/out punches, lunch deduction, shift code, mine, section, job class, premium codes.
4. Time records (badge, biometric, supervisor sheet); time edit log.
5. Per shift; aggregated weekly/bi-weekly.
6. Hands off to Payroll system.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: badge reader down at portal; biometric fail with muddy/cold fingers; supervisor enters time for an unauthorized employee.

### Timekeeping (Badges / Biometric / Supervisor Entry)
1. Method-of-capture configuration.
2. Mine Clerk.
3. Capture method, exceptions.
4. Time Capture Policy.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Payroll.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: BIPA-style biometric laws don't apply in WV/VA/KY (Illinois only), but employee consent best practice.

### Edit / Exception Handling
1. Missed punches, shift differentials, call-out approvals.
2. Supervisor; Mine Clerk; Payroll Administrator.
3. Exception type, reason, approver, original vs adjusted hours.
4. Time Edit Form; Missed Punch Affidavit.
5. Per pay period.
6. Hands off to Payroll.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: edit done by supervisor without employee initials → wage-hour audit risk.

### Overtime Authorization
1. Pre-authorization for OT.
2. Supervisor approves; Superintendent on multi-shift OT; HR audits.
3. Approved hours, reason, project/mine.
4. OT Authorization Form.
5. Per pay period.
6. Hands off to Payroll.
7. State daily OT: WV/VA/KY follow federal 40-hr weekly OT only.
8. Edge cases: OT worked without approval but FLSA still requires payment; OT abuse for retirement spike pay.

### Premium Pay
1. Holiday, Sunday, hazard, call-out, on-call, shift differential.
2. Payroll Administrator; classifications per union contract or policy.
3. Premium code, hours, rate factor.
4. Premium Pay Matrix; NBCWA Article on Premium Pay (for union).
5. Per pay period.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Finance.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: holiday falls on regular off-day; pyramiding OT and premiums prohibited but accidentally paid.

### Per Diem
1. Travel and away-from-home work allowances.
2. Payroll; Finance.
3. Days, rate, location.
4. Per Diem Authorization; Expense Report.
5. Per trip.
6. Hands off to Finance.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: per diem paid as taxable wages by mistake; over IRS rate triggers tax.

### Bonus Calculations
1. Production, safety, attendance bonuses.
2. HR with Operations and Safety (Mine Safety provides safety-incident inputs).
3. Bonus formula inputs, eligibility, accrual.
4. Bonus Plan document; calculation worksheet.
5. Monthly/Quarterly/Annual depending on plan.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Finance.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: safety bonus and MSHA enforcement: be careful that safety bonuses don't discourage injury reporting (an OSHA/MSHA concern); production bonus disputes by union.

### Garnishments
1. Court-ordered withholdings.
2. Payroll Administrator.
3. Order details, max %, priority order, remittance address.
4. Income Withholding Order (IWO) for child support; tax levy IRS Form 668-W; bankruptcy order.
5. Per garnishment.
6. Hands off to Remittance.
7. Garnishment limits federal (CCPA) plus state — WV/VA/KY follow federal max generally; KY child support follows IWO standard.
8. Edge cases: multiple competing orders; employee transfers states mid-order.

### Manual Checks
1. Off-cycle checks for terminations or bonus correction.
2. Payroll Administrator with HR Director approval.
3. Check number, reason, gross/net.
4. Manual Check Request.
5. Ad-hoc.
6. Hands off to Finance.
7. WV final-pay deadlines drive manual-check frequency (next regular payday or 72 hours, whichever first); VA next regular payday; KY next regular payday or 14 days, whichever is later.
8. Edge cases: termination right before payroll cutoff; final check + accrued vacation calculation error.

### Multi-State Withholding
1. Withholding for employees whose residence and work state differ.
2. Payroll Administrator.
3. Resident state, work state, reciprocity status, allocation %.
4. State W-4s; Multi-State Withholding Form.
5. On change.
6. Hands off to Payroll tax.
7. WV–KY no reciprocity; VA–KY reciprocity (employee files VA-4); WV–VA no reciprocity; WV–OH reciprocity but rarely relevant here.
8. Edge cases: employee works one shift in another state for emergency cover → withholding question; supervisor visits multiple state mines.

### Union Dues Deduction & Remittance
1. UMWA dues check-off and remittance to local/international.
2. Payroll Administrator; HR Director coordinates with local.
3. Dues per member per pay; assessments; PAC contributions where authorized.
4. Dues Check-Off Authorization (signed by member); monthly remittance report to UMWA.
5. Per pay period; monthly remittance.
6. Hands off to UMWA Local Treasurer.
7. UMWA-covered mines only. WV/VA/KY are right-to-work states (WV became RTW 2016; VA RTW longstanding; KY RTW 2017) — meaning dues check-off must be by individual written authorization.
8. Edge cases: revocation of check-off; mid-period union resignation; new hire who has not yet signed check-off but is union-eligible.

### Court-Ordered Withholdings, Charitable, 401(k) Loans
1. All voluntary and involuntary deductions beyond tax and garnishment.
2. Payroll Administrator.
3. Deduction type, amount, remittance schedule.
4. Various authorization forms.
5. Per pay period.
6. Hands off to recipients.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: 401(k) loan default on termination; charitable pledge revocation mid-year.

## Union / Labor Relations

### UMWA Collective Bargaining
1. Negotiation, ratification, and administration of collective bargaining agreements with UMWA local unions.
2. HR Director, VP Labor Relations (if dedicated), CEO involvement for major terms; outside labor counsel.
3. Wage scales by classification, benefit contributions, work rules, grievance procedure, no-strike/no-lockout, premium pay, shift bidding rules.
4. Local CBA document; memoranda of understanding (MOUs); letters of agreement.
5. Multi-year cycles (typically 3–5 years).
6. Hands off to all HR sub-functions, Operations, Finance (cost modeling), Mine Safety (work rules).
7. UMWA representation concentrated in WV/VA; less in KY (KY has historically been more non-union); minimal in AL/TN.
8. Edge cases: contract expiration without agreement → strike or contract extension; whipsaw bargaining across mines; non-union mine that becomes target of organizing campaign.

### NBCWA (National Bituminous Coal Wage Agreement)
1. Multi-employer agreement between BCOA (Bituminous Coal Operators Association) and UMWA covering union mines whose employer is a BCOA signatory or has agreed to NBCWA terms.
2. HR Director coordinates compliance; CFO models pension/benefit costs; Labor counsel.
3. Wage scale, premium pay, overtime rules, holidays, vacation, signatory hours for H&R Funds contributions, panel/seniority rules.
4. NBCWA document (most recent the 2025 ACNR Coal Wage Agreement and prior 2016/2021 versions); local supplements.
5. Multi-year, with wage reopeners.
6. Hands off to Payroll (contribution remittance to UMWA Health & Retirement Funds), Finance (MPPAA exposure modeling), Benefits.
7. Applies wherever the company is signatory regardless of state.
8. Edge cases: company exits BCOA but remains under NBCWA; merger of signatory and non-signatory operations; reopener disputes.

### Local Supplements
1. Mine-by-mine supplemental agreements on local issues (e.g., specific shift schedules, local seniority).
2. HR Director with mine HR and local union officers.
3. Local terms, effective dates, expiration.
4. Local Supplement document.
5. Per local cycle.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Operations.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: local agreement contradicts NBCWA national term; ratification failure at local.

### Seniority Lists & Panel Order
1. Master seniority by mine and craft; NBCWA "panel" of laid-off members with recall rights to other signatory mines.
2. HR Generalist; Union steward review.
3. Employee name, classification, mine seniority date, panel date, recall rights window.
4. Seniority List (posted); Panel Roster.
5. Posted quarterly/annually.
6. Hands off to Recruiting (panel members offered open jobs first), Layoff procedures.
7. NBCWA panel rules apply across signatory employers; per UMWA Panel Rights, panel members receive priority for jobs.
8. Edge cases: contested seniority date (date-of-hire vs date-of-classification); panel member refuses recall to distant mine — loses panel rights.

### Bidding Procedures
1. Internal job posting to union members per CBA; awarded by seniority and qualification.
2. HR Generalist posts; Superintendent verifies qualifications.
3. Posting date, bidders list, awarded employee, effective date.
4. Job Posting/Bid Form; Bid Award Notice.
5. Per open bargaining-unit position.
6. Hands off to Recruiting if no qualified bidder.
7. NBCWA Article on bidding for union mines.
8. Edge cases: bidder qualified-on-paper but not in practice → grievance; trial period failure on a bid award.

### Grievance Procedure
1. Multi-step dispute resolution: Step 1 (foreman), Step 2 (superintendent or designee), Step 3 (HR/Labor Relations), Arbitration.
2. Steward, Foreman, Superintendent, HR Director, Arbitrator.
3. Grievance number, date filed, contract article cited, facts, remedy requested, step decisions, dates of each step.
4. Grievance Form (per local); Step 2/3 written decisions; Arbitrator's Award.
5. Per grievance; arbitration scheduled.
6. Hands off to Legal/Outside Counsel for arbitration prep; Payroll for back-pay awards.
7. NBCWA grievance procedure standardized for signatories.
8. Edge cases: untimely filing waiver argument; group grievance vs individual; bypass grievance (alleged violation of senior employee bypassed for assignment).

### Arbitration Records
1. Tracker of pending and decided arbitrations.
2. HR Director; Labor counsel.
3. Arbitrator, hearing date, transcript cost, award, monetary exposure.
4. Demand for Arbitration; Submission Agreement; Award.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to Finance (reserve booking), Payroll (back-pay execution).
7. None.
8. Edge cases: precedential arbitration that affects multiple sites; vacatur litigation under FAA/LMRA §301.

### LMRA Section 8(a) Compliance
1. Avoidance of unfair labor practices — no interference with protected activity, no domination of labor org, no discrimination for union activity, no retaliation for filing charges, no refusal to bargain.
2. HR Director; Labor counsel; supervisor training.
3. Investigation of any 8(a) charge; supervisor incident notes.
4. NLRB Charge response; position statement; affidavits.
5. Continuous; per charge.
6. Hands off to NLRB Regional Office.
7. NLRB applies federally; right-to-work state status doesn't change 8(a) duties.
8. Edge cases: supervisor TIPS-violation (Threats/Interrogation/Promises/Surveillance) during organizing campaign; protected concerted activity by non-union employees.

### Just Cause Discipline Standards
1. Seven-test (Daugherty) or NBCWA's specific just-cause framework applied before discipline of bargaining-unit employees.
2. Supervisor with HR Director; Labor counsel for terminations.
3. Notice, investigation, evidence, proportionality, prior record, consistency, due process.
4. Disciplinary Action Form; Investigation File; Pre-Discipline Meeting Notes.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to Grievance (likely outcome).
7. NBCWA standards apply at signatory mines.
8. Edge cases: dishonesty supports termination without progressive discipline; off-duty conduct nexus to work; group misconduct selective discipline.

### Weingarten Rights
1. Union employee's right to representation in investigatory interview that could lead to discipline.
2. Supervisor/Investigator must offer; HR confirms.
3. Date, time, employee request for rep, rep present.
4. Investigation Notes; Weingarten Acknowledgement.
5. Per investigation.
6. Hands off to Discipline.
7. Federal NLRA right.
8. Edge cases: rep is also a witness; rep refused by employer (illegal); non-union employee invokes — generally no Weingarten right post-2004 NLRB reversal.

### Layoff Procedures (LIFO by Seniority)
1. Reduction-in-force following NBCWA seniority rules (typically last-in, first-out within classification at mine).
2. HR Director with Superintendent; Steward consultation.
3. Layoff list, dates, classifications affected, panel placement.
4. Layoff Notice; WARN Notice if applicable; Panel addition.
5. Per RIF event.
6. Hands off to Payroll (final pay, severance if any), Benefits (COBRA), Unemployment (UI response).
7. UMWA-covered LIFO. Non-union: at-will but documented selection criteria.
8. Edge cases: super-seniority for stewards; bumping rights across mines; reverse-bumping into preferred shift.

### Recall Lists
1. Panel of laid-off employees with recall rights for set period.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Name, panel date, contact info, refusals.
4. Recall Notice (certified mail); Panel List.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Recruiting (recalled before external hire), Benefits (recall reinstates benefits per NBCWA).
7. Recall period per NBCWA; non-union per policy.
8. Edge cases: recalled employee can't be reached (lost contact); recall to different mine — refusal handling.

### Plant Closure / WARN Act Compliance
1. 60-day advance written notice of plant closing or mass layoff under federal WARN (29 USC §2101); state mini-WARN if any.
2. HR Director; CFO; Legal; CEO; State Dislocated Worker Unit.
3. Affected sites, employee counts, expected separation dates, bumping rights, contact for each state's dislocated worker unit.
4. WARN Notice letters (to employees/union, state DWU, chief elected official of local government); 90-day look-back analysis.
5. Per closure event.
6. Hands off to Payroll (pay-in-lieu if applicable), Unemployment, UMWA Panel.
7. WV: state Dislocated Worker Unit at WorkForce WV. VA: VA Employment Commission Rapid Response. KY: Kentucky Career Center Rapid Response. No state mini-WARN in WV/VA/KY currently — federal WARN governs. Mining-specific complication: "closure" can be a long idle vs permanent — triggers WARN if 6+ months idle.
8. Edge cases: "temporary" idling stretches past 6 months → triggers WARN retroactively (e.g., Mettiki Coal investigation 2026); unforeseeable business circumstances or natural disaster (mine fire/flood) exception; faltering company exception (closures only); the 50/100/500 employee thresholds at a single site.

### MPPAA Withdrawal Liability
1. Multi-employer pension plan withdrawal liability exposure under ERISA Title IV / MPPAA (1980) — for UMWA H&R signatory employers, the UMWA 1974 Pension Plan, plus Combined Fund, 1992 Plan, 1993 Plan obligations.
2. CFO with Outside actuary and ERISA counsel; HR Director provides headcount/contribution data.
3. Allocable share of unfunded vested benefits; total potential withdrawal liability; assessment by plan trustees; payment schedule.
4. Estimate Letter from Plan; Notice of Withdrawal Liability; demand for payment; arbitration demand under MPPAA §4221.
5. Estimate annually; full assessment on withdrawal.
6. Hands off to Finance (contingent liability disclosure under ASC 450), Legal (arbitration), CEO/Board.
7. Plan-specific, not state-specific.
8. Edge cases: complete vs partial withdrawal; sale-of-assets exception (ERISA §4204); construction industry exception (does not apply to coal); successor liability; "evade or avoid" liability under §4212(c); 20-year cap on payments; mass withdrawal triggers higher liability.

### Sister Local Coordination
1. Cross-local coordination among UMWA locals at affiliated mines.
2. HR Director; Local presidents.
3. Joint issues, cross-mine transfers.
4. Joint meeting minutes.
5. As-needed.
6. Hands off to Operations.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: a strike at one local affecting others; differing local enforcement of national terms.

## Benefits

### Health Insurance (Medical/Dental/Vision)
1. Group health plans for active employees and dependents.
2. Benefits Coordinator with Broker; carriers.
3. Plan, tier, dependents, EOBs (carrier-side), enrollment changes.
4. SPD, SBC, plan documents, Section 125 plan doc, enrollment forms.
5. Annual renewal; continuous administration.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Carriers, COBRA admin.
7. Network adequacy varies — WV/VA/KY rural areas have thin specialist networks; consider PPO over HMO/EPO; mental health/substance use parity (MHPAEA) compliance.
8. Edge cases: domestic partner taxation; ACA affordability/MEC for variable-hour employees; gag-clause attestation annually.

### Plan Design (HDHP/HSA, PPO, EPO)
1. Plan menu and design.
2. Benefits Coordinator with Broker; HR Director.
3. Premium, deductible, OOP max, network, formulary.
4. Plan design comparison; SBC.
5. Annual.
6. Hands off to Employees (enrollment).
7. None.
8. Edge cases: HSA eligibility lost if dependent on FSA; embedded vs aggregate family deductible.

### COBRA Administration
1. Continuation of coverage post-qualifying event.
2. COBRA TPA or Benefits Coordinator.
3. QE date, notice date, election date, premium payments, termination date.
4. General COBRA Notice (at enrollment); Specific QE Notice (within 44 days); Election Form; Premium coupons.
5. Per QE.
6. Hands off to Carrier (eligibility), TPA (collection).
7. WV mini-COBRA for groups <20; VA Continuation; KY very limited mini-COBRA — federal COBRA applies to 20+ FTE plans regardless.
8. Edge cases: divorce QE not reported timely; second QE extension to 36 months; disability extension to 29 months.

### HSA / FSA / DCFSA
1. Tax-advantaged accounts.
2. Benefits Coordinator; Section 125 administrator.
3. Annual elections, contributions, balances, qualified expenses.
4. Section 125 plan document; HSA bank custodial agreement; substantiation receipts for FSA.
5. Per pay period.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Custodian/TPA.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: over-contribution to HSA; mid-year HDHP change affecting HSA eligibility; FSA forfeiture vs $640 carryover (2024 limit; verify current year); ICHRA alternatives.

### Wellness Program
1. Voluntary wellness with biometric screenings, coaching, premium discount incentives.
2. Wellness Coordinator (often dual-role with safety nurse); Benefits.
3. Participation, biometric data (kept by vendor, not employer), incentives earned.

6. Hands off to Carrier (premium adjustments), Payroll.

### EAP

### Life Insurance (Basic / Voluntary / Dependent)

### AD&D, STD, LTD
1. Accident & dismemberment; short-term disability; long-term disability.

4. Plan docs; STD/LTD claim forms; physician APS.
5. Per claim.
6. Hands off to Carrier, FMLA, Workers Comp coordinator.
7. WV/VA/KY have no state disability insurance program (unlike NY/NJ/CA); private STD/LTD only.

### 401(k) Administration
1. Defined-contribution retirement plan.

### Pension (Legacy DB)
1. Frozen or active defined-benefit plan if any legacy exists.
2. Benefits Coordinator; Actuary; Plan trustees.
3. Accrued benefits, eligibility, payment options.
4. DB plan document; SPD; pension benefit statements; AFTAP certifications.
5. Annual valuation; per retirement.
6. Hands off to Actuary, PBGC if covered.

### UMWA Health & Retirement Funds
1. Multi-employer UMWA Funds — Combined Fund, 1992 Plan, 1993 Plan (retiree health), 1974 Pension Plan (now-merged into Steelworkers Pension Trust for some plans; the 1974 Pension Plan was rescued via the American Rescue Plan Act / Special Financial Assistance), 2012 Pension Plan.
2. HR Director coordinates remittance; CFO models exposure; Plan trustees administer.
3. Signatory hours per employee per pay period; contribution rates per NBCWA; eligibility-credit hours.
4. Monthly contribution report per Fund; remittance check or ACH; eligibility verification for retirees and dependents.
5. Monthly remittance.
6. Hands off to Funds, Finance.
7. UMWA Funds participation drives WV/VA/KY/PA mines; non-UMWA mines unaffected.
8. Edge cases: misreported hours; retiree dies and dependent eligibility; surviving spouse coverage; orphan retirees from a failed signatory; SFA-recipient plan rules.

### Retiree Medical (OPEB)
1. Employer-sponsored retiree health for non-UMWA retirees, or supplemental for UMWA.
2. Benefits Coordinator; Actuary; CFO.
3. Eligible retirees, coverage, employer share, OPEB liability under GASB/FASB.
4. Plan documents; Medicare-eligible Part D coverage notice (creditable); Section 162(l) for >2% S-corp shareholders if applicable.
5. Annual OPEB valuation.
6. Hands off to Finance (OPEB liability disclosure), Carriers.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: pre-65 vs Medicare-eligible plan switching; spouse coverage outliving retiree; carving down benefits and Yard-Man (now overruled in M&G Polymers v. Tackett) presumption.

### Vacation / PTO Accrual
1. Accrual tier by service.
2. HR Generalist; Payroll.
3. Accrual rate, balance, used, carryover, cap.
4. Vacation/PTO policy; NBCWA vacation provisions for union.
5. Per pay period.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Final Pay (vacation payout per state and policy).
7. WV: vacation is "wages" under WPCA if earned per policy — must pay out at separation if policy provides. VA: vacation/PTO is a fringe benefit — payout only if policy says so. KY: no payout requirement absent policy.
8. Edge cases: use-it-or-lose-it (allowed in VA/KY if policy clear; WV courts skeptical if earned); negative balances at termination.

### Sick / Personal Days
1. Paid time for illness or personal reasons.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Accrual, used.
4. Sick leave policy; FMLA coordination.
5. Per pay period.
6. Hands off to FMLA tracker.
7. WV/VA/KY have no statewide private-sector paid sick leave mandate.
8. Edge cases: sick leave coordinating with intermittent FMLA; pattern abuse (Mondays/Fridays).

### Bereavement, Jury Duty, Military Leave
1. Paid/unpaid leaves for specific events.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Leave dates, relationship (bereavement), summons (jury), military orders (USERRA).
4. Bereavement Policy; Jury Duty Policy; Military Leave Policy; USERRA notice (DOL "Your Rights Under USERRA" poster).
5. Per event.
6. Hands off to Payroll.
7. WV/VA/KY all protect jury duty; VA jury duty requires unpaid leave but no retaliation. USERRA is federal.
8. Edge cases: USERRA reinstatement after long deployment with benefit accrual; jury duty extended beyond paid days.

### FMLA Administration
1. Federal Family and Medical Leave Act — up to 12 weeks unpaid job-protected leave, 26 weeks military caregiver.
2. Benefits Coordinator or dedicated FMLA admin (often TPA).
3. Eligibility (12 months service, 1,250 hours, 50 within 75 miles), certification of serious health condition, intermittent tracking.
4. WH-381 (eligibility/rights notice), WH-382 (designation), WH-380-E (employee HC cert), WH-380-F (family member HC cert), WH-384 (military qualifying exigency), WH-385 (military caregiver).
5. Per event; intermittent ongoing.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Benefits (continuation of coverage at employee-rate), Operations.
7. WV/VA/KY no state FMLA mini-act; federal FMLA only. VA has state contractor pregnancy accommodation; PWFA federal applies 15+.
8. Edge cases: intermittent FMLA abuse (always Friday-Monday); recertification at start of leave year; failure to return → COBRA event; second/third opinion at employer cost.

### State Family Leave
1. None mandated in WV/VA/KY at present (no state PFML akin to CA/NY/NJ).
2. N/A.
3. N/A.
4. N/A.
5. N/A.
6. N/A.
7. As above — verify if any 2026 enactments; WV/VA/KY private-sector employers should monitor.
8. Edge cases: federal contractor paid sick leave (EO 13706) for federal contracts.

### Workers Compensation Interface
1. Coordination between WC indemnity payments and HR pay/leave.
2. HR Generalist; WC Coordinator; TPA.
3. Lost-time start, indemnity rate, return-to-work date.
4. State WC forms (see Workers Comp section).
5. Per claim.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Benefits, FMLA tracker (runs concurrent generally).
7. Per state.
8. Edge cases: WC offset against STD; FMLA running concurrent; ADA after MMI.

### Black Lung Benefits
1. Federal Black Lung Benefits Act (BLBA) compensation, administered by DOL OWCP Division of Coal Mine Workers' Compensation; coal operator liability for claims by miners last employed by the operator.
2. HR Director coordinates with OWCP and outside counsel; CFO models reserve; Mine Safety provides employment-history confirmation; Risk Manager for insurance.
3. Notice of Claim, employment history of claimant, medical evidence, "responsible operator" determination, payment schedule if liable.
4. CM-1093 Notice of Claim; LS-208 Notice of Final Payment of Compensation; DOL Form CM-911 (Operator Response); evidence per 20 CFR Part 718, 725, 726.
5. Per claim; ongoing for paying claims.
6. Hands off to Finance (reserves), Insurance (BLBA carrier), Legal, Mine Safety (NIOSH surveillance program for active miners).
7. Federal; applies to all coal operators wherever operating. Self-insurance authorization or BLBA insurance carrier; 20 CFR Part 726 sets self-insurance requirements (DOL approval, security/bond).
8. Edge cases: "last responsible operator" disputes between successive employers; survivor claims after miner death; surviving spouse remarriage (no longer disqualifying post-2010 PPACA Section 1556); 30-day operator response window; final rule 2024 adjustments.

### Section 125 Cafeteria Plan
1. Pre-tax elections under Section 125.
2. Benefits Coordinator; TPA.
3. Elections, mid-year change events.
4. Section 125 plan document; election forms; non-discrimination testing.
5. Annual.
6. Hands off to Payroll.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: failed NDT requiring HCE refund; mid-year election change rules.

## Drug & Alcohol Testing Program

### Pre-Employment Testing
1. Mandatory pre-employment screen.
2. Recruiter; Collection site; MRO.
3. Specimen, result.
4. Federal CCF; MRO verification.
5. Per hire.
6. Hands off to Offer/Onboarding.
7. WV mining mandatory under §22A-1A; VA/KY per policy.
8. Edge cases: see Pre-Employment Screening.

### Random Testing (DOT-Style Driver Pools)
1. Computer-randomized selection from defined pool.
2. D&A Coordinator; Collection vendor.
3. Pool list, selections per quarter, completion rate.
4. Random Selection Report; CCF.
5. Quarterly at minimum.
6. Hands off to MRO.
7. WV coal: random required at rates set by Office of Miners' Health, Safety and Training. DOT drivers under 49 CFR Part 382 separately.
8. Edge cases: employee out on leave when selected → tested on return; dual DOT/non-DOT pools; selection of safety-sensitive positions.

### Post-Accident Testing
1. Mandatory after accidents meeting trigger criteria.
2. D&A Coordinator with Safety; Mine Safety often triggers per MSHA accident.
3. Trigger event, time-to-test, result.
4. Post-Accident Authorization; CCF.
5. Per incident.
6. Hands off to MRO, MSHA accident investigation.
7. WV mandatory; DOT drivers per 49 CFR Part 382; OSHA's post-accident testing limits don't apply to mining (which is MSHA-regulated).
8. Edge cases: test impossible due to medical emergency; refusal at hospital.

### Reasonable Suspicion Testing
1. Test based on observed signs.
2. Trained supervisor observes; second supervisor confirms; D&A Coordinator authorizes.
3. Observation form, witness sign-off, test result.
4. Reasonable Suspicion Observation Form; Supervisor training certificate; CCF.
5. As warranted.
6. Hands off to MRO.
7. WV requires supervisor training under §22A-1A.
8. Edge cases: medical condition mimicking impairment; subjective single-supervisor call → vulnerable to grievance.

### Return-to-Duty & Follow-Up Testing
1. After positive result and SAP-cleared return.
2. D&A Coordinator with SAP; MRO.
3. SAP recommendations, RTD test, follow-up schedule (minimum 6 tests in 12 months for DOT).
4. SAP Evaluation; RTD CCF; follow-up schedule.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to MRO.
7. DOT under 49 CFR Part 40 Subpart O; WV mining mirror.
8. Edge cases: employee fails to complete SAP plan; second positive during follow-up = termination.

### Test Administration
1. Vendors — collection sites, lab (SAMHSA-certified), MRO.
2. D&A Coordinator manages vendor.
3. Vendor contracts, lab certifications.
4. Vendor agreements; lab cert.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to all testing functions.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: split-specimen retest; chain-of-custody break.

### Result Handling & Confidentiality
1. Confidential routing of results.
2. D&A Coordinator; MRO; HR Director.
3. Results stored separately from personnel file (medical file).
4. Confidential result log.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to HR (consequence), Legal if challenged.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: inadvertent disclosure; subpoena.

### Refusal / Dilute / Positive Handling
1. Defined consequences.
2. D&A Coordinator with HR Director.
3. Result type, consequence applied.
4. Consequence matrix.
5. Per result.
6. Hands off to Discipline.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: shy bladder protocol; substituted/adulterated specimen = refusal.

### State Medical Marijuana Considerations
1. Policy on positive THC for cardholders.
2. HR Director with Legal.
3. Cardholder disclosure (voluntary), accommodation requests.
4. Policy statement; denial-of-accommodation documentation if invoked.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Legal.
7. WV: medical program; mining safety-sensitive carve-out — positive THC still disqualifying. VA: medical cannabis broader; safety-sensitive carve-out generally applies. KY: limited medical (HB 829 effective 2025); narrow. None of these states force accommodation for safety-sensitive mining roles.
8. Edge cases: off-duty THC use with medical card and a positive test — termination defensible but document carefully; ADA underlying-condition accommodation separate from drug testing.

## Absence / Leave Management

### FMLA Tracking
See Benefits → FMLA Administration.

### ADA Accommodations
1. Interactive process for qualified disabled employees.
2. HR Director or ADA Coordinator with Manager; Safety nurse.
3. Request, condition documentation (medical), interactive process notes, accommodation provided or undue hardship denial.
4. ADA Accommodation Request Form; physician APS; interactive process log; written accommodation grant or denial.
5. Per request.
6. Hands off to Operations; Workers Comp coordinator if injury-related.
7. ADA federal; WV/VA/KY mirror via state human rights acts.
8. Edge cases: indefinite leave generally not reasonable accommodation; essential-function analysis for safety-sensitive roles; reassignment to vacant position.

### Pregnancy Accommodations (PWFA)
1. Federal PWFA reasonable accommodation for known limitations related to pregnancy/childbirth.
2. HR Director.
3. Request, limitation, accommodation.
4. PWFA accommodation request; interactive process notes.
5. Per request.
6. Hands off to Operations.
7. PWFA federal (15+ EE). WV state PWFA (12+ EE since 2014). VA Pregnant Workers Fairness Act expanded 2020 (5+ EE). KY Pregnant Workers Act (2019, 15+ EE). All require reasonable accommodation absent undue hardship.
8. Edge cases: temporary light duty for pregnancy when not provided for other reasons; lactation accommodation under PUMP Act.

### Military Leave (USERRA)
1. Job protection and reemployment after military service up to 5 years cumulative.
2. HR Director; Benefits.
3. Orders, leave dates, reemployment date, escalator position.
4. Notice of military service; orders; reemployment request within statutory window.
5. Per event.
6. Hands off to Payroll, Benefits (continuation rules), Pension (service credit).
7. USERRA federal; some states add (none extra in WV/VA/KY).
8. Edge cases: reemployment to escalator position with promotions employee would have had; continued benefits during leave (up to 24 months); state National Guard activation.

### Jury Duty
1. Time off for jury service.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Summons date, service days.
4. Jury Duty Policy; summons copy.
5. Per event.
6. Hands off to Payroll.
7. WV/VA/KY all prohibit retaliation for jury service; payment policies vary by employer.
8. Edge cases: lengthy trial; grand jury.

### Workers Comp Leave Coordination
See Workers Compensation section.

### LTD Transition & Unpaid Personal Leave
1. Transition from short-term to long-term disability; discretionary unpaid leave.
2. Benefits Coordinator; HR Director.
3. Leave dates, return date.
4. LTD claim, leave request, benefits continuation letter.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to Carrier, Benefits.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: LTD denied while STD ended; failure to return at end of approved unpaid leave.

## Workers Compensation

### Claim Intake (First Report of Injury)
1. Initial reporting of work injury or illness.
2. Foreman/Supervisor reports; HR or Safety Coordinator files with carrier/TPA; coordinates with Mine Safety on MSHA-reportable accidents (separate workflow).
3. Date/time, location, body part, mechanism, witnesses, treatment, return-to-work plan.
4. WV: OIC-WC-1 (Employees' & Physicians' Report) and OIC-WC-2 (Employers' Report of Occupational Injury or Disease) — file within 5 days of notice. VA: First Report of Injury (FROI) electronic — must be reported to insurer/Commission within 10 days. KY: Form IA-1 Employer's First Report of Injury or Illness — must be filed with insurer within 3 days of notice; Form 101 is the employee's later Application for Resolution of Injury Claim filed within 2 years of injury.
5. Per injury.
6. Hands off to Carrier/TPA, Mine Safety (if MSHA-reportable), OSHA 300 log (if recordable).
7. WV: deregulated 2008 — private carrier or self-insured market; BrickStreet was the dominant successor. VA: Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission; private market. KY: Kentucky Department of Workers' Claims; private market plus state-administered coal workers' fund; Form 102-CWP for pneumoconiosis.
8. Edge cases: delayed reporting (employee waited weeks); aggravation of pre-existing; cumulative trauma; PTSD from incident.

### Self-Insured WC Programs
1. Large coal employers often self-insure with TPA administering claims.
2. Risk Manager; TPA; HR.
3. Claim reserves, loss runs, IBNR estimate.
4. Self-insurance authorization (per state); annual security/bond filings; loss-development triangle.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Finance (reserves), CFO.
7. WV self-insurance approval by Insurance Commissioner. VA by VWCC. KY by DWC.
8. Edge cases: catastrophic claim exceeds excess insurance retention; runoff of claims after exiting self-insurance.

### TPA Coordination
1. Third-party administrator manages claims, payments, vendor mgmt.
2. Risk Manager; HR Generalist.
3. Claim notes, payments, reserves.
4. TPA service agreement; claim files.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Carrier (if applicable), Legal.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: TPA missed deadline; reserve adequacy disputes.

### Light-Duty / Return-to-Work Program
1. Modified-duty offer to limit lost-time and TTD exposure.
2. HR/Safety nurse with Foreman.
3. Offer date, restrictions, accepted/refused.
4. Modified Duty Job Offer Letter; physician restrictions; modified job description.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to TPA (TTD termination if accepted).
7. Refusal of a bona fide modified duty offer can terminate TTD in WV/VA/KY.
8. Edge cases: physician unwilling to release; modified duty disliked, employee finds new restriction.

### Modified-Duty Job Bank
1. Inventory of jobs available for restricted employees.
2. HR with Site Safety.
3. Job list, restrictions accommodated.
4. Job Bank document.
5. Maintained continuously.
6. Hands off to RTW program.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: union grievance over bargaining-unit work performed by restricted-duty employee.

### Medical Case Management
1. Nurse case manager (employer-side) coordinates care.
2. NCM (vendor); HR coordinates.
3. Treatment plan, appointments, progress.
4. NCM reports; physician notes.
5. Per claim.
6. Hands off to TPA, Physician.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: claimant attorney objects to NCM at appointments; over/under-treatment concerns.

### IME Coordination
1. Independent Medical Examination to resolve disputed medical questions.
2. TPA/Legal schedules; HR coordinates.
3. IME report.
4. IME notice; report.
5. Per dispute.
6. Hands off to Litigation.
7. State rules on IME (number per year, choice of physician panel) vary.
8. Edge cases: employee refusal to attend; "doctor shopping" allegations.

### Subrogation
1. Recovery from third party at fault.
2. Legal; TPA.
3. Third-party claim, recovery.
4. Subrogation file.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to TPA reimbursement.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: contractor injury — subrogation against equipment manufacturer.

### Litigation Management
1. Defense of contested claims.
2. Legal; outside defense counsel.
3. Case status, exposure estimate.
4. Pleadings; orders.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to TPA, Finance.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: bad faith claim against insurer; deliberate-intent claim under WV §23-4-2 (only state with statutory deliberate intent exception to exclusive remedy).

### Permanent Partial / Permanent Total Ratings
1. Impairment ratings and award.
2. Physician; State Commission; defense counsel.
3. Body part, % impairment, schedule weeks.
4. PPI award; AMA Guides rating.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to TPA payments.
7. State PPI schedules differ; WV uses AMA Guides 4th Edition still; VA uses 6th Edition typically; KY uses AMA Guides 5th Edition for injuries before specified date.
8. Edge cases: pre-existing condition apportionment; psychological overlay.

### Settlement (Compromise & Release)
1. Final lump-sum settlement closing claim.
2. Legal; Risk Manager; TPA.
3. Settlement amount, terms, release scope, Medicare Set-Aside if applicable.
4. C&R agreement; MSA report; CMS approval if required.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to Payroll if wages portion; Finance.
7. WV: C&R must be approved. VA: settlement approved by Commission. KY: agreed Form 110 with Board approval.
8. Edge cases: MSA for Medicare-eligible claimants; resignation as condition of settlement; reopening rights waived.

### Reserves & Case Management
1. Setting and adjusting reserves on each claim.
2. TPA; Risk Manager reviews.
3. Indemnity, medical, expense reserves; updates.
4. Reserve worksheet.
5. Monthly review.
6. Hands off to Finance (loss accruals).
7. None.
8. Edge cases: stair-stepped reserves on serious claim; reserves redacted from settlement discussions.

### OSHA 300 / 300A / 301 Logs
1. Federal recordkeeping for non-mining establishments (Coal mines are MSHA, not OSHA — but office, lab, and prep plant operations may be OSHA-jurisdiction); MSHA logs handled by Mine Safety. OSHA 300 is for OSHA-covered locations; surface operations vary.
2. HR/Safety Coordinator.
3. Recordable injuries/illnesses, days away/restricted, body part, event.
4. OSHA Form 300, 300A (annual summary), 301 (incident detail).
5. Continuous; 300A posted Feb 1 – Apr 30 each year; electronic submission for establishments >250 EE by March 2 to OSHA ITA.
6. Hands off to OSHA reporting, Mine Safety (parallel MSHA records).
7. None.
8. Edge cases: jurisdictional question (MSHA vs OSHA at prep plant/processing); restricted-duty vs lost-time classification.

### Black Lung Claims Workflow (BLBA)
See Benefits → Black Lung Benefits.

## Contractor / Vendor Workforce

### Pre-Qualification
1. Vetting contractors before site access.
2. Procurement; Risk Manager; HR (for D&A and training docs); Safety.
3. Insurance limits, EMR, OSHA/MSHA citation history, financials, DBE/MBE status if relevant.
4. Pre-qualification questionnaire (ISN/Avetta/Veriforce commonly); MSHA Mine Data Retrieval System screen.
5. Annual recert.
6. Hands off to Master Service Agreement, Site Access.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: contractor with citation history at prior mine; subcontractor of contractor — flow-down expectations.

### Master Service Agreement
1. Standard contract.
2. Procurement; Legal; Risk.
3. Indemnification, insurance, scope, term, pricing.
4. MSA template.
5. Per contractor.
6. Hands off to Risk (COI), Legal.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: insurance carve-outs; MSHA-required additional insured endorsements.

### Insurance Verification (COI)
1. Certificate-of-Insurance tracking.
2. Risk Manager; Procurement.
3. Carrier, limits, expiration, additional insured, waiver of subrogation, primary/non-contributory.
4. ACORD 25 COI; endorsements.
5. Annual; renewal alerts.
6. Hands off to Site Access.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: COI not actually backing endorsement language; lapsed renewal.

### Indemnification Provisions
1. Risk-shifting language.
2. Legal; Risk.
3. Indemnity scope.
4. MSA section.
5. Per contract.
6. Hands off to Litigation if invoked.
7. State anti-indemnity statutes vary; KY has limited; WV/VA generally enforce.
8. Edge cases: enforceability against sole-negligence indemnity; mutual indemnity vs one-way.

### Site-Specific Training & Sign-In
1. Contractor employees must complete site orientation, sign in daily, follow PPE rules.
2. Mine Clerk; Site Safety.
3. Contractor name, employees on site, hours, scope.
4. Sign-in log; visitor/contractor badge; site orientation acknowledgement.
5. Per visit/shift.
6. Hands off to Mine Safety (MSHA Part 46/48 verification for contractors).
7. None.
8. Edge cases: contractor employee without current MSHA training; sub-tier worker not on roster.

### Drug Test Verification (Contractors)
1. Confirming contractor employees meet D&A program standards.
2. Risk; Procurement; Contractor.
3. Contractor's drug-test policy and recent test verification.
4. ISN/Avetta record; contractor letter.
5. Annual.
6. Hands off to Site Access.
7. WV mining requires drug-free workplace for all on-site personnel.
8. Edge cases: contractor uses different panel; positive that contractor concealed.

### MSHA Part 46/48 Training Verification
1. Confirmation contractor employees have current MSHA training before site access.
2. Mine Safety primary; HR coordinates with contractor HR.
3. 5000-23 training records.
4. MSHA Form 5000-23 (handed off — Mine Safety domain).
5. Per access.
6. Hands off to Mine Safety.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: stale 5000-23; refresher overdue.

### Background Check Verification
1. Background screening of contractor personnel (some sites require).
2. Risk; Contractor.
3. Background completion confirmation.
4. Attestation letter.
5. Per personnel.
6. Hands off to Site Access.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: criminal record concealed.

### Scope of Work
1. Defining and tracking scope.
2. Project Manager; Procurement.
3. Scope, deliverables, milestones.
4. SOW; change orders.
5. Per project.
6. Hands off to AP for payment.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: scope creep without change order; out-of-scope safety issues.

### Performance Evaluation
1. Contractor performance scoring.
2. Project Manager; Procurement.
3. Scores on safety, quality, schedule, cost.
4. Vendor scorecard.
5. Per project/annual.
6. Hands off to Pre-qualification renewal.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: subjective scoring; contractor disputing.

### Issue Tracking & Offboarding
1. Issue log; offboarding when complete.
2. Project Manager; Procurement; HR coordinates badge deactivation.
3. Issues, resolutions; final invoice, badge return.
4. Issue log; off-boarding checklist.
5. Continuous; at project end.
6. Hands off to AP, IT.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: open warranty issues after off-boarding; final payment held for safety violations.

## Equal Opportunity / EEO / Diversity

### EEO-1 Filing
1. Federal EEO-1 Component 1 report.
2. HR Director; EEO Coordinator.
3. Workforce by race/ethnicity/gender × EEO-1 job category × establishment.
4. EEOC EEO-1 portal; snapshot pay period in Q4.
5. Annual (typically due Q1).
6. Hands off to EEOC.
7. Required for private employers with 100+ employees and federal contractors with 50+ on $50K+ contract. Southern Coal at 300-1200 EE likely required.
8. Edge cases: establishment definition (mines may each be establishments); affirmative action plan (only if federal contractor).

### VETS-4212
1. Annual veteran reporting for federal contractors at $150K+.
2. HR Director.
3. Workforce by protected veteran category × job group × establishment.
4. VETS-4212 portal (DOL/VETS).
5. Annual (by September 30).
6. Hands off to DOL VETS.
7. Only if federal contractor. Most coal companies are not federal contractors unless they sell to federal facilities.
8. Edge cases: contractor threshold determination; reservist hiring tracking.

### OFCCP Compliance (If Federal Contractor)
1. Affirmative action plans for veterans (VEVRAA) and individuals with disabilities (Section 503); race/gender AAP if applicable.
2. HR Director; outside AAP consultant.
3. Availability analysis, placement goals, hiring/promotion/termination data.
4. AAP narrative; Itemized Listing data; outreach log.
5. Annual.
6. Hands off to OFCCP if audited.
7. Only if federal contractor. Class scheduling letter / desk audit response.
8. Edge cases: audit selection; pay equity findings; outreach effectiveness review.

### Workforce Diversity Reporting & Pay Equity
1. Internal diversity metrics and pay equity analysis.
2. HR Director; Comp Analyst; outside counsel for privileged analyses.
3. Composition, hiring, promotion, attrition, pay gaps.
4. Diversity dashboard; pay equity report (often under privilege).
5. Annual or semi-annual.
6. Hands off to Leadership.
7. State pay transparency laws emerging — VA pay range disclosure proposals; WV/KY no requirements as of 2026.
8. Edge cases: small N at mines; unintended adverse impact; remediation increases for pay disparities.

### Title VII / ADA / ADEA / GINA Compliance
1. Federal anti-discrimination compliance.
2. HR Director; Legal.
3. Charges, investigations, training.
4. Policies; complaint investigation files.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to EEOC, State human rights agencies.
7. WV Human Rights Act covers 12+ EE (broader than federal); VA Human Rights Act covers 5+ for some claims; KY Civil Rights Act covers 8+ EE.
8. Edge cases: state law lower employee threshold makes more claims viable; GINA family medical history in wellness questionnaires.

### Sexual Harassment Training
1. Mandatory or voluntary training on harassment prevention.
2. HR; outside training vendor.
3. Completion records.
4. Training materials; sign-in.
5. Annual recommended.
6. Hands off to Personnel records.
7. WV/VA/KY do not mandate sexual harassment training for private employers (unlike CA, NY, IL).
8. Edge cases: supervisor liability; bystander training.

### Complaint Intake / Investigation
1. Receiving and investigating complaints.
2. HR Director; outside investigator if conflict.
3. Allegations, witnesses, evidence, findings, action.
4. Investigation Plan; Witness Statement template; Investigation Report.
5. Per complaint.
6. Hands off to Discipline, Legal.
7. State retaliation protections vary.
8. Edge cases: anonymous complaints; complainant requests confidentiality but witness needed; supervisor as alleged harasser.

### EEOC Charges
1. Response to EEOC and state agency charges.
2. HR Director; outside counsel.
3. Charge specifics, position statement, document production.
4. Notice of Charge; position statement; mediation offer.
5. Per charge.
6. Hands off to EEOC, Legal.
7. WV Human Rights Commission; VA Office of Civil Rights at Office of Attorney General; KY Commission on Human Rights — worksharing agreements with EEOC.
8. Edge cases: pattern-and-practice expansion; conciliation vs litigation.

### Internal Complaint Hotline
1. Anonymous/non-anonymous reporting channel.
2. HR Director with third-party hotline vendor.
3. Reports, intake records, triage decisions.
4. Hotline vendor reports.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Investigation, Compliance.
7. None.

### Investigation Workflow
1. Structured investigation steps.
2. HR Investigator or outside.
3. Allegations, interviews, evidence, findings.
4. Investigation Plan; Report.
5. Per case.
6. Hands off to Discipline, Legal.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: privilege (attorney-client) management; investigator bias claims.

### Witness Statements
1. Documented witness accounts.
2. Investigator.
3. Statement, signature.
4. Witness Statement form.
5. Per witness.
6. Hands off to Investigation file.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: union witness invoking Weingarten; witness intimidation allegations.

### Outcome Documentation
1. Findings memorialized.
2. Investigator; HR Director.
3. Findings, basis.
4. Investigation Report.
5. Per investigation.
6. Hands off to Discipline.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: inconclusive findings; outcome later challenged.

### Disciplinary Action Records
1. Maintenance of discipline files.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Records.
4. Disciplinary forms.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Personnel File.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: NBCWA may limit how long discipline stays "active" for future progressive purposes.

### Wrongful Termination Defense File
1. Building defensible file for terminations.
2. HR Director with Legal.
3. Documentation supporting just cause or legitimate reason.
4. Defense file.
5. Per termination.
6. Hands off to Legal.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: gaps in documentation; comparable treatment of similarly-situated employees.

### Reference Response Policy
1. Standard "name/rank/serial number" reference policy.
2. HR Director only authorized to respond.
3. Requests, responses.
4. Reference Response Policy; release form for fuller reference.
5. Per request.
6. Hands off to none.
7. State qualified privilege for good-faith references in WV/VA/KY.
8. Edge cases: detailed reference at employee's written request; defamation claim from former employee.

5. Per term.

4. Cert tracker.

## Personnel Records / File Management

### Active Employee Files
1. Active personnel files.
2. HR Generalist.
3. All HR documents.
4. File contents per checklist.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Termination archive.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: incomplete files for legacy hires.

### Terminated Employee Files
1. Retained per retention schedule.
2. HR Generalist.
3. Last role, separation, retention until date.
4. Termination File.
5. Continuous archive.
6. Hands off to Destruction at retention end.
7. State retention varies; common practice 7 years post-termination; payroll records 4 years (FUTA), I-9 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination (whichever later), OSHA 300 5 years, MSHA-related records longer (handed to Mine Safety), benefits records 6 years (ERISA), workers comp records typically 10 years post-claim closure.
8. Edge cases: pending litigation extends retention indefinitely (legal hold).

### Medical Files (Separate)
1. Medical info segregated from personnel file per ADA/HIPAA.
2. HR Director or Benefits.
3. Medical, FMLA certs, ADA, workers comp medical.
4. Medical file.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to limited access.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: medical doc accidentally in personnel file.

### I-9 Files (Separate)
1. I-9s stored separately.
2. HR Generalist.
3. I-9 docs.
4. I-9 binder; E-Verify case file.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to ICE if audited.
7. Federal.
8. Edge cases: ICE audit; missing I-9s.

### Drug Test Records
1. D&A program records.
2. D&A Coordinator.
3. Test records.
4. CCFs, MRO reports.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to legal/audit.
7. DOT records retained per 49 CFR Part 382: negatives 1 year; positives 5 years; random selection records 2 years; supervisor training records 2 years from end of employment. WV mining program: typically 5 years.
8. Edge cases: subpoena; ex-employee request.

### Investigation Files
1. Investigation records — kept privileged where possible.
2. HR Director or outside investigator.
3. Files.
4. Investigation files.
5. Continuous.
6. Hands off to Legal.
7. None.
8. Edge cases: privilege waiver if used as defense; subpoena.
