## Certificate of Insurance (COI) Management

### Incoming COIs from Contractors
- **What it is:** Verification that contractors/vendors maintain required insurance.
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager / Compliance; project managers feed.
- **Data captured:** Contractor, project, required limits per contract, COI received, expiration, additional insured endorsement attached, waiver of subrogation, primary & non-contributory language, named insured matches contracting entity.
- **Documents / forms:** ACORD 25 (Certificate of Liability); ACORD 28 (Property); CG 20 10 (additional insured ongoing operations endorsement); CG 20 37 (completed operations); CG 24 04 (waiver of sub); endorsement copies.
- **Frequency:** At engagement; auto-renewal tracking.
- **Hand-offs:** AP (no COI = no pay), Procurement, Operations.
- **State differences:** Anti-indemnity statutes in WV, VA, KY for construction contracts (WV §55-8-14; VA §11-4.1; KY §371.180) limit ability to require indemnity for indemnitee's sole negligence; affects insurance requirements.
- **Edge cases:** Expired COIs; "Certificate Holder Only" rather than "Additional Insured"; AI endorsement not actually attached; insufficient limits relative to contract.

### Outgoing COIs to Customers / Lessors
- **What it is:** Issuing COIs to customers, landlords, lessors demonstrating SCC's coverage.
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager / broker.
- **Data captured:** Recipient, project/contract, limits provided, AI added, expiration.
- **Documents / forms:** ACORD 25; endorsements as required.
- **Frequency:** On request; renewal updates.
- **Hand-offs:** Broker.
- **State differences:** N/A.
- **Edge cases:** Customer demanding higher limits than carried; conflicting AI requirements across customers.

## Surety / Bonding

### Reclamation Surety Bonds
- **What it is:** Bonds required for SMCRA reclamation obligations per permit per state.
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager + GC; surety broker; treasurer for collateral.
- **Data captured:** Permit ID, state, bond #, surety, bond amount, effective date, anniversary date, premium, collateral pledged, indemnity agreement reference, release status (Phase I/II/III in WV/VA/KY SMCRA programs).
- **Documents / forms:** Surety bond form (each state has approved forms — WV SR-1 type forms, VA DMLR bond forms, KY DNR forms); GIA (General Indemnity Agreement) with surety; collateral pledge.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; annual renewals; Phase release applications event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental (reclamation cost calculation), Permitting, Finance/Treasury (collateral).
- **State differences:** WV — surety bonds, collateral bonds (cash, CDs, real estate lien, LOCs, securities), self-bond, or combinations under §22-3-11; alternative WV Special Reclamation Fund supplements ABS. VA & KY also operate bond pools (alternative bonding systems / ABS). All three have specific forms; OSMRE-approved.
- **Edge cases:** Surety exit from coal market (Continental, RLI, Indemnity National changes); collateral calls; self-bonding largely curtailed post-Alpha/Patriot bankruptcies; substitute bonding on permit transfer; bond forfeiture proceedings; AML reclamation under WV Special Reclamation Trust Fund.

### Permit Bonds (Non-Reclamation)
- **What it is:** Bonds tied to specific permit conditions beyond reclamation (e.g., subsidence, water replacement).
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager.
- **Data captured:** Permit, bond type, amount, surety.
- **Documents / forms:** State-specific.
- **Frequency:** Per permit.
- **Hand-offs:** Permitting.
- **State differences:** Each state has unique add-on bond categories.
- **Edge cases:** Water supply replacement bonds (WV requires subsidence/water bonds for underground); blasting bonds.

### Performance Bonds (Construction)
- **What it is:** Bonds guaranteeing performance of construction contracts (capital projects, prep plant builds).
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager.
- **Data captured:** Project, contractor, bond #, amount.
- **Documents / forms:** AIA A312 Performance Bond form typical.
- **Frequency:** Per project.
- **Hand-offs:** Project owner role.
- **State differences:** N/A.
- **Edge cases:** Surety takeover on contractor default.

### Payment Bonds
- **What it is:** Bonds protecting subcontractors and suppliers from non-payment.
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager (typically required of GC on a SCC capital project where SCC is owner; or required from SCC if SCC is contractor).
- **Documents / forms:** AIA A312 Payment Bond.
- **Frequency:** Per project.
- **Hand-offs:** AP.
- **State differences:** Mechanic's lien statutes interplay — WV Chapter 38 Article 2; VA §43-1 et seq.; KY §376.
- **Edge cases:** Little Miller Act on state projects; Miller Act on federal.

### Tax Bonds
- **What it is:** Bonds required by IRS / state tax authority to suspend collection or post during appeal.
- **Who performs it:** GC + CFO.
- **Data captured:** Liability, bond, period.
- **Documents / forms:** IRS Form 656 / 8821; state-specific.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Tax.
- **State differences:** WV severance tax bonds; VA fuels tax bonds.
- **Edge cases:** Coal severance tax disputes.

### License / Permit Bonds (Misc)
- **What it is:** Various small bonds — fuel dealer, motor carrier, contractor license in some jurisdictions.
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager.
- **Data captured:** License, bond, amount.
- **Frequency:** Per license.
- **Hand-offs:** Per business function.
- **State differences:** Each state's licensing.
- **Edge cases:** Often overlooked at renewals.

### Court Bonds / Supersedeas
- **What it is:** Appeal bonds to stay enforcement of judgment.
- **Who performs it:** GC + outside counsel.
- **Data captured:** Judgment, supersedeas amount, posting deadline.
- **Documents / forms:** Supersedeas bond form per court.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance.
- **State differences:** WV — judgment + 1.5x to bond appeals; VA Code §8.01-676.1 — 1.25x cap; KY CR 73.04 — 1.5x.
- **Edge cases:** Caps on supersedeas (tort reform statutes — WV caps at $50M for non-economic in some matters; punitive damage stays); reduction motions.

### Surety Indemnity Agreement (GIA) & Collateral
- **What it is:** Master agreement with surety company giving surety right to indemnification and collateral.
- **Who performs it:** GC + Treasurer.
- **Data captured:** Surety, GIA date, indemnitors (often parent + affiliates + principals personally), collateral type, amount, terms of release.
- **Documents / forms:** General Indemnity Agreement; Personal Indemnity Agreement; collateral pledge; LOC; cash escrow.
- **Frequency:** At surety relationship inception; modified on capacity changes.
- **Hand-offs:** Treasurer (LOCs from bank), Banking.
- **State differences:** N/A (federal common law on suretyship).
- **Edge cases:** Cross-defaults across affiliates; surety's right to demand additional collateral on triggering event (financial covenant breach, claim filed); pre-litigation collateral demand; surety's right to settle even over principal's objection.

### Annual Surety Credit Reviews
- **What it is:** Annual underwriting refresh — financials, permits, claims experience.
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager + CFO.
- **Data captured:** Financials submitted, ratios, permit status, claims, surety capacity granted.
- **Documents / forms:** Surety bond questionnaire; reviewed financials; permit list.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance.
- **State differences:** N/A.
- **Edge cases:** Credit downgrade; surety reduces capacity mid-cycle.

### Bond Claim Defense
- **What it is:** Defending claims made against bonds.
- **Who performs it:** GC + surety counsel.
- **Data captured:** Claim, claimant, basis, surety response, principal defenses.
- **Documents / forms:** Surety claim notice; principal's response.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Surety.
- **State differences:** N/A.
- **Edge cases:** Forfeiture proceedings on reclamation bonds.

### Bond Release Tracking
- **What it is:** Release of reclamation bonds at Phase I, II, III completion.
- **Who performs it:** Environmental + Risk.
- **Data captured:** Permit, phase, application date, release amount, granted date.
- **Documents / forms:** Bond release application (state-specific); public notice; inspection report.
- **Frequency:** Per phase per permit.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental, Permitting.
- **State differences:** All three primacy states have Phase I (initial regrading + drainage), II (revegetation), III (full liability — typically 5-year vegetation period in non-arid East, often longer).
- **Edge cases:** Citizen opposition to release; off-site impact extending liability; AMD discharges blocking release.

### Coverage Gap Monitoring
- **What it is:** Identifying permits without active bonds, or bonds in lapse.
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager.
- **Data captured:** Permit-to-bond cross-reference; gap report.
- **Frequency:** Monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Permitting, Surety.
- **State differences:** N/A.
- **Edge cases:** Bond mid-replacement gap; surety insolvency leaving permits unbonded.

## Indemnification Register

### Indemnity Tracking
- **What it is:** Cross-contract register of all indemnification obligations — who indemnifies whom, scope, cap, defense rights, insurance backing.
- **Who performs it:** Contract Manager + GC.
- **Data captured:** Contract, indemnitor, indemnitee, scope (third-party claims, IP, environmental, employment, breach of rep), cap (% contract value, $ cap, uncapped exceptions), defense rights (sole, joint, control), insurance backing, notice provisions, survival period.
- **Documents / forms:** Indemnity Register; contract abstracts.
- **Frequency:** At contract execution.
- **Hand-offs:** Insurance (verify backed by coverage), Finance (potential exposure).
- **State differences:** Anti-indemnity statutes — WV §55-8-14 (construction); VA §11-4.1; KY §371.180; AL §8-1-1; TN §62-6-123. Mining-specific carve-outs in some.
- **Edge cases:** Indemnity for sole negligence of indemnitee voided in many states for construction; "to extent" vs. "arising out of" magnitudes; mutual indemnities net out poorly.

## Ethics & Compliance

### Code of Conduct / Ethics Policy
- **What it is:** Top-level company ethics framework.
- **Who performs it:** GC + Ethics/Compliance Officer.
- **Data captured:** Policy version, effective date, training completion.
- **Documents / forms:** Code of Conduct; Acknowledgment Form.
- **Frequency:** Annual acknowledgment.
- **Hand-offs:** HR.
- **State differences:** N/A.
- **Edge cases:** Distinct from "Business Conduct Guidelines" — code is foundational.

### Conflict of Interest Disclosures
- **What it is:** Annual disclosure of personal/family interests creating conflicts.
- **Who performs it:** Compliance Officer.
- **Data captured:** Employee, disclosure, mitigation plan.
- **Documents / forms:** COI Disclosure Form.
- **Frequency:** Annual + event.
- **Hand-offs:** HR.
- **State differences:** N/A.
- **Edge cases:** Family members at competitors / customers / vendors; outside business interests; gifts received from vendors.

### Gifts & Entertainment Policy
- **What it is:** Limits and tracking of gifts/entertainment given and received.
- **Who performs it:** Compliance.
- **Data captured:** Recipient, value, occasion, approver.
- **Documents / forms:** Gifts Log.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (T&E reimbursement matching).
- **State differences:** Public-official gift rules — WV Ethics Act §6B-2-5; VA SOC §2.2-3100; KY Executive Branch Ethics Code KRS 11A.
- **Edge cases:** Customer entertainment that crosses kickback line; political event tickets; speaker honoraria.

### Anti-Bribery / FCPA
- **What it is:** FCPA compliance program (relevant if exporting met coal to foreign buyers/agents).
- **Who performs it:** Compliance + GC.
- **Data captured:** Foreign agent due diligence, payments, training.
- **Documents / forms:** FCPA Policy; Foreign Agent Due Diligence Questionnaire; FCPA Certification.
- **Frequency:** Annual training; per engagement diligence.
- **Hand-offs:** Sales (export), AP.
- **State differences:** N/A federal; UK Bribery Act applies to UK-nexus transactions.
- **Edge cases:** Facilitating payments exception narrow; charitable contributions in foreign country; merger-acquired subsidiary's pre-acquisition FCPA exposure.

### Antitrust / Competition
- **What it is:** Sherman, Clayton, Robinson-Patman compliance; relevant in trade association meetings (NMA, WVCMI, VCEA, KCRA), customer interactions, joint bidding.
- **Who performs it:** Compliance + GC.
- **Data captured:** Training, meeting protocols.
- **Documents / forms:** Antitrust Policy; Trade Association Meeting Guidance; Pre-Meeting Briefing.
- **Frequency:** Annual training; per major industry event.
- **Hand-offs:** Sales, BD.
- **State differences:** State antitrust laws (Donnelly-like statutes; WV §47-18; VA §59.1-9.1; KY §367.175).
- **Edge cases:** Coal bid coordination / market allocation; price signaling at industry conferences; benchmarking surveys (need third-party aggregation); joint ventures requiring HSR.

### Insider Trading
- **What it is:** Less relevant for private company; relevant if any debt or affiliated company is public.
- **Who performs it:** Compliance.
- **Data captured:** Restricted lists, trading windows (for relevant persons).
- **Documents / forms:** Insider Trading Policy; pre-clearance requests.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance.
- **State differences:** N/A federal.
- **Edge cases:** Material non-public information about counterparty (customer) used in unrelated trade.

### Hotline / Whistleblower
- **What it is:** Anonymous reporting channel for ethics/compliance concerns.
- **Who performs it:** Compliance + GC; third-party hotline vendor (NAVEX EthicsPoint, ClearView).
- **Data captured:** Report ID, date, category, status, investigation, outcome.
- **Documents / forms:** Hotline reports; investigation files.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** HR (employment matters), GC (investigations).
- **State differences:** SOX §806, Dodd-Frank §922 whistleblower protections; state whistleblower acts — WV §6C-1; VA Fraud and Abuse Whistle Blower Protection Act; KY KRS 61.102; KY mining-specific whistleblower under coal mine safety; federal Mine Act §105(c) very strong.
- **Edge cases:** §105(c) discrimination claim from safety report; retaliation post-internal report; anonymous reports difficult to investigate.

### Investigation Workflow
- **What it is:** Process for handling internal investigations.
- **Who performs it:** GC + Compliance; outside investigation counsel where independence needed.
- **Data captured:** Allegation, scope, interviewees, evidence, findings, remediation.
- **Documents / forms:** Investigation plan, witness interview memos (Upjohn warnings), findings memo.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** HR (discipline), GC (privilege).
- **State differences:** State privilege variations.
- **Edge cases:** Upjohn warnings ("I represent the company, not you"); witness preparation lines; privilege waiver via inadvertent disclosure; document preservation; cooperator vs. target distinction.

### Compliance Training
- **What it is:** Recurring training on ethics, harassment, antitrust, FCPA, cyber, safety.
- **Who performs it:** Compliance + HR.
- **Data captured:** Course, attendees, completion, score.
- **Documents / forms:** LMS records.
- **Frequency:** Annual + new-hire.
- **Hand-offs:** HR.
- **State differences:** Some states require harassment training annually (not WV/VA/KY but CT/NY/IL — relevant if remote workers).
- **Edge cases:** Training fatigue; coverage of new regulations.

### Sanctions Screening (OFAC)
- **What it is:** Screening of customers, vendors, employees, lessors against OFAC SDN, sectoral sanctions, denied parties lists.
- **Who performs it:** Compliance.
- **Data captured:** Party, screen date, result, false-positive resolution.
- **Documents / forms:** Screening reports; OFAC interpretive guidance.
- **Frequency:** At onboarding; quarterly refresh for active counterparties; transaction-based for high-risk.
- **Hand-offs:** AP, AR, HR.
- **State differences:** N/A federal.
- **Edge cases:** Russian / Belarus / China coal export restrictions; Iran general license intricacies; SDN hits; 50% rule (entities ≥50% owned by SDN are themselves blocked); coal end-use restrictions in EU.

## Cyber / Data / Privacy (Legal Side)

### Data Breach Response
- **What it is:** Incident response coordination on data breach.
- **Who performs it:** GC + CISO + Compliance + outside breach counsel + forensics.
- **Data captured:** Incident, scope, affected data, jurisdictions, notification deadlines.
- **Documents / forms:** IR Plan; engagement letter with breach counsel (preserves privilege); forensics SOW; notification letters.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** IT, HR, Comms.
- **State differences:** Breach notification laws — WV §46A-2A-101; VA §18.2-186.6; KY §365.732; AL §8-38; TN §47-18-2107. Timelines vary (VA "without unreasonable delay"; KY 35 days; AL 45 days; TN 60 days). HIPAA if health data. Newer: VA CDPA effective 2023 for consumer privacy (limited applicability to coal operator).
- **Edge cases:** Multi-state notification matrix; AG notification triggers (thresholds); credit monitoring offer; class action defense; cyber insurance coverage triggers.

### Incident Classification & Notification
- **What it is:** Triaging incidents for notification obligation.
- **Who performs it:** GC + IT.
- **Data captured:** Incident type, data elements, residency of affected, regulatory triggers.
- **Documents / forms:** Triage decision tree.
- **Frequency:** Per incident.
- **Hand-offs:** External counsel.
- **State differences:** As above.
- **Edge cases:** Ransomware payment OFAC implications (Treasury 2020 advisory).

### Vendor Privacy Contracts (DPAs)
- **What it is:** Data Processing Addenda with vendors handling personal data.
- **Who performs it:** Contract Manager + GC.
- **Data captured:** Vendor, DPA effective date, processing scope, sub-processor list.
- **Documents / forms:** DPA template (GDPR-style; CCPA-style).
- **Frequency:** At vendor onboarding.
- **Hand-offs:** Procurement.
- **State differences:** VA CDPA, CCPA (CA employees / customers), CO/CT/UT etc.
- **Edge cases:** GDPR if EU employees of foreign customer; SCCs (Standard Contractual Clauses).

### Cyber Insurance Coordination
- **What it is:** Coordination with cyber insurer through incident.
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager + GC.
- **Data captured:** Carrier notification, panel counsel, panel forensics, costs covered.
- **Documents / forms:** Cyber policy; carrier-approved vendor list.
- **Frequency:** Per incident.
- **Hand-offs:** Insurance.
- **State differences:** N/A.
- **Edge cases:** Carrier insistence on its panel vendors vs. SCC's existing relationships.

### Regulatory Notification
- **What it is:** State AG / regulator notifications.
- **Who performs it:** GC + outside breach counsel.
- **Data captured:** AG notice filed, date, recipient.
- **Documents / forms:** State-specific AG notification forms (WV via online portal; VA via OAG; KY via OAG).
- **Frequency:** Per breach.
- **Hand-offs:** N/A.
- **State differences:** Each state's AG notification thresholds and content vary.
- **Edge cases:** Coordinated NAAG-level inquiries.

## Environmental Legal

### CERCLA / Superfund Liability Monitoring
- **What it is:** Tracking historical and acquired properties for §107 PRP exposure.
- **Who performs it:** GC + Environmental.
- **Data captured:** Sites, EPA Region, status (NPL, removal, deferred), PRP letters, allocations.
- **Documents / forms:** §104(e) information request response; PRP letter; AOC; settlement.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental.
- **State differences:** State Superfund analogs (WV Hazardous Waste Emergency Response Fund; VA Voluntary Remediation Program).
- **Edge cases:** Bona fide prospective purchaser defense (requires AAI Phase I + ongoing care); innocent landowner defense; arranger liability; successor liability via de facto merger.

### RCRA / TSCA / EPCRA / CAA / CWA Enforcement
- **What it is:** Multi-statute federal environmental enforcement defense.
- **Who performs it:** Environmental + GC + outside specialty counsel.
- **Data captured:** Action, statute, agency.
- **Documents / forms:** Specific to each statute.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental.
- **State differences:** Many programs delegated to states (NPDES, RCRA Subtitle C, air permits).
- **Edge cases:** Citizen suits (CWA §505, RCRA §7002) with 60-day NOI letters; SCC has historic experience here.

### Coal Refuse Disposal Reform Act (CRDRA) / SMCRA
- **What it is:** Federal coal mining law enforcement, plus state primacy programs.
- **Who performs it:** Environmental + GC.
- **Data captured:** Actions, citations.
- **Documents / forms:** SMCRA citations; AML reclamation orders.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental, Operations.
- **State differences:** Primacy in WV, VA, KY, AL, TN (TN program returned to OSMRE oversight for a period historically; check current status).
- **Edge cases:** AML reclamation liability for acquired properties; sliver-permit transfers; bond forfeitures triggering Special Reclamation Fund.

### NRD Claims
- **What it is:** Natural Resource Damages claims by federal/state trustees.
- **Who performs it:** GC + outside NRD counsel.
- **Data captured:** Site, trustees, assessment, settlement.
- **Documents / forms:** NRD assessment plan; consent decree.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven; long-running.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental.
- **State differences:** State trustee designations vary (typically natural resource agencies).
- **Edge cases:** Trustees not bound by EPA Superfund settlement; cost allocation across PRPs.

### Citizen Suits
- **What it is:** Suits by environmental groups under CWA §505, RCRA §7002, SMCRA §520.
- **Who performs it:** Outside environmental defense counsel.
- **Data captured:** NOI letter, lawsuit, settlement.
- **Documents / forms:** 60-day NOI; complaint.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental.
- **State differences:** N/A federal (state law analogues less common).
- **Edge cases:** Sierra Club, OVEC, Appalachian Voices have active CWA citizen suit dockets in WV/VA/KY; pre-suit NOI period allows cure but starts statute of limitations clock; diligent prosecution defense if agency has acted.

## Employment Legal

### Employment Agreements
- **What it is:** Executive and key employee written agreements.
- **Who performs it:** GC + HR.
- **Data captured:** Employee, position, base, bonus, equity, severance, restrictive covenants, IP assignment.
- **Documents / forms:** Employment Agreement.
- **Frequency:** At hire; renewals.
- **Hand-offs:** HR, Payroll.
- **State differences:** As above on restrictive covenants.
- **Edge cases:** Walking the at-will line; verbal promises; offer letter vs. employment agreement.

### Severance / Separation Agreements
- **What it is:** Agreements paying separation benefits in exchange for release.
- **Who performs it:** HR + GC; outside counsel for executive.
- **Data captured:** Employee, separation date, payment, release scope, OWBPA review.
- **Documents / forms:** Separation Agreement & General Release; OWBPA disclosure schedules for group RIFs; ADEA-compliant 21/45 day consideration + 7-day revocation.
- **Frequency:** Per separation.
- **Hand-offs:** HR, Payroll.
- **State differences:** State analogs to ADEA / WARN — WV has WV HRA age claim release; CA's stricter rules irrelevant.
- **Edge cases:** Section 409A on deferred severance; tax withholding on settlement payments; non-prosecution clauses re EEOC barred (cannot waive right to file; can waive monetary recovery).

### Restrictive Covenants
- **What it is:** Non-compete, non-solicit of employees/customers, non-disclosure.
- **Who performs it:** GC + HR.
- **Data captured:** Employee, scope (geographic, temporal, functional), consideration.
- **Documents / forms:** Restrictive Covenant Agreement (standalone or in employment agreement).
- **Frequency:** At hire / promotion.
- **Hand-offs:** HR.
- **State differences:** WV §47-25-1 et seq. (2023) — non-competes void for "low-wage" workers; reasonableness test for others. VA §40.1-28.7:7 — void for low-wage workers (defined as ≤avg weekly wage). KY — common-law reasonableness, recent case law restrictive. FTC final non-compete rule (2024) faces court challenges as of cutoff — track.
- **Edge cases:** Consideration for mid-employment imposition (some states require independent consideration); choice-of-law to circumvent state restrictions; garden leave alternative.

### Independent Contractor Agreements
- **What it is:** Engagement of 1099 contractors.
- **Who performs it:** Contracts + HR.
- **Data captured:** Contractor, scope, classification analysis basis.
- **Documents / forms:** Independent Contractor Agreement; W-9.
- **Frequency:** Per engagement.
- **Hand-offs:** HR (classification), AP.
- **State differences:** ABC test states vs common-law / IRS 20-factor; CA AB-5 (irrelevant unless CA contractor); WV uses common-law; VA similar.
- **Edge cases:** Misclassification — DOL, IRS, state UI, state WC each have own test; coal mining contractor (true contractor labor force vs employee labor force); 1099 vs corp-to-corp.

### WARN Act Notice
- **What it is:** 60-day notice of plant closing or mass layoff.
- **Who performs it:** HR + GC.
- **Data captured:** Site, affected employees, notice date, exceptions.
- **Documents / forms:** WARN Act Notice; state mini-WARN where applicable.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** HR, Operations.
- **State differences:** No state mini-WARN in WV/VA/KY/AL/TN — federal WARN only.
- **Edge cases:** Unforeseeable business circumstances exception; faltering company exception; sales-of-business successor liability; coal-specific — sudden mine idling.

### EEO Investigation Response
- **What it is:** Responding to internal complaints and external charges.
- **Who performs it:** HR + GC.
- **Data captured:** Complaint, investigation, findings, remediation.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** HR.
- **State differences:** As above.
- **Edge cases:** Cross-complaint mid-investigation; harassment investigation involving senior officers.

### Class / Collective Action Defense
- **What it is:** FLSA collective, Rule 23 class, state-law class.
- **Who performs it:** Outside class action counsel.
- **Data captured:** Notice issued, opt-in/opt-out, certification, settlement structure.
- **Documents / forms:** Notice forms; settlement notice (court-approved).
- **Frequency:** Per matter.
- **Hand-offs:** HR.
- **State differences:** Class action procedures per state.
- **Edge cases:** Arbitration clauses with class action waivers (Epic Systems enforces); PAGA equivalents not in SCC states.

## Commercial Disputes

### Customer Disputes
- **What it is:** Coal sale customer disputes — quality (BTU, ash, sulfur, moisture), force majeure invocation by either side, payment timing, take-or-pay.
- **Who performs it:** GC + Sales.
- **Data captured:** Customer, contract, dispute, exposure.
- **Documents / forms:** Coal sales agreement; quality dispute notice; force majeure notice.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Sales, Finance (AR write-down / reserve).
- **State differences:** UCC Article 2 applies to coal sales; choice of law per contract.
- **Edge cases:** Force majeure under contract vs. common law; spec disputes — sampling protocols; pricing index disputes (NYMEX, API, custom); declared FM not accepted by counterparty.

### Supplier Disputes
- **What it is:** Disputes with equipment, parts, supplies, fuel vendors.
- **Who performs it:** GC + Procurement.
- **Data captured:** Vendor, dispute, contract, damages.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Procurement.
- **State differences:** UCC Article 2.
- **Edge cases:** Warranty claims on rebuilt equipment; lemon equipment; recall coordination.

### Royalty Disputes
- **What it is:** Disputes with lessors over royalty calculation, audit findings, deductions, take-or-pay.
- **Who performs it:** GC + Land Department + outside oil&gas/coal lease counsel.
- **Data captured:** Lessor, lease, audit period, contested deductions, amount.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Land/Royalty.
- **State differences:** Lease interpretation under each state's coal lease jurisprudence; WV has extensive case law on what's deductible from royalty; KY similar.
- **Edge cases:** Heirship issues (royalty owners deceased intestate); unmined minerals tax; royalty in kind vs. royalty in cash; minimum royalty / wheelage credits; offsetting unmined coal property tax.

### Insurance Coverage Disputes
- See Insurance section.

### Construction Disputes
- **What it is:** Capital project disputes — prep plant, conveyor, impoundment construction.
- **Who performs it:** GC + outside construction counsel.
- **Data captured:** Project, contractor, dispute, change orders, delays, damages.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Project Management.
- **State differences:** Mechanic's lien statutes; pay-if-paid vs pay-when-paid enforceability (WV — pay-if-paid enforceable; VA — pay-if-paid limited by §11-4.6; KY — enforceable).
- **Edge cases:** Differing site conditions; design liability; consequential damages waivers.

### Mechanics Liens
- **What it is:** Lien filings against SCC real estate by contractors / suppliers.
- **Who performs it:** GC; outside counsel for bonding off or litigation.
- **Data captured:** Lien claimant, property, amount, perfection date, statute deadline, response.
- **Documents / forms:** Notice of Lien; affidavit; bond to discharge lien.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** AP, Project Management.
- **State differences:** WV §38-2-1 (90 days from last work to file); VA §43-4 (90 days from completion + 6 months to sue); KY §376.080 (6 months to file + 12 months to sue). All have memorandum of lien with strict content requirements.
- **Edge cases:** Pre-lien notices in some states; trust fund statutes on lender draws; bonding-off vs paying; subcontractor liens via privity of contract or notice; coal lease leasehold liens.

## Real Estate / Title Legal

### Title Opinions
- **What it is:** Pre-acquisition title review on coal, surface, mineral interests.
- **Who performs it:** Outside title counsel (often local — extensive in coal counties of WV, VA, KY).
- **Data captured:** Tract, abstract period, chain of title, exceptions, encumbrances, opinion limitations.
- **Documents / forms:** Drilling title opinion / mineral title opinion; certificate of title; title insurance commitment.
- **Frequency:** Per acquisition.
- **Hand-offs:** Land/Acquisitions.
- **State differences:** Title insurance for minerals limited / unavailable in some counties; reliance on attorney opinion.
- **Edge cases:** Severance gap (mineral severed pre-1900 with heirs untraceable); broadform deed issues (KY); coal under streams; AML overlay; permit interest vs fee interest distinction.

### Title Curative Actions
- **What it is:** Heirship cleanup, missing instruments, defective acknowledgments.
- **Who performs it:** Outside counsel.
- **Data captured:** Defect, curative steps, completion.
- **Documents / forms:** Quiet title complaint; curative deeds; affidavits of heirship; trust certifications.
- **Frequency:** As needed.
- **Hand-offs:** Land.
- **State differences:** Heirship rules per state intestacy statutes; affidavit of heirship admissibility varies.
- **Edge cases:** Genealogical research firms; published service on unknown heirs; partition actions.

### Forced Partition
- **What it is:** Partition of jointly owned mineral tracts when co-tenants won't cooperate.
- **Who performs it:** Outside counsel.
- **Data captured:** Tract, co-tenants, partition method (in kind vs. by sale).
- **Documents / forms:** Partition complaint; commissioner's report; judicial sale.
- **Frequency:** Project-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Land.
- **State differences:** WV §37-4-1; VA §8.01-81; KY §381.135 — all permit partition; minerals often partitioned by sale because indivisible.
- **Edge cases:** Heirs property statutes (UPHPA adopted in some states — protects against forced sale).

### Easement / ROW Enforcement
- **What it is:** Enforcing easements (haul roads, conveyors, water lines, powerlines) against interfering landowners.
- **Who performs it:** GC + outside counsel.
- **Data captured:** Easement, holder, dominant/servient, encroachment.
- **Documents / forms:** Easement; injunction complaint.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Operations.
- **State differences:** Easement law differences; KY — common law of easements; VA — strict construction.
- **Edge cases:** Prescriptive easements; abandonment; overburdening claims; secondary easements for maintenance.

### Property Tax Appeals
- **What it is:** Appeals of ad valorem assessment, especially unmined coal valuation.
- **Who performs it:** Tax + GC + outside property tax counsel.
- **Data captured:** Tax year, parcel, assessed value, appraisal, board decision, court appeal.
- **Documents / forms:** Per state — WV Board of Equalization & Review (annual February meetings); appeal to Office of Tax Appeals or Circuit Court; VA Board of Equalization then Circuit Court; KY local Board of Assessment Appeals then Kentucky Claims Commission.
- **Frequency:** Annual cycle.
- **Hand-offs:** Tax, Land.
- **State differences:** Coal valuation methodologies — WV uses unmined coal assessment formula (§11-1C); VA uses "fair market value" with coal-specific guidance; KY uses fair cash value.
- **Edge cases:** Unmined coal valuation often contested — present value of recoverable reserves vs. fee simple value; equalization claims; market-based vs. income-based vs. cost-based approaches.

### Eminent Domain
- **What it is:** Defense or offensive (for haul roads in some states with coal-condemnation statutes).
- **Who performs it:** Outside ED counsel.
- **Data captured:** Condemning authority, parcel, valuation, takings claim.
- **Documents / forms:** Petition for condemnation; commissioner's report; appeal.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Land.
- **State differences:** WV §54-1 et seq. (limited private ED rights); VA §25.1 (constitutional amendment 2012 restricted private-purpose ED); KY KRS 416 — coal mining-specific ED for haul roads exists historically.
- **Edge cases:** Pipeline / transmission line ED on SCC fee; haul road ED across recalcitrant surface owner.

### Quiet Enjoyment / Surface Owner Damages
- **What it is:** Surface owner claims for blasting, vibration, dust, water contamination, subsidence.
- **Who performs it:** GC + outside counsel.
- **Data captured:** Claimant, parcel, claim, damages, settlement.
- **Documents / forms:** Complaint; pre-blast survey records; subsidence claim.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Operations, Environmental.
- **State differences:** WV broad-form deed reform 1990s; surface owner damages from underground mining statutes; VA Coal Surface Mining Reclamation Act; KY broadform deed amendment 1988 (constitutional amendment requiring surface owner consent for certain methods).
- **Edge cases:** Pre-blast surveys lacking; water well replacement disputes; subsidence presumption rules; class actions for blasting/dust over wide area.

## Tax Legal

### Tax Audit Defense (Federal / State / Local)
- See Regulatory Enforcement — Tax Audits section. Tax-specific litigation venues:

### IRS Appeals
- **What it is:** Administrative appeal of IRS examination.
- **Who performs it:** Tax + outside controversy counsel.
- **Documents / forms:** Protest letter, Appeals conference, Form 870-AD.
- **State differences:** N/A federal.

### US Tax Court / Court of Federal Claims / District Court
- **What it is:** Petition Tax Court pre-payment within 90 days of Notice of Deficiency; alternatively pay and sue for refund in COFC or district court.
- **Who performs it:** Outside controversy counsel.
- **Documents / forms:** Tax Court petition; refund complaint.

### State Tax Appeals
- WV: **Office of Tax Appeals** (independent of WV Tax Division) — petition within 60 days; further to Kanawha County Circuit Court.
- VA: Tax Commissioner determination → Circuit Court within 1 year.
- KY: **Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals** (now Kentucky Claims Commission, Tax Appeals Division); appeal to Franklin/county Circuit Court.
- AL: **Alabama Tax Tribunal** (independent of Department of Revenue).
- TN: Tennessee Chancery Court (no specialized tax tribunal).

### Severance Tax & Sales/Use Tax Disputes
- **What it is:** Coal severance tax basis & rate disputes; mining machinery sales/use exemption.
- **Edge cases:** WV severance tax sale price methodology; VA Coal Surface Mining Reclamation tax; KY severance tax variations; mining machinery exemption scope (which equipment qualifies).

### Tax Controversy Reserves (FIN 48 / ASC 740-10)
- See Finance domain for accounting; legal sets reserves with Tax based on probable / more-likely-than-not analysis.

## Government Relations / Lobbying

### Federal Lobbying Registration (LDA)
- **What it is:** Registration if employees spend ≥20% of time lobbying federal officials.
- **Who performs it:** Government Affairs / GC.
- **Data captured:** Registrants, lobbying activities, expenses.
- **Documents / forms:** LD-1 Registration; LD-2 Quarterly Report; LD-203 Semi-Annual Contribution Report.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly + semi-annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance.
- **State differences:** N/A federal.
- **Edge cases:** Trade association lobbying through dues — reportable in some thresholds.

### State Lobbying Registration
- **WV** — Ethics Commission registration; per-legislator reports; gifts limits.
- **VA** — Secretary of the Commonwealth registration; annual filing; quarterly disclosure.
- **KY** — Legislative Ethics Commission; biennial registration; monthly reports during session.
- **AL** — Ethics Commission.
- **TN** — Bureau of Ethics & Campaign Finance.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; per-session reporting.
- **Edge cases:** Grassroots lobbying; in-house vs. contract lobbyists; client disclosure.

### PAC Administration
- **What it is:** Corporate-affiliated PAC for political contributions.
- **Who performs it:** Compliance + Treasurer.
- **Data captured:** Contributions in/out, recipients.
- **Documents / forms:** FEC Form 1, 3X, 5; state PAC equivalents.
- **Frequency:** Monthly / quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance.
- **State differences:** Corporate contribution prohibition federal (FECA); states vary (some states allow direct corporate contributions in state races — VA permits; WV permits; KY limited).
- **Edge cases:** Pay-to-play rules where contracting with state (most relevant where bidding state coal supply; less direct for SCC).

### Trade Association Memberships
- **What it is:** NMA (National Mining Association), West Virginia Coal Association, Virginia Mining Association, Kentucky Coal Association, regional groups.
- **Who performs it:** Government Affairs.
- **Data captured:** Membership, dues, committee participation, advocacy positions.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Compliance (antitrust safe harbor on association activities).
- **Edge cases:** Position-taking inconsistent with company position; antitrust risk in benchmarking surveys.

### Political Contributions Tracking
- **What it is:** Tracking corporate vs. personal vs. PAC contributions for compliance.
- **Who performs it:** Compliance.
- **Data captured:** Donor, recipient, date, amount.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** N/A.
- **Edge cases:** Officer personal contributions to officials who deal with SCC.

## Public Records / FOIA

### Incoming FOIA Requests
- **What it is:** State / federal FOIA requests for SCC information held by regulators (where SCC submitted data).
- **Who performs it:** GC monitors; outside counsel for objections.
- **Data captured:** Request, requester, agency, scope, our objection grounds, agency decision.
- **Documents / forms:** Reverse FOIA objection letter; CBI (confidential business information) designation per 40 CFR Part 2.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven; cyclical from environmental groups.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental.
- **State differences:** WV FOIA §29B; VA FOIA §2.2-3700; KY Open Records Act §61.870; AL §36-12-40; TN §10-7-503.
- **Edge cases:** Trade secret / CBI claims; redaction disputes; reverse FOIA suit to enjoin agency disclosure.

### Outgoing FOIA Requests
- **What it is:** SCC's own FOIA requests to regulators (e.g., to understand citizen complaints, comparable enforcement).
- **Who performs it:** GC / outside counsel.
- **Data captured:** Request, agency, scope, response.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.

## M&A / Transactions

### Due Diligence
- **What it is:** Buy-side and sell-side diligence on coal asset transactions.
- **Who performs it:** GC + outside M&A counsel + specialists (environmental, tax, employment).
- **Data captured:** DD checklist, data room contents, findings memo, allocation of risk.
- **Documents / forms:** DD checklist; data room inventory; environmental Phase I (ASTM E1527-21); Phase II as needed.
- **Frequency:** Per transaction.
- **Hand-offs:** All functions.
- **State differences:** Permit transfer mechanisms differ — WV permit transfer required, often slow; VA similar; KY similar.
- **Edge cases:** Hidden bond liability; AML exposure on acquired properties; predecessor BLBA liability flows to successor as RO; CERCLA liability for predecessor activity.

### Data Rooms
- **What it is:** Virtual data rooms (Intralinks, Datasite, Box).
- **Who performs it:** Outside counsel or VDR vendor.
- **Data captured:** Documents, access log.
- **Frequency:** Per transaction.

### Definitive Agreements
- **What it is:** APA, SPA, Membership Interest Purchase Agreement, Merger Agreement.
- **Who performs it:** Outside M&A counsel.
- **Documents / forms:** APA / SPA / MIPA.
- **Edge cases:** Working capital adjustments; earnouts; representation & warranty insurance.

### Disclosure Schedules
- **What it is:** Schedules of exceptions to reps & warranties.
- **Who performs it:** Sellers' counsel + business.
- **Documents / forms:** Disclosure schedules per article.

### Reps & Warranties Insurance
- **What it is:** Insurance product for breach of reps in M&A.
- **Who performs it:** Insurance broker + outside counsel.
- **Data captured:** Policy, limit, retention.
- **Documents / forms:** R&W policy + underwriting binder + DD memo.

### Indemnity Escrow
- **What it is:** Escrowed purchase price portion for indemnification.
- **Who performs it:** Outside counsel.
- **Data captured:** Escrow amount, release schedule, claims.
- **Documents / forms:** Escrow Agreement.

### Closing Checklist
- **What it is:** Comprehensive checklist of all closing conditions and deliverables.
- **Who performs it:** Outside counsel.

### Post-Closing Integration
- **What it is:** Permit transfers, bond replacements, license updates, contract assignments.
- **Who performs it:** GC + functional leads.
- **Data captured:** Integration plan with workstream owners and dates.
- **Hand-offs:** All.
- **Edge cases:** Bond transition gaps; permit transfer delays; assumed lease/contract assignment consents.

## Governance / Board

### Board Calendar
- **What it is:** Annual schedule of board meetings, agendas, materials.
- **Who performs it:** Corporate Secretary.
- **Data captured:** Meeting date, location, attendees, agenda, materials, minutes.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly typical for private; ad hoc.

### Resolutions / Written Consents
- **What it is:** Formal acts of board / shareholders / members.
- **Who performs it:** Corporate Secretary + GC.
- **Documents / forms:** Resolutions; written consents.

### Committee Charters
- **What it is:** Charter documents for audit, compensation, risk committees.
- **Frequency:** Annual review.

### Officer Appointments
- See Officer Register.

### D&O Insurance Coordination
- **What it is:** D&O policy procurement, run-off, claims notice.
- **Who performs it:** Risk Manager + GC.

### D&O Indemnification
- **What it is:** Bylaws/operating agreement indemnification provisions and individual indemnification agreements.
- **Who performs it:** GC.
- **Documents / forms:** Indemnification Agreement; advancement of expenses provisions.
- **Edge cases:** Mandatory vs permissive indemnification; advancement before final disposition; conduct exceptions (DGCL §145).

---

## Information Governance

### Privilege Protection
- **What it is:** Attorney-client + attorney work product protection.
- **Who performs it:** GC sets policy; everyone protects.
- **Data captured:** Privilege log; privileged communication labeling protocol.
- **Documents / forms:** Privilege policy; counsel labeling guidance.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** Upjohn application to corporate employees; common-interest privilege; functional equivalent doctrine (consultants treated as employees); inadvertent waiver; reliance-on-counsel waiver (advice-of-counsel defense); investigation privilege limits (Kellogg / Barko).

### Common Interest / Joint Defense Agreements
- **What it is:** Written agreements among allied parties to share privileged communications.
- **Who performs it:** GC + outside counsel.
- **Documents / forms:** Joint Defense Agreement; Common Interest Agreement.
- **Frequency:** Per matter.
- **Edge cases:** Withdrawal effect on privilege; in-writing requirement varies by jurisdiction.

### Confidentiality of Investigation Materials
- **What it is:** Protecting internal investigation materials from disclosure.
- **Who performs it:** GC.
- **Edge cases:** Selective waiver doctrine (most circuits reject); waiver in regulatory cooperation contexts.

## Edge Cases — Cross-Cutting

- **Multi-state venue disputes** — *forum non conveniens* litigation when plaintiff sues in plaintiff-favored forum (KY plaintiffs' bar reputation; WV mass tort plaintiffs' bar); choice of law disputes on coal lease interpretation.
- **Privilege waiver across jurisdictions** — federal common law vs state privilege rules in diversity cases (FRE 501); choice-of-law for privilege.
- **Insurance bad faith** — WV strong (Hayseeds attorney fee shifting); KY very strong (Wittmer); VA limited.
- **Regulator settlement coordination** — federal/state co-plaintiff settlement under SCC's existing CD framework; cooperator vs. target distinction in multi-defendant matters.
- **Corporate veil piercing** — SPE / single-member LLC structures vulnerable; minute book lapses, undercapitalization, commingling create exposure across coal entity stack.
- **Permit blocks via AVS** — federal SMCRA Applicant/Violator System cross-references officers/owners across all entities; one entity's unabated violation blocks new permits everywhere.
- **Successor liability** — environmental (CERCLA, RCRA, AML), BLBA (responsible operator), product warranty, employment (de facto merger / mere continuation), tax (transferee liability).
- **Coal-specific privilege issues** — geological / reserves data confidentiality vs SEC reserve disclosure if any debt registered; competitor data via FOIA / public records.
- **Force majeure cascades** — single weather event invoking FM under coal sales, transportation, lease, and consent decree simultaneously.
- **Litigation funding / contingent fee defense** — increasing plaintiffs' use of third-party funding in mass tort and environmental contexts.

# Domain 10: IT, OT, Communications, Cybersecurity & Physical Security

# IT, OT, Communications, Cybersecurity & Physical Security

Domain inventory for Southern Coal Corporation (SCC) operations across WV, VA, KY, AL, TN — corporate offices, multiple underground and surface mine sites, prep plants, loadouts, rail/barge terminals, remote field outposts, refuse impoundments, and contractor camps.

For each function: (1) What it is, (2) Who performs it, (3) Data captured, (4) Documents/forms/standards, (5) Frequency, (6) Hand-offs, (7) State-specific differences, (8) Common edge cases.

---

## 1. IT Infrastructure — Network & Connectivity

### 1.1 Corporate Wide Area Network (WAN)
- **What:** Private MPLS/VPLS or SD-WAN overlay connecting corporate HQ, regional offices, mine site offices, prep plants, loadouts, and remote field locations. Mix of fiber (where carrier serves), licensed microwave point-to-point (mine-to-mine in hollers without fiber), LTE/5G primary in marginal areas, satellite (Starlink Business / Hughes / Viasat) as fallback.
- **Who:** Network engineer / network admin (corporate IT); managed by IT director; carrier circuits ordered through procurement; on-site terminations by site IT lead or contract electrician.
- **Data captured:** Circuit IDs, LOA-CFAs, IP addressing plan, BGP ASNs, throughput / latency / loss telemetry, uptime SLAs, MRR, transport vendor per site.
- **Documents/standards:** Network diagram (Visio/Lucid), IP address management (IPAM) records, RFC 1918 plan, MSA/SOW with each carrier, SD-WAN policy doc, ITIL change record. NIST SP 800-53 SC-7 (boundary protection).
- **Frequency:** Continuous monitoring (SNMP/Flow); design refresh annually; circuit audit quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (circuit invoice GL coding), procurement (MSA), security (firewall edge), site managers (outage comms).
- **State-specific:** WV holler topology forces microwave because last-mile fiber doesn't reach; VA Mountain Empire and KY eastern fields similar; AL/TN have better fiber availability. State PUC certificate filings for any private microwave at >900 MHz licensed bands (FCC, not state).
- **Edge cases:** Microwave path blocked by new overburden pile; LTE tower service-affecting outage during mine emergency; SD-WAN tunnel flapping during thunderstorm; circuit cut by contractor backhoe; Starlink Gen3 router IP changes after firmware push.

### 1.2 Site LAN (switches, cabling, structured wiring)
- **What:** Layer-2/Layer-3 switching infrastructure at each site office, prep plant control room, loadout shack, warehouse, scale house. Cat6/Cat6A copper, OM4 fiber backbone; PoE+ for APs, cameras, phones.
- **Who:** Site IT tech (or regional); structured cabling contractor for new pulls; corporate network engineer for design and core switch config.
- **Data captured:** Switch port maps, MAC address tables, VLAN assignments, PoE budget, link utilization, cable test results (Fluke certs).
- **Documents/standards:** TIA-568, BICSI cabling standards, port-to-jack-to-cubicle map, switch config backup (RANCID/Oxidized), warranty registrations.
- **Frequency:** Daily monitoring; quarterly port audit; pre-move/add/change planning.
- **Hand-offs:** Facilities (cable pathways/conduit), electrical contractor (panel power), site manager (downtime windows).
- **State-specific:** Mine site equipment rooms in WV/VA/KY often share space with mine-rated comms; physical access control must respect MSHA mine office rules.
- **Edge cases:** Switch overheats in un-air-conditioned scale house; PoE budget exhausted by added cameras; copper run length exceeds 100m to scale-house outbuilding; lightning surge through unprotected outdoor run.

### 1.3 Wi-Fi (corporate, guest, IoT, harsh-environment)
- **What:** Wireless LAN with separate SSIDs for corporate (802.1X), guest (captive portal), IoT/OT (PSK + segmented VLAN), and ruggedized outdoor APs at maintenance shops, fueling islands, truck wash, scale houses.
- **Who:** Network engineer; site IT for AP physical install; cloud-managed controller (Meraki / ExtremeCloud / Aruba Central / Ubiquiti UniFi) administered by corporate.
- **Data captured:** Client count, SSID utilization, RSSI heatmaps, rogue AP detections, WIDS alerts, guest MAC and email captures.
- **Documents/standards:** Wi-Fi survey reports, AP placement plan, SSID/VLAN/security matrix, NIST SP 800-153 wireless guidance, WPA3-Enterprise on corp.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; site survey at deployment and after layout changes; firmware quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** Security (cert provisioning), HR (guest policy), ops (truck-shop coverage demands).
- **State-specific:** Outdoor APs at WV/KY mines need NEMA 4X or rated enclosures for coal dust + freeze-thaw.
- **Edge cases:** AP fried by lightning; coal dust packing in radome reduces gain; rogue Wi-Fi router brought in by contractor; guest network used to exfiltrate via tethered phone; AP MAC-flapping at maintenance bay.

### 1.4 Internet Uplinks & Failover
- **What:** Primary broadband per site (fiber/cable/fixed-wireless) plus secondary failover (LTE/5G modem, satellite). Path control via SD-WAN or simple route-priority on firewall.
- **Who:** Network engineer; site IT verifies failover; carrier account manager.
- **Data captured:** Public IP, ASN, throughput, latency, packet loss, failover events, monthly data usage on cellular.
- **Documents/standards:** Carrier contracts, SLA matrix, failover runbook, change ticket for any DNS/IP move.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly failover test; cellular usage reviewed monthly.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (carrier invoices), procurement (renewals).
- **State-specific:** Rural KY/WV often has only one terrestrial provider; cellular data caps blow up on Starlink fallback during long outages.
- **Edge cases:** Both primary and secondary go through the same regional fiber ring (single point of failure undetected); SIM deactivated by carrier for non-payment; static IP changed by ISP without notice; satellite throughput drops during weather.

### 1.5 VPN — Site-to-Site & Remote Access
- **What:** IPsec/SD-WAN tunnels between corporate, sites, and cloud; SSL/VPN client (Cisco AnyConnect, GlobalProtect, FortiClient, Zscaler ZPA) for remote-access; ZTNA migration in progress.
- **Who:** Network engineer; security engineer for policy; help desk for end-user enrollment.
- **Data captured:** Tunnel state, IKE/IPsec rekey events, user logins, source IP, device posture, session duration.
- **Documents/standards:** VPN policy, NIST SP 800-77 (IPsec), conditional-access policies in Entra ID, split-tunnel rules.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly certificate rotation; annual policy review.
- **Hand-offs:** HR/IAM (joiner-mover-leaver triggers VPN provisioning/revocation).
- **State-specific:** None material.
- **Edge cases:** Dual-stack v4/v6 mismatch breaks tunnel; cert expires on a long-running tunnel; contractor uses personal VPN to bypass DNS filtering; remote user's home ISP doubles NAT and breaks IPsec.

### 1.6 SD-WAN
- **What:** Software-defined WAN overlay (Cisco Meraki MX / Viptela, Fortinet Secure SD-WAN, Palo Alto Prisma SD-WAN, Versa, Cato) providing dynamic path selection, application-aware routing, integrated security.
- **Who:** Network/security engineer; managed via cloud orchestrator.
- **Data captured:** Per-tunnel SLA metrics, app classification, jitter/loss/latency, policy hits.
- **Documents/standards:** SD-WAN policy doc, application priority matrix.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; policy review quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** Voice (QoS for SIP), Ops (priority for SCADA traffic crossing WAN).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Brownout (high-loss link not failing fast enough); BGP route flap; application identification miscategorizes proprietary mine software.

### 1.7 Microwave & Wireless Backhaul (point-to-point / point-to-multipoint)
- **What:** Licensed (6/11/18/23 GHz) or unlicensed (5/24/60 GHz — Cambium, Ubiquiti AirFiber, Mimosa, Aviat, Ceragon) radios linking ridge-top to mine office, portable office, drag-line, blasting trailer.
- **Who:** Wireless contractor for path engineering and tower install; site IT for low-side cabling; FCC license filings via consultant.
- **Data captured:** Receive signal level (RSL), modulation, errored seconds, antenna alignment readings, weather fade events.
- **Documents/standards:** FCC license (Form 601), path study, tower structural cert, coordination notice (PCN), antenna mount inspections.
- **Frequency:** Continuous link monitoring; semi-annual tower inspection (FCC AM detuning if near AM broadcaster); license renewal every 10 years.
- **Hand-offs:** Survey (line-of-sight verification when overburden grows), permitting (any new tower).
- **State-specific:** WV and VA mountain terrain requires very high tower or relay hop; KY ridge mining means LOS changes with mining progression.
- **Edge cases:** Mining advance blocks Fresnel zone; new growth or tree-line; ice loading takes link down; co-channel interference from neighbor mine; lightning strike to tower.

### 1.8 Cellular Boosters / Signal Extension
- **What:** Indoor/vehicle cellular signal boosters (Wilson/weBoost, Cel-Fi, SureCall) at mine offices, scale houses, mancamps with marginal carrier signal.
- **Who:** Site IT or comms tech; FCC registration with carrier when required.
- **Data captured:** Pre/post-boost RSRP/RSRQ readings, carrier-approved booster serial.
- **Documents/standards:** FCC consumer-signal-booster registration with carrier; manufacturer install guide.
- **Frequency:** Survey at install; annual check.
- **Hand-offs:** Carrier (registration), facilities (donor antenna mast).
- **State-specific:** Required almost universally at WV/VA/KY underground mine portals and prep plant control rooms.
- **Edge cases:** Carrier denies registration; oscillation (uplink and donor too close); booster blows after lightning.

### 1.9 Satellite (Starlink, Hughes, Viasat, Iridium for voice)
- **What:** Satellite broadband as primary at extreme-remote outposts (refuse impoundment monitoring shed, water-treatment plant in adjacent hollow) or as DR/emergency at all sites. Iridium handhelds for executive travel and mine rescue.
- **Who:** Site IT; corporate IT manages account inventory; mine rescue team for handhelds.
- **Data captured:** Dish kit serial, terminal IMEI, account number, MRC, usage GB/month.
- **Documents/standards:** Starlink Business terms, FCC blanket earth-station license (carrier-held), inventory of Iridium handhelds with sat phone numbers.
- **Frequency:** Continuous availability check; monthly invoice reconciliation; semi-annual sat-phone battery / sim activation test.
- **Hand-offs:** Emergency response team, finance.
- **State-specific:** Mountain ridges in WV/KY/VA reduce Starlink visibility north; obstruction surveys required.
- **Edge cases:** Starlink router reboot loop; Iridium SIM auto-suspended after long inactivity; satellite dish stolen from unattended portable office; severe weather degrades Ka-band.

### 1.10 DNS / DHCP / NTP (Core Network Services)
- **What:** Internal DNS (Active Directory integrated or BIND/Infoblox), DHCP scopes per VLAN, NTP synced to authoritative source (USNO/NIST or GPS appliance).
- **Who:** Network engineer; AD admin; sysadmin.
- **Data captured:** DNS query logs, DHCP lease records, NTP drift metrics, conditional forwarders.
- **Documents/standards:** Internal naming convention; DNSSEC for public zones; NIST SP 800-81 DNS guidance.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; lease audits quarterly; NTP source health checked weekly.
- **Hand-offs:** Security (DNS as detection signal), OT (separate NTP for control network).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** DHCP scope exhaustion at large training event; rogue DHCP on guest VLAN; NTP drift causes Kerberos failures; DNS amplification attack from open resolver.

## 2. Identity, Access & Endpoint Management

### 2.1 Active Directory / Entra ID (Azure AD)
- **What:** Hybrid identity — on-prem AD DS with Entra Connect to Entra ID for Microsoft 365 and SaaS SSO. Forest/domain design, OU structure by region/site/function.
- **Who:** Identity/AD admin; security engineer for privileged-tier model; HR drives input.
- **Data captured:** User objects, security groups, GPOs, sign-in logs, audit logs (4624/4625/4720/4732), risky-sign-in detections.
- **Documents/standards:** AD tier model (Microsoft), NIST SP 800-63 IAL/AAL, naming conventions, Entra access reviews export.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly access reviews; KRBTGT rotation 2x/year.
- **Hand-offs:** HR (JML), help desk (provisioning), security (privileged escalation review).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Stale service accounts with weak passwords; orphaned mailbox after offboarding; Entra Connect sync break; password sync vs federation drift; legacy NTLM service still on shop-floor PC.

### 2.2 Group Policy & Endpoint Configuration
- **What:** GPOs for domain-joined Windows; Intune/MDM configuration profiles for cloud-managed.
- **Who:** AD/Endpoint admin.
- **Data captured:** Policy GUIDs, link order, security filtering, gpresult outputs, Intune compliance reports.
- **Documents/standards:** CIS Benchmarks (Windows 11 / Server 2022 / Edge / Office), STIGs if federal data.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly GPO audit; annual baseline review.
- **Hand-offs:** Help desk (user-impacting setting changes).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** GPO conflict with Intune (co-management); RSoP misleading; lockout from misapplied login restriction.

### 2.3 SSO / Identity Provider (Okta, Entra ID)
- **What:** Federated SSO for SaaS apps (M365, Salesforce, ERP web, ServiceNow, mining-specific cloud apps).
- **Who:** IAM engineer; app owners for SCIM provisioning.
- **Data captured:** SSO logs, app assignment, group-based provisioning, SCIM events.
- **Documents/standards:** SAML metadata exchange, OIDC client registrations, NIST SP 800-63C.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly app catalog review.
- **Hand-offs:** App owners, vendor success teams.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Vendor breaks SAML during platform upgrade; loop after metadata cert rotation; shadow IT app not behind SSO.

### 2.4 Multi-Factor Authentication / Passwordless
- **What:** MFA for all users (Authenticator push, FIDO2 keys for privileged), conditional access enforced; passwordless rollout for execs and IT admins.
- **Who:** Security engineer; help desk for enrollment.
- **Data captured:** Registered methods per user, MFA challenge events, fraud reports.
- **Documents/standards:** NIST SP 800-63B AAL2/AAL3, FIDO2 device registry, MFA exemption register (with expiry).
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly stale-method cleanup.
- **Hand-offs:** Help desk (lost-device reset), HR (offboarding).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Miner phone died/forgotten — bypass workflow needed; SIM-swap targeted attack on exec; FIDO key lost at mine portal; voice/SMS MFA fails at signal-poor sites.

### 2.5 DNS Filtering / Web Security
- **What:** Cisco Umbrella / Cloudflare Gateway / Zscaler / Forcepoint blocking malicious domains, content categories, and DNS-tunneling C2.
- **Who:** Security engineer.
- **Data captured:** Blocked queries, top users, categorization, threat intel hits.
- **Documents/standards:** Acceptable Use Policy, category-block rationale.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; policy review quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** HR (policy violations).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Legitimate mining vendor site miscategorized; DNS-over-HTTPS in browser bypasses agent; smart-TV in conference room beacons.

### 2.6 Email Security Gateway
- **What:** M365 Defender for O365 / Proofpoint / Mimecast / Barracuda — anti-spam, anti-phish, malware sandboxing, DMARC/DKIM/SPF, BEC protection.
- **Who:** Security engineer.
- **Data captured:** Quarantine logs, click-time URL detonation, impersonation alerts, DMARC reports.
- **Documents/standards:** DMARC policy (p=reject), SPF/DKIM records, phishing playbook.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly false-positive review; annual DMARC review.
- **Hand-offs:** End users (release requests), HR (repeated phishers/repeat clickers).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Banker spoofs CFO to redirect ACH (BEC); vendor invoice swap; quarantine release of malicious file by user; auto-forward rule set by attacker after compromise.

### 2.7 File Services (NAS, SharePoint, OneDrive)
- **What:** On-prem file shares for legacy/Engineering CAD data; SharePoint Online for collaboration; OneDrive for personal; mine survey deliverables, geological models stored on NAS with versioning.
- **Who:** Sysadmin; SharePoint admin; data steward by business unit.
- **Data captured:** Access logs, version history, retention labels, sensitive-data classifications.
- **Documents/standards:** Information classification policy, retention schedule, M365 sensitivity labels.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly orphan/abandoned site review.
- **Hand-offs:** Records mgmt, legal (hold notices), HR (departing-user OneDrive transfer).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Survey deliverables exceed OneDrive sync limit; PII in random Excel on team site; ransomware encrypts SharePoint via sync; external sharing link forgotten.

### 2.8 Print Services
- **What:** Print server / PrinterLogic / Universal Print; MFP fleet under managed-print contract (Lexmark, Xerox, Canon, Sharp).
- **Who:** Help desk; vendor for break-fix.
- **Data captured:** Page counts (color/mono), toner levels, jam logs, print-release events.
- **Documents/standards:** Managed-print services agreement, secure-print policy.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly fleet review.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (per-page billing), site facilities.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Sensitive map left in tray; MFP HDD not wiped at lease return; SMBv1 protocol enabled for legacy scan-to-folder.

### 2.9 Endpoint Management — MDM/UEM (Intune, JAMF, Workspace ONE)
- **What:** Centralized config, app delivery, compliance, conditional access for Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, ruggedized tablets (Panasonic Toughbook, Zebra, Getac), and mine-rated devices (MSHA permissibility approval for in-mine use).
- **Who:** Endpoint admin.
- **Data captured:** Device inventory, OS version, encryption state, last sync, app inventory, compliance state.
- **Documents/standards:** CIS Benchmarks, baseline images, BitLocker/FileVault key escrow, MSHA permissibility approvals for intrinsically safe devices.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; monthly compliance reports.
- **Hand-offs:** Help desk, procurement (device refresh), HR (return on offboard).
- **State-specific:** MSHA approval (30 CFR Part 18) required for electronic devices used in gassy underground areas — non-permissible phone underground is a violation.
- **Edge cases:** Toughbook in surface haul truck rolls over and breaks BitLocker recovery; ruggedized tablet stolen from unlocked truck; jailbroken phone bypasses MDM; macOS upgrade orphans JAMF agent.

### 2.10 Hardware Lifecycle (Procurement → Deployment → Refresh → Decommission)
- **What:** Standardized SKUs, imaging via Autopilot, refresh cadence (3-yr laptop / 5-yr desktop / 4-yr ruggedized / 5-yr server), secure decommission with NIST 800-88 wipe or physical destruction, e-waste recycling.
- **Who:** IT procurement; help desk for deploy; IT director approves refresh schedule.
- **Data captured:** Asset tag, serial, MAC, assigned user, purchase date, refresh date, disposal cert.
- **Documents/standards:** NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 (media sanitization), R2/e-Stewards recycler cert, certificate of destruction (CoD), capital-vs-expense per finance policy.
- **Frequency:** Refresh planning annual; disposals event-driven; inventory reconciliation quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (capex), accounting (asset write-off), security (data-bearing media verified).
- **State-specific:** State e-waste laws differ (WV no specific; VA, KY follow EPA general).
- **Edge cases:** Drive returned under warranty but contains PII (vendor non-disclosure required); old server in mine office never decommissioned and still in AD; lost-laptop report without remote wipe.

---

## 3. Servers, Cloud & Data Center

### 3.1 Server Hosting (on-prem / colo / cloud)
- **What:** Mix of on-prem servers at HQ (rack room), small server closet per site (DC at the edge), regional colo (Lumen/Equinix/Cologix), and cloud workloads in Azure/AWS for SCC-OS itself and SaaS-adjacent.
- **Who:** Sysadmin / infrastructure engineer; cloud engineer; colo escort by cage badge holder.
- **Data captured:** Server inventory (CMDB), hypervisor host metrics, rack/U position, power draw, OS lifecycle.
- **Documents/standards:** Rack elevations, BIOS/firmware baselines, vendor support contracts (Dell ProSupport, HPE Foundation Care).
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly capacity review.
- **Hand-offs:** Facilities (HVAC, UPS), security (data-center physical access).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** A/C failure in HQ rack room over weekend; UPS battery age-fail; colo cross-connect cut by neighbor work.

### 3.2 Virtualization (VMware, Hyper-V, Nutanix, Proxmox)
- **What:** Hypervisor clusters; vMotion/HA; storage SAN/HCI; broader migration considerations post-Broadcom-VMware pricing shift.
- **Who:** Virtualization admin.
- **Data captured:** Cluster health, VM inventory, resource utilization, snapshot age.
- **Documents/standards:** Hypervisor architecture diagram, license entitlements, snapshot policy.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly capacity; annual license true-up.
- **Hand-offs:** App owners, finance (licensing).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Snapshot left for months on a busy DB VM; storage RAID double-disk-failure; HA event during patch window.

### 3.3 Cloud (Azure / AWS / GCP) — for SCC-OS
- **What:** Cloud subscriptions for SCC-OS app hosting, data lake, AI services. Landing zones, IaC (Terraform/Bicep), management groups, billing alerts.
- **Who:** Cloud engineer; FinOps owner; security.
- **Data captured:** Resource inventory, tags, cost by service, RI/savings-plan utilization, IAM bindings.
- **Documents/standards:** CIS Azure/AWS Benchmarks, well-architected reviews, landing-zone reference architecture, tag policy.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; monthly cost review; quarterly architecture review.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (chargeback), security (CSPM).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Runaway compute from misconfigured pipeline; public S3 bucket leaks survey CSV; expired credit-card on PAYG sub causes outage.

### 3.4 Containers / Kubernetes
- **What:** Container platform (AKS/EKS, OpenShift, K3s at edge) for SCC-OS microservices; image registry; secrets via Key Vault / SSM.
- **Who:** Platform engineer; SRE.
- **Data captured:** Cluster events, pod logs, deployment manifests, vulnerability scans of images.
- **Documents/standards:** CNCF best practices, NSA Kubernetes hardening guide, Pod Security Standards.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; image scans on every build; quarterly upgrades.
- **Hand-offs:** App devs, security.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Pod escape via privileged container; image with embedded creds; expired cert breaks ingress.

### 3.5 Patching (Windows, Linux, Network, Firmware)
- **What:** WSUS / Intune / Azure Update Manager for Windows; Ansible/Satellite for Linux; vendor tools for switch IOS-XE/EOS; out-of-band firmware (iDRAC/iLO).
- **Who:** Sysadmin / network engineer; change managed.
- **Data captured:** Patch compliance %, missing critical, last-reboot, exception register.
- **Documents/standards:** Patch SLA (Critical 7d, High 14d, Medium 30d), CISA KEV catalog cross-reference, change record.
- **Frequency:** Monthly Patch Tuesday cycle; emergency for KEV/zero-day.
- **Hand-offs:** Change board, ops (OT downtime windows for industrial network gear).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Mine-office PC offline for months — accumulates 6 months patches; reboot causes BSOD on driver mismatch; firmware bricks a stack switch; OT vendor disallows patching without their tech.

### 3.6 Vulnerability Scanning
- **What:** Authenticated and unauthenticated scans (Tenable Nessus/Tenable.io, Qualys, Rapid7 InsightVM, Defender for Endpoint VM); external attack-surface monitoring (Censys, BitSight, SecurityScorecard).
- **Who:** Security engineer; remediation owners by asset type.
- **Data captured:** CVE list, CVSS, exploit availability, age in days, remediation SLA breach.
- **Documents/standards:** Vulnerability mgmt policy, remediation SLA matrix, exception register.
- **Frequency:** Weekly external; monthly internal; continuous agent-based.
- **Hand-offs:** Sysadmin, network, app owners.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Scanner credentials disabled (false-clean result); legacy SCADA host crashes when scanned (must exclude); long-tail of decommissioned IPs still showing CVEs.

### 3.7 Asset & Software Inventory / License Tracking
- **What:** Hardware + software inventory via Intune, SCCM, Lansweeper, Snipe-IT, ServiceNow CMDB; SaaS spend management (Zylo, Productiv).
- **Who:** Asset manager / sysadmin.
- **Data captured:** Hardware list, installed software, license entitlements, true-up exposure.
- **Documents/standards:** Software asset policy, vendor license agreements.
- **Frequency:** Continuous discovery; quarterly reconciliation; annual true-up.
- **Hand-offs:** Procurement, finance.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Unlicensed AutoCAD on mine engineer's laptop; concurrent-license overuse; SaaS sub paid on personal AmEx.

## 4. Backup, DR & Business Continuity

### 4.1 Backup (Veeam, Rubrik, Cohesity, Commvault)
- **What:** Image and file backups of servers, M365 (Veeam for M365 / AvePoint / Druva), endpoints (where required), and OT historians; immutable target (S3 Object Lock, hardened repo).
- **Who:** Backup admin.
- **Data captured:** Job status, success rate, RPO actual vs target, restore-test results, capacity.
- **Documents/standards:** Backup policy (3-2-1-1-0), retention schedule (legal + ops), NIST SP 800-209.
- **Frequency:** Daily incrementals; weekly synthetic full; monthly air-gap snapshot.
- **Hand-offs:** Legal (litigation hold extends retention), security (ransomware playbook).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Backup job fails for weeks unnoticed; tape mailed without encryption; ransomware encrypts backup repo because not immutable; M365 retention misunderstood (Microsoft doesn't back up).

### 4.2 Backup Verification / Restore Drills
- **What:** Scheduled restore tests — file-level, VM-level, full-DR exercise.
- **Who:** Backup admin + app owners.
- **Data captured:** Restore time, integrity check pass/fail, drill report.
- **Documents/standards:** Restore-test playbook, DR exercise after-action.
- **Frequency:** Monthly file-level; quarterly VM; annual full-DR.
- **Hand-offs:** Business owners verify functional after restore.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Restore succeeds but app fails (DB schema mismatch); incomplete dataset (orphaned files); restore is to wrong VLAN.

### 4.3 Disaster Recovery Site & BCP
- **What:** Secondary site or cloud DR (Azure Site Recovery, AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery, Zerto); BCP plans per business function with RTO/RPO.
- **Who:** IT director; BCP coordinator; business unit owners.
- **Data captured:** RTO/RPO targets vs actuals, runbook library, contact tree.
- **Documents/standards:** BIA, BCP, DRP, tabletop after-action, ISO 22301 alignment.
- **Frequency:** Annual BIA refresh; semi-annual tabletop; annual full failover.
- **Hand-offs:** Executive sponsor, HR (employee comms), Legal, PR.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** DR cloud quota too low to spin up at failover; key person on vacation during drill; missing dependency (a SaaS app not in DR scope).
