## 5. OT / SCADA / Industrial Control Systems (Prep Plant, Loadout, Mine)

### 5.1 PLCs at Prep Plants
- **What:** Programmable logic controllers — Rockwell/Allen-Bradley ControlLogix/CompactLogix, Siemens S7-1500/S7-1200, Schneider Modicon Quantum/M580, GE PACSystems — controlling flotation, heavy-media, screens, conveyors, thickener, dewatering at the wash plant.
- **Who:** Control system engineer; plant electrician; OEM integrator (often local — Roberts & Schaefer / KECO / Industrial Resources).
- **Data captured:** I/O state, ladder logic versions, alarms, setpoint changes, faults.
- **Documents/standards:** P&IDs, electrical drawings, ladder logic version control (Rockwell Asset Centre, Versiondog), IEC 61131-3, IEC 62443 zoning.
- **Frequency:** Continuous operation; logic changes event-driven; firmware annually (planned outage).
- **Hand-offs:** Plant operations (downtime windows), MSHA (any change affecting safety interlocks may trigger plan revision).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Logic change made on Friday afternoon, no backup taken; engineer plugs laptop in via USB and bridges IT/OT; PLC battery dies and program lost on power-cycle.

### 5.2 HMI Workstations
- **What:** Operator workstations running FactoryTalk View SE, WonderWare/AVEVA InTouch, Ignition Vision/Perspective, Citect — in plant control room and mobile panels.
- **Who:** Control system engineer; plant operator uses.
- **Data captured:** Operator actions, screen navigation, alarm acks, shift handover notes.
- **Documents/standards:** HMI style guide (ISA-101), alarm management standard (ISA-18.2 / IEC 62682).
- **Frequency:** Continuous; HMI graphics changes event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Plant ops; engineering for revisions.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** HMI PC infected via USB drive used for log download; operator-shift screen orientation differs from another shift.

### 5.3 SCADA Servers (Wonderware/AVEVA, Ignition, Citect)
- **What:** Supervisory layer aggregating PLC data, providing trending, recipe management, batch/load reports.
- **Who:** Control system engineer / SCADA admin; OEM support.
- **Data captured:** Tag values, alarms, batch records, recipe versions, audit trail.
- **Documents/standards:** SCADA design spec, tag database, IEC 62443, NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (OT security).
- **Frequency:** Continuous; tag/recipe changes event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering, quality (recipe tied to product spec).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** SCADA license server runs out; tag overrun on poll group; SCADA crashes when historian disk full.

### 5.4 Process Historian (OSIsoft/AVEVA PI, Canary, GE Proficy, Ignition Historian)
- **What:** Time-series storage of all process tags; basis for production reports, KPIs, downtime analytics.
- **Who:** Historian admin; data engineer.
- **Data captured:** Compressed tag history, event frames, downtime reasons, tonnages.
- **Documents/standards:** Tag dictionary, compression/exception settings, retention policy.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly tag-quality audit.
- **Hand-offs:** Analytics team, production reporting, ESG/CO2 calc inputs.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Historian disk full causes tag drops; clock drift puts events in wrong order; tag deleted by mistake loses years of history if not backed up.

### 5.5 Belt Scale Electronics & Loadout Batch Weighing
- **What:** Conveyor belt scales (Thermo Ramsey, Siemens Milltronics, Tecweigh) integrating tons-shipped to dispatch and accounting; train-loadout batch weighing systems with scale houses for unit-train batch certification.
- **Who:** Plant electrician; weighmaster; QA for cert.
- **Data captured:** Tons per shift, belt scale calibration data, batch weights, certificate numbers.
- **Documents/standards:** NIST Handbook 44 weights & measures; state weights-and-measures certification (annual); MSHA / FRA / customer specs.
- **Frequency:** Continuous operation; calibration weekly check, monthly material test; annual W&M certification.
- **Hand-offs:** Accounting (revenue), sales (BOL), railroad (certified weights for billing).
- **State-specific:** WV, VA, KY each have weights-and-measures agencies; certified scale operator credentials may be required.
- **Edge cases:** Belt scale drift between calibrations; load-cell knocked out of alignment by mechanical impact; scale-house PC reboot during batch (lost weight).

### 5.6 Truck Scale Integrations (Mettler-Toledo, Rice Lake, Avery Weigh-Tronix, Cardinal)
- **What:** Static truck scales at coal pickup and at loadouts; ticketing software (TruckLogics, IntelliScale, vendor-supplied) integrating to ERP/AR/AP.
- **Who:** Weighmaster; site IT for network; vendor service for calibration.
- **Data captured:** Truck ID, tare, gross, net, BOL, hauler, ticket #, time-in/out.
- **Documents/standards:** NTEP/CC certificate per scale, state W&M annual cert, NIST Handbook 44.
- **Frequency:** Continuous use; annual W&M cert; monthly accuracy check.
- **Hand-offs:** Accounting, sales, hauler reconciliation.
- **State-specific:** State scale cert by Dept of Ag / W&M division in each state.
- **Edge cases:** Driver tares with body raised; LPR misreads, double-bills; scale indicator stuck after lightning.

### 5.7 Mine Ventilation & Atmospheric Monitoring
- **What:** Continuous CO, methane, O2 monitoring; fan status; air-velocity sensors; smoke detection — required by 30 CFR Part 75 Subpart D.
- **Who:** Mine examiner; vent foreman; MSHA-certified electrician for installation.
- **Data captured:** Gas concentrations, alarm events, fan RPM, pressure differential.
- **Documents/standards:** Approved vent plan (MSHA-filed), 30 CFR 75.351 atmospheric monitoring system (AMS), pre-shift exam records, weekly examiner books.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; pre-shift; weekly; monthly calibration; annual full vent survey.
- **Hand-offs:** Mine foreman, MSHA inspector, safety dept.
- **State-specific:** WV Office of Miners' Health, Safety & Training adds state plan; VA DMME (now DEE) has parallel state inspectors; KY OMSL.
- **Edge cases:** Sensor failure goes undetected (open circuit alarm); fan stoppage detected late; calibration gas expired.

### 5.8 Mine Personnel Tracking & Two-Way Communication (MSHA / MINER Act)
- **What:** Post-accident wireless two-way communication and electronic tracking required by the MINER Act of 2006 and 30 CFR 75.1600-3; deployed via leaky-feeder systems (Becker SmartCom, Varis MineConnect), mesh radio (Mine Site Technologies ImPact, Strata CommTrac/Strata Connect), or hybrid; tracking via RFID readers on tag boards and at strategic points underground.
- **Who:** Mine comms tech / electrical; control room dispatcher; mine foreman; safety director; MSHA approval coordinator.
- **Data captured:** Last-known location per miner, tag read events, two-way call logs, system health (battery, node up/down), 24-hour standby-power state.
- **Documents/standards:** MSHA Emergency Response Plan (ERP) per 30 CFR 75.1502; approval under 30 CFR Part 23 (intrinsic safety); standby power adequate for evacuation/rescue (typically 24 hours at 5/5/90 duty cycle per MSHA guidance); P14-V-01 Program Policy Letter; 30 CFR 75.1600-3.
- **Frequency:** Continuous operation; functional test each shift; weekly comprehensive; annual MSHA-witnessed test; ERP updated every 6 months.
- **Hand-offs:** MSHA District Manager (ERP approval); state mine safety agency (WV/VA/KY); mine rescue teams; family-notification liaison if emergency.
- **State-specific:** WV §22A-2-55 mirrors federal; some state requirements predate MINER Act and add state certifications for mine electricians installing the equipment; KY and VA align with federal; surface-only operations exempt from MINER Act tracking.
- **Edge cases:** Tracking system outage during a shift (per ERP, must address before continuing or evacuate per plan); leaky feeder cable severed by mining advance / roof fall; tag battery dies; miner forgets tag (recorded as "not in mine"); MSHA citation if system not on standby power.

### 5.9 Surface Mine Vehicle Radios & Trunked Dispatch
- **What:** UHF/VHF Motorola/Kenwood/Tait/Icom mobile and handheld radios for haul truck dispatch, drill, dozer, blasting crew, water truck; trunked DMR/P25 for larger operations.
- **Who:** Comms tech; dispatcher; radio shop vendor.
- **Data captured:** Channel list, talk-group assignments, radio IDs, GPS-over-radio location (if equipped).
- **Documents/standards:** FCC radio license (Part 90), narrowbanding compliance, ID-to-user assignment list.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly fleet audit; annual repeater PM.
- **Hand-offs:** Mine ops, safety, emergency.
- **State-specific:** WV/VA/KY mine emergency notification networks may overlay.
- **Edge cases:** Repeater fails mid-shift, channel co-existence with neighbor mine, lost/stolen radio not removed from group.

### 5.10 Mine Pager Phones, Call Boxes, PA / Mine-Wide Page
- **What:** Mine pager phone system (intrinsically safe phones along entries), emergency call boxes at portals, mine-wide page/PA for evacuation tones, surface PA at prep plant and loadout.
- **Who:** Mine electrician; safety dept.
- **Data captured:** Call records, page activations.
- **Documents/standards:** 30 CFR Part 23 (intrinsic safety), Part 75 communications requirements, monthly examination records.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; weekly functional check.
- **Hand-offs:** Mine emergency response.
- **State-specific:** WV, VA, KY each have state mine safety requirements layered on federal.
- **Edge cases:** Phone cable cut by mobile equipment; PA horn corroded silent; intrinsic safety compromised by unapproved repair.

### 5.11 Equipment Telematics (Mobile Fleet)
- **What:** OEM telematics platforms:
  - **Caterpillar:** Product Link + VisionLink (fleet management, performance, location).
  - **Komatsu:** KOMTRAX (surface) / KOMTRAX Plus (mining-class); My Komatsu mixed-fleet portal.
  - **Hitachi:** ConSite / Global e-Service; Wenco mine fleet management (Hitachi-owned) for haul-truck dispatch/payload.
  - **Sandvik:** OptiMine, My Sandvik.
  - **Liebherr:** LiDAT / LiData.
  - **Joy Global / Komatsu Mining (P&H, Joy underground):** JoySmart Solutions / Komatsu MineCare.
  - **Volvo:** CareTrack.
  - **John Deere:** JDLink (utility / surface support).
  - Mixed-fleet aggregators: Hexagon MinePlan, Trimble OpsManager, ISAAC, custom data lake via OEM APIs.
- **Who:** Fleet manager; maintenance planner; OEM dealer rep.
- **Data captured:** Hours, fuel, location, idle, payload, fault codes (J1939/CAN), DEF level, productivity (TPH, cycle times).
- **Documents/standards:** Data ownership clause in OEM purchase, telematics API access agreements, ISO 15143-3 (AEMP 2.0) for mixed-fleet.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; daily KPI reports; weekly maintenance planning.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance (CMMS work orders from fault codes), production reporting, finance (depreciation, capex planning), warranty admin.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** OEM portal data ownership disputes; cellular dead-zone (no upload until topside); time-sync drift skews cycle times; mixed-fleet integration breaks after OEM API change.

### 5.12 Drone Data Ingestion & Photogrammetry / LiDAR
- **What:** Routine drone (DJI Enterprise — M30T, M350 RTK; senseFly eBee; Skydio X10; Wingtra) flights for stockpile volumetrics, pit progression, pre/post-blast, refuse impoundment surveys, inspection. Processing in Pix4D, DroneDeploy, Bentley ContextCapture, Propeller Aero, Agisoft Metashape.
- **Who:** Licensed Part 107 remote pilot (often surveyor or mine engineer); GIS analyst.
- **Data captured:** Imagery, point clouds, DSMs, orthomosaics, volumetric reports, change-detection.
- **Documents/standards:** FAA Part 107 pilot certificate, waiver if BVLOS/night, pre-flight log, MSHA "Drone Operations" approval where over active mine workings, no-fly compliance.
- **Frequency:** Stockpile monthly; pit progression weekly/biweekly; impoundment quarterly.
- **Hand-offs:** Survey, engineering, accounting (inventory tons), regulatory (impoundment cert).
- **State-specific:** None directly, but state-specific impoundment cert thresholds may set drone-survey frequency.
- **Edge cases:** Drone loses GPS in pit walls; SD card corruption loses flight; DJI geo-fencing locks out near airport; vendor cloud (DJI servers in China) data sovereignty concerns.

### 5.13 Mining Design & Geological Software
- **What:** Carlson Mining, Hexagon MinePlan (formerly MineSight), Maptek Vulcan, Seequent Leapfrog Geo, Datamine, Surpac, AutoCAD Civil 3D for mine design, geological modeling, reserve estimation.
- **Who:** Mine engineer; geologist; surveyor.
- **Data captured:** Block models, drill-hole DB, reserves, design files, surface DTMs.
- **Documents/standards:** SK-1300 / NI 43-101 reserve disclosure (where public), license entitlements, master CAD standards.
- **Frequency:** Continuous use; monthly mine plan update; quarterly reserve refresh; annual reserves report.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance (reserves into LOM and depletion), operations (short-term plan to dispatch), permitting (mine plan supports applications).
- **State-specific:** Mine plans for permits per WV/VA/KY/AL/TN regulatory.
- **Edge cases:** License server outage halts engineering; CAD file corruption; version-skew between offices.

### 5.14 Survey Instruments (GPS/RTK, Total Stations)
- **What:** Trimble, Leica, Topcon RTK rovers, base stations, total stations; corrections via base, network RTK, or CORS.
- **Who:** Mine surveyor (often state-licensed Professional Surveyor for stamped maps).
- **Data captured:** Survey points, breaklines, stamped maps, monument coordinates.
- **Documents/standards:** State-licensed surveyor stamp, mine-map filing requirements (state mine map office), MSHA mine-map currency (monthly per 30 CFR 75.1200).
- **Frequency:** Daily field use; monthly mine map update; annual permit map refresh.
- **Hand-offs:** Engineering, permitting, regulators (mine map filing).
- **State-specific:** WV Office of Miners' Health Safety & Training mine map office; VA DEE; KY DMRE; required filings frequency varies.
- **Edge cases:** Base station coordinate shift goes undetected; instrument drops & loses calibration; cellular RTK correction dead-zone.

### 5.15 Conveyor & Belt Monitoring (Beltavision, CCTV+AI, Splice Monitoring)
- **What:** Visual + thermal monitoring of conveyors for rock damage, mis-tracking, belt tears, hot bearings, splice integrity; rip-detection sensors (Bridgestone/Continental).
- **Who:** Maintenance planner; control room operator.
- **Data captured:** Belt speed, tracking offset, IR temps, splice condition, rip-detect events.
- **Documents/standards:** MSHA conveyor safety standards (Part 75 Subpart R for underground, 77 surface), manufacturer thresholds.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; daily walkdown; quarterly splice inspection.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance (work order on alarm), safety.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Camera lens coated with coal dust hides defect; false rip-detect causes nuisance trips; thermal sensor sees ambient sun instead of bearing.

### 5.16 Pump, Fan, Substation, Generator, Compressor Telemetry
- **What:** Telemetry on dewatering pumps (level, runtime, current), main fans, mine substations (voltage, current, power factor), gensets (runtime, fuel), air compressors at shops and underground.
- **Who:** Plant electrician; site maintenance; SCADA admin.
- **Data captured:** Run state, runtime hours, alarms, energy consumption.
- **Documents/standards:** Electrical drawings, MSHA Part 75 Subpart F (substations), NESC.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; daily walkdown; monthly recorded readings.
- **Hand-offs:** Maintenance, energy management.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Pump runs dry (cavitation), no alarm; generator runs out of fuel during outage; sub PT/CT failure under-reports load.

### 5.17 Refuse Impoundment Instrumentation
- **What:** Piezometers (phreatic surface), settlement monuments, inclinometers, flow measurement at decant, freeboard sensors; tied to MSHA-required impoundment hazard plan and 5-yr cert by professional engineer.
- **Who:** Geotechnical engineer (PE); environmental tech; surveyor for monuments.
- **Data captured:** Piezometer pressures, monument positions, freeboard, pond elevation.
- **Documents/standards:** MSHA 30 CFR Part 77 / Part 50; PE-certified impoundment plan; SMCRA bond; state dam-safety where applicable; OSMRE annual inspection.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly read minimum; weekly during high-water; annual cert; 5-year MSHA cert.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental, regulatory, exec (any anomaly).
- **State-specific:** WV DEP Dam Safety, VA DCR Dam Safety, KY DOW Dam Safety overlay where state-classified high-hazard.
- **Edge cases:** Piezometer reads zero (failed) misinterpreted as low phreatic; survey monument disturbed by equipment; sensor data gap during storm event.

### 5.18 Continuous Emission Monitoring (CEMS) & Opacity
- **What:** Where Title V or state air permits require — stack CEMS (NOx, SO2, CO, O2, opacity) on coal dryers, boilers; data acquisition system (DAS) and EPA-format quarterly excess emission reports.
- **Who:** Environmental engineer; CEMS service vendor for cert and quarterly audits.
- **Data captured:** Pollutant concentrations, opacity %, calibration cycles, downtime, excess emissions.
- **Documents/standards:** 40 CFR Part 60 App. F (QA), 40 CFR Part 75 Subpart B (Acid Rain), EPA ECMPS submittals, state air agency CMS plan.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; daily calibration; quarterly RATA; annual cert.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental compliance, state air agency, EPA via ECMPS.
- **State-specific:** WV DEP DAQ, VA DEQ Air, KY EEC Air rules each have minor variants.
- **Edge cases:** Calibration drift uncaught; data acquisition gap (must be flagged as missing); CEM analyzer fails QA — emissions calculated by alternate method.

### 5.19 Water Level / Flow Telemetry — Outfalls, Sediment Ponds, Sample Stations
- **What:** Telemetered level sensors, V-notch weirs with flow loggers, conductivity/pH continuous probes at NPDES outfalls; sample-collector controllers (ISCO, Teledyne).
- **Who:** Environmental tech; water-quality engineer.
- **Data captured:** Stage, flow, conductivity, pH, sample-collection events, rainfall.
- **Documents/standards:** NPDES permit conditions, WV/VA/KY DEP-specific monitoring plans, eDMR submittals.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; daily check; monthly DMR; permit-specific.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental compliance (DMR submission), permitting.
- **State-specific:** WV's selenium and conductivity scrutiny; VA's TDS/TMDL; KY similar.
- **Edge cases:** Probe fouled; battery dies in remote sampler; sample bottles freeze; sensor data interruption during a violation event (defensibility).

### 5.20 Laboratory Instrument Data / LIMS
- **What:** Lab info management system tying sample collection → instrument data (XRF, calorimeter, sulfur analyzer, moisture, ash) → certificate of analysis (CoA) for coal quality and environmental samples.
- **Who:** Lab tech; quality manager; LIMS admin.
- **Data captured:** Sample IDs, instrument readouts, results, QC reference standards, CoA.
- **Documents/standards:** ASTM D4239 (sulfur), D5865 (calorific), D3173 (moisture), D3174 (ash), D3176 (ultimate); ISO 17025 if accredited.
- **Frequency:** Per-sample; QC standards daily; instrument calibration per ASTM cadence.
- **Hand-offs:** Customers (CoA delivered with shipment), sales (price adjustments), regulatory (NPDES sample results).
- **State-specific:** None for ASTM but state-certified labs for some NPDES sample types (state lab cert program).
- **Edge cases:** Sample mix-up; instrument out of cert; data manipulated by operator (LIMS audit trail material).

## 6. OT/IT Convergence & IIoT

### 6.1 Purdue Model Segmentation
- **What:** Network zoning per ISA-95/ISA-99: Levels 0–1 (field, control), Level 2 (supervisory), Level 3 (manufacturing ops), Level 3.5 (DMZ), Levels 4–5 (enterprise).
- **Who:** OT/ICS security engineer; network engineer; control system engineer.
- **Documents/standards:** ISA/IEC 62443, NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3.
- **Frequency:** Architecture review annual.
- **Hand-offs:** All OT/IT.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Vendor laptop bridges levels; "temporary" rule that becomes permanent; new IIoT sensor publishes direct to cloud, bypassing DMZ.

### 6.2 IT/OT DMZ & Data Diodes
- **What:** Industrial DMZ with replicated historian, jump host, AV update relay; unidirectional gateways (Owl, Waterfall) for crown-jewel asset egress only.
- **Who:** OT security engineer.
- **Documents/standards:** IEC 62443-3-3, vendor architecture docs.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly rule review.
- **Hand-offs:** Plant ops, enterprise data team.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Replication lag breaks enterprise reports; diode firmware update; bypass cable for a "quick fix."

### 6.3 IIoT Platforms / Edge Gateways
- **What:** PTC ThingWorx, AVEVA Insight, GE Predix, AWS IoT, Azure IoT Hub/Edge for connecting field assets to cloud analytics; edge gateways (Stratus ztC Edge, Dell Edge, Moxa) for buffering.
- **Who:** IIoT/data engineer.
- **Documents/standards:** OPC UA over MQTT (Sparkplug B), MQTT broker hardening.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Data team, OT.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Broker offline; cert pinning issue; cloud-vendor cost surprise.

### 6.4 Time-Series DBs & Dashboards
- **What:** InfluxDB, TimescaleDB, AVEVA PI System / PI Vision; Grafana, Power BI for real-time dashboards.
- **Who:** Data engineer; analytics team.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Ops, executives.
- **Edge cases:** Tag rename breaks dashboards; retention policy purges data needed for incident review.

### 7.2 Mine Pager Phones / Emergency Call Boxes / PA
- See 5.10.

### 7.3 Underground Leaky-Feeder / Mesh / Wired-Node Tracking System
- See 5.8.

### 7.4 Trunked Dispatch Radio
- See 5.9.

### 7.6 Surface Telephony / UC
- **What:** Microsoft Teams Phone / Cisco Webex Calling / RingCentral / Zoom Phone for office voice; analog/POTS for fax-required workflows (still used for some banking/regulator); SBCs for SIP trunking.
- **Who:** UC admin; help desk.
- **Data captured:** Call records (CDR), voicemails, conference details, e911 location.
- **Documents/standards:** Kari's Law / RAY BAUM's Act (direct 911 dial + dispatchable location), FCC requirements.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly e911 location verification.
- **Hand-offs:** Facilities (location info), HR (user onboarding).
- **State-specific:** Some states have stricter e911 obligations (Kari's Law is federal floor).
- **Edge cases:** E911 routes to wrong PSAP; user moves desk and location stale; PSTN outage when fax to bank required.

## 8. Cybersecurity Program

### 8.1 SIEM / Log Aggregation
- **What:** Microsoft Sentinel / Splunk / Elastic / LogRhythm collecting AD, M365, EDR, firewall, VPN, cloud, SaaS, OT historian audit logs.
- **Who:** Security analyst (SOC); SIEM engineer; MSSP may be co-managed.
- **Data captured:** Log sources, ingestion volume (EPS/GB), detections, incident counts.
- **Documents/standards:** Log source inventory, detection-as-code repo, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, NIST SP 800-92.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; weekly tune; monthly source coverage audit.
- **Hand-offs:** IR lead, legal (preservation), HR.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Critical source silently stopped logging; alert fatigue; license cap exceeded; OT log volume swamps SIEM after Purdue tap added.

### 8.2 EDR / XDR
- **What:** CrowdStrike Falcon / SentinelOne / Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on all servers and endpoints; managed-threat-hunting subscription typical.
- **Who:** Security analyst; help desk for deployment.
- **Data captured:** Process telemetry, file events, network telemetry, detections, response actions.
- **Documents/standards:** EDR coverage report, exclusion list (OT-specific exclusions), playbook for containment.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; weekly exclusion review.
- **Hand-offs:** Help desk (re-image), IR lead.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** EDR blocks SCADA process — outage; uninstalled by tech during troubleshooting and not re-enrolled; coverage gap on OT host that "can't" run agent.

### 8.3 Firewall Management
- **What:** Palo Alto / Fortinet / Cisco FTD perimeters at HQ, DC, each major site; cloud firewalls; internal segmentation; IDS/IPS modules.
- **Who:** Network/security engineer.
- **Data captured:** Rules, hit counters, threat logs, IDS alerts.
- **Documents/standards:** Firewall policy review (quarterly per PCI/NIST), rule-change request form, IEC 62443 zones-and-conduits.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly rule audit; semi-annual penetration test.
- **Hand-offs:** Change board, ops.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Stale rules permitting decommissioned IP; "any-any" temporary; bypass tunnel created by tech.

### 8.4 DLP (Data Loss Prevention) & CASB
- **What:** Microsoft Purview / Symantec DLP / Forcepoint scanning for PII, reserves data, customer pricing in email/file/cloud; CASB (Defender for Cloud Apps, Netskope) for SaaS shadow IT and policy.
- **Who:** Security engineer; data steward.
- **Data captured:** Policy violations, blocked transfers, sanctioned-app catalog.
- **Documents/standards:** Data classification policy, DLP rule library.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; monthly tuning.
- **Hand-offs:** Legal (egress events), HR.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Geologist exports reserves to personal Dropbox; encrypted file slips DLP; CASB miscategorizes app.

### 8.5 Privileged Access Management (PAM) & Secrets
- **What:** CyberArk / BeyondTrust / Delinea for admin credential vaulting, session recording, JIT access; HashiCorp Vault / AKV / AWS SSM for app secrets.
- **Who:** Security engineer.
- **Data captured:** Privileged sessions, credential check-out, password rotations, secrets audit.
- **Documents/standards:** Privileged access policy, NIST SP 800-53 AC-6, session recordings retention.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly access review.
- **Hand-offs:** Audit, HR.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Shared local admin not vaulted; service account password in script repo; vendor RDP without PAM.

### 8.6 Identity Governance, Conditional Access, Quarterly Access Reviews
- **What:** Entra ID conditional-access policies (location, device, risk-based), Entra access reviews / SailPoint / Saviynt for periodic certification.
- **Who:** IAM engineer; managers as reviewers.
- **Data captured:** Access certifications, revocations, role assignments.
- **Documents/standards:** Access review policy, segregation-of-duties matrix.
- **Frequency:** Quarterly access reviews; continuous CA evaluation.
- **Hand-offs:** Managers, HR, internal audit.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Rubber-stamp reviews; departing user retains access for weeks; contractor extended without re-cert.

### 8.7 NIST CSF / IEC 62443 Maturity & Compliance Frameworks
- **What:** Annual self-assessment against NIST CSF 2.0 (and IEC 62443 for OT); roadmap to close gaps; SOC 2 readiness for SCC-OS itself; CMMC if DoD-adjacent revenue.
- **Who:** CISO/security director; outside assessor.
- **Documents/standards:** NIST CSF 2.0, IEC 62443-2-1 / -3-3, NIST SP 800-171 (CUI), CMMC L2 if applicable, SOC 2.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Exec, board, customers requesting attestation.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Maturity score regression after staffing change; OT gaps unaddressed because no OT-specific assessor used.

### 8.8 Tabletop Exercises & Incident Response
- **What:** Tabletop exercises (ransomware on prep plant SCADA, BEC against finance, data-leak via departing geologist) plus written IR plan and on-call rotation; retainer with IR firm (Mandiant / CrowdStrike Services / Unit 42).
- **Who:** IR lead; cross-functional (legal, comms, HR, ops, OT).
- **Documents/standards:** IR plan, playbooks per scenario, retainer agreement, after-action report.
- **Frequency:** Tabletops semi-annual; full IR test annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Legal, exec, board, insurance.
- **State-specific:** State notification laws (WV §46A-2A-101 et seq. "without unreasonable delay"; VA §18.2-186.6; KY KRS 365.732; AL §8-38-1 et seq. 45 days; TN §47-18-2107 45 days).
- **Edge cases:** Cyber insurer mandates use of their breach-counsel; OT incident requires MSHA notification; multi-state breach notification timing conflicts.

### 8.9 Phishing Simulation & Security Awareness Training
- **What:** KnowBe4 / Proofpoint Security Awareness / Microsoft Attack Simulation; monthly phish + quarterly training; mining-specific scenarios (fake equipment-recall email, fake bank wire change).
- **Who:** Security awareness lead.
- **Data captured:** Click rates, report rates, training completion.
- **Documents/standards:** Awareness training program; HR discipline matrix for repeat clickers.
- **Frequency:** Monthly sim; quarterly training; annual KnowBe4 maturity.
- **Hand-offs:** HR for compliance and discipline.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Click rate spikes after vacation; training compliance low at remote sites; senior exec opted out.

### 8.10 Vendor / Third-Party Risk Management
- **What:** Security review of new SaaS / hosted vendor; SIG-Lite, CAIQ, SOC 2 / ISO 27001 review; ongoing rating (BitSight, SecurityScorecard).
- **Who:** Vendor risk analyst.
- **Data captured:** Vendor risk register, residual-risk rating, DPA on file, breach notification clause.
- **Documents/standards:** Vendor onboarding checklist, DPA template, BAA if any health data, MSA security exhibits.
- **Frequency:** Pre-contract; annual re-review for critical vendors.
- **Hand-offs:** Legal, procurement.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Vendor sub-processors not disclosed; SOC 2 expired; vendor breach (Snowflake-style) hits Southern Coal data.

### 8.11 Penetration Testing / Red Team / Purple Team
- **What:** Annual external + internal pen test; periodic red-team simulation; purple-team detection-building.
- **Who:** External pentest firm; SOC engineer.
- **Documents/standards:** SoW, Rules of Engagement, scope, retest, executive report.
- **Frequency:** Annual.
- **Hand-offs:** Remediation owners.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Pentest causes OT outage if not properly scoped; finding not closed before next year.

### 8.12 Backup Immutability & Ransomware Resilience
- **What:** Immutable / air-gap backups (object lock, tape vault, hardened repo), tested restore at scale; defined RTO/RPO; cyber-insurance-mandated controls.
- **Who:** Backup admin + security.
- **Documents/standards:** Backup policy, immutability proof, cyber-insurance attestation.
- **Frequency:** Annual full DR test; quarterly partial.
- **Hand-offs:** Insurance carrier, exec.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Backup repo creds in same domain as attacker; attacker dwells long enough to corrupt immutability window.

### 8.13 Threat Intelligence / CISA Alerts / KEV
- **What:** Subscriptions (CrowdStrike, Recorded Future, Mandiant); CISA AA alerts and KEV catalog tracked; E-ISAC for any owned generation/substation that interconnects.
- **Who:** Security analyst.
- **Documents/standards:** CISA KEV, MITRE ATT&CK, sector-specific advisories.
- **Frequency:** Daily.
- **Hand-offs:** Patch ops on KEV hits.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Mining lacks its own ISAC; reliance on cross-sector intel; E-ISAC membership requires utility/co-op status.

### 8.14 Cyber Insurance Compliance
- **What:** Annual application requires MFA, EDR, backups, training, IR plan, segmentation; broker-led renewals; control attestation.
- **Who:** Risk manager + CISO + broker.
- **Data captured:** Premium, limits, sublimits (ransomware, social engineering), retention, panel counsel, breach hotline.
- **Documents/standards:** Application, binder, IR contacts.
- **Frequency:** Annual renewal.
- **Hand-offs:** Finance, exec, legal.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Misrepresented control causes claim denial; sublimit on ransomware too low.

### 8.15 Joiner / Mover / Leaver (Account Provisioning & Deprovisioning)
- **What:** HR-triggered automation for account creation on hire, role change on transfer, deprovisioning on termination; same-day exec offboard.
- **Who:** IAM + HR.
- **Data captured:** Tickets, SLA timings, orphaned-account scan.
- **Documents/standards:** JML playbook, term-checklist.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven; weekly orphan audit.
- **Hand-offs:** HR ↔ IT ↔ Manager.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Contractor account left active; mover keeps old + new permissions (SoD); term not communicated to IT.

### 8.16 Audit Log Retention
- **What:** Defined retention (typically 1-yr hot / 7-yr cold for finance-relevant) for AD, M365 unified audit log, firewall, EDR.
- **Who:** SIEM engineer; legal sets retention.
- **Documents/standards:** Retention schedule; M365 audit retention SKU; legal hold policy.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Legal, audit.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Default M365 90-day retention insufficient; SIEM retention drops mid-investigation.

## 9. Data Governance, Data Platform, BI

### 9.1 Master Data Management
- **What:** Authoritative records for Employee, Customer, Vendor, Equipment, Mine, Permit, GL Account, Chart of Accounts, UoM/Codes.
- **Who:** Data steward per domain; MDM engineer.
- **Documents/standards:** MDM policy, golden-record rules, survivorship logic, DAMA-DMBOK.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** All consuming apps.
- **Edge cases:** Duplicate customer in CRM and ERP; equipment renamed without history continuity; mine renumbered after permit change.

### 9.2 Data Catalog & Lineage
- **What:** Collibra / Alation / Atlan / Microsoft Purview catalog of datasets with lineage, ownership, sensitivity.
- **Who:** Data governance lead.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly governance council.
- **Edge cases:** Shadow datasets not cataloged; lineage broken after Fivetran reconfig.

### 9.3 Data Quality Monitoring
- **What:** Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, dbt tests checking freshness, null rates, schema drift on key tables.
- **Who:** Data engineer.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** SLA missed silently; alert fatigue; producer-side schema change.

### 9.4 Data Warehouse / Lakehouse
- **What:** Snowflake / Databricks / Synapse / BigQuery for analytics; bronze/silver/gold zones; dbt models.
- **Who:** Data engineer; analytics engineer.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; daily/hourly loads.
- **Edge cases:** Cost runaway; PII unintentionally in clear; query concurrency hits limits.

### 9.5 ETL / ELT (Fivetran, Stitch, Airbyte, dbt, ADF)
- **What:** Pipelines from ERP, CRM, HRIS, LIMS, historians, telematics, SaaS apps into warehouse.
- **Who:** Data engineer.
- **Frequency:** Hourly/daily.
- **Edge cases:** Source API rate-limit; pipeline backfill duplicates rows; credential rotation breaks pipeline.

### 9.6 BI / Self-Service Analytics
- **What:** Power BI / Tableau / Looker; semantic model; certified datasets vs. self-service workspace.
- **Who:** BI lead; business analyst.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** Two reports same KPI, different numbers; row-level security gap; "PROD-final-v4" file persistence.

### 9.7 Data Sharing Agreements
- **What:** Outbound shares with customers (coal-quality data), banks (financial covenants), sureties (bond data), auditors, regulators.
- **Who:** Legal + data governance.
- **Documents/standards:** Data sharing agreements, NDAs, SFTP credentials inventory.
- **Frequency:** Event-driven.
- **Edge cases:** Recipient mishandles data; share retained past project end.

## 11. Integrations

### 11.1 API Management
- **What:** Mulesoft / Azure API Management / Kong / Apigee for internal API gateway; OAuth 2.0; rate-limit.
- **Who:** Integration engineer.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** Quota exhaustion; expired client secret breaks integration.

### 11.2 iPaaS
- **What:** Workato / Boomi / Zapier / Power Automate; citizen-developer governance.
- **Who:** Integration engineer; business power-users.
- **Edge cases:** Personal Zapier account on personal email used for prod flow.

### 11.3 EDI
- **What:** EDI with railroads (BNSF, CSX, NS, KCS) — 404 (Rail Carrier Shipment), 410 (freight invoice), 417 (Rail Carrier Waybill), 161 (Train Sheet); customer EDI for orders/invoices.
- **Who:** EDI analyst; SC/A.
- **Documents/standards:** ANSI X12, Railinc-mediated for rail, AS2/SFTP transport.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** Trading partner upgrades version; 997 functional ack not received; mapping breaks after partner field addition.

### 11.4 File Transfer
- **What:** Managed file transfer (MOVEit, GoAnywhere, Cleo, Globalscape EFT) for bank H2H, customer, regulator submissions.
- **Who:** Integration engineer.
- **Documents/standards:** PGP keys, SFTP creds inventory; cipher hardening.
- **Edge cases:** MOVEit-style supply-chain breach exposes shared file repository.

### 11.5 Banking Integrations
- **What:** H2H file exchange for ACH, positive pay, lockbox; Plaid for app-side connectivity; SWIFT for wires (rare).
- **Who:** Treasury + IT.
- **Documents/standards:** BAI2, NACHA, bank-specific file specs.
- **Edge cases:** Positive pay file misses by 1 min and check rejects; ACH return file unprocessed.

- **What:** ServiceNow / Jira Service Mgmt / Freshservice / Halo ITSM for ticket intake, SLA tracking, knowledge base.

- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** Mine site has no signal; phone-only intake at remote office; major incident not declared in time.

### 12.2 Change & Configuration Management (CMDB)
- **What:** Change Advisory Board, CAB calendar; CMDB with CIs, relationships, owners.
- **Who:** Change manager; CMDB owner.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; weekly CAB.
- **Edge cases:** Emergency change without CAB; stale CMDB.

### 12.3 New User Onboarding & Training

- **Who:** Help desk; HR; manager.
- **Frequency:** Per hire.
- **Edge cases:** Hire starts at remote site with no IT presence; equipment arrives day 3.

### 12.4 BYOD / Remote Work
- **What:** BYOD policy with MAM (Intune App Protection) on personal phones; remote-work stipend; home-internet eligibility rules.
- **Who:** Security + HR.
- **Edge cases:** Personal phone compromised holds corp email; offshore remote worker accesses M365 from non-allowed geo.

## 14. Physical Security, Surveillance & Access Control

### 14.1 Site Fencing & Perimeter Alarms
- **What:** Chain-link or anti-climb fence around critical areas (substation, fuel, magazine, prep plant control), with PIR / fiber-optic disturbance sensors at sensitive perimeters.
- **Who:** Facilities; security director; alarm vendor.
- **Data captured:** Alarm events, daily walks.
- **Documents/standards:** SCC site security plan; MSHA Part 56/57 site security where applicable; ATF magazine setback (per type).
- **Frequency:** Continuous; daily walk; quarterly fence inspection.
- **Hand-offs:** Local LE.
- **State-specific:** Coal-yard theft is a significant issue in some KY/WV regions — additional perimeter measures common.
- **Edge cases:** Fence cut for scrap-metal theft; alarm panel beaten by lightning; nuisance alarms (wildlife).

### 14.2 Gates with Access Control (Vehicle / Pedestrian)
- **What:** Manned or swipe-card vehicle gates at site entry; pedestrian turnstile at offices; gate operators (Doorking, LiftMaster, FAAC) integrated to ACS.
- **Who:** Security; site safety; ACS admin.
- **Data captured:** Credential reads, vehicle classification, exception entries.
- **Documents/standards:** Gate operator UL 325 compliance; ACS policy.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Visitor mgmt, time & attendance.
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Tailgating; gate fails in open position; credential lent.

### 14.3 Guard Stations / Contract Security
- **What:** Where used (high-value loadout, critical infrastructure, after-incident posture) — contract security (Allied Universal, Securitas, regional firm).
- **Who:** Security director; contracted firm.
- **Data captured:** Guard tour reports (DETEX or app), incident reports, daily activity reports.
- **Documents/standards:** Post orders, state guard licensing (WV/VA/KY/AL/TN all license private security).
- **Frequency:** Per posting hours.
- **Hand-offs:** Local LE, exec.
- **State-specific:** State guard licensing & armed-officer requirements vary; WV/VA/KY have stricter armed-guard licensing than the regional norm.
- **Edge cases:** Guard sleeping; armed guard with lapsed license; vendor misclassifies hours.

### 14.4 Visitor Management
- **What:** Envoy / Sine / SwipedOn / Genetec ClearID for visitor pre-registration, NDA acknowledgment, MSHA "Part 46" contractor verification, ID scan, badge print.
- **Who:** Receptionist; safety dept; security.
- **Data captured:** Visitor name, host, time-in/out, vehicle, MSHA training status, NDA accepted.
- **Documents/standards:** 30 CFR Part 46/48 contractor training; SCC visitor policy.
- **Frequency:** Per visit.
- **Hand-offs:** Safety (orientation), security (badge), host.
- **State-specific:** None additional.
- **Edge cases:** Contractor with expired Part 46/48 admitted; visitor wanders unescorted.

### 14.5 Time & Attendance / Badge-In Kiosks
- **What:** Biometric / RFID kiosks at site entry feeding HRIS for hourly time, integrated with mine personnel-tracking when underground.
- **Who:** HR/payroll; IT.
- **Data captured:** Clock-in/out, breaks, exceptions.
- **Documents/standards:** FLSA / state wage law; biometric privacy considerations.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** Payroll.
- **State-specific:** While none of the 5 SCC states has a strict BIPA-style law (IL-only), reasonable consent for biometrics still best practice.
- **Edge cases:** Buddy-punching; kiosk offline at shift change creates manual entries; biometric template breach.

### 14.6 Coal Yard / Loadout Theft Prevention
- **What:** Cameras, LPR at scales, GPS asset trackers, lighting, gate control, employee BG checks; coordination with state LE.
- **Who:** Security; loadout manager; weighmaster.
- **Documents/standards:** Internal theft policy; chain-of-custody on tickets.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Hand-offs:** LE; insurance.
- **State-specific:** Coal theft is a known persistent issue in parts of KY/WV; some state laws (KY) categorize coal theft specifically.
- **Edge cases:** Inside job at scale house; truck swap (LPR on cab, swap trailer); ghost tickets.

### 14.7 Explosive Magazine Security (ATF)
- **What:** Type 1/2/4 magazines per 27 CFR Part 555 Subpart K (Storage) — construction per §555.207/208/210, locking per §555.205, theft-or-loss reporting within 24 hours per §555.30, daily inspection logs, magazine inventory.
- **Who:** Blasting supervisor (state-licensed blaster); ATF Responsible Person; safety; security.
- **Data captured:** Magazine inventory, daily inspection log, receipt/issuance records, theft/loss reports.
- **Documents/standards:** 27 CFR Part 555 (esp. Subparts G, K); ATF license/permit; ATF Form 5400.5 (theft/loss); MSHA blasting plan; state blaster's license (WV §22A-6, VA, KY each).
- **Frequency:** Daily inspection; per-issuance log; immediate (24-hr) theft report; ATF inspection roughly every 3 years.
- **Hand-offs:** ATF (theft notification: 1-800-800-3855), local LE, MSHA, state mine agency.
- **State-specific:** WV, VA, KY, AL, TN all have additional state blasting laws and licensing (WV WV Office of Explosives & Blasting; VA DPOR; KY OMSL; AL State Fire Marshal; TN OSHA).
- **Edge cases:** Magazine inventory short by 1 cap = federal reportable; lock damaged; alarm fail (must add staffing); magazine encroached by mining setback.

### 14.8 Substation / Fuel Storage / Critical Asset Security
- **What:** Anti-climb fence, locked gate, intrusion sensors, cameras with analytics, lighting.
- **Who:** Facilities; security.
- **Documents/standards:** NESC for substation; SPCC plan for fuel; UL 142 tanks; state fire-marshal rules.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; monthly inspection.
- **Hand-offs:** Environmental (any spill), LE.
- **State-specific:** State fire-marshal AST permits vary.
- **Edge cases:** Copper theft from substation; fuel-tank theft with siphon; vandal damages SCADA in substation.

### 14.9 Office Building Access Control
- **What:** HID / Genetec Synergis / Brivo / Lenel OnGuard / Software House CCURE / Avigilon Alta with card readers, mobile credentials, door schedules, anti-passback.
- **Who:** ACS admin; security.
- **Data captured:** Door events, schedules, badge inventory, after-hours access.
- **Documents/standards:** SCC access policy; ACS admin guide.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly badge audit; annual schedule review.
- **Hand-offs:** HR (badge issue/return).
- **State-specific:** None.
- **Edge cases:** Terminated employee badge still active; door propped open; controller offline doesn't fail-safe properly.

### 14.10 Biometric Readers
- **What:** Fingerprint / face readers at high-sensitivity doors and time-clock kiosks.
- **Who:** ACS admin.
- **Documents/standards:** Biometric retention/consent policy; while no SCC state has BIPA, follow it as best-practice; SCC consent form.
- **Edge cases:** Coal dust fouls fingerprint reader; face reader fails with PPE.

### 14.11 License Plate Recognition (LPR) at Gates
- **What:** Genetec AutoVu / Vigilant Solutions / Avigilon LPR at scale-house gates linked to ACS and ticketing.
- **Who:** Security + scale-house ops.
- **Edge cases:** Misread on muddy plate; out-of-state plate not in DB; LPR camera coated in dust.

### 14.12 Drone Monitoring / Counter-UAS
- **What:** Emerging — DroneShield / Dedrone detection of unauthorized drones near sensitive areas (impoundment, magazine); active counter-measures generally not legal for private operators per current FAA/FCC rules.
- **Who:** Security director; safety; legal.
- **Documents/standards:** FAA 49 USC §40103, 18 USC §32; CISA C-UAS guidance for non-federal operators.
- **Frequency:** Where deployed, continuous; otherwise event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** Local LE; FAA.
- **State-specific:** State trespass-by-drone laws vary; WV has aerial-trespass language, KY/VA evolving.
- **Edge cases:** Unauthorized drone over impoundment during emergency; can't legally jam or shoot down.

### 14.13 Asset GPS Trackers
- **What:** Hidden trackers (Cake, AirTag, Samsara, Geotab, Bouncie) on high-value mobile assets, fuel trailers, water trucks for theft recovery.
- **Who:** Security; fleet manager.
- **Edge cases:** Battery dies; thief jams cellular; tracker in wrong asset.

### 14.14 Surveillance / VMS (NVR, AI-enhanced)
- **What:** Video management system (OpenEye Web Services, Genetec Security Center, Milestone XProtect, Avigilon Alta/ACC, Hanwha Wisenet WAVE, Hikvision HikCentral, Verkada, Rhombus) with cameras at perimeter, scale houses, loadouts, prep plant, fuel, magazine, office; AI analytics (DragonFruit AI, BriefCam, Calipsa, Ambient.ai) for theft, loitering, PPE compliance.
- **Who:** Security director; site IT; VMS admin; AI analytics ops.
- **Data captured:** Continuous video, motion clips, analytics events, retention per camera (typically 30–90 days; 180+ for cases pending), license-plate captures.
- **Documents/standards:** Camera coverage plan, retention schedule, evidence chain-of-custody, NDAA Section 889 compliance for federally adjacent contracts (Hikvision/Dahua restrictions).
- **Frequency:** Continuous record; daily health check; quarterly camera-coverage review.
- **Hand-offs:** Legal (subpoena/evidence), HR (employee incidents), LE (criminal).
- **State-specific:** WV/VA/KY follow standard subpoena process; recording-consent (two-party) varies but video is generally fine in workplace with notice.
- **Edge cases:** Camera offline at moment of incident; subpoena for footage past retention; AI false-positive flagging legitimate worker; NDAA-banned camera procured by site IT not knowing.

## 15. Emergency / Safety Communications

### 15.1 Mass Notification System
- **What:** Everbridge / Rave Mobile Safety / AlertMedia / OnSolve for mine-site emergencies, severe weather, recall to shelter, evacuations.
- **Who:** Emergency mgmt coordinator; safety director.
- **Data captured:** Contact list (multi-channel: SMS, voice, email, app push), acknowledgment, delivery results.
- **Documents/standards:** Emergency notification plan; updated contact data from HRIS.
- **Frequency:** Continuous standby; quarterly test; event-driven.
- **Hand-offs:** HR (contact list), HSE.
- **State-specific:** None additional.
- **Edge cases:** Stale contact data misses critical employee; vendor outage during real event; opt-out by employee.

### 15.2 Severe Weather Alerting
- **What:** Subscription weather services (DTN, AccuWeather Professional, WeatherSentry, Earth Networks lightning) for lightning, tornado, wind, severe storm at each site.
- **Who:** Safety; site superintendent.
- **Documents/standards:** Lightning shutdown policy (e.g., 10-mile rule at fueling), weather plan.
- **Frequency:** Continuous.
- **Edge cases:** Lightning detected but radios down; tornado warning at mine portal.

### 15.3 Mine Emergency Notification Trees & Crisis Comms
- **What:** Written emergency call trees (MSHA contacts, state mine agency, families, exec, PR), crisis-communication playbook integrating with corporate comms team.
- **Who:** Safety director; HR; exec; outside PR.
- **Documents/standards:** ERP (Emergency Response Plan per 30 CFR 75.1502); state agency notification (WV §22A-2; VA §45.2; KY KRS Ch.351); MSHA 15-minute notification rule (30 CFR Part 50.10) for serious accidents.
- **Frequency:** Annual drill; updated after any change.
- **Hand-offs:** MSHA, state mine agency, family liaison, PR, legal.
- **State-specific:** Each state's mine agency notification, plus state-EOC where required.
- **Edge cases:** Family notification before official ID; rumor on social media; reporter at gate before official statement.

## 16. Regulatory-Driven IT

### 16.1 MSHA Tracking & Communication Certification
- **What:** ERP and the underlying tracking + two-way comm system must be MSHA-approved; PE-certified design where applicable; system technicians trained per OEM.
- **Documents/standards:** 30 CFR 75.1502, 75.1600-3, MSHA Approval & Certification Center decisions; OEM intrinsic-safety approvals under 30 CFR Part 23.
- See 5.8.

### 16.2 Occupational Health Data (HIPAA controls)
- **What:** Where SCC maintains a self-insured plan or onsite clinic — HIPAA Privacy & Security Rule controls; drug-test and pulmonary-function-test data segregation.
- **Documents/standards:** HIPAA Security Rule §164.308–312, BAA with vendors.
- **Edge cases:** Sending PHI by unencrypted email to physician; supervisor receives test result instead of MRO.

### 16.3 PCI-DSS (if any card acceptance)
- **What:** SAQ-A or higher depending on architecture; tokenized via Stripe/Square if needed for any customer payment portal.
- **Documents/standards:** PCI DSS v4.0.1, SAQ, AOC.
- **Edge cases:** Cardholder data stored in CRM notes.

### 16.4 Federal-Contractor IT (NIST 800-171 / CMMC)
- **What:** Required if SCC handles CUI for any federal contract (rare for coal but possible for federal land or grant-tied work).
- **Documents/standards:** NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 / CMMC L2.
- **Edge cases:** Subcontractor flow-down missed.

### 16.5 State Data-Breach Notification Readiness
- **What:** Pre-drafted templates; counsel relationships; AG-portal credentials per state.
- **Documents/standards:**
  - **WV:** W.Va. Code §46A-2A-101 et seq. — "without unreasonable delay" notification; >1,000 affected triggers credit-reporting-agency notice.
  - **VA:** Va. Code §18.2-186.6 — "without unreasonable delay"; AG notice for >1,000 residents.
  - **KY:** KRS 365.732 — "most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay."
  - **AL:** Ala. Code §8-38-1 et seq. — 45-day deadline.
  - **TN:** Tenn. Code §47-18-2107 — 45-day deadline.
- **Edge cases:** Multi-state breach triggers conflicting deadlines (use shortest as floor); AG portal credentials lost; encryption-exemption applicability.

### 16.6 Records Retention (IT-managed records)
- **What:** Retention schedules for email, files, SaaS data, logs, recordings, video.
- **Documents/standards:** SCC retention schedule; legal-hold process.
- **Edge cases:** Cloud-app default purge contradicts hold; backup retention exceeds policy creating spoliation risk.

---

## 17. Vendor / SaaS Management

### 17.1 SaaS Inventory & Subscription Renewals
- **What:** Centralized SaaS catalog (Zylo / Productiv / Vendr / spreadsheet) with renewal calendar, owner, cost, contract terms.
- **Who:** Procurement + IT + finance.
- **Documents/standards:** Vendor contract repository; auto-renewal flag list.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; monthly renewal lookahead.
- **Edge cases:** Auto-renewal slipped past cancel window; shadow SaaS not in catalog.

### 17.2 Vendor Security Reviews & DPAs
- See 8.10.

### 17.3 SLA Monitoring
- **What:** Track vendor SLA achievement; credit claims; quarterly business review.
- **Frequency:** Continuous; quarterly review.

### 17.4 License Compliance Audits
- **What:** Internal & vendor-initiated true-up audits (Microsoft, Adobe, Oracle, Autodesk).
- **Frequency:** Internal annual; vendor-initiated event-driven.
- **Edge cases:** Audit finds Oracle DB used in container — large back-payment.

---

## 18. Cross-Cutting Common Edge Cases (Pattern Library for SCC-OS)

1. **Remote site connectivity loss** during shift — degrade to local-cache mode for SCC-OS; queue & sync.
2. **OT/IT segmentation failure** (lateral movement risk) — must alert and isolate.
3. **Ransomware on prep plant SCADA** — recovery playbook with safe-state and offline-controls fallback.
4. **MSHA tracking system outage** — automatic ERP-required escalation; cannot resume normal production until restored or evacuation triggered.
5. **Surveillance footage subpoena** — chain-of-custody export; preservation hold; verify retention.
6. **Contractor laptop on production network** — NAC quarantine; MAC-based exception aging-out.
7. **Departing geologist takes reserves data** — DLP egress alert + offboarding evidence preservation.
8. **Magazine inventory short** — 24-hr ATF notification, internal investigation, state mine agency, LE.
9. **Lightning strike at substation** — IT/OT damage triage; surge-failure-mode recovery.
10. **Vendor breach (e.g., MFT supplier)** — emergency reauth, integration suspension, AG notice scoping.
11. **Mass-notification false alarm** — corrective comms, lessons learned.
12. **BEC against finance** — wire-transfer reversal window (24 hrs typical), bank fraud team, FBI IC3.
13. **Drone in restricted airspace over impoundment** — FAA, LE, evidence capture.
14. **Insider threat from privileged admin** — PAM session-review, JIT removal, monitoring.
15. **CEMS down at coal dryer** — substitute-data procedure per 40 CFR 75 App. C; report excess emissions correctly.
16. **Major M365 outage** — pre-arranged fallback comms (mass-notification SMS, sat phone for execs).

## Cross-Domain Synthesis Notes

This inventory is intentionally redundant where domains overlap. The same function may appear in two domains seen from different angles (e.g., MSHA citations appear in Mine Safety from the operational/abatement side and in Legal from the contestation/litigation side). When building the SCC-OS data model, dedupe at the entity level but preserve both perspectives at the workflow level so each persona's UI surfaces the view they need.

## How to Use This Document

- **For product scoping:** every function listed implies at least one screen, one data entity, and one workflow inside SCC-OS. Use this as the master backlog source.
- **For Visual Forge:** pair this document with `SCC_Visual_Forge_Master_Context.md`. The latter describes how things look; this one describes everything they must do.
- **For database schema design:** entities and data points named here should map to existing tables in Supabase project `zymenlnwyzpnohljwifx` or trigger a migration discussion.
- **For client demos:** any prospect should be able to find every aspect of their operation represented here. If they ask "do you handle X?" and X is in this document, the answer is yes.
- **For regulatory audit:** the State-Specific and Documents dimensions of every function should provide a defensible mapping of "what we track" to "what regulators require."

## Living Document Disclaimer

Regulatory citations and form numbers were verified at the time of authorship (May 2026). State agencies, tax rates, MSHA rule revisions, and reporting forms change frequently. Before relying on any specific citation, frequency, or threshold for production compliance use, re-verify against the current rule or agency publication.
